items.name: Locally finite operators and ordinary projectors
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian ring with maximal ideal m_R and finite residue field, and Mod^comp(R) the category of m_R-adically complete and separated R-modules. Let M ∈ Mod^comp(R) and T ∈ End_R(M). Definition 2.11.1: T is locally finite on M if for all n ≥ 0, M/m_R^n M is an inductive limit of finite type R-modules stable under T. Lemma 2.11.2: if T_1 and T_2 commute and are both locally finite on M, then T_1T_2 is locally finite on M. Lemma 2.11.3 ([Pil20, Lem. 2.1.2]): T is locally finite on M if and only if it is locally finite on M/m_R M. Lemma 2.11.4 ([Pil20, Lem. 2.1.3]): if T is locally finite on M, then lim_{n→∞} T^{n!} converges pointwise in the m_R-adic topology to a projector e(T) on M, the ordinary projector attached to T. T and e(T) commute, and M = e(T)M ⊕ (1 − e(T))M is a T-stable decomposition, with T bijective on e(T)M and topologically nilpotent on (1 − e(T))M. Derived version: let D(R) be the derived category of R-modules, D^flat(R) the full subcategory generated by bounded complexes of flat m_R-adically complete and separated R-modules, and D^perf(R) the full subcategory generated by bounded complexes of finite free R-modules. For M ∈ D^flat(R), T ∈ End(M) is locally finite if some bounded complex of flat modules N representing M carries an endomorphism T_0 representing T that is locally finite in each degree. By [Pil20, Lem. 2.3.1], this holds if and only if T is locally finite on the cohomology groups H^i(M ⊗^L_R R/m_R) and some bounded complex of flat modules representing M carries an endomorphism representing T. A locally finite representative (N, T_0) gives an idempotent e(T_0) ∈ End(N). By [Pil20, Lem. 2.3.2], if e(T_0)M ∈ D^perf(R) for one locally finite representative, then for any other locally finite representative (N', T_1), e(T_1)M ∈ D^perf(R) and there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism e(T_0)M → e(T_1)M. When this holds, e(T) denotes this projector.
items.locator: §2.11 with Definition 2.11.1 and Lemmas 2.11.2–2.11.4, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Pilloni, Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weight, Lemmas 2.1.2 and 2.1.3)
items.note: Status: missing. PadicFamilies:L0a plans the special case of a complete separated module presented as an inverse limit of finite discrete quotients: pointwise convergence of U^{n!}, invertibility on eM, topological nilpotence on (1−e)M, and the degreewise application to perfect complexes. L0a does not yet state local finiteness when the quotients M/m^nM are only ind-finite, the criterion of Lemma 2.11.3, or the D^flat/D^perf formalism and its independence of the representative. The extraction of Pilloni 2020, the source of Lemmas 2.11.3 and 2.11.4 and of the derived statements, records the same material as missing (its Definition 2.1.1, Lemmas 2.1.2 and 2.1.3, Definitions 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, Proposition 2.3.1, which this paper cites as [Pil20, Lem. 2.3.1], and Lemma 2.3.2) and routes it by a source route to PadicFamilies:L0a, which is to add it in this general form. This item should follow the same routing, as a source route to PadicFamilies:L0a rather than as new work in the higher Hida roadmap, so that the material is planned once, in L0a, and imported by higher Hida and Coleman theory. Mathlib has the Fitting decomposition for Noetherian Artinian modules (LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow), which is an ingredient only. None of Lemmas 2.11.2–2.11.4 is cited by number elsewhere, so bundling them is acceptable.

items.name: The similitude groups G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 and its subgroup G
items.statement: Let F be totally real, V = O_F^4 with the O_F-linear symplectic form ⟨,⟩_1 given by J, and ⟨,⟩ = Tr_{F/Q}∘⟨,⟩_1. Then G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 is the group of F-linear symplectic automorphisms of (V_Q,⟨,⟩_1) up to a similitude factor ν in Res_{F/Q}G_m, and G ⊂ G_1 is the subgroup with similitude factor in G_m, that is G = G_1 ×_{ν,Res_{F/Q}G_m} G_m. G admits a PEL Shimura variety with a moduli interpretation, integral models and integral compactifications; G_1 gives a Shimura variety of abelian type, and the connected components of the G_1-Shimura varieties are quotients of those of the G-Shimura varieties by finite groups, following Deligne's strategy for abelian type.
items.locator: §3 introduction and §3.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Deligne, Variétés de Shimura, §2.7)
items.note: G is the similitude group of the PEL datum (O_F, V, ⟨ , ⟩), and PELModuli:M0 plans such similitude groups in general. Weil restriction of affine group schemes along finite separable extensions is planned by ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a and applied to the Hilbert groups in ShimuraData:D0, but GSp_4 with its similitude character ν (item 11) is not planned, and G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 is constructed nowhere, so the item stays missing. J is the matrix ((0, s), (−s, 0)) with s = ((0,1),(1,0)) from §2.1.1.

items.name: Definition 3.2.1: neat compact open subgroups
items.statement: Definition 3.2.1. For g = (g_l)_l ∈ G_1(A^∞) and each l, let Γ_{g_l} be the subgroup of Q̄_l^× generated by the eigenvalues of g_l under any faithful linear representation of G_1. Then g is neat if ∩_l (Q̄^× ∩ Γ_{g_l})_{tors} = 1. For g ∈ G_1(A^{∞,p}), g is neat if ∩_{l≠p} (Q̄^× ∩ Γ_{g_l})_{tors} = 1. A compact open subgroup K ⊂ G_1(A^∞) (resp. K^p ⊂ G_1(A^{∞,p})) is neat if all of its elements are neat.
items.locator: Definition 3.2.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties, Definition 1.4.1.8)
items.note: ShimuraData:D5 plans this definition. The only addition needed is the prime-to-p variant (intersection over l ≠ p, for K^p ⊂ G_1(A^{∞,p})), which D5 does not name; it is to be instantiated at D5, so that no consumer plans neatness again. The definition is used again on arXiv p. 212 (a level Iw_1(v) at a place of residue characteristic greater than 5 is neat). The item stays with ShimuraData D5. Its consumers, HilbertSiegelModularVarieties (Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field) and AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (the levels of §§7.7–7.8), import it from there rather than listing it as missing.

items.name: The Shimura varieties for G and G_1 over C, and Lemmas 3.2.2 and 3.2.3
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G_1(A^∞) be a neat compact open subgroup. The Shimura variety of G_1 is S_K^{G_1}(C) := G_1(Q)\(G_1(R) × G_1(A^∞))/Z(R)^0 K_∞^0 K. Here Z(R)^0 ≅ R_{>0}^{Hom(F,R)} is the identity component of the centre of G_1(R) ≅ GSp_4(R)^{Hom(F,R)}, and K_∞^0 is the identity component of a maximal compact subgroup of G_1(R), a product of copies of U(2); thus G_1(R)/Z(R)^0K_∞^0 = (𝓗 ∪ −𝓗)^{Hom(F,R)}, where 𝓗 is the Siegel half space of symmetric A + iB ∈ M_{2×2}(C) with B positive definite. Put G_1(Q)^+ := ν^{−1}(F^{×,+}). By strong approximation G_1(A^∞) = ⊔_c G_1(Q)^+ c K, where c runs through a finite set of elements of G_1(A^∞) whose multipliers ν(c) represent the strict class group F^{×,+}\(A^∞ ⊗_Q F)^×/ν(K). Hence S_K^{G_1}(C) = ⊔_c Γ_1(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)} with Γ_1(c,K) := G_1(Q)^+ ∩ cKc^{−1}. The double quotient S_K^G(C) := G(Q)\(G(R) × G_1(A^∞))/R_{>0}K_∞^0K is not the PEL Shimura variety of G. It satisfies S_K^G(C) = ⊔_c Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)} with Γ(c,K) := G(Q)^+ ∩ cKc^{−1}, where c now runs through elements whose multipliers represent the infinite set Q^{×,+}\(A^∞ ⊗_Q F)^×/ν(K). The inclusion G(R) ⊂ G_1(R) induces a surjection S_K^G(C) → S_K^{G_1}(C). On connected components it is the natural map Q^{×,+}\(A^∞⊗_Q F)^×/ν(K) → F^{×,+}\(A^∞⊗_Q F)^×/ν(K), and for each c ∈ G_1(A^∞) it gives a surjection Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)} → Γ_1(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)}. The centre Z(Γ_1(c,K)) is a finite-index subgroup O_F^×(K) of O_F^×. Let Δ(K) := Γ_1(c,K)/(O_F^×(K), Γ(c,K)), the quotient by the subgroup generated by O_F^×(K) and Γ(c,K). It is a finite group, independent of c, isomorphic to ν(Γ_1(c,K))/ν(O_F^×(K)) = (O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K))/ν(O_F^×(K)). Lemma 3.2.2: ν(Γ_1(c,K)) = O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K). Lemma 3.2.3: the map Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)} → Γ_1(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)} is finite étale with group Δ(K).
items.locator: §3.2 with Lemmas 3.2.2 and 3.2.3, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: ShimuraVarieties:V0–V1 plan the double-coset Shimura variety of any Shimura datum, with its decomposition into components and the arithmetic groups G(Q)_+ ∩ gKg^{−1}. S_K^{G_1}(C) is an instance of that construction for the Hilbert–Siegel datum of Res_{F/Q}GSp_4, which is not among the examples listed in ShimuraData:D5. S_K^G(C), which is not a Shimura variety, the group Δ(K) and Lemmas 3.2.2–3.2.3 are specific to this paper and not planned, so the item stays missing. Lemma 3.2.3 is used in Proposition 3.3.17.

items.name: The parahoric level subgroups at v|p described by chains of lattices
items.statement: Let p be a prime totally split in F and v a prime of O_F above p, so that F_v = Q_p and p is a uniformizer. In F_v^4 consider the chain of O_{F_v}-lattices V_0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → V_4, where V_0 = V ⊗_{O_F} O_{F_v} = ⊕_{i=1}^4 O_{F_v}e_i and V_j = ⟨p^{−1}e_1, …, p^{−1}e_j, e_{j+1}, …, e_4⟩. V_4 is identified with V_0 by multiplication by p, and indices are read in Z/4Z. The perfect pairing ⟨ , ⟩ on V_0 induces perfect pairings on V_2 × V_2 and on V_1 × V_3 (namely p⟨ , ⟩). Writing Aut of a chain for the automorphisms of F_v^4 preserving every lattice in it: GSp_4(O_{F_v}) = Aut(V_0) ∩ GSp_4(F_v) (hyperspecial); Par(v) = Aut(V_1 → V_3) ∩ GSp_4(F_v) (paramodular); Si(v) = Aut(V_0 → V_2) ∩ GSp_4(F_v) (Siegel parahoric); Kli(v) = Aut(V_0 → V_1 → V_3 → V_0) ∩ GSp_4(F_v) (Klingen parahoric); and Iw(v) = Aut(V_0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → V_0) ∩ GSp_4(F_v) (Iwahori).
items.locator: §3.3.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Planned. Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII), stage RG2.3, constructs for every facet the smooth affine parahoric group scheme. It characterizes the scheme by its integral points and records the distinctions between connected parahorics, fixer group schemes and hyperspecial models. Since p is totally split in F, F_v = Q_p. The five groups are then the hyperspecial, paramodular, Siegel, Klingen and Iwahori subgroups of GSp_4(Q_p). These are the standard parahoric subgroups that §2.1.1 lists by matrix shapes (item 159, also planned at RG2.3), here described as stabilizers of the lattice chains built from V_0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → V_4. Nothing specific to Hilbert modular varieties enters. The identification of each group with its lattice chain, and its agreement with the matrix descriptions of §2.1.1, are GSp_4 computations for the consuming roadmap. The lattice-chain conventions for Kli(v), Si(v), Iw(v) and Par(v) should match those fixed for the Siegel threefold in Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII). That proposed roadmap is where the extraction of Pilloni's Duke paper routes the Klingen and paramodular integral models.

items.name: Definition 3.3.3 and the moduli problem 𝕐_K: reasonable level structures
items.statement: Let p be a prime totally split in F, ALG/Z_(p) the category of Noetherian Z_(p)-algebras and AFF/Z_(p) its opposite category. A level structure is a compact open subgroup K ⊂ G_1(A^∞). Definition 3.3.3: K = K^pK_p is reasonable if K^p ⊂ G_1(A^{∞,p}) (printed G(A^{∞,p})) is neat and K_p = ∏_{v|p} K_v with K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Si(v), Kli(v), Iw(v)} for each v|p. For K reasonable, 𝐘_K is the groupoid over AFF/Z_(p) whose fibre over S = Spec R has as objects the tuples (A, ι, λ, η, η_p) such that: (1) A → Spec R is an abelian scheme; (2) ι : O_F → End(A) ⊗ Z_(p) (printed End(G)) is an action; (3) Lie(A) is a locally free O_F ⊗_Z R-module of rank 2; (4) λ : A → A^t is a prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-polarization, that is a Z_(p)^×-polarization in the sense of [Lan13, Defn. 1.3.2.19], such that for all v|p, Ker(λ : A[v^∞] → A^t[v^∞]) is trivial if K_v ≠ Par(v) and is a group scheme of order p^2 if K_v = Par(v); (5) η is a K^p-level structure; (6) η_p is a K_p-level structure. The K_p-level structure consists of: for each v|p with K_v = Kli(v), a subgroup scheme H_v ⊂ A[v] of order p; for each v with K_v = Si(v), a subgroup scheme L_v ⊂ A[v] of order p^2, totally isotropic for the Weil pairing; for each v with K_v = Iw(v), subgroups H_v ⊂ L_v ⊂ A[v] of orders p and p^2 with L_v totally isotropic for the Weil pairing. For the K^p-level structure, take S connected with a geometric point s̄. Then λ gives a symplectic Weil pairing ⟨ , ⟩_λ : H_1(A_s̄, A^{∞,p}) × H_1(A_s̄, A^{∞,p}) → H_1(G_{m,s̄}, A^{∞,p}), equivalently an F-linear pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{1,λ} with values in H_1(G_{m,s̄}, A^{∞,p}) ⊗ F. A K^p-level structure η is a K^p-orbit of pairs (η_1, η_2), where η_1 : V ⊗_Z A^{∞,p} ≅ H_1(A_s̄, A^{∞,p}) and η_2 : F ⊗_Z A^{∞,p} ≅ F ⊗_Z H_1(G_{m,s̄}, A^{∞,p}) are O_F ⊗ A^{∞,p}-linear isomorphisms of π_1(S,s̄)-modules satisfying ⟨η_1x, η_1y⟩_{1,λ} = η_2(⟨x,y⟩_1) (diagram (3.3.4)). An element k ∈ K^p sends (η_1, η_2) to (η_1k, ν(k)η_2). A morphism (A, ι, λ, η, η_p) → (A', ι', λ', η', η'_p) is an O_F-linear prime-to-p quasi-isogeny f : A → A' ([Lan13, Defn. 1.3.1.17]) such that f^*λ = rλ' for a locally constant function r : S → Z_(p)^{×,+} := Q^×_{>0} ∩ Z_(p)^×, f(η_p) = η'_p and H_1(f) ∘ η = η', meaning H_1(f)∘η_1 = η'_1 and η'_2 = r^{−1}η_2. η_2 is determined by η_1 (Remark 3.3.5). The similitude factor of the level structure lies in A^{∞,p} ⊗_Q F(1), but quasi-isogenies only have similitude factor in A^{∞,p}(1) (Remark 3.3.6). The structural map Π_0 : 𝐘_K → Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1) sends an object to the class of η_2(1). The target is the set Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p), with Gal(Q̄/Q) acting through the cyclotomic character Gal(Q̄/Q) → ∏_{l≠p} Z_l^× ⊂ (A^{∞,p})^×. This action is unramified at p, and the target is represented by an infinite disjoint union of finite étale Z_(p)-schemes. Z_(p)^{×,+} acts freely on (A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p) (Remark 3.3.7). When ν(K^p) = (O_F ⊗ ∏_{l≠p} Z_l)^×, the Galois action is trivial and the target is a disjoint union of copies of Spec Z_(p) (Remark 3.3.8).
items.locator: Definition 3.3.3 and §3.3.2, with Remarks 3.3.5–3.3.8, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: PELModuli:M1 plans PEL moduli functors with prime-to-p level orbits (the étale sheaf of trivializations of the prime-to-p Tate module) and prime-to-p quasi-isogenies, and M2 plans representability at good level with no level at p. At hyperspecial level, 𝐘_K is a disjoint union of such Kottwitz moduli problems for G, by the proof of Proposition 3.3.9. The parahoric level structures at p, the paramodular polarization condition and the G_1-similitude level structure are not planned, so the item stays missing. Two printed misprints, present in both versions: 'K^p ⊂ G(A^{∞,p})' in Definition 3.3.3 should read G_1(A^{∞,p}), and 'End(G)' in condition (2) should read End(A); the same 'End(G)' recurs in the Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli problem of §5.9 (published p. 317).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.9: representability of the integral model Y_K
items.statement: Proposition 3.3.9. Let K be reasonable. The groupoid 𝐘_K is representable by a quasi-projective scheme Y_K with structural morphism Π_0 : Y_K → Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1), and Π_0 has geometrically connected fibres. For c ∈ Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p), let c : Spec C → Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1) be the associated morphism (for the usual choice of primitive roots of unity in C), and let Y_{K,c} be the fibre of Y_K over c. Then there is an isomorphism of analytic spaces (Y_{K,c})^{an} ≅ Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.3.9, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Proof: 𝐘_K ≅ ⊔_{g ∈ G(A^{∞,p})\G_1(A^{∞,p})/K^p} 𝐘^{G,Kott}_{gK^pg^{−1} ∩ G(A^{∞,p})}, a disjoint union of Kottwitz PEL moduli problems for G, and the result follows from [Kot92, §§5, 8], written in Lan's notation. The complex fibres miss some geometrically connected components of S_K^G(C), because only polarizations of degree prime to p are allowed. At hyperspecial level at p, this is the good-prime PEL representability of PELModuli:M2–M3, with quasi-projectivity from ShimuraCompactifications:C5. The parahoric levels are not planned, so the item stays missing.

items.name: The action of totally positive units on Y_K, and Lemmas 3.3.12 and 3.3.13
items.statement: The group (O_F)_(p)^{×,+} of totally positive elements of F^× prime to p acts on Y_K by scaling the polarization: x sends (A, ι, λ, (η_1, η_2), η_p) to (A, ι, xλ, (η_1, xη_2), η_p), and the subgroup Z_(p)^{×,+} acts trivially. The group also acts on the set of connected components Π_0(Y_K). The stabilizer of each component is O_F^{×,+}(Π_0) := ((O_F)_(p)^{×,+} ∩ Z_(p)^{×,+}ν(K^p)∏_{l≠p}Z_l^×)/Z_(p)^{×,+}, naturally identified with O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K^p)∏_{l≠p}Z_l^×; this equals O_F^{×,+} when ν(K^p) = (O_F ⊗ ∏_{l≠p}Z_l)^× (Remark 3.3.11). The subgroup O_F^{×,+}(ν(K^p)) := O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K^p) acts trivially on each connected component of Π_0(Y_K). The quotient stack of connected components [((O_F)_(p)^{×,+}/Z_(p)^{×,+})\(Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1))] has coarse moduli space (O_F)_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1), a finite étale covering of Spec Z_(p). 𝐘_K^{G_1} := [Y_K/((O_F)_(p)^{×,+}/Z_(p)^{×,+})] is the Shimura stack of G_1 at level K. Let O_F^{×,+}(K^p) := {x^2 : x ∈ O_F^× ∩ K^p}, with O_F^× viewed as scalar matrices in G_1(A_f^{(p)}); it is a finite-index subgroup of O_F^{×,+}(ν(K^p)) and of O_F^{×,+}(Π_0). Lemma 3.3.12: the restriction of the action of (O_F)_(p)^{×,+} on Y_K to O_F^{×,+}(K^p) is trivial. More precisely, there is a canonical natural transformation from the action of O_F^{×,+}(K^p) on 𝐘_K to the trivial action, given by multiplication by x^{−1} : (A, ι, λ, η, η_p) → (A, ι, x^2λ, η, η_p). Lemma 3.3.13: for any geometric point x of Y_K, the stabilizer of x under the action of (O_F)_(p)^{×,+} is O_F^{×,+}(K^p).
items.locator: The action of (O_F)_(p)^{×,+}, Remark 3.3.11, Lemmas 3.3.12 and 3.3.13 (§3.3), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 47–49; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 208–210
items.note: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H3 plans the analogous action of totally positive units only for Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli, so the GSp_4 case is missing. Proof of Lemma 3.3.13: a morphism in the groupoid respecting η_1 is an automorphism of A, not just a quasi-isogeny (Lan13, Lem. 1.3.5.2). α = f f̄^{−1} is trivial by neatness. One then shows f ∈ F by cases (A simple; A isogenous to A_1 × A_2 with A_1, A_2 not isogenous; A isogenous to A_1^2), each time using neatness to exclude the eigenvalues ±√ε. The printed proof of Lemma 3.3.12 takes 'x ∈ O_F^{×,+} ∩ K^p' where the definition has x ∈ O_F^× ∩ K^p; this is a harmless slip, since positivity of x is never used.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.1 and Corollary 3.4.2: local models and the geometry of the integral models
items.statement: Let K be reasonable. For each v|p let M^loc_{K_v} be the moduli space over O_{F_v} of chains of lattices corresponding to K_v; for example M^loc_{Par(v)} is the moduli space of totally isotropic direct factors of rank 2 of V_1 ⊗_{O_F} O_{F_v}. Put M^loc_{K_p} := ×_{v|p} M^loc_{K_v}. By [RZ96, §6], each geometric point of the special fibre of Y_K (printed Y_K^G) has an étale neighbourhood isomorphic to an étale neighbourhood of a geometric point of M^loc_{K_p}. Proposition 3.4.1: the scheme Y_K is flat over Spec Z_(p), normal, and a local complete intersection (in particular Cohen–Macaulay) of pure relative dimension 3[F:Q]. If K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for all v|p it is smooth; in general it is smooth away from codimension 2. Corollary 3.4.2: Y_K^{G_1} is normal, flat over Spec Z_(p), and a local complete intersection.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4.1 and Corollary 3.4.2 (§3.4, Local models), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Görtz; de Jong; Rapoport–Zink; Tilouine)
items.note: Proof: flatness, the local complete intersection property and smoothness (or smoothness away from codimension 2) are étale-local and preserved by products, so it suffices to check them on the M^loc_{K_v}. This is trivial at hyperspecial level; Tilouine [Til06b, §2] treats Kli(v), Si(v) and Iw(v), and Yu [Yu11, Prop. 2.5, Thm. 2.11] treats Par(v). Normality follows from Cohen–Macaulay together with smoothness away from codimension 2. Corollary 3.4.2 follows because Y_K → Y_K^{G_1} is étale and surjective. No layer plans local models for GSp_4 at parahoric level; HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2 plans only the Hilbert integral models and their local model. Proposition 3.4.1 is cited on its own (arXiv pp. 67 and 69); Corollary 3.4.2 is not cited again, so the bundling is harmless.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.1: toroidal compactifications of Y_K at parahoric level
items.statement: Setting: K = K^pK_p ⊂ G_1(A^∞) is reasonable. Choose a lattice V' ⊂ V_F such that K^p stabilizes V' ⊗_Z A^{∞,p}, V' ⊗ O_{F_v} = V ⊗ O_{F_v} for the v|p with K_v ≠ Par(v), and V' ⊗ O_{F_v} = V_3 for the v with K_v = Par(v). Then (O_F, V', ⟨ , ⟩) is an integral PEL datum and K ⊂ G'_1(Ẑ), where G'_1 is the group scheme over Z of symplectic similitudes of V'. The theory of toroidal compactification attaches to it lattices L_{W,K,γ} for (W, γ) ∈ 𝔆 × G_1(A^∞) ([Lan13, §5.3], [Lan16, §3]). Theorem 3.5.1. (1) Let Σ be a K-admissible rational polyhedral cone decomposition which is projective. There is a toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K. It has a stratification indexed by (G(Q)^+ ∩ K_p)\Σ/K^p = G(Q)^+\Σ/K, and its boundary, the reduced complement of Y_K in X_{K,Σ}, is a relative Cartier divisor D_{K,Σ}. (2) The universal abelian scheme A → Y_K extends to a semi-abelian scheme A → X_{K,Σ}. (3) If Σ' is a refinement of Σ, there is a projective map π_{Σ',Σ} : X_{K,Σ'} → X_{K,Σ} with Rπ_{Σ',Σ,*}O_{X_{K,Σ'}} = O_{X_{K,Σ}}. If I_{X_{K,Σ}} and I_{X_{K,Σ'}} are the invertible ideal sheaves of the boundaries, then Rπ_{Σ',Σ,*}I_{X_{K,Σ'}} = I_{X_{K,Σ}}, and π_{Σ',Σ}^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} ⊂ I_{X_{K,Σ'}}. The paper also prints the equality π_{Σ',Σ}^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} = I_{X_{K,Σ'}}, which is false in general: when Σ is smooth and Σ' ≠ Σ the inclusion is strict (see the note). (4) For K reasonable, X_{K,Σ} is flat over Spec Z_(p), normal and Cohen–Macaulay. If Σ is smooth (with respect to the lattices L_{W,K,γ}), X_{K,Σ} → Spec Z_(p) is moreover a local complete intersection. Finally, if K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for all v|p and Σ is smooth, then X_{K,Σ} → Spec Z_(p) is smooth. By the convention stated just before the theorem, the decompositions used in the rest of the paper are projective and smooth with respect to the L_{W,K,γ} unless explicitly stated otherwise, so the smoothness hypothesis of (4) holds for them; consistently, Proposition 3.5.4 states the local complete intersection property without a smoothness hypothesis.
items.locator: Theorem 3.5.1 with the choice of integral PEL datum before it (§3.5), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 51–52; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 213–214 (Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties, and Lan 2016, 2017, Thm. 6.1)
items.note: Proof in the paper: by [Lan17, Thm. 6.1]. For K_p = G_1(Z_p) the compactification is constructed in [Lan13]. When every K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}, it is a closed subscheme of a toroidal compactification of a Siegel variety with prime-to-p polarization (Zarhin's trick). At general parahoric level it is a closed subscheme of the product of the compactifications of the Y_{K^pK'_p} along the degeneracy maps to levels K'_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}, possibly after a blow-up or blow-down at the boundary. ShimuraCompactifications:C5 plans integral PEL toroidal compactifications only at good primes, with no level at p, so the parahoric case is missing. The combinatorial data (the set 𝔆, the cones, K-admissibility) are a separate new item, planned by ShimuraCompactifications:C0–C1. The printed proof of (4) cites Proposition 3.5.4, which is itself deduced from this theorem; the intended reference is presumably Proposition 3.4.1, the local-model geometry of Y_K (recorded as a source issue). Theorem 3.5.1(3) is stated without the printed identity π_{Σ',Σ}^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} = I_{X_{K,Σ'}}, which reads the same in both versions and is recorded as a source issue. By (1) the boundary is reduced, and near the stratum of a smooth cone ⟨s_1, …, s_r⟩ the completion is toric with boundary x_1⋯x_r = 0. A refinement Σ' ≠ Σ of a smooth Σ must add a primitive ray u = Σ a_is_i, with integers a_i ≥ 1, in the relative interior of a face of dimension at least 2. Along the corresponding boundary divisor E of X_{K,Σ'}, π^*(x_1⋯x_r) vanishes to order Σ a_i ≥ 2, whereas the reduced boundary vanishes to order 1. For example, in the blow-up chart x_1 = a, x_2 = ab one has π^*(x_1x_2) = a^2b, while I_{X_{K,Σ'}} = (ab). Only the inclusion π^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} ⊂ I_{X_{K,Σ'}} holds. The only later use is Lemma 3.8.2. It needs just four facts: Rπ_*O = O, Rπ_*I_{X_{K,Σ'}} = I_{X_{K,Σ}}, the pullback of the canonical extension of ω^κ along π_{Σ',Σ}, and the projection formula. So nothing else is affected. The identical statement in Pilloni's Duke paper (Theorem 6.1.5.1(2)) is recorded as an error in the extraction of that paper.

items.name: Lemmas 3.6.4 and 3.6.5: the Klingen type correspondence p_1, p_2 at a place w|p
items.statement: Fix K^p and a place w|p. Let K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v ⊂ G_1(Z_p) be reasonable with K_w = GSp_4(O_{F_w}). Let K'_p = ∏_{v≠w}K_v × Kli(w), also reasonable, and K''_p = ∏_{v≠w}K_v × Par(w). Put K = K^pK_p, K' = K^pK'_p and K'' = K^pK''_p. Lemma 3.6.4: there are natural proper, surjective, generically finite étale forgetful maps p_1 : Y_{K'} → Y_K and p_1 : Y^{G_1}_{K'} → Y^{G_1}_K, which forget the subgroup H_w. Fix once and for all an element x_w ∈ F^{×,+} that is a uniformizer in F_w and a unit in F_v for every other v|p; it is well defined up to multiplication by (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}. Lemma 3.6.5: there is a proper, surjective, generically finite étale map p_2 : Y_{K'} → Y_{K''}, depending on x_w. It sends (A, ι, λ, η, η_p) to (A', ι', λ', η', η'_p), where: A' = A/H_w^⊥, with H_w^⊥ ⊂ A[w] the orthogonal of H_w for the Weil pairing (a group scheme of order p^3) and π : A → A' the quotient isogeny; ι'(x) = π∘ι(x)∘π^{−1}; λ' is the quasi-polarization obtained by descending x_w^2·λ from A to A'; η' = π∘η; and η'_p is deduced from η_p through the isomorphisms π : A[v] → A'[v] for v ≠ w above p. It induces a canonical map p_2 : Y^{G_1}_{K'} → Y^{G_1}_{K''}: the dependence on x_w disappears after passing to the quotient stacks by (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} and to coarse moduli. Remark 3.6.6: A ↦ A/H_w gives another map Y_{K'} → Y_{K''}, which is not used. By the opening paragraph of §3.6, these maps extend to toroidal compactifications for suitable choices of cone decompositions.
items.locator: Lemmas 3.6.4 and 3.6.5 and Remark 3.6.6 (§3.6.3), with the opening paragraph of §3.6; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 53–54, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from the former item, which also covered the Siegel correspondence (§3.6.7). That correspondence and the prime-to-p maps of §§3.6.1–3.6.2 are separate items. Status missing: there is no library declaration, and no atlas layer constructs level-changing maps for the Hilbert–Siegel moduli problem at parahoric level at p. For GL_2 over a totally real field, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H4 constructs Iwahori and Γ_0(p^n) level structures and R18.4 the degeneracy maps. ShimuraCompactifications C3 extends Hecke translations to toroidal compactifications with compatible fans, and the integral PEL compactifications of C5 keep good-prime hypotheses.

items.name: §3.7: the sheaves ω^κ, weights for G and G_1, the descent datum and the canonical extension
items.statement: From §3.7 on, p splits completely in F and one works over Z_p. S_p is the set of places above p, O_F ⊗_Z Z_p = ∏_{v|p}Z_p, and v : O_F → Z_p is the v-th projection. (1) Over Y_K the prime-to-p isogeny class of abelian schemes gives a canonical Barsotti–Tate group 𝒢. Its conormal sheaf ω_𝒢 carries an O_F-action and decomposes as ω_𝒢 = ∏_{v|p}ω_{𝒢,v}, each ω_{𝒢,v} locally free of rank 2 over Y_K. (2) A dominant algebraic weight for G is a tuple κ = (k_v, l_v)_{v∈S_p} of integers with k_v ≥ l_v for all v. It is classical if moreover l_v ≥ 2 for all v. The locally free sheaf attached to κ is ω^κ = ⊗_{v∈S_p}(Sym^{k_v−l_v}ω_{𝒢,v} ⊗ det^{l_v}ω_{𝒢,v}), printed with ∏_v for the tensor product. (3) A weight for G_1 is ((k_v, l_v)_{v∈S_p}, w) with k_v ≥ l_v and k_v − l_v ≡ w (mod 2) for each v, classical if l_v ≥ 2 for all v. The paper takes w even and later fixes w = 2. For such w and x ∈ (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}, the isomorphism ω^κ_{(A,ι,x^{−1}λ,η,η_p)} = ω^κ_{(A,ι,λ,η,η_p)} → ω^κ_{(A,ι,λ,η,η_p)} is multiplication by ∏_v v(x)^{(k_v+l_v−w)/2}; the first identification is tautological, since ω^κ does not depend on the polarization. These isomorphisms form a descent datum for the étale map Y_K → Y_K^{G_1}. They are compatible with the identifications from x = ε^2 ∈ O_F^{×,+}(K^p) with ε ∈ O_F^× ∩ K^p, because ε acts by κ(ε) = ∏_v v(ε)^{k_v+l_v} = ∏_v v(ε^2)^{(k_v+l_v−w)/2}·N_{F/Q}(ε)^w and N_{F/Q}(ε)^w = 1 for w even. The datum is effective: on connected components it reduces to finite étale descent for Δ(Π_0). The resulting sheaf on Y_K^{G_1} is also written ω^κ; it depends on w. (4) Remark 3.7.3. Over F_p, let κ = (k_v, l_v)_{v|p} be a weight for G with k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 0 (mod p − 1). Then the tautological isomorphisms ω^κ_{(A,ι,x^{−1}λ,η,η_p)} = ω^κ_{(A,ι,λ,η,η_p)}, for x ∈ (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}, form a canonical descent datum from Y_{K,1} to Y^{G_1}_{K,1}, because the character ε ↦ ∏_{v|p}[v(ε)^{k_v+l_v} mod p] of O_F^× is trivial. (5) The sheaf ω_𝒢 has the canonical extension e^*Ω^1_{A/X_{K,Σ}} to X_{K,Σ}, where A is the semi-abelian scheme of Theorem 3.5.1(2) and e its identity section. This extends ω^κ to X_{K,Σ} and to X^{G_1}_{K,Σ}; the extensions are denoted by the same symbol.
items.locator: §3.7 (§§3.7.1 and 3.7.2, Remark 3.7.3 and the closing paragraph on canonical extensions); arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 55–56, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: The paper writes ω^κ = ∏_v Sym^{k_v−l_v}ω_{𝒢,v} ⊗ det^{l_v}ω_{𝒢,v}. The product over v is a tensor product, for two reasons. The descent isomorphism is multiplication by the single scalar ∏_v v(x)^{(k_v+l_v−w)/2}. And for k_v = l_v the sheaf is a line bundle, which is the case of the Hasse invariants (Remark 3.7.3, §4.1). This is notation, not a misprint. Status missing. AutomorphicBundles B2 and B3 plan automorphic bundles over the canonical model and their canonical and subcanonical extensions. That roadmap's completion conditions ask for classical forms over the specified integral PEL/Hilbert models, whose compactifications (ShimuraCompactifications C5) keep good-prime hypotheses. The integral sheaves at parahoric level at p, the weights for G_1 and the w-dependent descent to Y_K^{G_1} are planned nowhere. Item 143 records what is planned.

items.name: Proposition 3.8.3 and Lemma 3.8.5: the pullback from X_K^{G_1} to X_K splits
items.statement: Proposition 3.8.3. The pullback maps RΓ(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ) → RΓ(X_K, ω^κ) and RΓ(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) → RΓ(X_K, ω^κ(−D)) split in the derived category of Z_p-modules. Remark 3.8.4: this transfers properties of the cohomology of X_K, which has a moduli interpretation, to X_K^{G_1}. Lemma 3.8.5, corrected. Let G be a finite group whose order is invertible on S, let I_G ⊂ Z[G] be its augmentation ideal, and let f : T → S be a finite étale morphism with Galois group G. Then the natural map O_S ⊕ (I_G ⊗_{Z[G]} f_*O_T) → f_*O_T is an isomorphism; in particular O_S → f_*O_T is split. The printed lemma has no hypothesis on #G. The paper deduces Proposition 3.8.3 by applying Lemma 3.8.5 to the finite étale Galois covers X_{K,c} → X^{G_1}_{K,π(c)} with group Δ(Π_0) = O_F^{×,+}(Π_0)/O_F^{×,+}(K^p), so its argument proves the proposition when p does not divide #Δ(Π_0).
items.locator: Proposition 3.8.3, Remark 3.8.4 and Lemma 3.8.5 (§3.8.1); arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 57–58, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Recorded source issue E36 (error, affects a stated result; the same in arXiv v3 and the published version): Lemma 3.8.5 needs #G invertible on S, and Proposition 3.8.3 then needs p ∤ #Δ(K^p). For T = S × Z/p over S = Spec Z_p the map O_S ⊕ (I_G ⊗_{Z[G]} f_*O_T) → f_*O_T has index p. The proof of Proposition 3.8.3 applies Lemma 3.8.5 with G = Δ(Π_0) over Z_p-schemes, and nothing in §§3.2–3.8 makes #Δ(Π_0) prime to p. By (3.3.15) and Remark 3.3.11, when ν(K^p) = (O_F ⊗ ∏_{ℓ≠p}Z_ℓ)^× one has Δ(Π_0) = O_F^{×,+}/{x^2 : x ∈ O_F^× ∩ K^p}. Its order is [O_F^{×,+} : (O_F^×)^2]·[O_F^× : {±1}(O_F^× ∩ K^p)], and the second index is not a priori prime to p. Pullback along a finite étale Galois cover whose group has order divisible by p need not be split injective on coherent cohomology. For example, for an ordinary elliptic curve E over F̄_p, the Verschiebung E^{(p)} → E is an étale Z/p-cover and induces zero on H^1(O). So the argument proves the proposition when p ∤ #Δ(Π_0). It is enough that p ∤ #Δ(K^p), where Δ(K^p) = O_F^{×,+}(ν(K^p))/O_F^{×,+}(K^p) ⊂ Δ(Π_0) (3.3.16) is the stabilizer of a geometrically connected component: the rest of Δ(Π_0) only moves the base, where the trace is surjective. When p divides #Δ(K^p) the proposition can fail: for F = Q(√7) and p = 3 a neat level gives Δ(Π_0) = Δ(K^p) ≅ Z/36, and an Artin–Schreier class shows that Proposition 3.8.3 fails. The hypothesis p ∤ #Δ(K^p) has to be carried to its use in §4.2 (p. 78), to Proposition 4.4.3, whose proof is that of Proposition 3.8.3 (p. 99: 'See the proof of Proposition 3.8.3'), and to §6.3.8. The proof of Lemma 3.8.5 also writes 'O_X[G]-modules' where O_S[G]-modules are meant. Status missing: no library or atlas layer.

items.name: §3.8.8 and Lemma 3.8.9: coherent duality for embeddable morphisms and f^!O_Y between local complete intersections
items.statement: Let S be an affine Noetherian scheme. A morphism f : X → Y of S-schemes is embeddable if it factors as X →^i P ×_S Y → Y with P a smooth S-scheme, i finite and the second map the projection. It is projectively embeddable if P can be taken to be a projective space over S; the paper prints 'p'. D_qcoh(O_X) is the derived category of O_X-modules with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves, and D^+_qcoh(O_X) its bounded-below part. For f embeddable there is an exact functor of triangulated categories f^! : D^+_qcoh(O_Y) → D^+_qcoh(O_X). If f is projectively embeddable, f^! is right adjoint to Rf_*, and the counit is the trace map Rf_*f^! ⇒ Id of endofunctors of D^+_qcoh(O_Y). For X → S a local complete intersection, K_{X/S} is the relative canonical sheaf, the determinant of the cotangent complex. Lemma 3.8.9 ([Pil20, Cor. 4.1.3.1]). Let f : X → Y be an embeddable morphism between two embeddable S-schemes such that X → S and Y → S are local complete intersections of pure relative dimension n. Then f^!O_Y = K_{X/S} ⊗_{O_X} f^*K_{Y/S}^{−1}, an invertible sheaf.

Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Lemma 3.8.9 is Pilloni, Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights, Cor. 4.1.3.1)

Recorded misprint E37 (affects nothing, present in both versions): 'projectively embeddable if p can be taken to be a projective space' should read P. These are §§4.1–4.2 of Pilloni's paper and the source of §§3.8.8–3.8.15 here. items.name: Definitions 3.9.1 and 3.9.2: correspondences and cohomological correspondences
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme and X, Y S-schemes. Definition 3.9.1. A correspondence C over X and Y is a diagram of S-morphisms X ←^{p_2} C →^{p_1} Y in which X, Y and C have the same pure relative dimension over S and p_1, p_2 are projectively embeddable. Definition 3.9.2. Let 𝓕 be a coherent sheaf on X and 𝓖 a coherent sheaf on Y. A cohomological correspondence from 𝓕 to 𝓖 is a correspondence C over X and Y together with a map T : R(p_1)_*p_2^*𝓕 → 𝓖; by adjunction T is equivalently a map p_2^*𝓕 → p_1^!𝓖. It induces a map on cohomology, still written T: the composite RΓ(X, 𝓕) →^{p_2^*} RΓ(C, p_2^*𝓕) = RΓ(Y, R(p_1)_*p_2^*𝓕) →^{T} RΓ(Y, 𝓖).

Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (after Pilloni, Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights, Definition 4.3.1 and Remark 4.3.2)

items.name: Theorem 3.9.6 (Kempf), Remark 3.9.7 and Example 3.9.9: Cousin complexes of maximal Cohen–Macaulay sheaves
items.statement: Theorem 3.9.6. Let X be a Noetherian scheme with a filtration Z : Z_0 = X ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ ⋯ by closed subschemes such that, for all i, (1) codim_X(Z_i) ≥ i and (2) the morphism Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1} → X is affine. Then for every maximal Cohen–Macaulay coherent sheaf 𝓕 on X, the augmentation 𝓕 → Cous_Z(𝓕) is a quasi-isomorphism ([Kem78, Thm. 10.9]; 𝓕 is called locally Cohen–Macaulay with respect to Z when Cous_Z(𝓕) is a resolution of it, [Kem78, p. 358]). Remark 3.9.7. If moreover each Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1} is affine, Cous_Z(𝓕) is a complex of acyclic sheaves ([Kem78, Thm. 9.6]). Example 3.9.9. Let s_t : O_X → 𝓛_t (1 ≤ t ≤ i) be effective Cartier divisors that intersect properly: for every n, the twisted Koszul complex Kos(s_1^n, …, s_i^n) : 0 → ⊗_t𝓛_t^{−n} → ⊕_{t'}⊗_{t≠t'}𝓛_t^{−n} → ⋯ → ⊕_t𝓛_t^{−n} → O_X → 0 is a locally free resolution of O_X/(s_1^n, …, s_i^n), printed O_X/(𝓛_1^{−n}, …, 𝓛_t^{−n}). Let Z = V(𝓛_1^{−1}, …, 𝓛_i^{−1}) be the common zero locus and 𝓕 a locally free coherent sheaf. Then 𝓔xt^j(O_X/(s_1^n, …, s_i^n), 𝓕) = 0 for j ≠ i, and 𝓔xt^i(O_X/(s_1^n, …, s_i^n), 𝓕) = Coker(⊕_t s_t^n : ⊕_t(⊗_{t'≠t}𝓛_{t'}^n) ⊗ 𝓕 → (⊗_t𝓛_t^n) ⊗ 𝓕). The direct limit over n is R^iΓ_Z(𝓕).
items.locator: Theorem 3.9.6, Remark 3.9.7 and Example 3.9.9 (§3.9.5); arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 64–65, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Kempf, The Grothendieck–Cousin complex of an induced representation, Adv. Math. 29 (1978), Theorems 10.9 and 9.6)
items.note: Example 3.9.9, in arXiv v3 and in the published version, prints the quotient as O_X/(𝓛_1^{−n}, …, 𝓛_t^{−n}), where the last index should be i. Status missing. Mathlib's localCohomology defines H^i_I(M) = colim_n Ext^i(R/I^n, M) for modules over a commutative ring. For R Noetherian it identifies this with the colimit over all ideals whose radical contains I (localCohomology.isoSelfLERadical), and shows that it depends only on the radical of I (localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical). That is the affine, module-level form of the formula in Example 3.9.9. There are no sheaf-level local cohomology, Cousin complexes, Koszul complexes or Cohen–Macaulay sheaves in either library, and no atlas layer plans Kempf's theorem. Routing: it goes as a source to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (sheaf cohomology, localization, base change and compact support), in that layer's package of cohomology with supports. The merged extraction of Pilloni's paper sends the SGA 2 depth statement there too.

items.name: Propositions 3.9.11 and 3.9.15: Cousin complexes of the Ekedahl–Oort filtration and the prime-to-p Hecke action
items.statement: Assume K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(Z_p). Let X = X_{K,Σ}, f : X → X^* the map to the minimal compactification, X_n = X × Spec Z/p^nZ with interior Y_n, and Z the pull-back to X_n of the Ekedahl–Oort filtration Z^* of X_n^* (§3.9.10). Proposition 3.9.11. RΓ(X_n, ω^κ(−D)) is computed by Γ(X_n, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))). By Theorem 3.9.6, ω^κ(−D) → Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism. The degree-i term (j_{i+1})_*R^iΓ_{Z_i∖Z_{i+1}}(ω^κ(−D)|_{U_{i+1}}) is acyclic, since its Rf_* is concentrated in degree 0 and supported on the affine Z_i^* ∖ Z_{i+1}^*. Lemma 3.9.12. Restriction gives an injection of complexes Γ(X_n, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))) ↪ Γ(Y_n, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))). Lemma 3.9.13. For g ∈ G_1(A_f^p), printed G(A_f^p), the cohomological correspondence p_2^*ω^κ(−D) → p_1^!ω^κ(−D) of §3.9.3, reduced modulo p^n, induces a cohomological correspondence of complexes p_2^*Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D)) → p_1^!Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D)), compatible with the augmentation. Remark 3.9.14: p_2^* and p_1^! are applied termwise, and each p_1^!Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))^i is a sheaf. Proposition 3.9.15. The Hecke algebra H^p acts on RΓ(X^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) and on RΓ(X^{G_1}, ω^κ): the operators [K^pgK^p] of §3.9.3 compose according to the product of H^p. Proof: RΓ(X, ω^κ(−D)) is represented by lim_n Γ(X_n, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))), which injects into lim_n Γ(Y_n, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))); one restricts to the G_1 direct factor, the Ekedahl–Oort stratification being preserved by (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}; the relations are known on lim_n Γ(Y_n^{G_1}, Cous_Z(ω^κ(−D))); the case of ω^κ follows by Serre duality. Remark 3.9.16. For three tame levels K_1^p, K_2^p, K_3^p and suitable cone decompositions Σ_1, Σ_2, Σ_3, the composite of [K_1^pg_1K_2^p] : RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K_2^pK_p,Σ_2}, ω^κ) → RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K_1^pK_p,Σ_1}, ω^κ) and [K_2^pg_2K_3^p] : RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K_3^pK_p,Σ_3}, ω^κ) → RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K_2^pK_p,Σ_2}, ω^κ) is the Hecke operator [K_1^pg_1K_2^p][K_2^pg_2K_3^p].

The merged extraction of Pilloni's paper puts in that roadmap the statement that the Hecke relations hold on RΓ of the automorphic bundles of Siegel threefolds. Proposition 3.9.15 is the Hilbert–Siegel analogue, proved by a different method; stating both there keeps a single owner for the general statement. items.name: Lemma 3.9.18: the normalized Siegel type Hecke operator T_{w,1} at w|p
items.statement: Let K = K^pK_p with K_p = G_1(Z_p), fix w|p, and let K' = K^pK'_p with K'_p = ∏_{v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) × Si(w). Let p_1, p_2 : X_{K'} → X_K be the Siegel type correspondence of §3.6.7, where p_2 depends on x_w. By Proposition 3.4.1: X_{K'} and X_K are relative complete intersections over Spec Z_p, pure of the same dimension; X_K is smooth over Z_p; and X_{K'} is normal and smooth over Z_p outside codimension 2. So we are in the lci situation of §3.8.11: p_1^!O_{X_K} is invertible and there is a fundamental class p_1^*O_{X_K} → p_1^!O_{X_K}. For κ = (k_v, l_v) with l_v ≥ 0, the differential of the isogeny p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 on X_{K'} gives p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^*ω^κ. Composing gives a cohomological correspondence Θ : p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ. Lemma 3.9.18. If l_w ≥ 2, Θ factors through p^3p_1^!ω^κ. The check is at the generic points of the special fibre of X_{K'}, classified by the multiplicative rank r ∈ {0, 1, 2} of p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢. At those points the fundamental class is divisible by p^3, p and p^0, and the map on ω^κ by p^0, p^{l_w} and p^{k_w+l_w}, respectively. T_{w,1} is the composite RΓ(X_K, ω^κ) → RΓ(X_{K'}, p_2^*ω^κ) →^{p^{−3}Θ} RΓ(X_{K'}, p_1^!ω^κ) →^{Tr} RΓ(X_K, ω^κ). It is defined in the same way on cuspidal cohomology and over X_K^{G_1}. On X_K it depends on x_w; on X_K^{G_1} it is canonical. Remark 3.9.19. The correspondence is that of the double coset [GSp_4(O_{F_w}) diag(1, 1, p^{−1}, p^{−1}) GSp_4(O_{F_w})], which differs by a central element from the spherical operator of §2.4.7; on spaces with fixed central character the normalized actions agree. Remark 3.9.23. The action of T_{w,1} is independent of the toroidal compactification (as for T_w in [Pil20, Prop. 7.2.1]).

The old text called the factors in Remark 3.9.21 'two Klingen cosets'; as printed they are double cosets between GSp_4(O_{F_w}) and the paramodular group Par(w). items.name: Theorem 3.10.1: localized coherent cohomology in degrees 0 and 1 and cuspidal automorphic representations
items.statement: Let K = ∏_vK_v ⊂ GSp_4(A_F^∞) = G_1(A_Q^∞) be an open compact subgroup (of the kind for which X_K^{G_1} is defined in §§3.3–3.5). Let S ⊃ S_p be a finite set of places with K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S. Let E be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O, and T̃ = ⊗_{v∉S}O[GSp_4(F_v)//GSp_4(O_{F_v})]. Theorem 3.10.1. Let κ = (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞} be a weight with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 and k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2), and let m ⊂ T̃ be non-Eisenstein. (1) For i = 0, 1 there is an Ē[GSp_4(A_F^∞)//K]-equivariant inclusion ⊕_π(π^∞)^K_m ⊗ Ē ⊆ H^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2}_m ⊗ Ē (3.10.2). On the right, the superscript |·|^2 denotes the subspace on which the diamond operators at places v ∉ S act via |·|^2. On the left, π runs over the cuspidal automorphic representations of GSp_4(A_F) of weight κ and central character |·|^2 such that π_v is holomorphic for every v|∞ with l_v > 2, and #{v|∞ : π_v is not holomorphic} = i. (2) There is an absolute constant R such that if, for each v|∞, k_v − l_v > R and either l_v = 2 or l_v > R, then (3.10.2) is an equality. (3) For i = 0, (3.10.2) is an equality. More precisely, without localizing at a non-Eisenstein ideal there is an Ē[GSp_4(A_F^∞)//K]-equivariant isomorphism H^0(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2} ⊗ Ē = ⊕_π(π^∞)^K (3.10.3), the sum running over the cuspidal automorphic π of weight κ and central character |·|^2 that are holomorphic at all infinite places. Remark 3.10.4: the results should hold in every degree and with a much weaker regularity hypothesis in (2); restricting to i ≤ 1 means only degree-0 boundary cohomology has to be considered.
items.locator: Theorem 3.10.1 with Remark 3.10.4 (§3.10); arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 70 (proof pp. 72–73), the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: The proof runs as follows. Lemma 3.10.7 reduces H^i(ω^κ(−D))_m, for i ≤ 1, to interior cohomology. Then come Harris's inclusions [Har90a, Thm. 2.7], multiplicity one from Arthur's multiplicity formula (items 32 and 33, conditional), [BHR94]'s temperedness under the regularity hypothesis of (2), Wallach's cuspidality theorem, Mirković's and [BHR94]'s archimedean vanishing, and the Künneth formula. Part (3) uses [Har90a, Prop. 2.7.2] and lowest weight theory. Each of these inputs is a new item, except Arthur's multiplicity formula (items 32–33) and the Künneth formula. Status missing. Routing: this item goes to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes). The Siegel threefold (F = Q) instances of these statements are already there, through the merged extractions of Calegari–Geraghty 2020 (Harris's Theorem 5.2 and interior cohomology, layer 6) and of Pilloni (Theorem 15.2.3.1 and Corollary 15.2.3.1). Theorem 3.10.1 generalizes them to Hilbert–Siegel varieties, and stating it there keeps a single owner for the comparison: parts (1)–(2) in layer 8, the isomorphism (3.10.3) of part (3) in layer 6. The varieties are imported from HilbertSiegelModularVarieties, and Arthur's classification from ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4.

items.name: §4: higher Hida theory for GSp_4 over a totally real field
items.statement: §4 constructs (higher) Hida theories for GSp_4(A_F). It assumes that p splits completely in F, and it allows the weight space at each place above p to be one- or two-dimensional. A classical weight κ = (k_v,l_v)_{v|p} with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 is singular at v if l_v = 2 and regular at v if l_v > 2. Fix a set I of places above p: at the places of I one interpolates forms of singular weight, and at the places of I^c forms of regular weight. Two special cases are already known. I = ∅ is classical Hida theory [Hid04], which gives a projective module over the 2[F:Q]-dimensional weight space. F = Q with I = {p} is the higher Hida theory of [Pil20], which gives a perfect complex of amplitude [0,1] over a one-dimensional hyperplane of the weight space. There is a Hecke operator U^I, an analogue of U_p, which acts locally finitely on a complex of p-adic automorphic forms. That complex is the cohomology of the following locus: infinite Klingen level over the locus of p-rank at least 1 at the places w ∈ I, and infinite Iwahori level over the ordinary (p-rank 2) locus at the places w ∈ I^c. This locus is not affine. Relating the cohomology of the toroidal and minimal compactifications shows that its cohomology is supported in degrees [0,#I]. The U^I-ordinary part M_I is a perfect complex over a weight space Λ_I, concentrated in degrees [0,#I]. There is a constant C with the following property: if k_v − l_v ≥ C and l_v = 2 for v ∈ I, and l_v ≥ C for v ∉ I, then H^0 of the specialization of M_I in weight κ agrees with the ordinary part of H^0 of X_K^{G_1}. There is also an injection of H^1 of the classical cohomology into H^1 of that specialization, which §6 uses. The expected quasi-isomorphism between the specialization and the ordinary part of the classical cohomology is not proved. The main theorem of §4, and the only one used later, is Theorem 4.6.1. Its proof has three steps. First, Nakayama's lemma for complexes reduces it to the cohomology modulo p in sufficiently large weight. Second, a computation with the sheaf ω^κ and in the Hecke algebra relates that cohomology to the cohomology of ω^κ over the locus X_{K,1}^{G_1,I} of the special fibre. This locus has p-rank at least 1 at the places w ∈ I and is ordinary at the places w ∈ I^c. Third, in sufficiently regular weight in characteristic p, the Hecke operators act by zero on the complement of X_{K,1}^{G_1,I}: through T_{w,1} (Siegel vanishing) on the non-ordinary locus for w ∈ I^c, and through T_w (Klingen vanishing) on the p-rank 0 locus for w ∈ I. So after taking ordinary parts the cohomology of X_{K,1}^{G_1,I} is finite and is controlled by that of the whole Shimura variety, which is proper. The overview says the two agree. What Theorem 4.2.1 actually proves is: perfectness in amplitude [0,#I], an isomorphism on H^0 and an injection on H^1, and a full quasi-isomorphism only when moreover l_w ≥ 3 for all w ∈ I.

items.name: §4.1: Hasse invariants, the secondary Hasse invariant, the p-rank stratification and its descent to X^{G_1}
items.statement:
§4.1.1 setting. Let K = K^pK_p with K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v and K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}. Fix a polyhedral cone decomposition Σ and write X = X_{K,Σ}. Let 𝓖 = A[p^∞] be the p-divisible group of the semi-abelian scheme A over X; it is well defined up to prime-to-p quasi-isogeny and decomposes as 𝓖 = ∏_{v|p}𝓖_v. If K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}), then 𝓖_v carries a principal quasi-polarization. If K_v = Par(v), it carries a quasi-polarization 𝓖_v → 𝓖_v^D of degree p^2. Let X_1 be the reduction of X modulo p.

Hasse invariant. Ha(𝓖_v) ∈ H^0(X_1, det ω_{𝓖,v}^{p−1}) is the Hasse invariant of 𝓖_v. It is compatible with étale isogenies and with duality. For v|p:
- X_1^{≥_v2} = X_1^{=_v2} is the open subscheme where Ha(𝓖_v) ≠ 0, the ordinary locus at v.
- X_1^{≤_v1} is its complement, the closed subscheme defined by Ha(𝓖_v) = 0, the non-ordinary locus at v. This subscheme is reduced, by the proof of [Pil20, Lem. 6.4.1].
The superscripts refer to the multiplicative rank of 𝓖_v.

Secondary Hasse invariant. As a very special case of the general constructions of Boxer [Box15] and Goldring–Koskivirta [GK19] (see also [Pil20, §6.3.2] when K = Par(v)), there is a secondary Hasse invariant Ha'(𝓖_v) ∈ H^0(X_1^{≤_v1}, det ω_{𝓖,v}^{p^2−1}).
- Its non-vanishing locus X_1^{=_v1} is the rank 1 locus at v.
- Its schematic complement X_1^{=_v0}, defined by Ha'(𝓖_v) = 0, is the supersingular locus at v. It carries a non-reduced scheme structure [Pil20, Rem. 6.4.1].

Strata. Take disjoint subsets I_1,…,I_r ⊂ {v|p}, symbols ∗(i) ∈ {≤,≥,=} and numbers a_i ∈ {0,1,2}. Then X_1^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i, i=1,…,r} is the intersection of the X_1^{∗(i)_va_i} over 1 ≤ i ≤ r and v ∈ I_i. X_1^{≥2} := X_1^{≥_{{v|p}}2} is the ordinary locus, and X_1^{≥1} := X_1^{≥_{{v|p}}1} is the rank 1 locus.

§4.1.2, descent. The p-rank stratification is independent of the polarization. So all these spaces carry an induced action of (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}, and the stratification descends to X_1^{G_1}. The sheaf det ω_{𝓖,v}^{p−1} descends canonically to X_1^{G_1} (Remark 3.7.3). Hence Ha(𝓖_v) and Ha'(𝓖_v), whose definition is independent of the polarization, descend to sections over X_1^{G_1} and X_1^{G_1,≤_v1} respectively. For each datum (I_i, ∗(i), a_i) there is a unique locally closed subscheme (X^{G_1}_{K,1})^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i} of X^{G_1}_{K,1} whose inverse image in X_{K,1} is (X_{K,1})^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i}.

Remark 4.1.3. §4.3.4 defines further locally closed subschemes of the special fibres at Klingen and Iwahori level. These are not defined through the p-ranks of the 𝓖_v[p]; they are defined through subschemes of 𝓖_v[p] given by the level structures.

The Calegari–Geraghty 2020 extraction proposed that SiegelModularFormsModPn (Part II of AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights) own the Hasse invariant of a p-divisible group over any F_p-scheme. SiegelModularFormsModPn keeps the secondary Hasse invariant Ha', both over F_p-schemes and on the Siegel threefold at spherical and paramodular level, together with the p-rank strata and the reducedness of V(Ha) (Pilloni's Lemma 6.4.1). items.name: §4.1: density of the ordinary and rank one loci
items.statement:
Setting. Let I_1,…,I_r ⊂ {v|p} be disjoint, with ∗(i) ∈ {≤,≥,=} and a_i ∈ {0,1,2}. Let v|p be a place not contained in I_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ I_r. Let K = K^pK_p with K_p = ∏_{w|p,w≠v}K_w × K_v, where K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Kli(v), Si(v), Iw(v)} and K_w ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_w}), Par(w)} for w ≠ v. The topological spaces |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i}|, |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i,=_v2}|, |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i,≤_v1}| and |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i,=_v1}| are defined through the p-rank stratification, using the p-rank of any Barsotti–Tate group of the chain. This makes sense because the p-rank is invariant under isogeny. Scheme structures defined by Hasse invariants would in general depend on which group of the chain is used.

Claims.
- |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i,=_v2}| is dense in |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i}|.
- If K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Kli(v)}, then |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i,=_v1}| is dense in |X_{K,1}^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i,≤_v1}|.

Proof. It suffices to prove the first claim for K_v = Iw(v) and the second for K_v = Kli(v), and then the corresponding statements for the local models. These follow from an explicit calculation. The first is proved by de Jong [dJ93]. The second follows from an analysis of the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification at Iwahori level and its image at Klingen level (C.-F. Yu [Yu11, Thm. 4.2]).

items.name: Theorems 4.2.4 and 4.2.13: Siegel vanishing and the ordinary locus
items.statement:
§4.2.3 setting: K = K^pK_p is a reasonable level with K_p = G_1(Z_p); X = X_{K,Σ} and X^{G_1} = X^{G_1}_{K,Σ}; κ = (k_v,l_v)_{v|p} is a weight.

Theorem 4.2.4. There is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F and not on the tame level K^p, with the following property. If J ⊆ S_p and l_w ≥ C for each w ∈ J, then RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_J2},ω^κ) has a locally finite action of T^J := ∏_{w∈J}T_{w,1}, and e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1},ω^κ) → e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_J2},ω^κ) is a quasi-isomorphism. In particular e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_J2},ω^κ) is a perfect complex. The analogous statements hold for cuspidal cohomology.

Theorem 4.2.13 (the strengthening used later; Remark 4.2.5). There is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F and not on K^p, with the following property. If I_a, J ⊆ S_p are disjoint and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ J, then RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1,≥_J2},ω^κ) has a locally finite action of T^{∅,J} := ∏_{w∈J}T_{w,1}, and e(T^{∅,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1},ω^κ) → e(T^{∅,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1,≥_J2},ω^κ) is a quasi-isomorphism. In particular the target is a perfect complex. Theorem 4.2.4 is the case I_a = ∅.

Proof structure. Both theorems are proved by induction on #J. The base case J = ∅ holds because X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1} is proper. In the inductive step, J = J' ⊔ {w}. The Siegel correspondence at level K' = K^pK'_p, with K'_p = ∏_{v≠w}K_v × Si(w), gives T_{w,1} (for l_w ≥ 2); it is reduced modulo p by Lemma 3.8.10 and restricted to X_1^{G_1,≥_{J'}2}. The step uses three lemmas.
- Lemma 4.2.8: Ha(𝓖_w) is not a zero divisor on X_1^{≥_{J'}2}, and p_2^*Ha(𝓖_w) is not a zero divisor on X_{K',1}^{≥_{J'}2}. (For i = 1, 2 the schemes p_i^{−1}(X_1^{≥_{J'}2,≤_w1}) have the same underlying space but different non-reduced structures.)
- Lemma 4.2.9: for all l_w ≥ p+2, T_{w,1} restricts to a cohomological correspondence T_{w,1}: p_2^*(ω^κ|_{X_1^{≥_{J'}2,≤_w1}}) → p_1^!(ω^κ|_{X_1^{≥_{J'}2,≤_w1}}).
- Lemma 4.2.10: there is a universal constant C, depending only on F and p and not on K^p, such that this restricted correspondence is zero for all l_w ≥ C. The proof shows that Θ(κ) = p^3T_{w,1} factors through p^3𝓘p_1^!ω^κ, where 𝓘 = p_1^*𝓙 and 𝓙 is the ideal of X_1^{≤_w1} in X. At each generic point x of V(𝓘), which has p-rank exactly one at w, the map p_2^*det ω_{𝓖_w} → p_1^*det ω_{𝓖_w} is zero over k(x), because the isogeny p_1^*𝓖_w → p_2^*𝓖_w is not étale at x. So Θ_1(κ): p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^*ω^κ factors through I(x)^{l_w}p_1^*ω^κ, where I(x) is the ideal of the closure of x. The Artin–Rees lemma then gives the factorization through p^3𝓘p_1^*ω^κ once l_w exceeds a constant. One constant suffices because there are finitely many orbits of such x under (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}.
It follows that T^J acts by zero on RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_{J'}2,≤_w1},ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p−1}_{𝓖_w}). Hence e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_{J'}2},ω^κ) = e(T^J)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_{J'}2},ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p−1}_{𝓖_w}), and the theorem follows from RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_J2},ω^κ) = colim_n RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≥_{J'}2},ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{n(p−1)}_{𝓖_w}). The commutation of T_{w,1} with Ha(𝓖_w) (Lemmas 4.2.6–4.2.7) is a separate item.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.12: Klingen vanishing and the strata X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1,≥_{I_b}1,≥_J2}
items.statement:
Setting: K_p = G_1(Z_p), and κ is a weight as in §4.2.

Theorem 4.2.12. Let I_a, I_b, J be pairwise disjoint subsets of S_p. Write X_1^{I_{a,b},J} := X_1^{≤_{I_a}1,≥_{I_b}1,≥_J2} and X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J} := X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1,≥_{I_b}1,≥_J2}, and set T^{I_b,J} = ∏_{w∈I_b}T_w ∏_{w∈J}T_{w,1}. There is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F and not on the tame level K^p, with the following property. Suppose k_w − l_w ≥ C and l_w ≥ 2 for all w ∈ I_b, and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ J. Then RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) carries a locally finite action of T^{I_b,J}, and:
(1) e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) is a perfect complex;
(2) e(T^{I_b,J})H^0(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1},ω^κ) → e(T^{I_b,J})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) is an isomorphism;
(3) e(T^{I_b,J})H^1(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1},ω^κ) → e(T^{I_b,J})H^1(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) is injective;
(4) if furthermore l_w ≥ 3 for all w ∈ I_b, then e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1},ω^κ) → e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) is a quasi-isomorphism.
The same results hold for cuspidal cohomology.

Proof structure. The proof is by induction on #I_b; the case I_b = ∅ is Theorem 4.2.13. In the inductive step, w ∈ I_b, I = I' ⊔ {w}, I'_a = I_a and I'_b = I' ∩ I_b. The Klingen correspondences T'_w and T''_w are those of the item on Lemmas 4.2.14, 4.2.15 and 4.2.19; T_w = T'_w∘T''_w, and T̃_w := T''_w∘T'_w acts on the cohomology over X_{K''}. The step uses the following.
- Corollary 4.2.16. Suppose l_v ≥ 2 and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I' (as printed), and l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ J. If l_w ≥ 2 and k_w ≥ 3, then T^{I_b,J} acts locally finitely on RΓ(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,=_w2},ω^κ).
- Restrictions to the ≤_w1 loci. Exactly as in Lemma 4.2.9, T'_w and T''_w restrict to cohomological correspondences on the ≤_w1 loci for l_w ≥ p+1 and k_w ≥ p+2.
- Lemma 4.2.20. If l_w ≥ p+1 and k_w ≥ 2p+3, then T_w = T'_{w,et}∘T''_{w,et} in End(RΓ(X_{K,1}^{I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ)), and T_wHa'(𝓖_w) = Ha'(𝓖_w)T_w as maps into RΓ(X_{K,1}^{I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p^2−1}_{𝓖_w}). Similarly, if k_w ≥ 2p+3, then T̃_w = T''_{w,et}∘T'_{w,et} in End(RΓ(X_{K'',1}^{I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ)), and T̃_w commutes with Ha'(𝓖_w).
- Corollary 4.2.21 (hypothesis corrected; the paper prints k_v ≥ C). Suppose l_v ≥ 2 and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I'_b, and l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ J. If l_w ≥ p+1 and k_w ≥ 2p+3, then T^{I_b,J} acts locally finitely on RΓ(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ). If k_w ≥ 2p+3, then T^{I'_b,J}T̃_w acts locally finitely on RΓ(X_{K'',1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ).
- Lemma 4.2.22. On the ≤_w1 loci, T'_w commutes with multiplication by Ha'(𝓖_w) (into ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p^2−1}_{𝓖_w}) for l_w ≥ p+1 and k_w ≥ 2p+3; T''_w does for l_w ≥ p+2 and k_w ≥ 2p+3. Since p_1^*Ha'(𝓖_w) is not a zero divisor, T'_w restricts to the supersingular loci (=_w0) for l_w ≥ p^2+p and k_w ≥ p^2+2p+2, and T''_w for l_w ≥ p^2+p+1 and k_w ≥ p^2+2p+2.
- Lemma 4.2.23 ([Pil20, Prop. 7.4.2.2]). There is a universal constant C', depending only on F and p and not on K^p, such that T'_w: p_2^*(ω^κ|_{(X_{K'',1}^{I'_{a,b},J})^{=_w0}}) → p_1^!(ω^κ|_{(X_{K,1}^{I'_{a,b},J})^{=_w0}}) is zero for all k_w − l_w ≥ C' and l_w ≥ p^2+p. C is then enlarged so that C ≥ C'.
- Lemma 4.2.24. Suppose l_v ≥ 2 and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I'_b, l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ J, l_w ≥ p+2 and k_w − l_w ≥ C. Then e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,≤_w1},ω^κ) → e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ) is a quasi-isomorphism; in particular the target is perfect.
- Lemma 4.2.25. Suppose l_v ≥ 2 and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I (as printed), l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ J, and l_w = p+1. Then e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ) is perfect, and e(T^{I_b,J})H^0(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,≤_w1},ω^κ) → e(T^{I_b,J})H^0(X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,=_w1},ω^κ) is an isomorphism.
- Corollary 4.2.26. Suppose l_v ≥ 2 and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I_b, and l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ J. Then T^{I_b,J} acts locally finitely on RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ), and its ordinary part is perfect. Moreover e(T^{I_b,J})H^0(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1},ω^κ) ≅ e(T^{I_b,J})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ), and e(T^{I_b,J})H^1(X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1},ω^κ) ↪ e(T^{I_b,J})H^1(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ). If furthermore l_w ≥ 3, then e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J},ω^κ) → e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) is a quasi-isomorphism. (Its proof establishes the perfectness and the H^0 and H^1 claims only when l_w ≥ 3; for l_w = 2 they are Corollary 4.2.29.)
- Corollary 4.2.29. Suppose k_v − l_v ≥ C and l_v ≥ 2 for all v ∈ I (as printed), and l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ J. Then e(T^{I_b,J})RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I_{a,b},J},ω^κ) is represented by a perfect complex, with the same isomorphism on H^0 and injection on H^1. The proof uses the triangle given by multiplication by Ha(𝓖_w), Corollary 4.2.26 and Lemma 4.2.25.
Theorem 4.2.12 is immediate from Corollaries 4.2.26 and 4.2.29.

Notes on the printed text (each reads identically in the published version):
- Corollary 4.2.21 is stated here with its hypothesis corrected from the printed 'k_v ≥ C' to 'k_v − l_v ≥ C' for v ∈ I'_b. Its proof applies Theorem 4.2.12 for smaller #I_b, which requires k_v − l_v ≥ C at those places. Corollary 4.2.16, Lemma 4.2.24 and Corollary 4.2.26 all assume k_v − l_v ≥ C, and every application of Corollary 4.2.21 (in Lemma 4.2.24 and Corollary 4.2.26) satisfies the corrected hypothesis.
- The hypotheses of Corollary 4.2.16 ('for all v ∈ I′'), Lemma 4.2.25 and Corollary 4.2.29 ('for all v ∈ I', with I = I′ ⊔ {w} ⊇ I_a) are quoted as printed. They constrain places of I_a, which Theorem 4.2.12 does not, but the proofs use them only at places of I′_b, resp. I_b, so the intended reading is I′_b, resp. I_b. As printed the statements remain true, since their hypotheses are only stronger. Nothing depends on the difference. Theorem 4.2.1 applies Theorem 4.2.12 with I_a = ∅, and in the induction I_a only acquires places of the original I_b, which satisfy these hypotheses.
- The display defining the characteristic-zero T''_w (p. 82; published p. 251) prints p_2^!(ω^κ|_{X_{K'}}). The intended target is p_2^!(ω^κ|_{X_{K''}}): §3.9.20 has p_2: X_{K'} → X_{K''} and T''_w: RΓ(X_K) → RΓ(X_{K''}), and the reduction modulo p two lines later has X_{K'',1}.
- The start of the induction (p. 83; published p. 251) says that the case I_b = ∅ was proved 'in Theorem 4.2.4'. It is Theorem 4.2.13; Theorem 4.2.4 is only the case I_a = ∅.
- In the proof of Corollary 4.2.26 (p. 91; published p. 261) the source of the displayed map is printed RΓ(X_1^{G_1}, ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{n(p−1)}_{𝓖_w}|_{V(Ha(𝓖_w)^n)}). By (4.2.27) and the expression displayed just before it, X_1^{G_1,I′_{a,b},J} is meant.
- Corollary 4.2.26 asserts perfectness, the H^0 isomorphism and the H^1 injection for all l_w ≥ 2, but its proof gives them only for l_w ≥ 3 (see the statement). The case l_w = 2 is supplied by Corollary 4.2.29 without circularity, so the results and Theorem 4.2.12 are unaffected.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.33: the Cousin complex K^• computing RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D))
items.statement:
§4.2.30, general construction. Let S be a smooth scheme over a field k and L = ⊗_{i=1}^d L_i an invertible sheaf, with non-vanishing sections s_i ∈ H^0(S,L_i). Let D_i = V(s_i) (effective Cartier divisors), s = ∏_i s_i, and assume D = V(s) = ∪_iD_i is a strict normal crossings divisor. For all n the complex
0 → O_S →^{s^n} L^n → ⊕_iL^n/s_i^n → ⊕_{i<j}L^n/(s_i^n,s_j^n) → ⋯ → L^n/(s_1^n,…,s_d^n) → 0
is exact. It has length d+2. In degree k+1 the term is ⊕_{i_1<⋯<i_k}L^n/(s_{i_1}^n,…,s_{i_k}^n), where L^n/(s_{i_1}^n,…) means L^n/L^n(s_{i_1}^nL_{i_1}^{−n},…). The differential sends (f_{i_1…i_k}) to (Σ_j(−1)^{i_j}f̄_{i_1…î_j…i_{k+1}}). Passing to the colimit over n, with transition maps given by multiplication by powers of s, gives an exact complex 0 → O_S → colim L^n → colim ⊕L^n/s_i^n → ⋯.

Lemma 4.2.31. Let 1 ≤ i_1 < ⋯ < i_k ≤ d, L' = ⊗_jL_{i_j}, s' = ∏_js_{i_j} and D' = V(s(s')^{−1}). There is a canonical isomorphism colim_{×s^n}L^n/(s_{i_1}^n,…,s_{i_k}^n) ≅ colim_{×(s')^n}((L')^n/(s_{i_1}^n,…,s_{i_k}^n))|_{S∖D'}.

Remark 4.2.32. The complex colim L^n → colim ⊕L^n/s_i^n → ⋯ is the Cousin complex of O_S for the stratification given by the divisors D_i.

Application. Take S = X_1^{G_1,I} (with K_p = G_1(Z_p)), L = ⊗_{w∈I}(det 𝓖_w)^{p−1}, L_w = (det 𝓖_w)^{p−1} and s_w = Ha(𝓖_w). That V(s) is a strict normal crossings divisor is an easy consequence of the Serre–Tate theorem and the product structure 𝓖 = ∏𝓖_w. Let K^0 → ⋯ → K^{#I} be the complex obtained by applying H^0 to colim_n L^n → colim_n ⊕L^n/s_w^n → ⋯, tensored with ω^κ(−D). By Lemma 4.2.31,
K^k = ⊕_{J⊂I,#J=k} colim_{×∏_{w∈J}Ha(𝓖_w)} H^0(X_1^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2}, ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝓖_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝓖_w)^n)).

Proposition 4.2.33. The complex K^• computes RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D)). The proof is as for Proposition 3.9.11: each sheaf ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝓖_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝓖_w)^n) on X_1^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2} is acyclic, for three reasons:
- X_1^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2} → X_1^{G_1,I} is affine;
- the sheaf is acyclic relative to the minimal compactification, by [Lan17, Thm. 8.6];
- its support in the minimal compactification is affine. That support is the locally closed subscheme defined by Ha(𝓖_w)^n = 0 and Ha'(𝓖_w) ≠ 0 for w ∈ J, and Ha(𝓖_w) ≠ 0 for w ∈ J^c.
In particular RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D)) is represented by a Hecke-stable complex in degrees [0,#I]; this gives the amplitude in Theorem 4.2.1(1).

Remark 4.2.34 (asserted with details left to the reader; not used). Using K^•, if l_w ≥ 2 and k_w ≥ 2p+3 for w ∈ I, and l_w ≥ 3 for w ∈ I^c, then the individual operators T_w (w ∈ I) and T_{w,1} (w ∈ I^c) act locally finitely on RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D)).

items.name: §§4.3.1–4.3.2 and Proposition 4.3.3: formal completions and the deep Klingen tower 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞)
items.statement:
Standing assumption of §4.3: K = K^pK_p and K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v with K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}.

§4.3.1, completion. For a scheme Z over Spec Z_{(p)}, write Z_n = Z ⊗ Z/p^nZ and 𝔷 := colim_n Z_n, the p-adic formal completion. 𝔛_K is the formal completion of X_K. 𝔛_K^{≥2} ⊂ 𝔛_K^{≥1} ⊂ 𝔛_K are the open formal subschemes whose underlying spaces are X_{K,1}^{≥2} (ordinary at every place above p) and X_{K,1}^{≥1} (p-rank at least 1 at every place above p). 𝔜_K is the complement of the boundary, with special fibre Y_{K,1}; 𝔜_K^{≥2} is the ordinary locus of the interior, and so on.

§4.3.2, deep Klingen level. For m ≥ 1, 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^m) → 𝔛^{≥1}_K is the formal scheme parametrizing subgroups H_m ⊂ 𝓖[p^m] which are locally for the étale topology isomorphic to μ_{p^m} ⊗ O_F. Equivalently, H_m = ∏_{w|p}H_{m,w} with H_{m,w} ⊂ 𝓖_w[p^m] isomorphic to μ_{p^m}.

Proposition 4.3.3 (proved as [Pil20, Lem. 9.1.1.1]). The morphism 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^m) → 𝔛^{≥1}_K is affine and étale. Its fibre 𝔛^{≥2}_{K,Kli}(p^m) over 𝔛^{≥2}_K is finite étale.

The limit. 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞) := lim_m 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^m) is the inverse limit in the category of p-adic formal schemes. It exists because the transition morphisms are affine ([Far08, Prop. D.4.1]; Stacks Project Tag 01YT for schemes). Over it, for every v|p, there is a Barsotti–Tate group H_{∞,v} ↪ 𝓖_v of height one and dimension one.

Pilloni's F = Q tower (his §9) is proposed, not planned, in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. Proposition 4.3.3 is used again in §5 (arXiv pp. 119 and 129).

items.name: §4.4: the weight space Λ_I, the descent character d, and the p-adic forms M_I^{pad,κ_I}
items.statement:
Standing assumptions (§4 and §4.3): p splits completely in F, S_p = I ⊔ I^c is a fixed partition of the places above p, and K = K^pK_p is a reasonable compact open subgroup with K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v, K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}. Let T_I = ∏_{v∈I}O_{F_v}^× × ∏_{v∈I^c}(O_{F_v}^×)^2 ≅ ∏_{v∈I}Z_p^× × ∏_{v∈I^c}(Z_p^×)^2 be the Galois group of the Igusa torsor IG_I → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞) of §4.3.4. Let Λ̃_I = Z_p[[T_I]], and let Ω^{κ̃_I} be the invertible sheaf of O_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ̃_I-modules of §4.3.5.
(§4.4.1) Assume p ≠ 2. Write T_I = T_I^f × T_I^0 with T_I^f finite and T_I^0 the pro-p subgroup, and set Λ_I = Z_p[[T_I^0]]. The canonical projection T_I → T_I^0 gives a canonical character κ_1 : T_I → Λ_I^×. It identifies Λ_I with the deformation space of the trivial character of T_I and makes Λ_I a quotient of Λ̃_I. Let κ_I = κ_1 ⊗ ((2,2)_{v|p}); the pair (κ_I, Λ_I) is the universal deformation space of the character ((2,2)_{v|p}) mod p. Let Ω^{κ_I} = Ω^{κ̃_I} ⊗_{Λ̃_I} Λ_I. Let κ = ((k_v,2)_{v∈I},(k_v,l_v)_{v∈I^c}) be a classical algebraic weight with k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1). Then the character ((x_v)_{v∈I},(x_v,y_v)_{v∈I^c}) ↦ ∏_{v∈I}x_v^{k_v−2}∏_{v∈I^c}x_v^{k_v−2}y_v^{l_v−2} of T_I factors through T_I^0, so it defines a Z_p-point f_κ : Λ_I → Z_p of Spf Λ_I. The specialization of κ_I along f_κ recovers κ.
(§4.4.2) Embed (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} diagonally in T_I by x ↦ ((x_v)_{v∈I},(x_v,x_v)_{v∈I^c}), where x_v ∈ O_{F_v}^× = Z_p^× is the image of x in F_v. For x ∈ T_I let x_0 be its projection to T_I^0. Since T_I^0 is pro-p and p > 2, x ↦ x^2 is bijective on T_I^0; for x ∈ T_I^0 let √x ∈ T_I^0 be the element with (√x)^2 = x. The descent character d : (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} → Λ_I^× is d(x) = √(x_0), viewed as a group element of Λ_I. The group (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} acts on 𝔛^I_K: x sends (A, ι, λ, η = (η_1, η_2), η_p) to (A, ι, xλ, (η_1, xη_2), η_p). This action lifts to Ω^{κ_I}: take x : x^*Ω^{κ_I} → Ω^{κ_I} to be the tautological isomorphism (the construction of Ω^{κ_I} does not depend on the polarization) followed by multiplication by d(x). This is an action, compatible with the construction of §3.7.2 for the choice w = 2. For n ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {∞} the action on 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^n) factors through a finite group acting freely. The quotient is denoted 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^n), and the maps 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^n) → 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^n) are étale. Ω^{κ_I} descends to a sheaf Ω^{κ_I} on 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞) by the descent datum given by d. The cohomology of p-adic cuspidal modular forms of weight κ_I is M_I^{p-ad,κ_I} = RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)). Proposition 4.4.3: the canonical map M_I^{p-ad,κ_I} → RΓ(𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)) is split in the derived category of Z_p-modules (by the proof of Proposition 3.8.3).

The declaration index has no Igusa or Hida declaration and no Iwasawa-algebra or completed-group-algebra declaration; the only declarations named after Iwasawa concern Iwasawa's simplicity criterion for group actions and the Iwasawa decomposition of PSL_2. The stages that touch Siegel varieties are PELModuli:M5 (Siegel moduli) and OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O8 (overconvergent coefficient sheaves on Siegel varieties); OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 treats ordinary forms on the Igusa tower only in the Hilbert setting. The Hilbert analogues of §4.4.2 are HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H3 (the action of totally positive units on polarizations, and the quotient) and OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O4 (descent of the p-adic sheaves along it); the design job should follow their conventions. The coefficient ring Λ_I = Z_p[[T_I^0]] is an instance of the completed group algebra of a profinite group, which two stages plan: Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups, Layer 9 prerequisites ('completedGroupAlgebra p Γ := lim_U ℤ_p[Γ/U]'), and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 (R[[G]]). The design job imports it from there and builds here only the weight space, the characters κ_1, κ_I and f_κ, the descent character d and the descended sheaves. The descent character d is used again in §6.3.8 (p. 148). There are misprints on p. 99, the same in both versions (published p. 271). The displayed lift 'x : x^*Ω^κ_I → Ω^κ_I' means x^*Ω^{κ_I} → Ω^{κ_I}. In d(x) = √(x_0), the right side means the group element of Λ_I attached to √(x_0) ∈ T_I^0: the notation x̃ is introduced for this in the preceding sentence but not used.

items.name: §§4.5.1 and 4.5.6: the Siegel-type operators U_{w,1} (w ∈ I^c) and U_{Kli(w),1} (w ∈ I) on p-adic modular forms
items.statement:
Let K = K^pK_p be reasonable with K_p = G_1(Z_p), fix m ≥ 1, and let 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) be the deep Klingen level formal scheme of §4.3.
(§4.5.1) Let w ∈ I^c and K' = K^pK'_p with K'_p = ∏_{v|p,v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) × Si(w). Let p_1, p_2 : 𝔛_{K'} → 𝔛_K be the p-adic completion (4.5.2) of the Siegel-type Hecke correspondence of §3.9.17. Here p_2 depends on a choice of x_w ∈ F^{×,+}, and the resulting operators do not depend on the polyhedral cone decompositions (as in Remark 3.9.23). Since w ∈ I^c, 𝒢_w is ordinary. Let 𝔠_{w,1}(p^m) be the open and closed formal subscheme of 𝔛_{K'} ×_{p_1,𝔛_K} 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) where the kernel of the canonical isogeny p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 has trivial multiplicative part. Let u_1 : 𝔠_{w,1}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) be the projection. Let u_2 : 𝔠_{w,1}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) be the lift of p_2 given by p_2^*H_m, the image of the multiplicative group p_1^*H_m, which the isogeny maps isomorphically onto it.
Lemma 4.5.4: there is a normalized trace map “p^{−3}Tr_{u_1}” : R(u_1)_*O_{𝔠_{w,1}(p^m)} → O_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m)}. Proof sketch: both formal schemes are smooth over Z_p, and u_1 is totally inseparable. At every closed point x of the interior, Serre–Tate theory shows that the map of completed local rings ⊗_{v|p}W(k(x))[[T_{1,v},T_{2,v},T_{3,v}]] → ⊗_{v|p}W(k(x))[[T_{1,v},T_{2,v},T_{3,v}]] is T_{i,v} ↦ T_{i,v} for v ≠ w and T_{i,w} ↦ (1+T_{i,w})^p − 1. Hence du_1 on top differentials is divisible by p^3. Modulo p^n, p^{−3}du_1 gives O_{C_{w,1}(p^m)_n} → u_1^!O_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p^m)_n}, hence by adjunction (§3.8.11) a trace modulo p^n, and one passes to the limit. Remark 4.5.5 gives a second proof: on the interior u_1 is finite flat of degree p^3, and the map is the usual trace divided by p^3; toroidal compactifications for a common cone decomposition extend this.
The canonical étale isogeny u_1^*𝒢 → u_2^*𝒢 gives isomorphisms u_2^*ω^κ → u_1^*ω^κ and u_2^*Ω^{κ_I} → u_1^*Ω^{κ_I}, with no normalization. Composed with the trace map, they define the Hecke operator U_{w,1} on RΓ(𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}), on RΓ(𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m), ω^κ) and on their cuspidal variants. Remark 4.5.3: U_{w,1} is the standard U_p operator at w of the theory of p-adic modular forms.
(§4.5.6) Now let w ∈ I, and form the Siegel-type correspondence (4.5.2) at w in the same way (with Si(w) at w). Let 𝔠_{Kli(w),1}(p^m) be the open and closed formal subscheme of 𝔛_{K'} ×_{p_1,𝔛_K} 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) where the kernel of p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 meets p_1^*H_m trivially, with projections v_1, v_2 to 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) obtained exactly as above. Lemma 5.3.2 gives a cohomological correspondence (4.5.7) U_{Kli(w),1} : R(v_1)_*v_2^*ω^2 → ω^2, defined with a trace normalized by 1/p^3. Tensoring it with the natural isomorphisms v_2^*Ω_0^{κ̃_I} → v_1^*Ω_0^{κ̃_I} gives U_{Kli(w),1} : R(v_1)_*v_2^*Ω^{κ_I} → Ω^{κ_I}. This operator is first used in §§5 and 7.
