The declaration index has no Hida or Igusa declaration and none about Siegel modular varieties (the only declarations named after Siegel concern Siegel's lemma). No stage description plans Hecke operators at p for GSp_4, or mentions its Klingen or paramodular levels or higher Hida theory. The local computation in the proof of Lemma 4.5.4 rests on two inputs. The first is the Serre–Tate theorem, planned at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4. The second is the Serre–Tate local coordinates at points ordinary at w, which are planned nowhere and form a separate item. The open and closed conditions defining 𝔠_{w,1}(p^m) and 𝔠_{Kli(w),1}(p^m) rest on the rigidity of groups of multiplicative type, also a separate item. The step from divisibility of the differential to the trace is Grothendieck duality modulo p^n (§3.8.11). The F = Q analogues are the normalized traces of Pilloni's §10.3 (Duke 2020). The Klingen-type operator U_{w,2} of §4.5.8, the commutativity Lemma 4.5.15 and the relation Lemma 4.5.17 are separate items.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1(1)–(2): the perfect Hida complex M_I
items.statement: Setting of §4.6: p ≠ 2 splits completely in F, S_p = I ⊔ I^c, and K = K^pK_p is a reasonable compact open subgroup with K_p = G_1(Z_p). Put U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2}. These are the operators of §4.5, and for v ∈ I^c, U_{v,1} is U_{Iw(v),1}. U^I is an endomorphism of M_I^{p-ad,κ_I} = RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)), an object of the bounded derived category of Λ_I-modules. Theorem 4.6.1. (1) The operator U^I is locally finite on M_I^{p-ad,κ_I}. (2) Let e(U^I) be the ordinary projector attached to U^I, and let M_I := e(U^I)M_I^{p-ad,κ_I} be the associated direct summand. Then M_I is a perfect complex of Λ_I-modules concentrated in the interval [0, #I]. Parts (1) and (2) are Lemma 4.6.27. Parts (3) and (4) of the theorem, the specialization to classical weights and the comparison with classical cohomology at spherical level, are stated separately.

The four parts of Theorem 4.6.1 are used separately. Parts (1)–(2) define the complex used in §7.8 (p. 213) and in Proposition 7.8.11 (p. 215). Part (3) is used in §6.6 before Proposition 6.6.1 (p. 164). Part (4) is used in the proof of Proposition 6.6.2 (p. 166). For F = Q and I = {p} the theorem is Pilloni's Theorem 11.3.1 (Duke 2020).

items.name: Lemmas 4.6.3, 4.6.4, 4.6.6 and 4.6.7: the correspondences modulo p and the Hasse invariants
items.statement:
(§4.6.2) Let w ∈ I^c. By Lemma 3.8.10, the special fibre C_{w,1}(p)_1 of the correspondence underlying U_{w,1} over X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1 gives, for each classical algebraic weight κ, a cohomological correspondence U_{w,1} : u_2^*(ω^κ|_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1}) → u_1^!(ω^κ|_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1}). Lemma 4.6.3: for w ∈ I^c, U_{w,1} commutes with the Hasse invariant: U_{w,1}∘u_2^*Ha(𝒢_w) = u_1^*Ha(𝒢_w)∘U_{w,1} as maps u_2^*ω^κ → u_1^!(ω^κ ⊗ det ω_{𝒢_w}^{p−1}). This holds because the kernel of u_1^*𝒢 → u_2^*𝒢 is étale and the formation of Ha commutes with étale isogenies.
For any w|p, take the special fibres of the correspondences of §4.5.8 with m = 1: C_{w,2,1}(p)_1, with r_1 : C_{w,2,1}(p)_1 → X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1 and r_2 : C_{w,2,1}(p)_1 → X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1, and C_{w,2,2}(p)_1, with s_1 : C_{w,2,2}(p)_1 → X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1 and s_2 : C_{w,2,2}(p)_1 → X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1. By Lemma 3.8.10 they give cohomological correspondences r_2^*ω^κ|_{X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1} → r_1^!ω^κ|_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1} and s_1^*ω^κ|_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1} → s_2^!ω^κ|_{X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1}. These define operators U'_w ∈ Hom(RΓ(X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ), RΓ(X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ)) and U''_w ∈ Hom(RΓ(X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ), RΓ(X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ)), and U_{w,2} = U'_w∘U''_w. Lemma 4.6.4 ([Pil20, Lem. 10.5.2.1]): for any w|p, U'_w and U''_w commute with multiplication by Ha(𝒢_w) in the same sense (r_2^*Ha and r_1^*Ha, resp. s_1^*Ha and s_2^*Ha, on the two sides).
(§4.6.5) Lemma 4.6.6 ([Pil20, Lem. 10.5.2.2]): for any w|p, the Hasse invariant Ha(𝒢_w) is not a zero divisor on C_{w,2,1}(p)_1 or on C_{w,2,2}(p)_1. For w ∈ I, let X^{I,=_w1}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, the rank-one locus at w, be the vanishing locus of Ha(𝒢_w) in X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1; for w ∈ I^c it is empty. Taking the zero loci of Ha(𝒢_w) in the correspondences, and using Lemmas 3.8.10 and 4.6.6, gives cohomological correspondences on the rank-one locus and operators U_{w,1}, U'_w, U''_w and U_{w,2} = U'_w∘U''_w there. By Lemmas 4.6.3 and 4.6.4, the long exact sequence H^*(X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ) →^{×Ha(𝒢_w)} H^*(X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ ⊗ det ω_{𝒢_w}^{p−1}) → H^*(X^{I,=_w1}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ ⊗ det ω_{𝒢_w}^{p−1}) is U_{w,2}- and U_{w,1}-equivariant. Lemma 4.6.7 ([Pil20, Lem. 10.5.3.1]): on the rank-one locus at w, U_{w,1}, U'_w and U''_w commute with multiplication by the secondary Hasse invariant Ha'(𝒢_w) : ω^κ → ω^κ ⊗ det ω_{𝒢_w}^{p^2−1}.

No library or atlas stage has the partial Hasse invariants Ha(𝒢_w) or the secondary Hasse invariants Ha'(𝒢_w) of the Barsotti–Tate groups of a Hilbert–Siegel variety, or these correspondences. Hasse invariants occur in the atlas only in other settings: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.3 (modular curves), HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2 and ShimuraCompactifications:C6 (the Hasse ideal of the Hilbert ordinary locus), HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T3 (Hasse neighbourhoods) and IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.2 (Hasse sections of Ekedahl–Oort strata in the setting of Caraiani–Scholze). Lemma 4.6.4 is also invoked in §5.7: Proposition 5.7.4 is 'implicitly contained in Lemma 4.6.4' (p. 130). Misprints, the same in both versions. (a) On p. 106 (published p. 281) and again for the rank-one locus on p. 108 (published p. 282), the cohomological correspondence underlying U''_w is printed s_2^*ω^κ|_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1} → s_1^!ω^κ|_{X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1}. Since s_1 maps to X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1 and s_2 to X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1, it should read s_1^*ω^κ|_{X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1} → s_2^!ω^κ|_{X^I_{K'',Kli}(p)_1}, as in the diagrams of Lemmas 4.6.4 and 4.6.7 and in the trace Tr_{s_2} of Lemma 4.5.13. (b) On p. 108 (published p. 283) the third term of the long exact sequence is printed on X^{I,=_w1}_{K'',Kli}(p)_1 but should be on X^{I,=_w1}_{K,Kli}(p)_1: it is the restriction to the vanishing locus of Ha(𝒢_w) in X^I_{K,Kli}(p)_1. (c) In the first diagram of Lemma 4.6.7 (same page) the lower right entry r_1^!(…) should be u_1^!(…). The statement uses the corrected forms. On p. 107 the text restricts C_{w,1}(p)_1, which §4.5.1 defines only for w ∈ I^c, to the rank-one locus at a place w ∈ I, and cites Lemma 4.6.3, which is stated only for w ∈ I^c; the design job should check this step against [Pil20, §10.5] (it presumably means the Iwahori operator U_{Iw(w),1} of §5.4). The remaining results of §4.6 are stated in their own items.

items.name: §5: the doubling phenomenon and the operator Z_w
items.statement: Overview of the doubling method, with the model case. The doubling results of §5 (Theorems 5.8.4 and 5.8.6) are the key input to local–global compatibility at p in §7.9. The general idea: certain spaces of ordinary low-weight forms admit two degeneracy maps to spaces of ordinary forms of higher weight or higher level; if the direct sum of two copies of the source embeds under the sum of the two maps, one can deduce local properties of the attached Galois representations (Gross; Edixhoven, Prop. 2.7; Wiese; Calegari–Geraghty). In the words of the outline (§1.3): two copies of the space of Klingen-ordinary forms embed through degeneracy maps into a space of Iwahori-ordinary forms, so the Galois representations are ordinary in the Iwahori sense in two ways, with α_w and with β_w as unramified subspaces, and the genericity assumption ᾱ_w ≠ β̄_w then forces a two-dimensional unramified summand; all earlier doubling arguments rested on the q-expansion principle, while this one is geometric and rests on the effect of Z_w = U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1} along the w-non-ordinary locus. Model case (§5.1): let X be the special fibre of the modular curve of level Γ_1(N) with N ≥ 5 and p ∤ N, ω its Hodge line bundle, Ha ∈ H^0(X, ω^{p−1}) the Hasse invariant and SS the finite set of supersingular points. For f ∈ H^0(X, ω), U_p f is a section of ω over X ∖ SS, and there is a commutative square whose top row is Ha·U_p : H^0(X, ω) → H^0(X, ω^p), whose vertical maps are restriction to SS, and whose bottom row H^0(SS, ω) → H^0(SS, ω^p) is an isomorphism (asserted, to be checked as for GSp_4 by describing U_p as a trace on differentials through Kodaira–Spencer). Consequently, if f ∈ H^0(X, ω) is a U_p-eigenform with non-zero eigenvalue then f|_{SS} = 0, so f = Ha·g with g ∈ H^0(X, ω^{2−p}); hence f = 0 if p > 2, and f is a multiple of Ha if p = 2. For GSp_4 the analogous bottom map is probably not injective, which is why the argument of §§5.6–5.8 also composes with U_{w,2}.

items.name: Lemmas 5.3.1 and 5.3.2: the Klingen operator U_{Kli(w),1} on 𝔛^I and its p-integrality
items.statement: Conventions (§5.2): fix I ⊂ S_p and w ∈ I; K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v); X_1^I = X^{≥_{v∈I}1, ≥_{v∈I^c}2}_{K_p(I)K^p,1}; X_1^{I,=_w2} ⊂ X_1^I is the open subspace where A[w^∞] is ordinary and X_1^{I,=_w1} its reduced complement, a divisor; Y_1^I, Y_1^{I,=_w2}, Y_1^{I,=_w1} are the interiors and 𝔛^I, 𝔜^I, … the corresponding formal schemes; ω = det ω_𝒢, ω_w = det ω_{𝒢_w}, and Ha_w = Ha(𝒢_w) ∈ H^0(X_1^I, ω_w^{p−1}). §5.3: with K = K^pK_p, K_p = ∏_v GSp_4(O_{F_v}), and K' = K^pK'_p, K'_p = Si(w) × ∏_{v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}), take the p-adic completion 𝔛_K ←(p_2)− 𝔛_{K'} −(p_1)→ 𝔛_K of the correspondence of §3.9.17. Since 𝔛^I → 𝔛_K is étale (Proposition 4.3.3), the fibre product 𝔛_{K'} ×_{p_1,𝔛_K} 𝔛^I is flat over Z_p, normal and Cohen–Macaulay, with dense ordinary locus in the special fibre. 𝔠_{Kli(w),1} is its open and closed formal subscheme where the kernel of the canonical isogeny p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 meets the multiplicative group p_1^*H_w trivially; v_1 : 𝔠_{Kli(w),1} → 𝔛^I is the projection, and v_2 : 𝔠_{Kli(w),1} → 𝔛^I lifts p_2 by taking H'_{w'} ⊂ p_2^*𝒢_{w'} to be the image of p_1^*H_{w'} for every w' ∈ S_p. Lemma 5.3.1: R(v_1)_*O_{𝔠_{Kli(w),1}} = (v_1)_*O_{𝔠_{Kli(w),1}}, and there is a trace map R(v_1)_*O_{𝔠_{Kli(w),1}} → O_{𝔛^I} (v_1 is finite and flat). For any weight κ = (k_v, l_v)_v (l_w ≥ 0 is not assumed), tensoring the map v_2^*ω^κ → v_1^*ω^κ[1/p] induced by the universal isogeny with this trace gives Θ_κ : (Rv_1)_*v_2^*ω^κ → ω^κ[1/p]; one sets U_{Kli(w),1} = p^{−l_w−1}Θ_κ if l_w ≤ 2 and U_{Kli(w),1} = p^{−3}Θ_κ if l_w ≥ 2. Lemma 5.3.2: U_{Kli(w),1} maps (Rv_1)_*v_2^*ω^κ into ω^κ. (Proof: over the ordinary locus Θ_κ is divisible by p^3 on the étale component and by p^{l_w+1} on the multiplicative-étale component, which makes both normalizations p-integral.)

items.name: Propositions 5.4.2 and 5.4.3 and Corollary 5.4.5: Z_w in non-positive weight
items.statement: Proposition 5.4.2. For any weight κ, as cohomological correspondences over X_1^{I,=_w2}: (1) Z_w Ha_w = Ha_w Z_w; (2) U_{Iw(w),1} Ha_w = Ha_w U_{Iw(w),1}. Proposition 5.4.3. If l_w ≤ 0, the cohomological correspondence U_{Kli(w),1} : (v_1)_*v_2^*ω^κ → ω^κ over X_1^I factors through ω^κ(−X_1^{I,=_w1}). Lemma 5.4.4 (used in the proof). Let BT/F_p be the smooth algebraic stack of quasi-polarized 1-truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of height 2 and dimension 1, E the universal object, Ha(E) : ω_E^{1−p} → O_{BT} the Cartier divisor, supported on the non-ordinary locus, π : BT_Iw → BT the representable finite flat map parametrizing a subgroup H ⊂ E of order p, g : E/H → E the universal morphism with kernel H^D (E and E/H identified with their duals through the polarizations), and dg : ω_E ⊗ ω_{E/H}^{−1} → O_{BT_Iw} its differential. Then (dg)^{⊗2} factors canonically as (ω_E ⊗ ω_{E/H}^{−1})^{⊗2} → π^*ω_E^{1−p} → O_{BT_Iw}, the second map being π^*Ha(E). Corollary 5.4.5. Let κ be a weight with l_w ≤ 0 and f ∈ H^0(X_1^I, ω^κ) with Z_w f = β_w f for some β_w ≠ 0. Then f = 0.

items.name: §5.5: the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism and its compatibilities
items.statement: Setting (§5.5): S is a Z_(p)-scheme, X a smooth S-scheme of relative dimension 3[F:Q], and (A, ι, λ) a tuple with A/X an abelian scheme of dimension 2[F:Q], ι : O_F → End(A) ⊗ Z_(p) making Lie(A) a locally free O_F ⊗_Z O_X-module of rank 2, and λ : A → A^t a prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-polarization with λ[p^∞] : A[p^∞] → A^t[p^∞] an isomorphism. The Hodge filtration 0 → ω_A → H^1_dR(A/X) → ω_{A^t}^∨ → 0 and the Gauss–Manin connection give the Kodaira–Spencer map ω_A → ω_{A^t}^∨ ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S}; composed with λ^* : ω_{A^t} ≅ ω_A it gives ω_A ⊗ ω_A → Ω^1_{X/S}, which factors through Sym^2_{O_X⊗O_F}ω_A (Lan, Prop. 6.2.5.18), and on top exterior powers gives det(ω_A)^3 = ∧^{3[F:Q]}(Sym^2_{O_X⊗O_F}ω_A) → K_{X/S} = ∧^{3[F:Q]}Ω^1_{X/S}. Proposition 5.5.1. If (A, ι, λ) and (A', ι', λ') are two such tuples and φ : A → A' is a prime-to-p quasi-isogeny with φι = ι'φ and φ^tλ'φ = xλ for some x ∈ O_F ⊗ Z_(p), then KS_A ∘ φ^* = N_{F/Q}(x)^3 · KS_{A'} as maps det(ω_{A'})^3 → K_{X/S}. Proposition 5.5.2. Let f : X → Y be a finite flat map of smooth S-schemes of relative dimension 3[F:Q] and (A, ι, λ)/Y a tuple. (i) Base change: the Kodaira–Spencer map of A_X is f^*det(ω_A)^3 ≅ det(ω_{A_X})^3 → K_{X/S}, equal to f^* of the Kodaira–Spencer map of A followed by pullback of differentials f^*K_{Y/S} → K_{X/S}. (ii) Traces: the Kodaira–Spencer map of A composed with f_*det(ω_{A_X})^3 → det(ω_A)^3 (the unnormalized trace f_*O_X → O_Y together with ω_{A_X} ≅ f^*ω_A) equals f_* of the Kodaira–Spencer map of A_X followed by the trace on dualizing sheaves f_*K_{X/S} → K_{Y/S}. Proposition 5.5.3. On 𝔜^I the Kodaira–Spencer map ω^3 → K_{𝔜^I/Z_p} is an isomorphism (from Lan, Thm. 6.4.1.1, and étale base change by Proposition 5.5.2).

Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501 (Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties, Prop. 6.2.5.18 and Thm. 6.4.1.1)

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 plans relative H^1_dR, its Hodge exact sequence and the Gauss–Manin connection, from which the Kodaira–Spencer map is built, and it identifies the tangent map of Serre–Tate deformations with the Hodge filtration. No stage plans the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism for PEL or Hilbert–Siegel moduli, or Propositions 5.5.1–5.5.2. ShimuraCompactifications C4 mentions Kodaira–Spencer only for the Tate curve. The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty, Minimal modularity lifting for nonregular symplectic representations (Duke Math. J. 169, 2020), records the Siegel case, det Ω^1 ≅ ω^3(−∞), as missing. It routes this by source to ShimuraCompactifications and asks C5 to add the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism. These are statements about the Hilbert–Siegel moduli themselves, and they belong with those moduli rather than with higher Coleman theory.

items.name: Definition 5.6.2 and Proposition 5.6.3: the partial Frobenius F_w
items.statement: Definition 5.6.2. Fix x_w ∈ F^{×,+} which is a uniformizer at w and a unit at every other v|p (§3.6.3). The partial Frobenius F_w : Y_1^I → Y_1^I sends a point (A, ι, λ, {H_v}_{v∈S_p}, η) to (Ã, ι̃, λ̃, {H̃_v}_{v∈S_p}, η̃), where L_w = ker(F : A[w^∞] → A[w^∞]^{(p)}) is a maximal isotropic subgroup of A[w], L̃_w = L_w × ∏_{v≠w}A[v] ⊂ A is a subgroup of degree p^{4[F:Q]−2}, π : A → Ã = A/L̃_w, λ̃ is the polarization of A/L̃_w descended from (p^2/x_w)λ, for which L̃_w is isotropic, ι̃ is the induced action of O_F ⊗ Z_(p), H̃_v = πH_v for v ≠ w, H̃_w = H_w^{(p)} ⊂ A[w^∞]^{(p)} ≅ (A/L_w)[w^∞], and η̃ = p^{−1}πη. It depends on the choice of x_w. Since Ã[w^∞] ≅ A[w^∞]^{(p)} and Ã[v^∞] ≅ A[v^∞] for v ≠ w, F_w is Frobenius on the w-factor of the Serre–Tate local product structure, and there are canonical isomorphisms F_w^*ω_w ≅ ω_w^p and F_w^*ω_v ≅ ω_v (v ≠ w). Proposition 5.6.3. F_w is finite flat of degree p^3, and restricts to a finite flat map F_w : Y_1^{I,=_w1} → Y_1^{I,=_w1} of degree p^2. Moreover, if the correspondence 𝔠^I_w over 𝔜^{I,=_w2} (an étale maximal isotropic L_w ⊂ A[w]; this is 𝔠^{=_w2,et}_{Kli(w),1}) is identified with 𝔜^{I,=_w2} through the isomorphism p_2, then p_1 on the special fibre is F_w restricted to Y_1^{I,=_w2}, the universal isogeny p_1^*𝒢_w → p_2^*𝒢_w becomes V : 𝒢_w^{(p)} → 𝒢_w, and the pullback p_2^*ω_w → p_1^*ω_w becomes Ha_w : ω_w → ω_w^p.

items.name: Propositions 5.6.1, 5.6.4, 5.6.5 and 5.6.7: U_{Iw(w),1} as a trace on differentials and its restriction to the rank one locus
items.statement: Let 𝔠^I_w be the correspondence over 𝔜^{I,=_w2} parametrizing an étale maximal isotropic subgroup L_w ⊂ A[w]: p_1 forgets L_w, and p_2 sends A to A/L_w with the polarization descended from x_wλ and the images of H_v and η; p_2 is an isomorphism. U_{Iw(w),1} is the composite p_{1,*}p_2^*ω^κ → p_{1,*}p_1^*ω^κ → ω^κ of pullback along the étale isogeny and p^{−3}Tr_{p_1}. Proposition 5.6.1. On 𝔜^{I,=_w2}, under the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphisms ω^3 ≅ K, U_{Iw(w),1} : p_{1,*}p_2^*ω^3 → ω^3 corresponds to (N_{F/Q}(x_w)^3/p^3)·tr : p_{1,*}p_2^*K_{𝔜^{I,=_w2}/Z_p} → K_{𝔜^{I,=_w2}/Z_p}, where p_2^*K is identified with K_{𝔠^I_w/Z_p}, tr is the trace for p_1 on dualizing sheaves and N_{F/Q}(x_w)^3/p^3 ∈ Z_(p)^×; tensoring with ω^{κ−3} gives the same description in any weight κ. On the special fibre in parallel weight 2 this gives U_{Iw(w),1} : F_{w,*}ω^2 → ω^2 on Y_1^{I,=_w2} as F_{w,*}(K ⊗ ω^{−1}) → F_{w,*}(K ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}) → K ⊗ ω^{−1}, the first map being multiplication by (N_{F/Q}(x_w)^3/p^3)Ha_w^{−1} and the second the twisted trace F_{w,*}(K ⊗ F_w^*𝓛) → K ⊗ 𝓛 for 𝓛 = ω^{−1}. Proposition 5.6.4. The map Ha_w·U_{Iw(w),1} : F_{w,*}ω^2 → ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1} of sheaves on Y_1^{I,=_w2} extends to Y_1^I, where under Kodaira–Spencer it is multiplication by (N_{F/Q}(x_w)^3/p^3)Ha_w^{p−1} : F_{w,*}(K_{Y_1^I} ⊗ ω^{−1}) → F_{w,*}(K_{Y_1^I} ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{(p−1)^2}) followed by the twisted trace to K_{Y_1^I} ⊗ ω_w^{p−1} ⊗ ω^{−1}. Proposition 5.6.5. Using K_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}} ≅ ω^3 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1}|_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}} (Proposition 5.5.3, adjunction, and O(Y_1^{I,=_w1}) ≅ ω_w^{p−1} via Ha_w): multiplication by Ha_w^{p−1} followed by the twisted trace F_{w,*}(K_{Y_1^I} ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{(p−1)^2}) → K_{Y_1^I} ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{p−1}, then restricted to the divisor, equals restriction F_{w,*}(K_{Y_1^I} ⊗ ω^{−1}) → F_{w,*}(K_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}} ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}) followed by the twisted trace for F_w on Y_1^{I,=_w1} and ω^{−1}. Define γ_1 : F_{w,*}(ω^2|_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}}) → ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1}|_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}} (diagram (5.6.6)) as N_{F/Q}(x_w)^3/p^3 times this twisted trace, transported by Kodaira–Spencer. Proposition 5.6.7. Restriction to Y_1^{I,=_w1} carries Ha_w·U_{Iw(w),1} : H^0(Y_1^I, ω^2) → H^0(Y_1^I, ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1}) to γ_1 : H^0(Y_1^{I,=_w1}, ω^2|) → H^0(Y_1^{I,=_w1}, ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1}|).

That is what the top row of Proposition 5.6.5 has, and the proof requires it: 'the maps on the bottom are already defined over Y_1^I'. The statement above uses K_{Y_1^I}. The diagram just before it is said to live on 'Y_1^{I,=_2w}', for Y_1^{I,=_w2}.

items.name: §5.7: U_{w,2} is the square of the partial Frobenius on the rank one locus
items.statement: The correspondence 𝔠^I_{w,2} over 𝔜^I, the composite of 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p) and 𝔠_{w,2,2}(p) of §4.5.8, parametrizes isogenies p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 whose kernel K_w is a totally isotropic subgroup of 𝒢_w[p^2] meeting p_1^*H_w trivially. For a point of 𝔜^I, let L'_w be the canonical multiplicative subgroup of order p of x_w^{−1}H_w/H_w^⊥ ⊂ 𝒢_w/H_w^⊥, let L_w ⊂ A[w^2] be its preimage under A → A/H_w^⊥ (totally isotropic of degree p^4), and let L̃_w = L_w × ∏_{v≠w}A[v^2]. Let 𝔜^I_{w-sph} be the formal completion of Y_{K_pK^p}, K_p = GSp_4(O_{F_w})∏_{v∈I,v≠w}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v), along the locus of the special fibre where A[w^∞] has p-rank ≥ 1, H_v is multiplicative for v ∈ I∖{w} and L_v is multiplicative for v ∈ I^c. Let f : 𝔜^I → 𝔜^I_{w-sph} forget H_w (étale and affine), and let ψ_w : 𝔜^I → 𝔜^I_{w-sph} send 𝒢 to 𝒢/L̃_w with the polarization descended from (p^4/x_w^2)λ, the induced O_F-action and the level structures p^{−2}πη and πH_v (v ≠ w). Lemma 5.7.1: 𝔠^I_{w,2} = 𝔜^I ×_{ψ_w, 𝔜^I_{w-sph}, f} 𝔜^I, with p_2 and p_1 the two projections. Lemma 5.7.2: p_1 : 𝔠^I_{w,2} → 𝔜^I is finite flat of degree p^4. Proposition 5.7.3: the restriction of p_2 to the scheme-theoretic preimage p_2^{−1}(Y_1^{I,=_w1}) is an isomorphism onto Y_1^{I,=_w1}, and under this identification p_1 becomes F_w^2 : Y_1^{I,=_w1} → Y_1^{I,=_w1}. Proposition 5.7.4: the pullback δ_0 : p_2^*ω_w → p_1^*ω_w along the universal isogeny is divisible by p, δ = p^{−1}δ_0 is an isomorphism, and under δ^{p−1} : p_2^*ω_w^{p−1} ≅ p_1^*ω_w^{p−1} one has p_1^*Ha_w = p_2^*Ha_w. Hence δ restricted to Y_1^{I,=_w1} is an isomorphism ω_w → (F_w^2)^*ω_w ≅ ω_w^{p^2}, a nowhere vanishing section of ω_w^{p^2−1}; δ' denotes the pullback isomorphism on ∏_{v≠w}ω_v. For l_w ≥ 0, U_{w,2} : p_{1,*}p_2^*ω^κ → ω^κ is the unnormalized trace p_{1,*}p_2^*O → O tensored with the unnormalized pullback p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^*ω^κ, normalized by p^{−3−l_w}. Proposition 5.7.5: on 𝔜^I, under Kodaira–Spencer, U_{w,2} : p_{1,*}p_2^*ω^3 → ω^3 is (N_{F/Q}(x_w)^6/p^6) times the trace for p_1 on dualizing sheaves; in parallel weight 2 it is (N_{F/Q}(x_w)^6/p^6)·tr ⊗ (δ'δ)^{−1} on p_{1,*}p_2^*(K ⊗ ω^{−1}). Proposition 5.7.6: restricted to Y_1^{I,=_w1} through Proposition 5.7.3 and Ha_w : O(Y_1^{I,=_w1}) ≅ ω_w^{p−1}, this becomes multiplication by δ|^{−p}δ'|^{−1} followed by N_{F/Q}(x_w)^6/p^6 times the twisted trace for F_w^2 on ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}. Define γ_2 : F_{w,*}(ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{p−1}|_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}}) → ω^2|_{Y_1^{I,=_w1}} (diagram (5.7.7)) through Kodaira–Spencer as multiplication by δ|^{−1} followed by N_{F/Q}(x_w)^3/p^3 times the twisted trace for 𝓛 = ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}. Proposition 5.7.8: γ_2∘γ_1 : (F_w^2)_*(ω^2|) → ω^2| is, under Kodaira–Spencer, multiplication by δ|^{−p} (the diagram's label reads δ^{−p}δ'^{−1}) followed by N_{F/Q}(x_w)^6/p^6 times the twisted trace for F_w^2 and ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}; this uses F_w^*δ| = δ|^p. Proposition 5.7.9: restriction to Y_1^{I,=_w1} carries U_{w,2} on H^0(Y_1^I, ω^2) to γ_2∘γ_1 on H^0(Y_1^{I,=_w1}, ω^2|).

Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Two exponent slips, the same in the published version (pp. 310–311); neither affects any result. (1) After Proposition 5.7.4 the text calls the restriction of δ an isomorphism δ|^{−1} : ω_w → (F_w^2)^*ω_w ≅ ω_w^{p^2}, equivalently a section δ|^{−1} of ω_w^{p^2−1}. Since δ : p_2^*ω_w → p_1^*ω_w, and p_2 = id, p_1 = F_w^2 on the divisor, this map is δ| itself. Diagram (5.7.7) multiplies by δ|^{−1} from K ⊗ ω^{−1} to K ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p^2}, which requires δ|^{−1} to be a section of ω_w^{1−p^2}. (2) The proof of Proposition 5.7.6 obtains δ|^{−p}δ'|^{−1} by multiplying (δδ')|^{−1} by 'δ|^{−1−p}'. That product is δ^{−2−p}δ'^{−1}, so the factor must be δ|^{1−p}, which is what relating p_1^*Ha_w and p_2^*Ha_w through δ^{p−1} (Proposition 5.7.4(2)) produces. A degree count confirms this. The bottom arrow goes from K ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p} to K ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ (F_w^2)^*(ω_w^{1−p}) ⊗ ω_w^{1−p^2} = K ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ ω_w^{1−p^3}, so it multiplies by a section of ω_w^{p−p^3} = (ω_w^{p^2−1})^{−p}. That section is δ|^{−p}, not δ|^{−2−p}. The statement above follows the diagrams.

items.name: Lemmas 5.8.1, 5.8.2 and 5.8.3: the doubling map and its equivariance
items.statement: Restriction H^0(X_1^I, ω^2(−D)) → H^0(X_1^{I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D)) is injective and equivariant for the Hecke operators away from w and for U_{w,2} and U_{w,0}. On H^0(X_1^{I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D)) one has U_{Kli(w),1} = U_{Iw(w),1} + Z_w (§5.4, l_w = 2), and Lemma 5.8.1: U_{Iw(w),1}Z_w = U_{w,2} (from Lemma 4.5.17). The doubling map is H^0(X_1^I, ω^2(−D)) ⊕ H^0(X_1^I, ω^2(−D)) → H^0(X_1^{I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D)), (f, g) ↦ f + Z_w g, with f and g restricted. On the source, the operator denoted U_{Iw(w),1} is the matrix [[U_{Kli(w),1}, U_{w,2}], [−1, 0]] acting on column vectors (f, g). Lemma 5.8.2: the doubling map is equivariant for U_{Iw(w),1} (by Lemma 5.8.1), and this matrix operator commutes with U_{w,2} (by Lemma 4.5.15). On the direct factor H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)), where ordinary projectors are defined, Lemma 5.8.3: (1) the doubling map sends e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D))^{⊕2} into e(U_{Iw(w),1}U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D)); (2) the matrix operator U_{Iw(w),1} is left and right invertible on e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D))^{⊕2}, with inverse U_{w,2}^{−1}[[0, −U_{w,2}], [1, U_{Kli(w),1}]]; (3) there U_{Kli(w),1} = U_{Iw(w),1} + U_{w,2}U_{Iw(w),1}^{−1}, so U_{Kli(w),1} and U_{Iw(w),1} commute. Part (3) is printed with U_{Iw(v),1}, for U_{Iw(w),1}.

items.name: Theorems 5.8.4 and 5.8.6: the main doubling results
items.statement: Theorem 5.8.4. Suppose w ∈ I and f ∈ H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)) satisfies U_{Kli(w),1}f = (α_w + β_w)f, U_{Iw(w),1}f = α_w f (on the restriction of f to X_1^{G_1,I,=_w2}) and U_{w,2}f = α_wβ_w f, where α_w, β_w ≠ 0. Then f = 0. Remark 5.8.5: granted the vanishing H^0(X^{G_1,I}_{K_p(I)K^p,1}, ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}(−D)) = 0 for w ∈ I, the same argument shows that U_{w,2}f ≠ 0 implies U_{Iw(w),1}f ∉ H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)). The paper sketches this vanishing in §5.9 (Proposition 5.9.1, item 74) for p > 3 and [F:Q] > 1, even without the cuspidal twist, and in that case Theorem 5.8.4 also holds for non-cuspidal forms; the remark itself says only 'p > 3' (source issue E3). Theorem 5.8.6 (Doubling). The doubling map e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)) ⊕ e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)) → e(U_{Iw(w),1}U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D)) is injective. Remark 5.8.7 (the form used in §7.9): let M ⊂ e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)) ⊗ F̄_p be a finite-dimensional subspace stable under U_{Kli(w),1} and U_{w,2}, and suppose there are distinct α_w, β_w ∈ F̄_p^× with U_{Kli(w),1} − (α_w + β_w) and U_{w,2} − α_wβ_w nilpotent on M. The subalgebra E ⊂ End(M) generated by U_{Kli(w),1} and U_{w,2} is local Artinian, and there are α̃_w, β̃_w ∈ E lifting α_w, β_w modulo m_E with (U_{Iw(w),1} − α̃_w)(U_{Iw(w),1} − β̃_w) = 0 on M ⊕ M. The maps ι_{ξ_w} : M → M ⊕ M, f ↦ (f, −ξ̃_w^{−1}f), for ξ_w ∈ {α_w, β_w}, give an isomorphism ι_{α_w} ⊕ ι_{β_w} : M ⊕ M → M ⊕ M whose composite with the doubling map is (f_1, f_2) ↦ (1 − β̃_wU_{Iw(w),1}^{−1})f_1 + (1 − α̃_wU_{Iw(w),1}^{−1})f_2. Its two components are injections M ↪ e(U_{Iw(w),1}U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D))_{U_{Iw,1}−ξ_w}, into the generalized ξ_w-eigenspace of U_{Iw(w),1}, for ξ_w = α_w and ξ_w = β_w respectively.

items.name: Propositions 5.9.1, 5.9.3 and 5.9.5 and Lemma 5.9.4: vanishing in partial negative weight through Fourier–Jacobi expansions (not used in the paper)
items.statement: Proposition 5.9.1. Assume w ∈ I. If p > 3 and [F:Q] > 1, then H^0(X^I_{K_p(I)K^p,1}, ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}) = 0. This partially strengthens Corollary 5.4.5, is not needed in the paper, and is the vanishing behind Remark 5.8.5. Remark 5.9.2: for p = 3 (the vanishing of H^0(X^I_{K_p(I)K^p,1}, ω^2 ⊗ ω_w^{1−p}(−D))) and for F = Q the authors have only sketches, lacking references for the needed properties of Fourier–Jacobi expansions. Setting of the proof: K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(O_{F_v}), K^p principal (Lan, §1.3.6), c ∈ Z_(p)^{×,+}∖(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p) indexing a connected component X_{K,1,c}, and a boundary stratum Z ↪ X_{K,1,c} attached to a one-dimensional totally isotropic factor, along which the semi-abelian scheme is an extension of an abelian scheme A of dimension [F:Q] with O_F-action by a torus of dimension [F:Q] with O_F-action. H = ker(Res_{F/Q}GL_2 → (Res_{F/Q}G_m)/G_m); Y_{H,1} is its connected Hilbert–Blumenthal variety mod p (moduli of (A, ι, λ, η) with Lie(A) locally free of rank 1 over O_F ⊗ R and λ a prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-polarization with trivial kernel on each A[v^∞]), X_{H,1} a toroidal compactification, A_v the partial Hasse invariants, Y^I_{H,1} ⊂ X^I_{H,1} the open where A_v is invertible for all v ∈ I^c, and Z^I = Z ×_{Y_{H,1}} Y^I_{H,1}. Proposition 5.9.3 (Fourier–Jacobi expansion principle): there is a natural injective map H^0(X^I_{K_p(I)K^p,1,c}, ω^2 ⊗ ω_v^{1−p}) → ∏_{ξ∈a^+} H^0(A^I_1, ω^2 ⊗ ω_v^{1−p} ⊗ 𝓛_ξ), where a is a fractional ideal of O_F with totally positive part a^+, A^I_1 → Y^I_{H,1} is an abelian scheme isogenous to the universal one, and 𝓛_ξ is an invertible sheaf on A^I_1 rigidified along the identity section (pulled back from a Poincaré bundle). The map restricts sections to the completion along Z^I, and injectivity uses the connectedness of X^I_{K_p(I)K^p,1,c}, from the irreducibility of the Igusa tower. Lemma 5.9.4: for an abelian scheme A → S and an invertible sheaf 𝓛 on A rigidified along the unit section, 𝓛^{n^3}|_{A[n]} is trivial for every n ≥ 1. Proposition 5.9.5: assume [F:Q] > 1, let κ = (k_v)_{v∈S_p} be a weight for H and suppose k_w < 0 for some w ∈ I. Then (1) H^0(Y_{H,1}, ω^κ) = 0; (2) H^0(Y^I_{H,1}, ω^κ) = 0; (3) H^0(A^I_1, ω^κ ⊗ 𝓛_ξ) = 0 for every ξ ∈ a^+.

items.note: Status missing confirmed. AutomorphicBundles B5 plans Fourier–Jacobi expansions at higher-dimensional boundary components and an expansion principle. It does not plan this expansion on the partially ordinary locus of the special fibre, whose injectivity rests on the connectedness of X^I_{K_p(I)K^p,1,c}, which comes from the irreducibility of the Igusa tower. No stage plans the vanishing of Hilbert modular forms of partial negative weight; Proposition 5.9.5(1) is a very special case of Diamond–Kassaei. Proposition 5.9.3 is stated with ω_v for an arbitrary v|p and applied with v = w. §5.9 is used nowhere else in the paper, so bundling it is harmless.

items.name: §6: higher Coleman theory for Hilbert–Siegel modular forms
items.statement: §6 constructs higher Coleman theories for GSp_4(A_F), with p split completely in F, for every I ⊆ S_p, the weight space at each v|p being one- or two-dimensional; for F = Q this is Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni and Pilloni, and many arguments are their product over v|p. Its main results are Theorem 6.5.8 (overconvergent cohomology classes of small slope are classical) and Theorem 6.6.4 (for #I ≤ 1 the cohomology of the Hida complex M_I of §4 is overconvergent once p is inverted). Together they improve the classicality results of §4, at the cost of inverting p, by not requiring large weight, which parallel weight 2 needs. Plan: §6.1 formal Banach sheaves of overconvergent locally analytic forms; §6.2 the vanishing theorem (cohomology in degrees [0, #I]) through the minimal compactification, which the authors cannot do purely analytically; §6.3 the analytic construction and the compactness of U^I; §6.4 the analytic BGG resolution; §6.5 small-slope classicality by Kassaei's analytic continuation; §6.6 application to the complexes of §4.6, possible only for #I ≤ 1. The outline in §1.3 summarizes this as a characteristic-zero classicality result for the H^0 of the Hida complexes together with the proof that the complexes are balanced (Euler characteristic zero, used through Theorem 6.6.5 in Proposition 7.8.11), by an interplay between the complexes of classical, overconvergent and Klingen-ordinary forms.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.3: cohomology of a projective formal scheme with an affine analytic model
items.statement: Theorem 6.1.3 (Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni, Thm. A.1.2.2, case (1) of its proof). Let 𝔖 be an admissible formal scheme over Spf O_{C_p} (§6.1.2) admitting a projective map 𝔖 → 𝔖' to an affine admissible formal scheme which induces an isomorphism of the associated analytic adic spaces over Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}). Let 𝔉 be a small formal Banach sheaf on 𝔖 and 𝔘 an affine cover of 𝔖. Then the Čech complex Čech(𝔘, 𝔉) ⊗_{O_{C_p}} C_p is acyclic in positive degrees.

Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501 (Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni, p-adic families of Siegel modular cuspforms, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Thm. A.1.2.2)

The extraction of Pilloni's paper (Duke Math. J. 169, 2020; merged, not yet reviewed) records the same theorem, with formal and small Banach sheaves, as missing. It routes them by source to AdicSpacesPartII (R0, R2, R3), and this item should follow that route rather than go to a new roadmap.

items.name: §§6.1.6–6.1.10: flag formal schemes, torsors and the formal Banach sheaves 𝔊^{κ_A,w} and 𝔉^{κ_A,w} (Lemmas 6.1.11 and 6.1.12)
items.statement: Flag formal schemes (§6.1.6): 𝔉𝔏_n → 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)} parametrizes locally free direct summands Fil ω^mod_𝒢 ⊂ ω^mod_𝒢 of rank one as O_F ⊗ O-modules, and 𝔉𝔏_n = ∏_{v|p}𝔉𝔏_{v,n}. For w = (w_v) ∈ ∏_{v|p}([0, ε_v] ∩ Q), 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} → 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) parametrizes rank-one direct summands Fil ω^mod_{𝒢_v} ⊂ ω^mod_{𝒢_v} with Fil ω^mod_{𝒢_v} = Fil_v^can mod p^{w_v}. For w' = (w'_v) ∈ ∏_v([0, w_v] ∩ Q), 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} parametrizes bases ρ_v : O → ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/Fil ω^mod_{𝒢_v} with ρ_v(1) = HT(e_{v,4}) mod p^{w'_v} for all v|p, and ν_v : O → Fil ω^mod_{𝒢_v} with ν_v(1) = HT(e_{v,3}) mod p^{w'_v} for v ∈ I^c. Groups (§6.1.7): ∏_{v∈I^c}B(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v})∏_{v∈I}Kli(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v}) acts on 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε), with quotient the admissible formal scheme 𝔛_{K(I,p^n)}(ε); 𝔗^0_{w'}(R) = ∏_{v∈I}(1 + p^{w'_v}R)∏_{v∈I^c}(1 + p^{w'_v}R)^2; 𝔗_{w'}(R) = ∏_{v∈I}O_{F_v}^×(1 + p^{w'_v}R)∏_{v∈I^c}(O_{F_v}^×(1 + p^{w'_v}R))^2; and 𝔗_{n,w'} = 𝔗_{w'} ×_{𝔗_{w'}/𝔗^0_{w'}} ∏_{v∈I^c}B(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v})∏_{v∈I}Kli(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v}), via the last two, respectively last, diagonal entries. Torsors (§6.1.8): 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} is a 𝔗^0_{w'}-torsor, and the action extends to 𝔗_{n,w'} compatibly with the finite group acting on 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε). Sheaves (§6.1.9): for a normal admissible O_{C_p}-algebra A and a character κ_A : ∏_{v∈I}O_{F_v}^×∏_{v∈I^c}(O_{F_v}^×)^2 → A^× that is w'-analytic (it extends to a pairing 𝔗_{w'} × Spf A → G_m), 𝔏^{κ_A} = ((π_1)_*O_{𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝔗^0_{w'}} (diagonal action) is an invertible O_{𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w}} ⊗̂ A-module; 𝔊^{κ_A,w} = (π_2)_*𝔏^{κ_A} (π_2 : 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} → 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) is affine) is a formal Banach sheaf on 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε), independent of w'; and 𝔉^{κ_A,w} = ((π_3)_*𝔊^{κ_A,w})^{𝔗_{n,w'}} is a formal Banach sheaf on 𝔛_{K(I,p^n)}(ε). Properties (§6.1.10): for (i_v)_{v∈I} with i_v ∈ {2, 3}, let 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) be the open where Fil_v^can is generated by HT(e_{v,i_v}) for all v ∈ I. Lemma 6.1.11: the restriction of 𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p^{inf_v w_v} to 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) is an inductive limit of coherent sheaves which are extensions of O_{𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε,(i_v))}/p^{inf_v w_v}. Lemma 6.1.12: 𝔊^{κ_A,w}/p is a flat O_{𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε)}/p-module.

items.name: §6.2: the neighbourhoods in the minimal compactification, Lemma 6.2.3, Proposition 6.2.5 and Theorem 6.2.6 (the vanishing theorem)
items.statement: Setting (§6.2, n_v = n for all v): 𝔛^*_K, 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}, 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} with det ω^mod_𝒢, 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)} and the sections s are as in the two items on §6.2.1. For ε = (ε_v) ∈ ∏_v([0, n − 2[F:Q]/(p−1)] ∩ Q), the formal scheme 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε) → 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} is cut out by HT(e_{v,1}) ∧ HT(e_{v,i}) ⊗_{v'≠v} HT(e_{v',j_{v'}}) ∧ HT(e_{v',k_{v'}}) ∈ p^{ε_v} det ω^mod_𝒢/p^{n−2[F:Q]/(p−1)} for all v|p and all 1 ≤ i, j_{v'}, k_{v'} ≤ 4, together with the same conditions with e_{v,2} in place of e_{v,1} for v ∈ I^c; and 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) = 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)} ×_{𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)}} 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε) (proof of Pilloni, Lem. 12.9.1.1). For ε ∈ (Q_{>0})^{S_p} and n ≥ sup_v n(ε_v), 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}(ε) → 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)} is cut out by s_{(i_{v'},j_{v'})_{v'}} ∈ p^{ε_v} det ω^mod_𝒢 for all v|p and all index tuples with i_v = 1, and for all v ∈ I^c and all index tuples with i_v = 2; and 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε) = 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} ×_{𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}} 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}(ε), both vertical maps being projective and isomorphisms on analytic generic fibres. For (i_v)_{v∈I} with i_v ∈ {2, 3}, 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) is the open where s_{(i_v,4)_{v∈I},(3,4)_{v∈I^c}} ≠ 0, and 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) the open where ⊗_{v∈I}HT(e_{v,i_v}) ∧ HT(e_{v,4}) ⊗_{v∈I^c}HT(e_{v,3}) ∧ HT(e_{v,4}) ≠ 0. Lemma 6.2.3: there is a projective map 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) → 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) which is an isomorphism on associated analytic adic spaces, and 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}(ε, (i_v)) is an affine formal scheme (the non-vanishing locus of a section of an ample sheaf). Proposition 6.2.5: for π : 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) → 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}(ε) and D the boundary divisor, R^iπ_*O_{𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε)}(−D) = 0 for all i > 0 (as in Pilloni, Prop. 12.9.2.1). Theorem 6.2.6: let ε = (ε_v) ∈ Q_{>0}^{S_p} and n = (n_v) with inf_v n_v ≥ sup_v n(ε_v). Then, for A, κ_A and w as in §6.1.9, RΓ(𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε), 𝔊^{κ_A,w} ⊗ (det ω^mod_𝒢)^2(−D))[1/p] has cohomology concentrated in degrees [0, #I]. The proof uses a Čech complex indexed by the faces of the hypercube [2,3]^I, together with Lemmas 6.1.11, 6.1.12, 6.2.3, Proposition 6.2.5 and Theorem 6.1.3.

items.name: §§6.3.1–6.3.8: the analytic spaces 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), the Banach sheaves ℱ^{κ_A,w} and the complexes C_cusp (Lemma 6.3.2, Proposition 6.3.6, descent to G_1)
items.statement: 𝒳_{K(p^n)}, 𝒳_K, 𝒳_{K(p^n)}(ε) and 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) are the generic fibres of 𝔛_{K(p^n)}, 𝔛_K, 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) and 𝔛_{K(I,p^n)}(ε). With ω^+_𝒢 ⊂ ω_𝒢 the integral differentials and ω^{mod,+}_𝒢 ⊂ ω^+_𝒢 the étale subsheaf generated by the image of HT, the fibres of 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) → 𝒳_K parametrize: for v ∈ I, a subgroup H_{v,n_v} ⊂ 𝒢_v[p^{n_v}], étale-locally isomorphic to Z/p^{n_v}Z and generated by some e_{v,1} with HT(e_{v,1}) = 0 in ω^{mod,+}_{𝒢_v}/p^{ε_v}; for v ∈ I^c, totally isotropic H_{v,n_v} ⊂ L_{v,n_v} ⊂ 𝒢_v[p^{n_v}], étale-locally isomorphic to Z/p^{n_v}Z and (Z/p^{n_v}Z)^2, with L_{v,n_v} generated by e_{v,1}, e_{v,2} where HT(e_{v,1}) = HT(e_{v,2}) = 0 in ω^{mod,+}_{𝒢_v}/p^{ε_v}. Fil^can_v = Im(HT : H_{v,n_v}^⊥ ⊗ O^+ → ω^{mod,+}_{𝒢_v}/p^{ε_v}) is étale-locally free of rank one over O^+/p^{ε_v}; Gr^can_v = ω^{mod,+}_{𝒢_v}/(p^{ε_v} + Fil^can_v); HT gives isomorphisms H_{v,n_v}^D ⊗ O^+/p^{ε_v} ≅ Gr^can_v for all v|p and (L_{v,n_v}/H_{v,n_v})^D ⊗ O^+/p^{ε_v} ≅ Fil^can_v for v ∈ I^c. 𝓕𝓛_{K(I,p^n),ε,w} → 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) is the space of flags Fil ω_𝒢 ⊂ ω_𝒢 with Fil ω_{𝒢_v} ∩ ω^{mod,+}_{𝒢_v}/p^{w_v} = Fil^can_v/p^{w_v}. 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)^+}(ε) → 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) is the étale cover of trivializations Z/p^{n_v}Z e_{v,4} ≅ H^D_{v,n_v} (all v|p) and Z/p^{n_v}Z e_{v,3} ≅ (L_{v,n_v}/H_{v,n_v})^D (v ∈ I^c). 𝓕𝓛^+_{K(I,p^n),ε,w,w'} parametrizes trivializations ρ_v : O → Gr ω_{𝒢_v} with ρ_v(1) = HT(e_{v,4}) mod p^{w'_v}, and ν_v : O → Fil ω_{𝒢_v} with ν_v(1) = HT(e_{v,3}) mod p^{w'_v} for v ∈ I^c. Lemma 6.3.2: 𝓕𝓛_{n,ε,w} = 𝓕𝓛_{K(I,p^n),ε,w} ×_{𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε)} 𝒳_{K(p^n)}(ε) and 𝓕𝓛^+_{n,ε,w,w'} = 𝓕𝓛^+_{K(I,p^n),ε,w,w'} ×_{𝒳_{K(I,p^n)^+}(ε)} 𝒳_{K(p^n)}(ε). The Banach sheaf ℱ^{κ_A,w} on 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) attached to 𝔉^{κ_A,w} is (π_*O_{𝓕𝓛^+_{K(I,p^n),ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝒯_{w'}}, invariants for the diagonal action (through κ_A on A). C_cusp(n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) := RΓ(𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ (det ω_𝒢)^2(−D)), with transition maps for ε' ≥ ε, n' ≥ n, w' ≥ w, and H^i_cusp(†, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) = colim_{n,ε,w} H^i(C_cusp(n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p})). Proposition 6.3.6: C_cusp(n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) is represented by a bounded complex of projective Banach A[1/p]-modules (a Čech complex; Pilloni, Prop. 12.8.2.1). Descent (§6.3.8): if κ_A is trivial on the torsion subgroup of ∏_{v∈I}O_{F_v}^×∏_{v∈I^c}(O_{F_v}^×)^2 (of order prime to p since p > 2), the action of (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} on 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}, which factors through a finite group, lifts to ℱ^{κ_A,w} through the tautological isomorphism and multiplication by the character d : (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} → Λ_I^× → A^× of §4.4.2. The descended sheaf on 𝒳^{G_1}_{K(I,p^n)} defines C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}), a direct factor of C_cusp(n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}), and H^i_cusp(G_1, †, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) = colim H^i(C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p})).

Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501 (Pilloni, §12.7 and Prop. 12.8.2.1)

items.name: Theorem 6.3.16: local constancy of the Euler characteristic in the weight
items.statement: §6.3.15. Let W_cl be the set of weights κ = ((k_v, l_v))_{v|p} with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p − 1) for all v|p, with the p-adic topology. For κ ∈ W_cl, C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ) is the n,ε-convergent, w-analytic cohomology of weight κ, that is, the complex of §6.3.8 with A = C_p and κ_A = κ ⊗ (−2, −2)_{v|p}, and H^i_cusp(G_1, †, κ) = colim H^i(C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ)); by Lemma 6.3.14 the groups e(U^I)H^i_cusp(G_1, †, κ) are finite-dimensional. Theorem 6.3.16. The map W_cl → Z, κ ↦ Σ_i (−1)^i dim e(U^I)H^i_cusp(G_1, †, κ), is locally constant. The proof follows Coleman [Col97, §A5] as in Pilloni §13.4: a perfect complex interpolates C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ) over the spectral variety, and the dimensions of the slope-zero parts of its terms are locally constant. Remark 6.3.17: if #I = 1, κ ↦ dim e(U^I)H^0_cusp(G_1, †, κ) − dim e(U^I)H^1_cusp(G_1, †, κ) is locally constant; §6.6 uses this to reduce the comparison of ordinary and overconvergent cohomology to high weight, where the control theorems of §4 apply.

Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501 (Coleman, p-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms, Invent. Math. 127 (1997), §A5; Pilloni, §13.4)

items.name: Proposition 6.4.1: slope bounds on overconvergent locally analytic cuspidal cohomology
items.statement:
Proposition 6.4.1. Let κ = ((k_v,l_v))_{v|p} be a dominant algebraic weight with l_v = 2 if v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p − 1) for all v|p (the standing assumption at the start of §6.4). Then:
- on H^i_cusp(G_1,†,κ), for every i, the slopes of the operators (U_{v,1})_{v∈I^c} and (U_{v,2})_{v|p} are ≥ −3;
- on H^0_cusp(G_1,†,κ) these slopes are ≥ 0.
Here H^i_cusp(G_1,†,κ) = colim_{(n,ε,w)} H^i(C_cusp(G_1,n,ε,w,κ)) is the (n,ε)-convergent, w-analytic overconvergent cuspidal cohomology of weight κ of §6.3.15. A slope of an operator is the valuation v(a), normalized by v(p) = 1, of one of its eigenvalues a on the finite slope part.
items.locator: Proposition 6.4.1, §6.4, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 153 (published version p. 337)
items.note:
Proof in the paper: the proof of Pilloni, Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights, Duke Math. J. 169 (2020), Prop. 13.3.1.1, 'goes through essentially without change'. That argument works for an arbitrary locally analytic weight. The proof of Corollary 6.4.3 applies these bounds to the cohomology of 𝓕^{s•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) for s ≠ 1. The weights s•κ there are neither dominant nor in W_cl, so the proposition is needed in the generality of the Pilloni argument, which is wider than the printed hypotheses.
Status missing:
- Mathlib and Tau Ceti: no declaration concerns slopes of Hecke operators on coherent cohomology. The index has no slope decomposition, overconvergent or Siegel-modular-form entries.
- Atlas: no layer plans slope bounds on higher coherent cohomology. PadicFamilies:L2 and LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4 give only the general theory of compact operators.
- PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (its Prop. 13.3.1.1) as missing.
Split: Proposition 6.4.2, the definition of 𝓕^{κ,w^-}, the Hecke equivariance of the BGG differentials and Corollary 6.4.3 are now separate items.

items.name: Theorem 6.5.8: overconvergent cohomology classes of small slope are classical
items.statement:
Theorem 6.5.8. Let κ = (k_v,l_v)_{v|p} be a dominant algebraic weight (a weight for G_1, so k_v ≥ l_v and k_v ≡ l_v mod 2), and let K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v).
- The canonical restriction map RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) → RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) is equivariant for the Hecke operators U_{v,1} and U_{v,2}.
- It induces a quasi-isomorphism
  RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D))[U_{v,2} < k_v+l_v−3 for v ∈ I, U_{v,1} < l_v−3 for v ∈ I^c] → RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D))[U_{v,2} < k_v+l_v−3 for v ∈ I, U_{v,1} < l_v−3 for v ∈ I^c].
Remark 6.5.9 fixes the meaning of the brackets. They denote the part of slope < k_v+l_v−3 for U_{v,2} at v ∈ I and < l_v−3 for U_{v,1} at v ∈ I^c. On the right-hand side the individual operators U_{v,1}, U_{v,2} do not act compactly. Their product ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1} does (Lemma 6.5.4), so the individual operators act compactly on the part of bounded slope for the product, and the small slope part is defined by the slope decompositions of §6.1.1.
Notation: 𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p} is the analytic space over C_p of the toroidal compactification, and 𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p} is the dagger space (6.5.5).
items.locator: Theorem 6.5.8 (§6.5.7) with Remarks 6.5.9 and 6.5.10, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 156, proof p. 164 (published version pp. 341–342 and 351)
items.note:
Remark 6.5.10: for I = ∅ and H^0 the theorem is proved in Bijakowski–Pilloni–Stroh, Classicité de formes modulaires surconvergentes, Ann. of Math. (2) 183 (2016), 975–1014 (the paper's [BPS16]). The earlier text named 'Bijakowski, Classicité de formes modulaires de Hilbert', which is not the reference cited. The remark adds that the bound l_v − 3 at v ∈ I^c might be improved.
Proof: Kassaei's analytic continuation method (Duke Math. J. 132 (2006)), extended to higher cohomology as in Pilloni 2020 §3, with the dynamics of §14 there. In the paper the theorem is Lemma 6.5.28 with S = ∅ and T = S_p. It is used in Proposition 6.6.2, in Theorem 6.6.5 and in the proof of Corollary 8.2.2 (with I = S_p).
Status missing:
- Mathlib and Tau Ceti have nothing on coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties.
- The classicality theorems the atlas plans are for other settings. PadicFamilies:L2 and ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2 treat modular symbols, and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.3 treats definite unitary groups.
- The OverconvergentAutomorphicForms document states that 'general finite-slope classicality, and higher Coleman cohomology are not endpoints of this roadmap'.
- PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (its Theorem 14.7.1) as missing.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.13: degrees under the U_{w,1}-correspondence for w ∈ I^c
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.13, §6.5.11, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 157–158 (published version p. 343)
items.note:
Proof in the paper: (1) and (2) hold because H_v → H'_v and L_v → L'_v are isomorphisms. (3) and (4) are Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), Prop. 2.3.1, 2.3.2 and Lem. 2.3.4, together with their proofs. The lemma is used in Corollary 6.5.14, Lemma 6.5.17 and Proposition 6.5.22.
