items.name: Proposition 6.6.1: for #I = 1, ordinary classes are overconvergent (injective on H^0, surjective on H^1)
items.statement:
Proposition 6.6.1. Suppose that #I = 1. Let κ be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p − 1) for all v|p. Consider the restriction map
  e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p,
where:
- U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2};
- M_I is the perfect Hida complex of Theorem 4.6.1;
- the target is identified by Theorem 4.6.1(3) with e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)), and the map is restriction from the dagger space to the multiplicative locus.
This map is injective on H^0 and surjective on H^1.
items.locator: Proposition 6.6.1, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 164–165 (published version pp. 352–353)
items.note:
For F = Q this is Pilloni 2020, Lem. 14.8.2. The paper presents it as a generalization of the argument of Buzzard–Taylor, Ann. of Math. 149 (1999), Lem. 1 (ordinary forms are overconvergent). Injectivity on H^0 is clear. Surjectivity on H^1 comes from three facts:
- the Čech description of the two complexes and the density of overconvergent sections (a separate item);
- the continuity of U^I;
- a finite-dimensional C_p-Banach space has no proper dense subspace.
The proposition is stated for #I = 1, but Proposition 6.6.2 and Theorem 6.6.4 use it for #I ≤ 1. For I = ∅ both sides are concentrated in degree 0 (Lemma 6.5.6, Theorem 4.6.1(2)) and only the H^0 statement is needed.
Status missing:
- Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.
- OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 compares ordinary Igusa forms with overconvergent Hilbert modular forms. It states that 'Ordinary Hida forms and finite-slope overconvergent forms are not identified as entire spaces' and treats no higher cohomology.
- PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (Lemma 14.8.2(b)) as missing.
Split: Proposition 6.6.2, Theorems 6.6.4 and 6.6.5, the comparison of T- and U-ordinary classical cohomology in the proof of Proposition 6.6.2, and the Katz–Mazur inequality of Remark 6.6.3 are now separate items.

items.name: Definition 7.1.2 and the set-up of §7.1: lifts of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} to GSp_4 with fixed similitude character, and the framed local lifting ring R_v^□
items.statement: Set-up of §7.1. E/Q_p is finite, with ring of integers O, uniformizer λ and residue field k. E is taken large enough that all irreducible components of all deformation rings considered, and all irreducible components of their special fibres, are geometrically irreducible, and that E contains all embeddings of F into an algebraic closure of E. For a complete Noetherian local O-algebra Λ with residue field k, CNL_Λ is the category of complete Noetherian local Λ-algebras with residue field k. F is a totally real field, S_p is the set of places of F above p, p > 2, and ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible. S is a finite set of finite places of F containing S_p and every place at which ρ̄ is ramified. F_S ⊂ F̄ is the maximal extension of F unramified outside S, and G_{F,S} = Gal(F_S/F). For each v ∈ S fix Λ_v ∈ CNL_O, and put Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S} Λ_v (completed tensor product over O), so that CNL_Λ is a subcategory of each CNL_{Λ_v}. Remark 7.1.1: in the applications Λ_v = O for v ∤ p, and Λ_v is an Iwasawa algebra for v | p. Fix a character ψ : G_{F,S} → Λ^× lifting ν∘ρ̄, where ν is the similitude character. Definition 7.1.2. A lift (or lifting) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is a continuous homomorphism ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) to a CNL_{Λ_v}-algebra A such that ρ mod m_A = ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} and ν∘ρ = ψ|_{G_{F_v}}. The set-valued functor 𝓓_v^□ on CNL_{Λ_v} that sends A to the set of lifts of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} to A is representable (Balaji, G-valued potentially semi-stable deformation rings, Ph.D. thesis, University of Chicago, 2012, Theorem 1.2.2). Its representing object is R_v^□.
items.locator: Definition 7.1.2 with Remark 7.1.1 and the set-up of §7.1 (Galois deformation rings), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 169 (published pp. 357–358); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split: Definition 7.1.4, Definition 7.1.5 with the global and T-framed functors, Lemma 7.1.6, and the paragraph on closed points and smooth points of R_v^□[1/p] are separate items. Missing. No layer of the atlas plans GSp_4-valued deformation functors: GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.3 and LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 are written for representations with fixed determinant, and GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 for polarized GL_n-valued problems over a CM field. Neither library has Galois deformation rings. Mathlib has Matrix.symplecticGroup and Tau Ceti has the symplectic group scheme TauCeti.Symplectic.groupScheme, but neither has the similitude group GSp_4.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.3: pure points of the unrestricted local deformation ring away from p are smooth
items.statement: Lemma 7.1.3. For v ∤ p a closed point x of the generic fibre of R_v^□ is smooth if and only if (ad^0ρ_x)(1)^{G_{F_v}} = 0; in particular if ρ_x is pure then x is smooth, since purity forces Hom(ρ_x, ρ_x(1)) = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 7.1.3 (§7.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 170 (published p. 358); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501. The first claim is a special case of Bellovin–Gee, G-valued local deformation rings and global lifts, Algebra Number Theory 13 (2019), Corollary 3.3.4 and Remark 3.3.6.
items.note: The terms 'closed point' and 'smooth' ((R_v^□[1/p])^∧_x regular), and ad^0ρ_x = 𝔤^0(E') = Lie Sp_4(E'), are defined in the new item on closed points of R_v^□[1/p]. For v ∤ p, purity is purity of the Weil–Deligne representation (§2.5). Purity rules out a nonzero map between the Weil–Deligne representations of ρ_x and ρ_x(1). The lemma's criterion is reused in the proof of Lemma 7.4.6 (arXiv p. 189), and the lemma is cited in §7.13 (arXiv pp. 233, 235). Missing: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1–R08.2 plan framed rings away from p for representations with fixed determinant, not GSp_4-valued rings or the Bellovin–Gee criterion. No layer description mentions Bellovin–Gee or G-valued deformation rings.

items.name: Proposition 7.2.1: the global presentation over the local deformation rings
items.statement: Let 𝓢 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, ψ, {𝓓_v}_{v∈S}) be a global deformation problem (Definition 7.1.5), and let R_v be the ring representing 𝓓_v. Let T ⊆ S contain S_p, with Λ_v = O and 𝓓_v = 𝓓_v^□ for all v ∈ S ∖ T. Put R_𝓢^{T,loc} = ⊗̂_{v∈T} R_v (over O), a Λ-algebra via ⊗̂_{v∈T}Λ_v ≅ ⊗̂_{v∈S}Λ_v. The maps 𝓓_𝓢^T → 𝓓_v, (ρ, {γ_v}_{v∈T}) ↦ γ_v^{-1}ρ|_{G_{F_v}}γ_v, give a local Λ-algebra map R_𝓢^{T,loc} → R_𝓢^T. Let adρ̄ = 𝔤(k) and ad^0ρ̄ = 𝔤^0(k) (the Lie algebras of GSp_4 and Sp_4), with the adjoint action through ρ̄. The trace pairing identifies ad^0ρ̄(1) with the Tate dual of ad^0ρ̄. Define H^1_{𝓢,T}(ad^0ρ̄) = ker(H^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄) → ∏_{v∈T} H^1(F_v, ad^0ρ̄)) and H^1_{𝓢^⊥,T}(ad^0ρ̄(1)) = ker(H^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈S∖T} H^1(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1))). Proposition 7.2.1. There is a local Λ-algebra surjection R_𝓢^{T,loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_𝓢^T with g = h^1_{𝓢^⊥,T}(ad^0ρ̄(1)) − h^0(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)) − Σ_{v|∞} h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) + Σ_{v∈S∖T} h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1)) + #T − 1.
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.1 with the definitions of R_𝓢^{T,loc}, H^1_{𝓢,T} and H^1_{𝓢^⊥,T} (§7.2, Galois cohomology and presentations), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 171–172 (published pp. 359–360); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Proof. The GSp_4 form of Kisin's Lemma 3.2.2 (Moduli of finite flat group schemes, and modularity) gives the surjection with g = h^1_{𝓢,T}(ad^0ρ̄) − h^0(F_S/F, adρ̄) + Σ_{v∈T} h^0(F_v, adρ̄). The Greenberg–Wiles formula (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Theorem 2.19), with h^0(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄) = 0, gives h^1_{𝓢,T}(ad^0ρ̄) = h^1_{𝓢^⊥,T}(ad^0ρ̄(1)) − h^0(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)) − Σ_{v|∞} h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) + Σ_{v∈S∖T} h^1(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) − Σ_{v∈S} h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄). Since p > 2, adρ̄ = ad^0ρ̄ ⊕ k, so h^0(F_S/F, adρ̄) = 1 and h^0(F_v, adρ̄) = h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) + 1. For v ∈ S ∖ T, all of which are prime to p, the local Euler characteristic formula and Tate duality give h^1(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) − h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) = h^2(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) = h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1)). Substituting gives the stated g. Used in Corollary 7.6.3 and §7.11. Missing in the GSp_4 form; the presentation for GL-valued problems is planned (item 151).

items.name: Definition 7.3.1: p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary representations
items.statement: Standing assumption of §7.3: p splits completely in F, so F_v = Q_p for v | p. For x ∈ k^×, λ_x : G_{F_v} → k^× is the unramified character with λ_x(Frob_v) = x. Definition 7.3.1. Let v | p. ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary if it is conjugate to a representation of the form [[λ_{ᾱ_v}, 0, *, *], [0, λ_{β̄_v}, *, *], [0, 0, ε̄^{-1}λ_{β̄_v}^{-1}, 0], [0, 0, 0, ε̄^{-1}λ_{ᾱ_v}^{-1}]] (rows listed) with ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v. If so, a lift ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(O) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary if ρ is conjugate to [[λ_{α_v}, 0, *, *], [0, λ_{β_v}, *, *], [0, 0, ε^{-1}λ_{β_v}^{-1}, 0], [0, 0, 0, ε^{-1}λ_{α_v}^{-1}]], with α_v, β_v lifting ᾱ_v, β̄_v; such a ρ is automatically semistable, though not necessarily crystalline. Remark 7.3.2 discusses the terminology. Remark 7.3.3: for potential modularity it would suffice to work with a stronger p-distinguishedness hypothesis, as in Calegari–Geraghty 2020. Assuming that none of ᾱ_v², β̄_v², ᾱ_vβ̄_v equals 1 would make the deformation rings of §7.3 formally smooth, but that hypothesis is very restrictive for p = 3. From here on, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is assumed p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for all v | p, with a fixed labelling ᾱ_v, β̄_v (the roles are symmetric).
items.locator: Definition 7.3.1 with Remarks 7.3.2 and 7.3.3 and the standing assumptions of §7.3, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 172 (published p. 361); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Used in Hypothesis 7.7.1, Theorem 8.4.1, and in §8.5 (Definition 8.5.1 and Theorem 8.5.2). Missing: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.4 and OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.2 mention p-distinguishedness only for GL_2 (Emerton's local–global compatibility; nearly ordinary Hida families). No layer defines the GSp_4 condition.

items.name: Proposition 7.3.4: the generic fibres of the ordinary local deformation rings R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} and R_v^P are irreducible of relative dimensions 16 and 14
items.statement: Keep the assumptions of §7.3: p splits completely in F, and for every v | p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary with a fixed labelling ᾱ_v, β̄_v. Let 𝔠̄_v ∈ {ᾱ_v, β̄_v}. Let R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} (over Λ_v = Λ_{v,2}) and R_v^P (over Λ_v = Λ_{v,1}) represent the (B, 𝔠̄_v)-ordinary and P-ordinary local deformation problems. Proposition 7.3.4. The generic fibres R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v}[1/p] and R_v^P[1/p] are irreducible, and are of relative dimensions 16 and 14 respectively over Q_p.
items.locator: Proposition 7.3.4 (§7.3), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 173 (published p. 363), proved on arXiv pp. 185–188 (published pp. 377–380) with Remark 7.3.17; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note:
Split: the ordinary deformation problems (arXiv pp. 172–173), Definition 7.3.11 with Lemma 7.3.12, Lemma 7.3.15 and Proposition 7.3.16 are separate items.

Proof. Proposition 7.3.16 gives the P-part. For R^B = R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} there is a presentation O[[x_1, …, x_r]]/(y_1, …, y_s) with r − s = 16, so R^B is formally smooth when H^2(Q_p, ad^0_B(ρ̄)) = 0. The cases of Lemma 7.3.14 are treated separately:
- in case (2b), the problem reduces to Lemma 7.3.6;
- cases (1) and (3) give complete intersections;
- in case (2a), an argument using Lemma 7.3.7(4b) shows that R^B is a complete intersection.
Connectedness of the generic fibre reduces to the P case. Normality follows because the locus where H^2(G_{Q_p}, ad^0_B ρ_x) ≠ 0 has dimension at most 14.

Misprint in case (2a) (arXiv p. 187; published p. 379). The paper says that 'the complement of U has dimension at most 12', and later that 'T ⊂ U. But we have already seen that U has dimension at most 12'. By the paper's own count just before, the complement of U has dimension at most 13 in case (2a), and T lies in the complement of U. The contradiction with dim T = 17 stands. Remark 7.3.17: in case (2a) the argument does not show that R^B is flat over O, or that R^B/λ is a complete intersection.

Used in §7.11 (arXiv p. 226) and §7.12 (arXiv p. 227).

Missing: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans GL_n ordinary deformation functors with a full invariant flag (after Allen et al. §6.2). It does not plan GSp_4 rings with fixed similitude or the P-ordinary condition.

items.name: Lemma 7.3.6: the ordinary GL_2 deformation ring R^{B_2} has irreducible generic fibre of relative dimension 5
items.statement: Set-up of §7.3.5. Let r̄ : G_{Q_p} → GL_2(k) be of the form [[λ_ᾱ, *], [0, ε̄^{-1}λ_ᾱ^{-1}]]. Let Λ = O[[1 + pZ_p]], and let θ : I_{Q_p} → Λ^× be the canonical character (through Art_{Q_p}^{-1}). For A ∈ CNL_Λ, a lift r : G_{Q_p} → GL_2(A) of r̄ is ordinary if it is ker(GL_2(A) → GL_2(k))-conjugate to [[χ, *], [0, ε^{-1}χ^{-1}]] with χ̄ = λ_ᾱ and χ|_{I_{Q_p}} = θ. This is a local deformation problem, represented by a CNL_Λ-algebra R^{B_2} = R^{B_2,□}, where B_2 is the upper triangular Borel subgroup of GL_2. Write r̄ = [[λ_ᾱ, ε̄^{-1}λ_ᾱ^{-1}η_{α²}], [0, ε̄^{-1}λ_ᾱ^{-1}]] with η_{α²} ∈ H^1(Q_p, ε̄λ_{ᾱ²}), and let ad^0_{B_2} r̄ be the trace-zero part of Lie B_2 with the adjoint action. Then h^2(Q_p, ad^0_{B_2} r̄) = 0 unless ᾱ² = 1 and η_{α²} = 0, in which case it equals 1. Lemma 7.3.6. The generic fibre R^{B_2}[1/p] is irreducible, and has relative dimension 5 over Q_p.
items.locator: Lemma 7.3.6 with the set-up of §7.3.5 (Ordinary deformation rings for GL_2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 174–176 (published pp. 363–366); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split: Lemmas 7.3.7, 7.3.9 and 7.3.14 are separate items. Proof: Mazur's argument gives a presentation O[[x_1, …, x_r]]/(y_1, …, y_s) with r − s = 5. If H^2 ≠ 0 then s = 1, and the ring is a complete intersection. Connectedness of the generic fibre follows Geraghty's Lemma 3.13. Normality comes from the open regular locus where H^2(G_{Q_p}, ad^0_{B_2} r_x) = 0; its complement (sums of two characters whose ratio is the cyclotomic character) has relative dimension at most 2. Missing: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans GL_n ordinary deformation functors, with dimensions and components only under its source's genericity or distinguishedness hypotheses. The fixed-determinant case that includes r̄ = 1 ⊕ ε̄^{-1} (up to an unramified quadratic twist) is not planned.

items.name: Lemma 7.3.18: pure points of the ordinary local deformation rings are smooth
items.statement: Keep the set-up of §7.3 (F_v = Q_p). A closed point x of R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v}[1/p] (resp. R_v^P[1/p]) is smooth if the local ring (R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v}[1/p])_x (resp. (R_v^P[1/p])_x) is regular. The corresponding ρ_x is pure if it is de Rham and WD(ρ_x) is pure, that is, WD(ρ_x) arises by base extension from a pure Weil–Deligne representation over a number field. Lemma 7.3.18. If x is a closed point of the generic fibre of R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v}[1/p] or of R_v^P[1/p], and x is pure, then x is smooth.
items.locator: Lemma 7.3.18 with the definitions preceding it (§7.3), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 188 (published p. 380); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note:
Misprint: in the P case of the definition, the paper prints (R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v}[1/p])_x; (R_v^P[1/p])_x is meant (the same in the published version).

Proof. For B, the proof of Proposition 7.3.4 shows that it suffices that H^2(G_{Q_p}, ad^0_B ρ_x) = 0. By Tate local duality it is then enough that Hom_{G_{Q_p}}(ρ_x, ρ_x(1)) = 0, and hence enough that there is no nonzero map WD(ρ_x) → WD(ρ_x(1)), which purity gives. The same argument covers R_v^{P,univ}[1/p]. By Lemma 7.3.15 and Proposition 7.3.16, the remaining non-smooth points of R_v^P[1/p] have a two-dimensional reducible subquotient that is non-smooth over Λ_v on R^{B_2}[1/p]. By Lemma 7.3.9 such a subquotient is an unramified twist of a crystalline extension of ε^{-1} by 1, which is not pure.

Used in §7.13 (arXiv p. 233). Missing, for the same reasons as Proposition 7.3.4.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.2: unrestricted deformation rings at v ∤ p with vanishing H^0(ad^0(1))
items.statement: Let v ∤ p (§7.4.1). Proposition 7.4.2. If H^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0, then R_v^□ is isomorphic to a power series ring over O in 10 variables. If furthermore ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified, then so are all of its lifts.
items.locator: Proposition 7.4.2 (§7.4.1, Unobstructed deformations), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 189 (published p. 381); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Proof: by Tate duality the hypothesis is H^2(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) = 0, and the rest is standard obstruction theory (Tilouine 1996, §5.2). Used in §7.7 to choose the auxiliary place v_0 at which all lifts are unramified (arXiv p. 210), and in §7.11. Missing in the GSp_4 form. The tangent–obstruction description for GL-valued problems is planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 (item 153).

items.name: Lemma 7.4.4: at a Taylor–Wiles place every lift is conjugate to a sum of four characters
items.statement: Set-up of §7.4.3. Let v be a place with q_v ≡ 1 mod p (so v ∤ p), with ψ|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} unramified and Λ_v = O. Assume that ρ̄(Frob_v) has 4 distinct eigenvalues in k, ordered as ᾱ_1, ᾱ_2, ᾱ_3 = ψ(Frob_v)/ᾱ_2, ᾱ_4 = ψ(Frob_v)/ᾱ_1. For i = 1, 2, let γ̄_i : G_{F_v} → k^× be the unramified character sending Frob_v to ᾱ_i. Lemma 7.4.4. Let ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) be any lift of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}. There are unique continuous characters γ_i : G_{F_v} → A^×, for i = 1, 2, such that ρ is GSp_4(A)-conjugate to a lift of the form γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ψγ_2^{-1} ⊕ ψγ_1^{-1}, where γ_i mod m_A = γ̄_i for i = 1, 2.
items.locator: Lemma 7.4.4 with the set-up of §7.4.3 (Taylor–Wiles deformations), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 189 (published p. 381); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501. Proved in exactly the same way as Genestier–Tilouine, Systèmes de Taylor–Wiles pour GSp(4), Lemma 5.1.1.
items.note: The O[Δ_v]-algebra structure on R_v^□ built from this lemma is a separate item. Used in §7.9 (arXiv p. 220). Missing: GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 and G7 plan Taylor–Wiles primes for GL-valued problems and for polarized GL_n over CM fields; no layer plans the GSp_4 local statement.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.6 and Proposition 7.4.8 with the set-up of §7.4.5: the Ihara avoidance deformation problems 𝓓_v^χ for GSp_4, and irreducibility of R_v^χ when χ_1, χ_2 ≠ 1 and χ_1 ≠ χ_2^{±1}
items.statement: Set-up of §7.4.5. Let v be a finite place of F with q_v ≡ 1 mod p, with ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial, ψ|_{G_{F_v}} unramified with trivial reduction modulo λ, and Λ_v = O. Let χ = (χ_1, χ_2) be a pair of continuous characters χ_i : O_{F_v}^× → O^× that are trivial modulo λ. Then 𝓓_v^χ is the functor of lifts ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} (so ν∘ρ = ψ|_{G_{F_v}}) such that, for all σ ∈ I_{F_v}, the characteristic polynomial of ρ(σ) is (X − χ_1(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ)))(X − χ_2(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ)))(X − χ_2(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{-1})(X − χ_1(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{-1}). It is a local deformation problem, represented by R_v^χ. Lemma 7.4.6. If χ_1, χ_2 ≠ 1 and χ_1 ≠ χ_2^{±1}, then every closed point of Spec R_v^χ[1/p] is smooth. Proposition 7.4.8. If χ_1, χ_2 ≠ 1 and χ_1 ≠ χ_2^{±1}, then Spec R_v^χ is irreducible of dimension 11, and its generic point has characteristic zero.
items.locator: Lemma 7.4.6 and Proposition 7.4.8 with the set-up of §7.4.5 (Ihara avoidance deformations), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 189–190 (published pp. 381–382); the proof of Proposition 7.4.8 is on arXiv pp. 197–198 (published p. 392); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501; after Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations II, §3 (Proposition 3.1)

items.name: §7.4.9 and Proposition 7.4.10: truncated exponential and logarithm, and the nilpotent strata 𝓝_i of Lie GSp_4 with their centralizers
items.statement: Throughout §§7.4.9–7.4.21, q is an integer not divisible by p, and p ≥ 3. Let 𝓤 ⊂ GSp_4/O be the closed subscheme of matrices with characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^4, and 𝓝 ⊂ Lie(GSp_4) the closed subscheme of matrices with characteristic polynomial X^4. The maps exp_2 : 𝓝 → 𝓤, N ↦ I + N + N²/2 + N³/2, and log_2 : 𝓤 → 𝓝, U ↦ (U − I) − (U − I)²/2, have images in 𝓤 and 𝓝 and are mutually inverse bijections. They commute with conjugation by GSp_4, and satisfy exp_2(mN + m*N³) = exp_2(N)^m and log_2(U^m) = m log_2(U) + m* log_2(U)³ for m ∈ Z, where m* = (m − m³)/3 ∈ Z. Put N_0 = 0, N_1 = E_{14}, N_2 = E_{13} + E_{24} and N_3 = E_{12} + E_{23} − E_{34} in 𝓝(O) (E_{ij} the matrix units). Let 𝓝_i ⊂ 𝓝 be the reduced locally closed subscheme of nilpotent matrices of rank i, so that N_i ∈ 𝓝_i. Proposition 7.4.10. (1) Z_{GSp_4}(N_i) is a smooth group scheme over Spec O with fibres of dimensions 11, 7, 5, 3 for i = 0, 1, 2, 3. Each connected component of Z_{GSp_4}(N_i) is irreducible with irreducible special fibre, and Z_{GSp_4}(N_i) is irreducible except when i = 2, in which case it has two components. (2) Locally in the étale topology, the universal nilpotent matrix over 𝓝_i is conjugate to N_i by a section of GSp_4. (3) 𝓝_i is smooth over Spec O with irreducible fibres of dimensions 0, 4, 6, 8 for i = 0, 1, 2, 3; in particular 𝓝_i is irreducible. Remark 7.4.11: unlike for GL_n, Z_{GSp_4}(N_i) need not be connected, and the universal matrix over 𝓝_i need not be Zariski-locally conjugate to N_i (both fail for i = 2).
items.locator: §7.4.9 (Preliminaries on nilpotent matrices) with Proposition 7.4.10 and Remark 7.4.11, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 190–192 (published pp. 382–385); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split: §§7.4.12–7.4.16 (spaces of polynomials and matrices), 𝓜(x, y; q) with Propositions 7.4.17–7.4.18, and §7.4.19 with Propositions 7.4.20–7.4.21 are separate items. The degree-two truncations replace Taylor's truncated exponential, which needs p ≥ n, so that p = 3 is allowed. For i = 2 the proof computes Z_{GSp_4}(N_2) ≅ O[x, y, z, w, α, β, γ, δ, (wx − yz)^{-1}]/(xy, wz, yγ − wα − xδ − zβ), whose components are x = w = 0 and y = z = 0. Missing: no layer description mentions nilpotent elements of Lie Sp_4 or Lie GSp_4, or their centralizers.

items.name: Definition 7.5.2: enormous and weakly enormous subgroups of GSp_4(k)
items.statement:
Definition 7.5.2. A subgroup H ⊂ GSp_4(k) is enormous if:
(E1) H^1(H, ad^0) = 0 for the 10-dimensional representation ad^0 (Lie Sp_4 with the adjoint action);
(E2) H acts absolutely irreducibly in its natural representation, so in particular H^0(H, ad^0) = 0;
(E3) for every simple k̄[H]-submodule W ⊂ k̄ ⊗ ad^0 there is h ∈ H that has 4 distinct eigenvalues (as an element of GSp_4(k)) and has 1 as an eigenvalue on W.
H is weakly enormous if it satisfies (E2) and (E3).
Lemma 7.5.3. If H, H' ⊂ GSp_4(k) have the same image in PGSp_4(k), then H is enormous (resp. weakly enormous) if and only if H' is. A group containing a weakly enormous subgroup is weakly enormous; this fails for enormous.
Lemma 7.5.14. If p ≥ 11 and H ⊂ GSp_4(k) is absolutely irreducible, then (E1) and (E2) hold.
Remark 7.5.4: no condition that H has no quotient of p-power order is imposed. That condition would exclude, for example, surjective ρ̄ : G_Q → GL_2(F_3) with cyclotomic determinant, and some subgroups that occur for p = 3.
items.locator: Definition 7.5.2 with Lemmas 7.5.3 and 7.5.14 and Remark 7.5.4 (§7.5.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 198, 201 (published pp. 392–393, 396); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501. Lemma 7.5.14 is Thorne, On the automorphy of l-adic Galois representations with small residual image, Theorem A.9.
items.note: Missing: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 plans the GL_n condition of Allen et al., Definition 6.2.29. That condition also requires no quotient of p-power order and uses regular semisimple elements of GL_n(k). No layer plans the GSp_4 conditions, weak enormousness, or Thorne's Theorem A.9.

items.name: Definitions 7.5.6 and 7.5.11: vast and tidy representations
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.5. Let p ≥ 3 and let ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) be continuous. There is an integer δ depending only on F such that the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} is independent of N for N ≥ 1 + δ if p ≥ 5, or for N ≥ 2 + δ if p = 3. If p is unramified in F one may take δ = 1. (δ is chosen so that, for all N, the image of Gal(F(ζ_{p^N})/F) in (Z/p^N Z)^× contains 1 + p^δ.) Definition 7.5.6. ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is vast if either (1) the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} is enormous for all sufficiently large N, or (2) the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} is weakly enormous for all sufficiently large N and the fixed field L of ad^0ρ̄ does not contain ζ_p. Remark 7.5.7: if p is unramified in F, 'sufficiently large N' may be replaced by N = 3. Remark 7.5.8: ρ̄ is vast if and only if any twist of ρ̄ by a character is vast. Definition 7.5.11. A subgroup H ⊂ GSp_4(k) is tidy if there is h ∈ H with ν(h) ≠ 1 such that no two eigenvalues of h have ratio ν(h) (the eigenvalues need not be distinct). A representation ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is tidy if its image is tidy. A group containing a tidy subgroup is tidy.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.5, Definitions 7.5.6 and 7.5.11 and Remarks 7.5.7 and 7.5.8 (§7.5), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 199, 201 (published pp. 393–395); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Vast and tidy are consumed together in Hypothesis 7.7.1(1): vastness gives Taylor–Wiles primes, and tidiness gives an auxiliary place v_0 at which all lifts are unramified and the level is neat. The bundle is therefore kept. Lemma 7.5.5 is also cited in Remark 7.5.23. Missing: the words 'vast' and 'tidy' occur in no layer description. The extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Modularity theorems for abelian surfaces, also records tidiness as missing.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.9: vanishing of Galois cohomology under the big image hypotheses
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.9. Let p ≥ 3, let ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) be a continuous representation, and let N ≥ 1. Suppose either (1) the fixed field L of ad^0ρ̄ does not contain ζ_p, or (2) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} has enormous image. Then H^1(Gal(L(ζ_{p^N})/F), ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0. In particular, if ρ̄ is vast, this holds for all sufficiently large N.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.9 with Remark 7.5.10 (§7.5), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 200 (published pp. 394–395); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501. Remark 7.5.10 says the first case is proved exactly as Lemma 5.3 of the paper's reference [Pil11] (Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011)).
items.note: Used in Lemma 7.6.1: by inflation–restriction, this group is the kernel of H^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)) → H^1(F_S/L(ζ_{p^N}), ad^0ρ̄(1)). Missing: GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 plans the auxiliary-prime argument for GL-valued problems, not this GSp_4 lemma.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.15: Sp_4(F_p) is enormous and GSp_4(F_p) is tidy; surjective ρ̄ with similitude ε̄^{-1} is vast and tidy
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.15. If p ≥ 3, then H = Sp_4(F_p) is enormous and G = GSp_4(F_p) is tidy. If ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F_p) is a surjective representation with similitude character ε̄^{-1}, then ρ̄ is vast and tidy.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.15 (§7.5), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 201 (published p. 396); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note:
Split: the following are separate items: Lemmas 7.5.12, 7.5.13, 7.5.17 (with §7.5.16), 7.5.18, 7.5.19, 7.5.21 (with §7.5.20), 7.5.22 (with Remark 7.5.23), and 7.5.25–7.5.27 (with §7.5.24).

Proof:
- (E3): ad^0 is absolutely irreducible, and every element with distinct eigenvalues has eigenvalue 1 on it.
- (E1): H^1(Sp_4(F_p), ad^0) = 0 is Lemma 7.5.14 for p ≥ 11, and a Magma computation for p = 3, 5, 7. A formal proof therefore needs those finite computations.
- Tidiness: for p > 3 this is Lemma 7.5.12. For p = 3, take an element of order 20 with ν = −1 and eigenvalues ζ, ζ³, ζ⁹, ζ²⁷.
- Vastness: the image of G_{F(ζ_{p^N})} is Sp_4(F_p) for all N, because Sp_4(F_p) has no quotient of p-power order.

Used in Lemma 9.2.2. Missing.

items.name: Lemma 7.6.1, Definition 7.6.2 and Corollary 7.6.3: Taylor–Wiles data killing the dual Selmer group, and the presentation with g = 2q − 4[F:Q] + #S − 1
items.statement:
Setting (§7.1, §7.6). p > 2 throughout §7. S = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, ψ, {D_v}_{v∈S}) is a global deformation problem (Definition 7.1.5): ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible, S is a finite set of finite places of F containing S_p and every place at which ρ̄ is ramified, and ψ : G_{F,S} → Λ^× lifts ν∘ρ̄. Taylor–Wiles data and the augmented problem S_Q are as in §7.6. For a Taylor–Wiles datum Q, H^1_{S_Q^⊥,S}(ad^0ρ̄(1)) = ker(H^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈Q} H^1(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1))).
Lemma 7.6.1. Assume that ρ̄ is vast, that p ≥ 3 is unramified in F, that ψ = ε^{−1}, and that k contains every eigenvalue of every element of ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}). Let q ≥ h^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)). Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (ᾱ_{v,1},…,ᾱ_{v,4})_{v∈Q_N}) such that (1) #Q_N = q; (2) q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N for each v ∈ Q_N; (3) h^1_{S_{Q_N}^⊥,S}(ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0.
Definition 7.6.2. ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F̄_p) is odd if its similitude character ψ is odd, i.e. ψ(c_v) = −1 for the complex conjugation c_v at each place v | ∞ of F.
Corollary 7.6.3. Assume that ρ̄ is odd, that ρ̄ is vast, and that k contains every eigenvalue of every element of ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}). Let q ≥ h^1(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)). Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (ᾱ_{v,1},…,ᾱ_{v,4})_{v∈Q_N}) such that (1) #Q_N = q; (2) q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N for each v ∈ Q_N; (3) there is a local Λ-algebra surjection R^{S,loc}_S[[X_1,…,X_g]] → R^S_{S_{Q_N}} with g = 2q − 4[F:Q] + #S − 1.
Proof of the corollary. Apply Proposition 7.2.1 to S_{Q_N} with T = S, and use (3) of Lemma 7.6.1 and h^0(F_S/F, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0 (from vastness). This gives g = #S − 1 − Σ_{v|∞} h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) + Σ_{v∈Q_N} h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1)). For v ∈ Q_N, h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) = 2, because q_v ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} has distinct eigenvalues. For v | ∞, h^0(F_v, ad^0ρ̄) = 4, because ρ̄ is odd.
items.locator: Lemma 7.6.1, Definition 7.6.2 and Corollary 7.6.3 (§7.6), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 208–209; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 405–406
items.note:
Why the three statements stay together: Lemma 7.6.1 is used only in the proof of Corollary 7.6.3, and Definition 7.6.2 only in its statement. The definition of a Taylor–Wiles datum and of S_Q, which no item covered, is now a separate item. The proof of Corollary 7.6.3 cites the lemma as 'Theorem 7.6.1'; this is sourceIssue E1, confirmed at arXiv p. 209.
Missing hypotheses in Corollary 7.6.3: as printed, it does not repeat two hypotheses of Lemma 7.6.1, 'p unramified in F' and 'ψ = ε^{−1}'. Both hold where the corollary is used (§7.11, under Hypothesis 7.8.1, where ψ = ε^{−1}). The lemma's proof uses 'p unramified' only to take N = 3 via Remark 7.5.7; taking N larger works equally well, since q_v ≡ 1 mod p^{N'} implies q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N. No step of that proof uses ψ = ε^{−1}.
Status: missing. The generic Chebotarev and dual-Selmer mechanism is item 149, planned at GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5. The GSp_4 instance is planned nowhere: vastness through Lemma 7.5.9 and condition (E3) of Definition 7.5.2, and the counts h^0 = 2 at Taylor–Wiles places and h^0 = 4 at real places. GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 plans only the auxiliary-prime lemma for polarized GL_n over CM fields. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.4 plans only the GL_n auxiliary sets of ACC+. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has Galois deformation rings or dual Selmer groups.

items.name: Hypotheses 7.7.1 and 7.8.1 and the auxiliary place v_0: the standing hypotheses on ρ̄
items.statement:
Setting of §7.7. F is a totally real field in which the prime p ≥ 3 splits completely, S_p is the set of places of F above p, and ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k) is absolutely irreducible.
Hypothesis 7.7.1. (1) ρ̄ is vast and tidy (Definitions 7.5.6 and 7.5.11); (2) for v ∈ S_p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary (Definition 7.3.1); (3) there is a set R of finite places of F, disjoint from S_p, such that (a) for v ∈ R, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial and q_v ≡ 1 (mod p), and q_v ≡ 1 (mod 9) if p = 3; (b) for v ∉ S_p ∪ R, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified.
Hypothesis 7.8.1. (1) F is totally real and p ≥ 3 splits completely in F. (2) ρ̄ is vast and tidy. (3) ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for each v ∈ S_p. (4) There is a set R of finite places, disjoint from S_p, satisfying (3)(a)–(b) of Hypothesis 7.7.1. (5) There is an ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 with central character |·|^2 such that (a) ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄; (b) π_v^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R ∪ S_p; (c) π_v^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} ≠ 0 for v ∉ R ∪ S_p.
The auxiliary place v_0. Under either hypothesis, Chebotarev and the tidiness of ρ̄(G_F) give a place v_0 ∉ R ∪ S_p with these properties: v_0 is unramified over Q; q_{v_0} ≢ 1 (mod p); no two eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_{v_0}) have ratio q_{v_0}; and the residue characteristic of v_0 is greater than 5. Fix one. Then H^2(F_{v_0}, ad ρ̄) = H^0(F_{v_0}, ad ρ̄(1))^∨ = 0, every lift of ρ̄|_{G_{F_{v_0}}} is unramified (Proposition 7.4.2), and S := R ∪ S_p ∪ {v_0}. From §7.7 on, ψ = ε^{−1} and ψ is dropped from the notation.
items.locator: Hypothesis 7.7.1 and the choice of v_0 (§7.7), arXiv p. 210, published pp. 406–407; Hypothesis 7.8.1 and the choice of v_0 (§7.8), arXiv p. 211, published p. 408
items.note:
Items split out:
- Definition 7.8.2 and Lemma 7.8.3 are now separate items. They are used separately: Lemma 7.8.3 is invoked in §7.7, and for every level with K_{v_0} = Iw_1(v_0), including the levels of Definition 7.13.4.
- The global deformation problems S_χ^{I,𝔠} and S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠} of §7.7, which no item covered, are also a new item.
On v_0: the paper says 'an unramified place v_0'. Lemma 7.8.3, applied with v = v_0, needs v_0 absolutely unramified, and §7.13 (8) says 'absolutely unramified' explicitly.
Status: missing. The atlas has no GSp_4 deformation or modularity layer, and the notions used here (items 88, 96 and 97) are themselves missing.

items.name: Lemmas 7.8.5 and 7.8.6 with Remark 7.8.7: RHom^0 duality for perfect complexes, and Pontryagin duals of finite free O-modules
items.statement:
Lemma 7.8.5. Let Λ ∈ CNL_O, and let M^• be a perfect complex of Λ-modules bounded below by 0. So M^• is quasi-isomorphic to a complex P^0 → P^1 → … → P^{l_0} of finite projective Λ-modules in degrees [0, l_0]. Set M := RHom^0_Λ(M^•, Λ), that is, M = coker(Hom_Λ(P^1, Λ) → Hom_Λ(P^0, Λ)). Write * for the dual of a finite-dimensional vector space and ∨ for the Pontryagin dual. Then: (1) M ⊗_Λ k = (H^0(M^• ⊗^L_Λ k))^*; (2) for every homomorphism of O-algebras Λ → E, M ⊗_Λ E = (H^0(M^• ⊗^L_Λ E))^*; (3) for every homomorphism of O-algebras Λ → O, M ⊗_Λ O = Hom(H^0(M^• ⊗^L_Λ E/O), E/O) = H^0(M^• ⊗^L_Λ E/O)^∨.
Lemma 7.8.6. Let φ : M → N be a morphism of finite free O-modules, and let φ_{E/O} = φ ⊗ E/O : M ⊗ E/O → N ⊗ E/O. Then the Pontryagin dual of φ_{E/O} is the map φ^∨_{E/O} : Hom(N, O) → Hom(M, O) given by composition with φ. In particular, the Pontryagin dual of ker(φ_{E/O}) is coker(φ^∨_{E/O}).
Remark 7.8.7. Calegari and Geraghty construct patched modules as Pontryagin duals of cohomology with E/O coefficients. Lemma 7.8.5 (3) shows that, when Λ = O, the RHom^0 construction used here agrees with theirs.
items.locator: Lemmas 7.8.5 and 7.8.6 and Remark 7.8.7 (§7.8), arXiv pp. 213–214; published pp. 411–412
items.note:
The two lemmas stay together because Lemma 7.8.6 is used only in the proof of Lemma 7.8.5 (3).
Status: missing. The content is general commutative algebra, not GSp_4 theory. The nearest planned stages are:
- DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7: perfect complexes over complete Noetherian local O-algebras, with their duals, derived tensor products and specialization results.
- CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3: continuous O-linear and Pontryagin duals. The Calegari–Geraghty 2018 and 2020 extractions already cite CC.3 for the O-linear Pontryagin dual Hom_O(−, E/O).
Neither stage states this lemma.
Routing: the item belongs in a source route to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra (P7), importing CC.3, rather than in the abelian-surfaces roadmap.
Libraries: neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti treats RHom of perfect complexes over CNL_O, or the O-linear dual Hom_O(−, E/O) and its duality for finite free O-modules. Mathlib has PontryaginDual for topological groups and CharacterModule, the dual Hom_Z(−, Q/Z) of an abelian group, but not the O-linear duality used here.

items.name: Definition 7.8.8 and Remark 7.8.9: weights for Λ_I, classical weights, κ_2 and κ_reg
items.statement:
Definition 7.8.8. Fix I ⊆ S_p. A weight is a homomorphism κ : Λ_I → O. It corresponds to a tuple (θ_{v,1}, θ_{v,2})_{v∈S_p} of characters θ_{v,i} : I_{F_v} → O^× with trivial reduction, with θ_{v,1} = θ_{v,2} for v ∈ I. Write p_κ ⊂ Λ_I for its kernel.
Classical weights. κ is classical if there are integers k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 with θ_{v,1} = ε^{(k_v+l_v)/2−2} and θ_{v,2} = ε^{(k_v−l_v)/2}, and with l_v = 2 if v ∈ I. Then k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 or p + 1 (mod 2(p−1)). For classical κ, ω^κ is the automorphic vector bundle of weight (k_v, l_v)_{v∈S_p} (§3.7).
κ_2 and κ_reg. For any I, κ_2 is the classical weight with k_v = l_v = 2 for all v. For I = ∅ one fixes a sufficiently regular classical weight κ_reg, for example θ_{v,1} = ε^{2N(p−1)}, θ_{v,2} = ε^{N(p−1)} for all v ∈ S_p, with N sufficiently large.
Remark 7.8.9. κ_reg is chosen so that Theorems 3.10.1 and 6.6.5 apply in weight κ_reg.
items.locator: Definition 7.8.8 and Remark 7.8.9 (§7.8), arXiv p. 214; published p. 412
items.note:
Split: the Hecke algebras, the maximal ideal (7.8.4) and the modules M^{χ,I,𝔠}, M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} (arXiv pp. 212–213) are now a separate construction item.
Notation: the paper's index is the fraktur letter 𝔠, a choice of ᾱ_v or β̄_v at each v ∈ S_p, not 'αβ'.
The weight space Λ_I itself is item 61.
Status: missing.

items.name: Proposition 7.8.11: M^{χ,∅,𝔠,Q} is finite free over Λ_∅[Δ_Q], and M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} is balanced over Λ_I[Δ_Q] when #I = 1
items.statement:
Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, and let χ, 𝔠 and a Taylor–Wiles datum Q be as in §7.8.
Proposition 7.8.11. (1) M^{χ,∅,𝔠,Q} is a finite free Λ_∅[Δ_Q]-module. (2) If #I = 1, then M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} is a balanced Λ_I[Δ_Q]-module (Definition 2.10.1).
Proof outline.
- Perfectness: the complex M^{•,I}_{K_1^p(Q)} of Theorem 4.6.1, at tame level K_1^p(Q), is a perfect complex of Λ_I[∏_{v∈Q∪R}T(k(v))]-modules of amplitude [0, #I], by Proposition 7.8.10 and the semi-local form of Lemma 4.6.22. Hence M^{•,I,χ}_{K_1^p(Q)} is perfect over Λ_I[Δ_Q] of amplitude [0, #I], and localization at m̃^{I,𝔠} preserves this.
- Central character: with C = F^×\A_F^×/U = C_p ⊕ C^p the component group, M̃^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} ≃ M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} ⊗_O O[C_p]. This step uses p ≠ 2.
- Part (1) follows because the amplitude is [0, 0].
- Part (2): by Lemma 2.10.2 it suffices that the localized complex of amplitude [0, 1] has Euler characteristic 0. This is checked modulo prime ideals of Λ_I, using Theorem 6.6.5 and Corollary 3.10.5.
items.locator: Proposition 7.8.11 (§7.8), arXiv pp. 215–216; published pp. 413–414
items.note:
Split: Proposition 7.8.10, previously bundled here, is used separately (in the proofs of Propositions 7.8.11 and 7.9.8) and is now a new item.
Correction: the old text gave the covering group of Proposition 7.8.10 as Δ_Q. It is ∏_{v∈Q∪R}T(k(v)).
The notion 'balanced' is §2.10 (item 150).
Status: missing.

items.name: Proposition 7.9.1 (Doubling): surjections M^{χ,I,𝔠} ⊗_{Λ_I} Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠} for I ⊆ I'
items.statement:
Setting. Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1. For I ⊆ I' ⊆ S_p, Λ_I → Λ_{I'} is the surjection corresponding to the closed immersion Spec Λ_{I'} → Spec Λ_I given by θ_{v,1} = θ_{v,2} for v ∈ I'. For v in the relevant I, Hensel's lemma and ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v give lifts α̃_v, β̃_v of ᾱ_v, β̄_v in the Hecke algebra with X^2 − U_{Kli(v),1}X + U_{v,2} = (X − α̃_v)(X − β̃_v). Write 𝔠̃_v for the lift of 𝔠_v, and {α_v, β_v} = {𝔠_v, 𝔠'_v}.
Proposition 7.9.1. For each choice of 𝔠 and each I ⊆ I', there are natural surjections M^{χ,I,𝔠} ⊗_{Λ_I} Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠} and M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} ⊗_{Λ_I} Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠,Q}. They commute with all Hecke operators away from I' \ I. For v ∈ I' \ I, they are equivariant for U_{v,0} and U_{v,2}, and intertwine U_{v,1} on the source with 𝔠̃_v on the target.
Proof outline.
- For I' = I ∪ {v}, the map is τ∘U_{v,1} − 𝔠̃'_v∘τ, where τ is induced by restriction along 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli(p^∞)} ⊂ 𝔛^{G_1,I'}_{K,Kli(p^∞)}.
- The intertwining uses Lemma 4.5.17, U_{v,1}(U_{Kli(v),1} − U_{v,1}) = U_{v,2}, i.e. (U_{v,1} − 𝔠̃'_v)(U_{v,1} − 𝔠̃_v) = 0 (7.9.2), together with Hensel's lemma.
- Surjectivity reduces, by Nakayama's lemma and Lemma 7.8.5 (1), to injectivity on the special fibre of the map (7.9.3), (U_{v,1} − 𝔠'_v) : e(U^{I'})H^0(X^{I',G_1}_{K^pK_p(I'),1}, ω^2(−D))_{m̃^{I',𝔠},χ,|·|^2} → e(U^I)H^0(X^{I,G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p,1}, ω^2(−D))_{m̃^{I,𝔠},χ,|·|^2}. That injectivity is Theorem 5.8.6, as in Remark 5.8.7.
items.locator: Proposition 7.9.1 with (7.9.2) and (7.9.3) (§7.9), arXiv pp. 216–218; published pp. 415–416
items.note:
The injectivity of (7.9.3) is reused in Proposition 7.13.9, now a new item.
Status: missing. The proposition depends on the doubling Theorem 5.8.6 (item 73) and the Hecke relations of §4.5 (item 62).

items.name: Theorem 7.9.4: the Galois representation ρ^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} : G_F → GSp_4(T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}) of type S^{I,𝔠}_{χ,Q}
items.locator: Theorem 7.9.4 (§7.9), arXiv pp. 218–220; published pp. 417–419

Proof outline.
- Case I = ∅. - General I: induction on #I through Proposition 7.9.1.

items.name: Proposition 7.9.8: (M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q})_{Δ_Q} ≅ M^{χ,I,𝔠}
items.statement:
Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, with χ, I, 𝔠 and a Taylor–Wiles datum Q as in §7.8.
Proposition 7.9.8. The natural map M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} → M^{χ,I,𝔠} induces an isomorphism (M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q})_{Δ_Q} → M^{χ,I,𝔠}.
Proof, following Khare–Thorne, Lemma 6.25. The isomorphism is the composite of two isomorphisms.
- (7.9.9) (M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q})_{Δ_Q} ≅ M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}_{K_0^p(Q)}. It suffices that (M^{•,I}_{K_1^p(Q)})^{∏_{v∈Q}T(k(v))} ≅ M^{•,I}_{K_0^p(Q)} in the derived category; the complex at level K_1^p(Q) is perfect over Λ_I[∏_{v∈Q}T(k(v))], and the isomorphism is immediate from Proposition 7.8.10.
- (7.9.10) M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}_{K_0^p(Q)} ≅ M^{χ,I,𝔠}. Write the map as the composite (M^{•,I}_{K_0^p(Q)})_{m̃^{an,Q},m̃_Q} → (M^{•,I}_{K_0^p(Q)})_{m̃^{an,Q}} → (M^{•,I}_{K^p})_{m̃^{an,Q}} → (M^{•,I}_{K^p})_{m̃^{an}}. By Lemma 7.9.7 the first two maps are quasi-isomorphisms if they induce isomorphisms on H^*(− ⊗ k); this follows from Lemmas 2.4.36–2.4.37 at each v ∈ Q, using, for K = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) and K' = Iw(v), the identities [K1K'][K'1K] = [K:K'] and [K'1K][K1K'] = e_K, where [K:K'] = (q_v+1)^2(q_v^2+1) is prime to p (the paper: 'since p > 2'; here q_v ≡ 1 mod p). For the last map it suffices, after applying RHom^0(−, Λ) and Lemma 7.8.5 (1), that H^0(M^{•,I}_{K^p} ⊗ k)_{m̃^{an,Q}} → H^0(M^{•,I}_{K^p} ⊗ k)_{m̃^{an}} is an isomorphism, i.e. that m̃^{an} is the unique maximal ideal of T̃ over m̃^{an,Q} in the support of H^0(M^{•,I}_{K^p} ⊗ k). This follows from local–global compatibility (deduced from Theorem 2.7.2, as in the proof of Theorem 7.9.4) and Chebotarev.

items.name: Proposition 7.11.2: the patched modules are maximal Cohen–Macaulay over (R_∞^{1,I,𝔠})' and (R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠})'
items.statement:
Setting. Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, fix I ⊆ S_p with #I ≤ 1 and a choice 𝔠, and let S_∞, R_∞^{1,I,𝔠}, R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}, M_∞^{1,I,𝔠} and M_∞^{χ,I,𝔠} be the patched objects of §7.11. For a complete Noetherian local O-algebra R, R' is its maximal O-flat quotient (the image of R in R[1/p]).
Proposition 7.11.2. M_∞^{1,I,𝔠} is a maximal Cohen–Macaulay (R_∞^{1,I,𝔠})'-module, and M_∞^{χ,I,𝔠} is a maximal Cohen–Macaulay (R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠})'-module.
Proof outline. By (7.11.1), the support of M_∞ in Spec S_∞ has codimension at least #I. Apply [CG18, Lem. 6.2] to a resolution S_∞^r → S_∞^r of M_∞ if #I = 1 (such a resolution exists by Lemma 2.10.2), or to M_∞ itself if #I = 0. This shows the codimension is exactly #I and depth_{S_∞} M_∞ = dim S_∞ − #I = dim(R_∞)'. Hence the depth of M_∞ over (R_∞)' is at least dim(R_∞)'.
items.locator: Proposition 7.11.2 (§7.11), arXiv p. 226; published pp. 426–427

[CG18, Lem. 6.2] is planned at DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9 (item 150).

items.name: Lemmas 7.12.2 and 7.12.3 with Remarks 7.12.6–7.12.7: cycles of modules over R̃^1 and R̃^χ and the multiplicities d'_η (Ihara avoidance)
items.statement:
Setting (§7.12). For R ∈ CNL_O, R' is its maximal O-flat quotient. Put R^1 = ⊗̂_{v∈R}R_v^1 and R^χ = ⊗̂_{v∈R}R_v^χ, and R̃^1 = R^1⊗̂R̃, R̃^χ = R^χ⊗̂R̃ for some R̃ ∈ CNL_O with R̃' irreducible. In applications R̃^1 = R_∞^{1,I,𝔠} and R̃^χ = R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}. For each v ∈ R, R_v^1/(λ) = R_v^χ/(λ). By Propositions 7.4.7 and 7.4.8, Spec(R_v^1)'/(λ) and Spec(R_v^χ)'/(λ) have the same underlying space as Spec R_v^1/(λ). This gives identifications Z((R^1)'/(λ)) = Z((R^χ)'/(λ)) and Z((R̃^1)'/(λ)) = Z((R̃^χ)'/(λ)).
Lemma 7.12.2. Let M^1 be a finite O-flat R̃^1-module and M^χ a finite O-flat R̃^χ-module, with M^1/λM^1 ≃ M^χ/λM^χ as R̃^1/(λ) = R̃^χ/(λ)-modules. Then Z(M^1/λM^1, (R̃^1)'/(λ)) = Z(M^χ/λM^χ, (R̃^χ)'/(λ)) under the identification above.
Generic points. The generic points of Spec(R^1)' (and of Spec(R̃^1)') are the tuples η = (η_v)_{v∈R} of generic points of Spec(R_v^1)'. By Proposition 7.4.7 and (7.12.1), the cycles η̄ of distinct generic points have disjoint supports. By Proposition 7.4.8, Spec(R^χ)' and Spec(R̃^χ)' are irreducible; η^χ denotes their generic point.
Lemma 7.12.3. Suppose given a finite O-flat R̃^1-module M^1, a finite O-flat R̃^χ-module M^χ, and an isomorphism M^1/λM^1 ≃ M^χ/λM^χ of R̃^1/(λ) = R̃^χ/(λ)-modules. Suppose also that M^1 is supported on at least one generic point of Spec(R̃^1)'. Then there are unique positive rational numbers d'_η, indexed by the generic points η = (η_v)_{v∈R} of Spec(R^1)', such that: (1) η̄^χ = Σ_η d'_η η̄ in Z((R^1)'/(λ)) = Z((R^χ)'/(λ)) (7.12.4); (2) len_{(R̃^1)'_η}(M^1_η) = d'_η · len_{(R̃^χ)'_{η^χ}}(M^χ_{η^χ}) for every generic point η of Spec(R̃^1)' (7.12.5). In particular, M^1 is supported on every generic point of Spec(R̃^1)'. The paper calls the d'_η positive integers; see the note.
Remark 7.12.6. The d'_η do not depend on M^1, M^χ or R̃.
Remark 7.12.7. This is the cycle-theoretic form of Taylor's Ihara avoidance. The key points are that R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}[1/p] is a domain and that R_∞^{1,I,𝔠}/(λ) = R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}/(λ).
items.note:
Lemma 7.12.2 is used only in the proof of Lemma 7.12.3. The recollections of §7.12 on cycles and completed tensor products are now two new items.
Integrality of d'_η: the proof shows d'_η = len(M^1_η)/len(M^χ_{η^χ}), a positive rational number. Each η̄ is an integral cycle whose coefficients might all be divisible by some m > 1, so disjointness of supports does not by itself make d'_η an integer; it would follow if each η̄ had coefficients with greatest common divisor 1 (for instance if the special fibres of the (R_v^1)' were generically reduced), which Proposition 7.4.7 does not state, and the paper gives no further argument. Integrality is not used later: the proof of Theorem 7.13.6 computes d'_η = d_ρ directly.
Status: missing.
Routing: once the local inputs are made hypotheses, the lemma is commutative algebra. The local inputs are the disjoint supports of the η̄, the irreducibility of (R_v^χ)', and the equality of the underlying spaces of the special fibres. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9 plans algebraic Ihara-avoidance comparisons of support, but not these length identities. A source route to P9 fits better than the abelian-surfaces roadmap.

items.name: Proposition 7.13.5 and the multiplicities d_η, d_ρ: Iwahori invariants of generic L-packets on the components of Spec R_v^1
items.statement:
Proposition 7.13.5. Let η_v be a generic point of Spec R_v^1 for some v ∈ R, where R_v^1 is the Ihara-avoidance ring of §7.4.5 with χ = 1. The set of y ∈ (Spec R_v^{1,η_v})(Ē) whose L-packet L(ρ_y) contains a generic representation is nonempty, and d_{η_v} := Σ_{π∈L(ρ_y)} dim π^{Iw(v)} is independent of such y. More explicitly, the rank n(η_v) of the monodromy operator N is generically constant on Spec R_v^{1,η_v}, and d_{η_v} = 8, 4, 4 or 1 according as n(η_v) = 0, 1, 2 or 3.
Proof outline, from Roberts–Schmidt [RS07b, Tables A.1, A.7 and A.15; RS07c, §1]. The L-packets containing a generic representation are: for n(η_v) = 0, singletons of type I (unramified principal series); for n(η_v) = 1, singletons of type IIa; for n(η_v) = 2, singletons of type IIIa or pairs {VIa, VIb}; for n(η_v) = 3, singletons of type IVa (unramified twists of Steinberg). Representations of type Va do not contribute, as they never correspond to residually trivial Galois representations.
The multiplicities d_η and d_ρ. A tuple η = (η_v)_{v∈R} gives a generic point of R^{1,I,𝔠,loc} and of R_∞^{1,I,𝔠} (§7.12); put d_η := ∏_{v∈R} d_{η_v}. For ρ as in Hypothesis 7.13.1, put d_ρ := d_η for the generic point of R^{1,I,𝔠,loc} on which the local representations of ρ lie; this point is unique because the ρ|_{G_{F_v}} are pure. Then d_ρ = 8^{|R_0|}4^{|R_1|+|R_2|}, where R_i = {v ∈ R : n(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) = i}.

items.name: Theorem 7.13.6: the ρ-eigenspace of p-adic forms at Iwahori level has dimension 8d_ρ when #I ≤ 1
items.statement:
Theorem 7.13.6. Assume Hypothesis 7.13.1 for ρ = ρ_x, in the notation of §7.13. For any I ⊆ S_p with #I ≤ 1 and any choice of 𝔠, dim_E S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,𝔠}] = 8d_ρ, with d_ρ as defined after Proposition 7.13.5.
Remark 7.13.7. The factor 8 = |W| appears because at the auxiliary place v_0 one works at the level Iw_1(v_0) of Definition 7.13.4 (the remark says 'Iwahori level') and imposes no condition on the Hecke operators there.
Proof outline.
- Case I = ∅. M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} is maximal Cohen–Macaulay (Proposition 7.11.2), so Lemma 7.12.3 applies to M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} and M_∞^{χ,∅,𝔠}, and M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} is supported on every component.
- M_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} is finite free over S_∞ and faithful over (R_∞^{1,∅,𝔠})^{red}, so Spec R_∞ → Spec S_∞ is surjective and generalizing. This gives regular-weight points x_reg on the component of x, and x^χ_reg.
- Proposition 7.13.11 gives the dimensions 8d_ρ and 8 at these points.
- Lemma 7.13.8 applies at the smooth points (by purity, Theorem 2.7.2 and Lemmas 7.1.3 and 7.3.18). It transports 8d_ρ to x and, with Lemma 7.12.3, gives d'_η = d_ρ.
- Case #I = 1. The same argument at the component η_π of the representation π of Hypothesis 7.13.1 gives d'_{η_π} = d_{ρ_{π,p}}. With the inequality (7.13.10) of Proposition 7.13.11 and Lemmas 7.12.3 and 7.13.8 it gives dim ≥ 8d_ρ. Proposition 7.13.9 gives dim ≤ 8d_ρ, the dimension of the I = ∅ space.
items.locator: Theorem 7.13.6 and Remark 7.13.7 (§7.13), arXiv p. 232, proof pp. 233–234; published p. 434, proof pp. 435–436
items.note:
Splits: Lemma 7.13.8 and Propositions 7.13.9 and 7.13.11, previously bundled here, are now new items, for different reasons:
- Proposition 7.13.9 is used again in §8 (arXiv pp. 236, 238 and 240).
- Lemma 7.13.8 is general commutative algebra with a different status.
- Proposition 7.13.11 carries the dependence on Arthur's classification (Theorem 2.9.3), through strong multiplicity one for GL_4.
Remark 7.13.12 is not an item. It records that the proof shows d'_ρ = d_ρ, and expects, following Shotton, that Z(Spec(R_v^χ)^{red}/(λ)) = Σ_{η_v} d_{η_v} η̄_v; that is a remark, not a result.

items.name: Theorem 8.2.1 and Corollary 8.2.2: gluing, and the automorphy of ρ
items.statement: Notation (§§7.7, 7.8, 7.13, 8.2). E is the coefficient field, S_p the set of places of F above p, R the finite set of places of Hypothesis 7.13.1(5) and v_0 the auxiliary place of Hypothesis 7.13.1(8). A choice αβ (printed with a Linear B sign) is a choice, at each v ∈ S_p, of ᾱ_v or β̄_v (§7.7); only the choices at v ∈ I^c matter, αβ_v ∈ {α_v, β_v} denotes the corresponding lift determined by ρ|_{G_{F_v}} as in Definition 7.3.1, and αβ'_v the other one. S^{I,αβ}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)} = (H^0(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}, ω^2(−D))_{m̃^{I,αβ}}) ⊗_𝒪 E[{U_{v,0}−1}_{v∈S_p}, {U_{v,0}−q_v^{−2}}_{v∈R}, {T_{v,0}−q_v^{−2}}_{v∉S_p∪R∪{v_0}}], with m̃^{I,αβ} the maximal ideal (7.8.4), and p̃_x^{I,αβ} ⊂ T̃^I is the ideal generated by the coefficients of det(X−ρ(Frob_v))−Q_v(X) for v ∉ S_p∪R∪{v_0} and by U_{v,0}−1, U_{v,2}−α_vβ_v (v ∈ S_p), U_{Kli(v),1}−α_v−β_v (v ∈ I) and U_{v,1}−αβ_v (v ∈ I^c). The overconvergent space is S^{I,αβ,†}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)} := e(U^I)H^0(𝒳^{G_1,mult,†}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}, ω^2(−D)) ∩ (S^{I,αβ}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)} ⊗_E C_p), the intersection taken inside e(U^I)H^0(𝒳^{G_1,I}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}, ω^2(−D)) through the injective restriction map from the dagger space 𝒳^{G_1,mult,†} of (6.5.5). Theorem 8.2.1. Assume that ρ satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1. Then for any I ⊆ S_p and any choice of αβ, dim_E S^{I,αβ}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,αβ}] = dim_{C_p} S^{I,αβ,†}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,αβ}] = 8d_ρ, where, as in Theorem 7.13.6 (the case #I ≤ 1), d_ρ = ∏_{v∈R} d_{η_v} for the generic points η_v on which the ρ|_{G_{F_v}} lie, that is d_ρ = 8^{|R_0|}4^{|R_1|+|R_2|} with R_i the set of v ∈ R such that n(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) = i. (The proof is an induction on #I: Theorems 7.13.6 and 6.6.4 give #I ≤ 1, and Proposition 7.13.9 gives the upper bound 8d_ρ.) Corollary 8.2.2. Suppose that ρ satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1. Then ρ is modular. More precisely, there is an ordinary automorphic representation π' of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ, and for every finite place v of F, WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}). (The corollary takes I = S_p with Theorems 6.5.8 and 3.10.1, gets the semisimplified compatibility from Corollary 7.9.6, and matches the monodromy at v ∈ R through Lemma 2.5.1 and the comparison of n(π_v) with parahoric fixed vectors.)

items.name: Lemmas 8.2.3 and 8.2.5: analytic continuation and descent of the glued forms
items.statement: Setting (§8.2, inductive step of Theorem 8.2.1): #I ≥ 2, I = J ⊔ {v_1, v_2}, the choice αβ fixed at the places of J ∪ I^c, and V_{αβ_1,αβ_2} ⊂ H^0(𝒳^{mult,†}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(J)}, ω^2(−D)), V_{αβ_1+αβ'_1,αβ_2} ⊂ H^0(𝒳^{mult,†}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(J∪{v_1})}, ω^2(−D)), V_{αβ_1,αβ_2+αβ'_2} ⊂ H^0(𝒳^{mult,†}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(J∪{v_2})}, ω^2(−D)) the 8d_ρ-dimensional eigenspaces supplied by the inductive hypothesis (U_{v_i,1}-eigenvalue αβ_i at Iwahori level at v_i, U_{Kli(v_i),1}-eigenvalue α_i+β_i at Klingen level). Regions: for (ε_v) ∈ [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c}, 𝒳_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}((ε_v)) is the open subspace where deg H_v ≥ 1−ε_v for v ∈ I (H_v the subgroup of order p of the Klingen level structure) and deg L_v ≥ 2−ε_v for v ∈ I^c (L_v ⊃ H_v the maximal isotropic subgroup of rank p^2 of the Iwahori level structure); 𝒳^{mult} = 𝒳((0)), 𝒳^{mult,†} = lim_{ε_v→0+} 𝒳((ε_v)), 𝒳^{mult,‡} the same limit over the places other than v_1, v_2; subscripts Iw(v_1), Iw(v_2), Iw(v_1,v_2) add Iwahori level there; d^H_i = deg H_{v_i}, d^L_i = deg L_{v_i}; superscripts impose the displayed inequalities; 𝒴 ⊂ 𝒳 denotes the corresponding good reduction loci. Lemma 8.2.3. The elements of V_{αβ_1,αβ_2} extend to 𝒳^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε,d^L_1>1,d^L_2>1}_{Iw(v_1,v_2)} for some ε > 0. Similarly, the elements of V_{αβ_1+αβ'_1,αβ_2} and V_{αβ_1,αβ_2+αβ'_2} extend to 𝒳^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2>1−ε,d^L_2>1}_{Iw(v_2)} and 𝒳^{mult,‡,d^H_1>1−ε,d^L_1>1,d^H_2≥1−ε}_{Iw(v_1)} respectively, for some ε > 0 (by Lemma 6.5.18, the forms being ordinary, hence of finite slope, for U_{w,1}). Lemma 8.2.5. Let U_ε := 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε,d^L_2>1}_{Iw(v_1,v_2)}; the restriction to U_ε of the finite étale map q_{v_2} is an étale map U_ε → 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε}_{Iw(v_1)}, which is surjective for ε small. After possibly further shrinking ε > 0, any element of V_{α_1,α_2+β_2} descends along q_{v_2} to 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε}_{Iw(v_1)}. With the isomorphism (U_{v_1,1}−β_1) : V_{α_1+β_1,α_2} ⊕ V_{α_1+β_1,β_2} ≅ V_{α_1,α_2} ⊕ V_{α_1,β_2} induced by (8.2.4) and its analogue for β_2 (each map injective by the doubling result Proposition 7.13.9, between spaces of equal dimension), these give the 8d_ρ-dimensional space V_{α_1+β_1,α_2+β_2}, the preimage of V_{α_1,α_2+β_2}, of eigenforms, Klingen at v_1 and v_2, whose elements descend to 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε}. This completes the inductive step of Theorem 8.2.1.

items.name: Lemmas 8.2.7, 8.2.8, 8.2.10, 8.2.11 and Corollary 8.2.9: connected components and the superspecial locus
items.statement: Lemma 8.2.7. If S → T is a finite étale map of adic spaces of finite type over a field, then the image of any connected component of S is a connected component of T (such spaces have finitely many connected components, which are therefore their connected clopen subsets, and finite étale maps are open and closed by Huber, Lemma 1.4.5 and Proposition 1.7.8). Lemma 8.2.8. Any connected component of Y^{I,=_{v_2}1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1} contains a point of Y^{I,=_{{v_1,v_2}}1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1}, and any connected component of Y^{I,=_{v_2}2}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1} contains a point of Y^{I,=_{v_1}1,=_{v_2}2}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1}. Here Y_{…,1} is the special fibre of the open Hilbert–Siegel variety. The superscript I denotes the locus where H_v is multiplicative for v ∈ I and the Iwahori structure at v ∈ I^c is the canonical ordinary one (§4, p. 96). The superscript =_v a (a = 2, 1, 0) denotes the locus where 𝒢_v has p-rank a. Corollary 8.2.9. Any connected component of either of the spaces 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1=d^H_2=1,=_{v_2}1}_{Iw(v_1)}, 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1=d^H_2=1,=_{v_2}2}_{Iw(v_1)} contains a point which is non-ordinary at v_1. Lemma 8.2.10. Let J ⊆ S_p and K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(O_{F_v}). Each irreducible component of Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p,1} contains a point of Y^{=_{S_p}0}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p,1} in its closure (via the Ekedahl–Oort stratification, which extends to the minimal compactification with affine open strata, the superspecial locus not meeting the boundary). Lemma 8.2.11. Let K_p^{Iw} = ∏_{v|p}Iw(v). For J ⊆ J' ⊆ S_p, any irreducible component of Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1,m-can}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p^{Iw},1} contains a point of Y^{=_{(J')^c}2,=_{J'}1,m-can}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p^{Iw},1} in its closure. Here Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1,m-can} is the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratum where, for w ∈ J^c, 𝒢_w is ordinary and L_w = 𝒢_w[F], and, for w ∈ J, 𝒢_w has p-rank 1, H_w is multiplicative and L_w = 𝒢_w[F]. Remark 8.2.12: a more direct proof of Lemma 8.2.11 would follow if the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification of Y_{K^{p,Iw}K_p^{Iw}} were known to extend to the minimal compactification with quasi-affine open strata. No reference for this is available.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.1: the similitude character of an irreducible symplectic representation
items.statement: Lemma 8.3.1. Let K be a number field and ρ : G_K → GL_4(Q̄_p) irreducible preserving a generalized symplectic form with similitude character ν. Then either ν is uniquely determined by ρ, or, if ρ also admits the similitude character νψ with ψ ≠ 1, then ψ has finite order and ρ is reducible over a quadratic subfield of the field cut out by ψ.
items.locator: Lemma 8.3.1 (§8.3, Solvable base change), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Lemma 8.3.2: solvable descent for Hilbert–Siegel modular forms
items.statement: Lemma 8.3.2. Suppose that p > 2 splits completely in the totally real field F/Q. Let F'/F be a solvable extension of totally real fields. Suppose that ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies: (1) ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; (2) for all v|p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary; (3) ρ̄ is vast and tidy; (4) ρ|_{G_{F'}} is irreducible, and there is an ordinary automorphic representation π' of GSp_4(A_{F'}) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 such that for every finite place w of F', WD(ρ|_{G_{F'_w}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_w ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) (so ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ|_{G_{F'}}). Then ρ is modular. More precisely, there is an ordinary automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π,p} ≅ ρ, and for every finite place v of F, WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}). (Proof: reduce to F'/F cyclic of prime degree. π' is of general type (Arthur), so corresponds to a cuspidal Π' of GL_4(A_{F'}). Cyclic descent (Arthur–Clozel, Ch. 3, Thm. 4.2) gives Π on GL_4(A_F) with BC_{F'/F}(Π) = Π'. In L^S(s,Π',∧^2⊗|·|^{−2}) = ∏_ψ L^S(s,Π,∧^2⊗|·|^{−2}ψ^{−1}), the left side has a simple pole at s = 1, while by Shahidi all but at most one factor on the right is holomorphic and non-vanishing there. Theorem 2.9.3 gives π of central character |·|^2ψ, a twist of which has ρ_{π,p} ≅ ρ over GL_4. Lemma 8.3.1 fixes the similitude character, and Corollary 7.9.6 with base change gives the local-global compatibility.) It is the GSp_4 analogue of Lemma 1.3 of Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential automorphy II.

items.name: Theorem 8.4.1: the main modularity lifting theorem
items.statement: Theorem 8.4.1. Suppose that p ≥ 3 splits completely in the totally real field F/Q. Suppose that ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies: (1) ν∘ρ = ε^{−1}; (2) ρ̄ is vast and tidy in the sense of Definitions 7.5.6 and 7.5.11; (3) for all v|p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary in the sense of Definition 7.3.1; (4) there exists π (a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F), as in Hypothesis 7.13.1(6)) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, which is ordinary at all v|p, such that ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄; (5) for all finite places v of F, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} are pure. Then ρ is modular. More precisely, there is an ordinary automorphic representation π' of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ, and for every finite place v of F, WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}). (Proof: choose a solvable extension of totally real fields F'/F, linearly disjoint from F^{ker ρ̄} over F, in which p splits completely, with two properties. First, at every place w of F' above a place v ∤ p where π_v or ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is ramified, ρ̄|_{G_{F'_w}} is trivial, ρ|_{G_{F'_w}} has only unipotent ramification and q_w ≡ 1 (mod p^2). Second, π has a base change π' to F' (rec_{GT,p}(π'_w) = rec_{GT,p}(π_v)|_{W_{F'_w}}) with (π'_w)^{Iw(w)} ≠ 0 at every finite w (Mok, Prop. 4.13). Then ρ|_{G_{F'}} satisfies Hypothesis 7.13.1, and Corollary 8.2.2 with Lemma 8.3.2 concludes.) All the potential modularity and modularity results of §§9–10 are deduced from this theorem.
items.locator: Theorem 8.4.1 (§8.4, The main modularity lifting theorem), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, read in arXiv:1812.09269v3, the final version; Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501

items.name: Definition 8.5.1 and Theorem 8.5.2: the version with relaxed central character
items.statement: Definition 8.5.1. A representation ρ : G_{Q_p} → GSp_4(Q̄_p) is twisted p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary if it is an unramified twist of a representation which is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary in the sense of Definition 7.3.1; an admissible representation π_p of GSp_4(Q_p) is twisted ordinary if it is an unramified twist of an ordinary representation. Theorem 8.5.2. Suppose that p ≥ 3 splits completely in the totally real field F/Q and that ρ : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies: (1) ν∘ρ = χε^{−1}, where χ is a totally even finite order character which is unramified at all places dividing p; (2) ρ̄ is vast and tidy in the sense of Definitions 7.5.6 and 7.5.11; (3) for all v|p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is twisted p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary; (4) there exists π of parallel weight 2, twisted ordinary at all v|p, such that ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄ (no condition on its central character); (5) for all finite places v of F, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} are pure. Then ρ is modular. More precisely, there is a twisted ordinary automorphic representation π' of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 with ρ_{π',p} ≅ ρ, and for every finite place v of F, WD(ρ|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π'_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}). The paper gives only a sketch. Write ν∘ρ_π = χ'ε^{−1}. Choose a quadratic extension of totally real fields F'/F, linearly disjoint from F^{ker ρ̄}, in which p splits completely and over which χ = ψ^2 and χ' = ψ'^2 for finite order characters ψ, ψ'; the obstruction lies in the 2-torsion of the Brauer group and vanishes above p and at infinity. Apply Theorem 8.4.1 to ρ|_{G_{F'}} ⊗ ψ^{−1} and π_{F'} ⊗ (ψ')^{−1}∘Art_{F'}, and descend by 'an obvious generalization' of Lemma 8.3.2 to other central characters. The paper states that it does not use this result elsewhere.
