items.note: ET.7a develops 'the required GL_m residual-spectrum/Speh classification and cyclic automorphic-induction/base-change steps from the Arthur–Clozel and Moeglin–Waldspurger proofs', and ML.5 registers cyclic base change and automorphic induction with exact hypotheses; solvable base change is their iteration, as GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4 does for GL_2 (item 154). The existence of isobaric sums π_1 ⊞ π_2 (Langlands, through Eisenstein series, with Jacquet–Shalika's strong multiplicity one) is named by no layer; it lies between AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.1–AS.4 and ET.7a, and the design job should confirm its owner. The Allen et al. 2023 extraction records the identical pair of definitions as one item planned at ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2; the two extractions should cite the same owners. Used for GL_4 in the proof of Lemma 8.3.2, for GL_2 in §9, in §2.9, and in Definition 9.1.1.

items.name: The spherical Hecke operators T_{v,i} of GSp_4 and the Hecke polynomial Q_v(X) (2.4.8)
items.statement: §2.4.7: β_{v,0} = diag(ϖ_v, ϖ_v, ϖ_v, ϖ_v), β_{v,1} = diag(ϖ_v, ϖ_v, 1, 1), β_{v,2} = diag(ϖ_v^2, ϖ_v, ϖ_v, 1), and T_{v,i} = [GSp_4(O_{F_v})β_{v,i}GSp_4(O_{F_v})] (i = 0, 1, 2), which are independent of ϖ_v. If π is an unramified representation of GSp_4(F_v) (π^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} ≠ 0, so that π is a constituent of an unramified principal series) and t_{v,i} is the eigenvalue of T_{v,i} on π^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})}, then the characteristic polynomial of rec_{GT,p}(π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})(Frob_v) is (2.4.8) Q_v(X) = X^4 − t_{v,1}X^3 + (q_vt_{v,2} + (q_v^3 + q_v)t_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^3t_{v,0}t_{v,1}X + q_v^6t_{v,0}^2.
items.locator: §2.4.7, equation (2.4.8), arXiv p. 22
items.note: The paper says the identity is easy to check from Proposition 2.4.6(2); it is consistent (the pairs of roots multiply to γ_v = q_v^3t_{v,0}, which is q_v for central character |·|^2, since then t_{v,0} = q_v^{−2}). SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 plans the Satake isomorphism and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.4 the Euler polynomial of an L-group representation, but no layer plans the GSp_4 spin polynomial in the T_{v,i}; IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3 plans only the GL_n polynomial and warns against asserting it for other groups. The Calegari–Geraghty 2020 extraction records the identical polynomial Q_x(X) as missing and routes it as a source to IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3, as does the Pilloni 2020 extraction for its version. Used in Definition 2.4.9, §3.9 and the proof of Theorem 7.9.4 (det(X − ρ(Frob_v)) = Θ_π(Q_v(X))).

items.name: §2.4.23: the normalized Hecke operators U_{Iw(v),i}, U_{Kli(v),i}, U_{Si(v),1} at v|p and the ordinary projectors e_reg, e_irreg, e(I)
items.statement: For v|p and integers k ≥ l ≥ 2 with k ≡ l (mod 2) (the weights of §2.6): U_{Iw(v),0} = p^2U^{naive}_{Iw(v),0}, U_{Iw(v),1} = p^{(k+l)/2−2}U^{naive}_{Iw(v),1}, U_{Iw(v),2} = p^{k−1}U^{naive}_{Iw(v),2}, and the same normalizations define U_{Kli(v),0}, U_{Kli(v),1}, U_{Kli(v),2} from the naive Klingen operators and the Siegel operator U_{Si(v),1} = p^{(k+l)/2−2}U^{naive}_{Si(v),1}. U_{v,i} denotes U_{Iw(v),i}; U_{v,0} also denotes p^2[K_vβ_{v,0}K_v] for any subgroup K_v of Iw(v) (U_{v,0} is central in the Iwahori Hecke algebra, so p^2[K_vβ_{v,0}K_v] = e_{K_v}U_{v,0}), and U_{v,2} also denotes U_{Kli(v),2} (Remark 2.4.18). e_reg is the ordinary projector (§2.11) associated to U_{Iw(v),1}U_{Iw(v),2} and e_irreg the one associated to U_{Kli(v),2}. For I ⊂ S_p (the places above p), K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v) ∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v) and e(I) = ∏_{v∈I}e_irreg ∏_{v∉I}e_reg.
items.locator: §2.4.23 and the definitions of K_p(I) and e(I) before Proposition 2.4.26, arXiv pp. 25–27
items.note: The ordinary projector of a locally finite operator is item 34 (§2.11), planned in substance by PadicFamilies L0a's group-independent projector; the GSp_4 Iwahori, Klingen and Siegel operators at p with these normalizations are planned nowhere. These normalized operators, not the naive ones, are the operators of §§4–7; with Remark 2.4.18 (and q_v = p, as p splits completely) they satisfy U_{Kli(v),1} = U_{Iw(v),1} + p^{l−2}U_{Iw(v),1}^{−1}U_{Iw(v),2}, which is the form α_v + p^{l_v−2}β_v of the U_{Kli(v),1}-eigenvalue noted after Proposition 2.4.26.

items.name: The Bernstein presentation of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of GSp_4, its centre, and the Satake isomorphism in the coordinates x_0, x_1, x_2
items.statement: Let v ∤ p (as in §2.4.29, where q_v ≡ 1 mod p), H = O[Iw(v)\GSp_4(F_v)/Iw(v)], θ_μ ∈ H the image of e_μ ∈ O[X_*(T)] under the embedding O[X_*(T)] ↪ H of §2.4.4 (normalized as in Proposition 2.4.2), and T_w = [Iw(v)ẇIw(v)] for w ∈ W and any representative ẇ ∈ GSp_4(O_{F_v}). The Bernstein presentation is an algebra isomorphism H ≅ O[X_*(T)] ⊗̃_O O[Iw(v)\GSp_4(O_{F_v})/Iw(v)], the twisted tensor product being determined by (2.4.32) T_{s_α}θ_λ = θ_{s_α(λ)}T_{s_α} + (q_v − 1)(θ_{s_α(λ)} − θ_λ)/(1 − θ_{−α^∨}) for simple reflections s_α and λ ∈ X_*(T). The centre of H is O[X_*(T)]^W, and x ↦ e_{Sph(v)}x (e_{Sph(v)} = [GSp_4(O_{F_v})]) is an isomorphism O[X_*(T)]^W ≅ O[GSp_4(O_{F_v})\GSp_4(F_v)/GSp_4(O_{F_v})] agreeing with the Satake isomorphism. With the cocharacters x_0 : t ↦ diag(t,t,1,1), x_1 : t ↦ diag(1/t,1,1,t), x_2 : t ↦ diag(1,1/t,t,1), the cocharacter x_0^2x_1x_2 is t ↦ diag(t,t,t,t) and O[X_*(T)] = O[x_0, x_1, x_2, (x_0^2x_1x_2)^{−1}] = O[x_0, x_1, x_2, (x_0x_1x_2)^{−1}]; the involutions s_1, s_2, s_1s_2s_1 ∈ W send (x_0, x_1, x_2) to (x_0, x_2, x_1), (x_0x_2, x_1, x_2^{−1}), (x_0x_1, x_1^{−1}, x_2) respectively and preserve the unordered quadruple (x_0, x_0x_1, x_0x_2, x_0x_1x_2). Let e_1, …, e_4 ∈ O[X_*(T)]^W be the elementary symmetric functions of x_0, x_0x_1, x_0x_2, x_0x_1x_2 (e_0 = 1), so that (X − x_0)(X − x_0x_1)(X − x_0x_2)(X − x_0x_1x_2) = Σ_{i=0}^{4}(−1)^ie_iX^{4−i} (the paper writes Σe_iX^i; see the note). Under x ↦ e_{Sph(v)}x, Σ_{i=0}^{4}(−1)^ie_iX^{4−i} maps to q_v^{−6}Q_v(q_v^{3/2}X) = X^4 − q_v^{−3/2}T_{v,1}X^3 + (q_v^{−2}T_{v,2} + (1 + q_v^{−2})T_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^{−3/2}T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + T_{v,0}^2, with Q_v as in (2.4.8) and T_{v,i} in place of t_{v,i} (the paper prints the powers q_v^{3/2}, q_v^2, 1 + q_v^2, q_v^{3/2}; see the note). When q_v ≡ 1 (mod p), and ignoring powers of q_v^{1/2} as the paper does from §2.4.29 on, this reads modulo λ: Σ(−1)^ie_iX^{4−i} ↦ X^4 − T_{v,1}X^3 + (T_{v,2} + 2T_{v,0})X^2 − T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + T_{v,0}^2, the form used in Lemma 2.4.36.
items.locator: §2.4.29, equation (2.4.32) and the paragraphs after Corollary 2.4.35, arXiv pp. 28–30 (Haines–Kottwitz–Prasad, §§1 and 4.6)
items.note: Split out of item 15, whose statement attached these GSp_4 facts to Proposition 2.4.2, a statement about an arbitrary split group. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1 plans Hecke algebras and idempotent corners and SR.4 the Satake isomorphism; the Iwahori Bernstein presentation and the isomorphism of its centre with the spherical algebra by the idempotent are planned by no atlas layer — they are the stated content of 'Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: parahoric centers', proposed by the Kisin–Pappas 2018 extraction and not yet in the atlas. Two corrections to the printed text. (i) The paper defines e_i by (X − x_0)(X − x_0x_1)(X − x_0x_2)(X − x_0x_1x_2) = Σe_i(x_0,x_1,x_2)X^i, but Lemma 2.4.36 ('T_{v,1} − e_1(γ_0,γ_1,γ_2)') and its proof (the ideal n generated by e_1 − e_1(γ), …, e_4 − e_4(γ) and x_0^2x_1x_2 − γ_0^2γ_1γ_2) use the elementary symmetric functions: with coefficients, e_4 = 1 and T_{v,1} acts as −e_1 on e_{Sph(v)}M. (ii) The printed characteristic-zero relation between the e_i and the T_{v,i} has its powers of q_v inverted relative to the paper's own normalizations: θ_μ acts on the normalized Jacquet module through the torus character (Propositions 2.4.2–2.4.3), so e_1 evaluates to the sum of the Frobenius eigenvalues of rec_{GT,p}(π), which by (2.4.8) and the proof of Proposition 2.4.12 is q_v^{−3/2}t_{v,1}; for the trivial character all four eigenvalues are 1, so e_1 = 4 while T_{v,1} acts by 4q_v^{3/2}, contradicting the printed e_1 = q_v^{3/2}T_{v,1}. Both slips affect nothing: the relation is used only modulo λ, where q_v ≡ 1 and the paper ignores powers of q_v^{1/2}.

items.name: Remark 2.4.18: the Klingen Hecke operators as images of Iwahori–Hecke elements under e_{Kli(v)}
items.statement: Let H_{Iw(v)}[1/p] be the Iwahori Hecke algebra of GSp_4(F_v) and Z_{Kli(v)}(H_{Iw(v)}[1/p]) the subalgebra generated by U^{naive}_{Iw(v),1} + q_v(U^{naive}_{Iw(v),1})^{−1}U^{naive}_{Iw(v),2}, U^{naive}_{Iw(v),2} and U^{naive}_{Iw(v),0}. This subalgebra commutes with e_{Kli(v)} = [Kli(v)] (by Bernstein's relation), so f ↦ e_{Kli(v)}f maps it to the Klingen Hecke algebra H_{Kli(v)}[1/p], and e_{Kli(v)}(U^{naive}_{Iw(v),1} + q_v(U^{naive}_{Iw(v),1})^{−1}U^{naive}_{Iw(v),2}) = U^{naive}_{Kli(v),1}, e_{Kli(v)}U^{naive}_{Iw(v),2} = U^{naive}_{Kli(v),2}, e_{Kli(v)}U^{naive}_{Iw(v),0} = U^{naive}_{Kli(v),0}. The identities are checked after restriction to the Levi GL_2 × GL_1 of the Klingen parabolic (Vignéras 1998, Prop. II.5) using Lemma 2.4.15; with Proposition 2.4.12 they give a second proof of Proposition 2.4.17.
items.locator: Remark 2.4.18, §2.4.16, arXiv p. 24 (Haines–Kottwitz–Prasad §1.15; Vignéras 1998, Prop. II.5)
items.note: Only sketched in the paper. It is the source of the convention U_{v,2} = U_{Kli(v),2} of §2.4.23 and, after that normalization (with q_v = p at v|p), of U_{Kli(v),1} = U_{Iw(v),1} + p^{l−2}U_{Iw(v),1}^{−1}U_{Iw(v),2}; the weight-two case is the quadratic relation U_{Iw(w),1}(U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1}) = U_{w,2} of Lemma 4.5.17 on p-adic forms (item 62), behind the doubling operator Z_w = U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1} of §5. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Propositions 2.4.13 and 2.4.20: an Iwahori- or Klingen-level U-eigenvector determines the unramified principal series
items.statement: Proposition 2.4.13: let π be an irreducible admissible representation of GSp_4(F_v) such that π^{Iw(v)} contains an eigenvector for the U^{naive}_{Iw(v),i} with eigenvalues u_{v,0} = q_v^{−2}, u_{v,1} = α_v and u_{v,2} = q_v^{−1}α_vβ_v, where no ratio of a pair of [α_v, β_v, q_vβ_v^{−1}, q_vα_v^{−1}] is q_v. Then π is the (irreducible) unramified principal series with Hecke parameters [α_v, β_v, q_vβ_v^{−1}, q_vα_v^{−1}]. Proposition 2.4.20: the same conclusion holds if π^{Kli(v)} contains an eigenvector for the U^{naive}_{Kli(v),i} with eigenvalues u_{v,0} = q_v^{−2}, u_{v,1} = α_v + β_v and u_{v,2} = q_v^{−1}α_vβ_v, where no ratio of a pair of {α_v, β_v, q_vβ_v^{−1}, q_vα_v^{−1}} is q_v.
items.locator: Propositions 2.4.13 and 2.4.20, §§2.4.10 and 2.4.16, arXiv pp. 23–24
items.note: Split out of item 19: Proposition 2.4.13 is cited in the proof of Theorem 7.9.4 without Proposition 2.4.12 (with Theorem 2.7.2, Propositions 2.4.28 and 2.4.30 and Remark 2.4.31). The proofs use Propositions 2.4.3, 2.4.6 and 2.4.17 and Frobenius reciprocity. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 2.4.24: classification of ordinary p-distinguished representations of weights k ≥ l ≥ 2
items.statement: Let v|p and let π be an ordinary p-distinguished irreducible smooth Ē[GSp_4(F_v)]-representation of weights k ≥ l ≥ 2 (item 22), with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v, β_v) (or {α_v, β_v} if l = 2), and assume that k > l > 3 or l = 2. (1) If k > l > 3, or l = 2 and k > 2, then π is an irreducible principal series. (2) If k = l = 2, then, in the sense of the tables of Roberts–Schmidt, π is of type Va if {α_v, β_v} = {1, −1}, of type IIIa if α_vβ_v = 1, of type IIa if #({α_v, β_v} ∩ {1, −1}) = 1, and otherwise an irreducible unramified principal series. In all cases π is generic and the L-packet L(π) contains no other ordinary representation. Moreover: if k > l > 3, then dim e_reg π^{Iw(v)} = 1, and U_{Iw(v),i} (i = 0, 1, 2) acts on it by 1, α_v, α_vβ_v; if l = 2, then dim e_reg π^{Iw(v)} = 2, with two eigenspaces for the U_{Iw(v),i} with eigenvalues 1, α_v, α_vβ_v and 1, β_v, α_vβ_v respectively, and dim e_irreg π^{Kli(v)} = 1, with U_{Kli(v),i}-eigenvalues 1, α_v + β_v, α_vβ_v.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.24, §2.4.23, arXiv p. 26 (Roberts–Schmidt, Tables for representations of GSp(4), 2007, §1)
items.note: Split out of item 22, whose statement of the k = l = 2 case was wrong: it omitted type IIa (the case #({α_v,β_v} ∩ {1,−1}) = 1, which is not a principal series) and said 'IIIa when α_vβ_v = 1 but {α_v,β_v} ≠ {1,−1}', a vacuous qualifier since 1·(−1) = −1; checked on the page image of arXiv p. 26. In the proof, the principal series with Satake parameters [α_v, β_v, β_v^{−1}p, α_v^{−1}p] is reducible exactly when one of α_v^2, β_v^2, α_vβ_v is 1; type II arises when exactly one of α_v^2 = 1, β_v^2 = 1 holds, type V when both hold, and type III when α_vβ_v = 1 (the cases are disjoint because α_v ≠ β_v). Used on its own in the proof of Proposition 7.13.11 and through Proposition 2.4.26. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 2.4.30 and Remark 2.4.31: the local parameter at a Taylor–Wiles place (q_v ≡ 1 mod p)
items.statement: Assume q_v ≡ 1 (mod p) (so v ∤ p). Identify O[T(F_v)/T(O_{F_v})_1] with its image in H_1 through the normalized homomorphism of Proposition 2.4.2; for ᾱ_1, ᾱ_2 ∈ F̄_p^×, m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2} is the kernel of the homomorphism O[T(F_v)/T(O_{F_v})_1] → F̄_p induced by the character of T(F_v)/T(O_{F_v})_1 which is trivial on T(O_{F_v}) and on diag(ϖ_v,ϖ_v,ϖ_v,ϖ_v) and sends diag(ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1,1) ↦ ᾱ_1 and diag(ϖ_v^2,ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1) ↦ ᾱ_1ᾱ_2. Proposition 2.4.30 (as corrected; see the note): let π be an irreducible smooth Ē[GSp_4(F_v)]-module with central character |·|^2 and (π^{Iw_1(v)})_{m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2}} ≠ 0, and suppose ᾱ_1^{±1}, ᾱ_2^{±1} are pairwise distinct. Then rec_{GT,p}(π) = γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ε^2γ_2^{−1} ⊕ ε^2γ_1^{−1} for characters γ_i of G_{F_v} with γ̄_i = λ_{ᾱ_i}, the unramified character sending Frob_v to ᾱ_i, and T(k(v)) acts on (π^{Iw_1(v)})_{m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2}} via (γ_i∘Art_{F_v})|_{O_{F_v}^×}. Equivalently, rec_{GT,p}(π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) = γ'_1 ⊕ γ'_2 ⊕ ε^{−1}γ'^{−1}_2 ⊕ ε^{−1}γ'^{−1}_1 with γ'_i = γ_i·(|·|^{−3/2}∘Art_{F_v}^{−1}), which agrees with γ_i on inertia and satisfies γ̄'_i = λ_{cᾱ_i}, where c = ±1 is the image in F̄_p of the fixed q_v^{3/2}. Remark 2.4.31: with Z the centre of GSp_4, Δ_v the maximal p-power quotient of T(k(v))/Z(k(v)) and Δ'_v = ker(T(k(v)) → Δ_v), if moreover ((π^{Iw_1(v)})^{Δ'_v})_{m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2}} ≠ 0, then Δ_v acts on it via (γ_i∘Art_{F_v})|_{O_{F_v}^×}.
items.locator: §2.4.29 with Proposition 2.4.30 and Remark 2.4.31, arXiv p. 28 (published p. 184)
items.note: Split out of item 24: Proposition 2.4.28 is used without it in the proof of Proposition 7.13.11, and item 24 had dropped the standing hypothesis q_v ≡ 1 (mod p) and the conclusion on the T(k(v))-action. As printed ('rec_{GT,p}(π) = γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ε^{−1}γ_2^{−1} ⊕ ε^{−1}γ_1^{−1}', in both versions) the statement cannot hold: its right side has similitude character ε^{−1}, while ν∘rec_{GT,p}(π) = rec(ω_π) = rec(|·|^2) = ε^2 by the normalization of §2.3. Through the normalization of Proposition 2.4.2, diag(ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1,1) and diag(ϖ_v^2,ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1) act on the relevant Jacquet constituent by Frobenius eigenvalues of rec_{GT,p}(π) itself (compare the proof of Proposition 2.4.12, where the Hecke parameter α_v is q_v^{3/2} times the character value), so the exact statement is the one with ε^2 and γ̄_i = λ_{ᾱ_i}. The proof of Theorem 7.9.4 reads it through Theorem 2.7.2, i.e. for rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}), whose similitude is ε^{−1}, while stating the T(F_v)-action through the same characters; that reading holds up to the sign c, one of the powers of q_v^{1/2} the paper ignores from §2.4.29 on. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 2.5.1: uniqueness and maximality of a pure monodromy operator
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite. If (V, r) is a semisimple representation of W_K (over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 of the cardinality of C), there is at most one N for which (V, r, N) is a pure Weil–Deligne representation; if such an N exists, then (V, r, N) is the unique choice which maximizes n(r,N), the rank of N.
items.locator: Lemma 2.5.1, §2.5, arXiv p. 31 (Taylor–Yoshida, Lemma 1.4(4))
items.note: Split out of item 26: used on its own in the proof of Corollary 8.2.2, to reduce local–global compatibility at the places of R to the inequality n(ρ|_{G_{F_v}}) ≤ n(π'_v). Planned nowhere (see item 26 for the partial owners of purity).

items.name: §2.6: W_R, the parameters φ_{w,n} and φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)}, the archimedean L-packets {π^H, π^W}, and the weights of automorphic representations of GL_2 and GSp_4
items.statement: W_R = C^× ∪ C^×j with jzj^{−1} = z̄ and j^2 = −1. For w ∈ R and an integer n ≥ 0, φ_{w,n} : W_R → GL_2(C) is z ↦ |z|^w·diag((z/z̄)^{n/2}, (z/z̄)^{−n/2}) = |z|^w·diag(z^n|z|^{−n}, z^{−n}|z|^n), j ↦ [[0, 1], [(−1)^n, 0]]; its determinant is |z|^{2w} if n is odd and sgn·|z|^{2w} if n is even (sgn trivial on C^× and −1 on j); φ_{w,n} also denotes its restriction to W_C; the GL_2(R) and GL_2(C) representations with parameter φ_{w,n} are cohomological if and only if n > 0 and w ∈ Z with w + n ≡ 1 mod 2. For integers m_1 > m_2 ≥ 0 and w ∈ R, φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)} : W_R → GSp_4(C) (for the antidiagonal J) is z ↦ |z|^w·diag((z/z̄)^{(m_1+m_2)/2}, (z/z̄)^{(m_1−m_2)/2}, (z/z̄)^{−(m_1−m_2)/2}, (z/z̄)^{−(m_1+m_2)/2}) and j ↦ the antidiagonal matrix with entries, from the top row down, 1, 1, (−1)^{m_1+m_2}, (−1)^{m_1+m_2}; its similitude sends j to (−1)^{m_1+m_2}, and through the embedding of {(A,B) : det A = det B} of §2.2 its composite with GSp_4(C) → GL_4(C) is φ_{w,m_1+m_2} ⊕ φ_{w,m_1−m_2}. The L-packet of GSp_4(R) attached to φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)} is {π^H_{(w;m_1,m_2)}, π^W_{(w;m_1,m_2)}}, holomorphic and generic respectively; up to twist they are non-degenerate limits of discrete series if m_2 = 0 and discrete series if m_2 > 0; their central character is a ↦ a^w; they are tempered when w = 0; the minimal K-type of π^H_{(w;m_1,m_2)} is det^{m_2+2} ⊗ Sym^{m_1−m_2−1}C^2 of U(2). The GSp_4(C)-parameter is not in general recovered from the GL_4(C)-parameter (φ_{(0;1,0)} preserves two symplectic forms whose similitudes differ by sgn). An automorphic representation π of GL_2(A_K), K a number field, has weight 0 if π_v corresponds to φ_{0,1} for each v|∞; an automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F), F totally real, has weight (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞} if k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2, k_v ≡ l_v mod 2 (which ensures algebraicity) and π_v is in the L-packet of φ_{(2;k_v−1,l_v−2)} for each v|∞; π has parallel weight 2 if it has weight (2,2)_{v|∞}.
items.locator: §2.6 (Archimedean L-parameters), before and after Lemma 2.6.1, arXiv pp. 32–33 (following Mok, §3.1, with the opposite sign of w; Schmidt 2017)
items.note: No layer plans archimedean L-parameters, discrete series or limits of discrete series of GSp_4(R) (the Calegari–Geraghty 2020 extraction records the Harish-Chandra parametrization for GSp_4(R) as missing). AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 plans (g,K)-modules and AF.4 algebraic weights with the C- and L-algebraic normalizations, but not these parameters or the weight (k,l) convention. The weight convention is used in every later statement about GSp_4 (Theorems 1.1.7, 2.7.1, 8.4.1; Definition 2.4.25). Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 32–33.

items.name: §2.1.2: the Artin map normalization, Weil–Deligne representations WD(ρ) (GL_n- and GSp_4-valued) and the Hodge–Tate multisets HT_τ
items.statement: For K/Q_p finite: K^nr is the maximal unramified extension, I_K the inertia subgroup, Frob_K ∈ G_K/I_K the geometric Frobenius, W_K the Weil group, and Art_K : K^× → W_K^{ab} the Artin map normalized to send uniformizers to geometric Frobenius elements. ε_p is the p-adic cyclotomic character and ε̄_p its reduction mod p. For ρ a continuous representation of G_K over Q̄_l, l ≠ p, valued in some GL_n or in GSp_4, WD(ρ) is the corresponding Weil–Deligne representation; a GSp_4-valued Weil–Deligne representation is a GSp_4-valued representation of the Weil–Deligne group, considered up to GSp_4-conjugacy. For ρ a de Rham representation of G_K on a Q̄_p-vector space W, WD(ρ) is the corresponding Weil–Deligne representation of W_K, and for a continuous embedding τ : K ↪ Q̄_p, HT_τ(ρ) is the multiset containing i with multiplicity dim_{Q̄_p}(W ⊗_{τ,K} K̂̄(i))^{G_K}, so that HT_τ(ε) = {−1}. For a number field K and a finite place v: k(v) is the residue field, q_v = #k(v) and Frob_v = Frob_{K_v}; for a real place v, [c_v] is the conjugacy class of complex conjugations at v.
items.locator: §2.1.2 (Algebra), arXiv p. 17
items.note: Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 plans the absolute local Artin map with its geometric normalization (geometricArtinMap, defined from the arithmetic map by inversion); ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2 plans WD(ρ) for l ≠ p with the Frobenius semisimplification; PadicHodgeTheory R06.2–R06.3 plan D_HT and the Weil–Deligne parameter of a de Rham representation. Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter gives ε_p on field automorphisms (without continuity); the pinned Tau Ceti has no local Artin map. The GSp_4-valued Weil–Deligne representation up to GSp_4-conjugacy is the GSp_4 refinement, supplied with item 14. These conventions fix the signs in (2.4.8), Definition 2.3.1 and Theorem 2.7.1.

items.name: Definition 9.1.6: automorphic and potentially automorphic abelian varieties
items.statement: Definition 9.1.6. Let A/K be an abelian variety over a number field. A is automorphic if the compatible system 𝓡_A is automorphic in the sense of Definition 9.1.1. It is potentially automorphic if there is a finite extension of number fields L/K such that 𝓡_A|_{G_L} is automorphic. Remark 9.1.7: suppose A is automorphic and the corresponding Π has one of the forms in Remark 9.1.2. Then the Gamma factors L_v(Π,s) and the conductor N(Π) agree with those defined for 𝓡_A in §2.8, the conductor respecting the local Langlands correspondence. Hence Λ_Π(𝓡_A,s) = Λ(𝓡_A,s), the functional equations (2.8.5) and (9.1.5) agree, and Λ(𝓡_A,s) has the expected meromorphic continuation and functional equation.
items.locator: Definition 9.1.6 and Remark 9.1.7 (§9.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 251; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 456
items.note: Split from item 121, which keeps Definition 9.1.8. The two definitions are used separately: Definition 9.1.6 in Proposition 9.2.1, Theorem 9.3.1 and Theorem 1.1.3, and Definition 9.1.8 in §§8, 9.2 and 10. No layer defines automorphy of the compatible system of an abelian variety of dimension > 1.

items.name: Proposition 9.1.12: G-extensions with prescribed local behaviour over a base change, by restriction of scalars
items.statement: Proposition 9.1.12. Let G be a finite group, E/Q a finite extension and S a finite set of places of E. Let E'/E be a finite extension, and F^{(avoid)}/E a finite extension linearly disjoint from E'/E. Let S' be the set of places of E' above places of S. For each finite place v ∈ S', let H'_v/E'_v be a finite Galois extension with a fixed inclusion φ_v : Gal(H'_v/E'_v) ↪ G with image D_v. For each real place v ∈ S', let c_v ∈ G have order dividing 2. Then there exist a number field K/E and a finite Galois extension of number fields L/K such that, with K' = KE' and L' = LE': (1) Gal(L'/K') ≅ G; (2) L'/E is linearly disjoint from E'F^{(avoid)}/E; (3) all places in S' split completely in K'; (4) for all finite places w of K' above v ∈ S', the local extension L'_w/K'_w equals H'_v/E'_v, compatibly with the embeddings into G (Gal(L'_w/K'_w) → D_w ⊂ G identified with φ_v : Gal(H'_v/E'_v) → D_v ⊂ G); (5) for all real places w of K' above v ∈ S', complex conjugation c_w ∈ G is conjugate to c_v. (For E' = E this is Calegari, Even Galois representations and the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture II, Prop. 3.2; see also Moret-Bailly 1990, Thm. 1.2. In general, Calegari's Theorem 3.1 is applied to Res_{E'/E}X_G instead of an open subscheme of X_G/E. In (4), both versions print Gal(L'_w/K'_v) in the diagram, a misprint for Gal(L'_w/K'_w).)
items.note: Split from item 123 (Proposition 9.1.11): the two are used separately, Proposition 9.1.12 in Lemma 9.2.7 and Proposition 9.1.11 in Theorem 9.2.8. R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly's theorem itself; InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2 plans Hilbert irreducibility and IG.4 solvable realizations. None plans G-extensions of an arbitrary finite group with prescribed local behaviour over a split base change.

items.name: Proposition 9.2.1: abelian surfaces not of type A or B[C_2] are potentially automorphic
items.statement: Proposition 9.2.1. Let A be an abelian surface over a totally real field F which is not of type A or B[C_2]. Then A is potentially automorphic. (Types D and F: A_L has CM, so 𝓡_A is potentially abelian. Types B[C_1], C and E other than E[D_n]: 𝓡_A = 𝓡_A^1 ⊕ 𝓡_A^2, each 𝓡_A^i an irreducible, odd, weight 0 weakly compatible system of rank 2 l-adic representations of G_F, potentially automorphic by Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, Thm. 5.4.1. Type E[D_n]: 𝓡_A ≅ Ind_{G_{F'}}^{G_F}𝒮 for a quadratic F'/F and a strongly irreducible weight 0 system 𝒮 = {s_l} defined over Q, with s_l^σ ≅ s_l ⊗ δ_l for a finite order character δ. By Lemma 9.1.10(2) and Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, Prop. 5.3.2, a density one set of l have the required properties; fix such an l > 7 with Sym^2 s̄_l|_{G_{F'(ζ_l)}} irreducible, l unramified in F', and s_l, ε_l crystalline above l. Proj s_l extends to G_F → PGL_2(Q̄_l) and lifts (Patrikis, Lem. 2.3.17, 2.7.4) to r̃ : G_F → GL_2(Q̄_l), unramified almost everywhere and Hodge–Tate with weights (0,1) above l, with r̃|_{G_{F'}} = s_l ⊗ ψ for a finite order ψ. After a twist, r̃ is crystalline above l. It is odd by Calegari–Gee, Prop. 2.5, hence potentially automorphic by Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, Thm. 4.5.1, and ρ_{A,l} ≅ Ind_{G_{F'}}^{G_F}(r̃|_{G_{F'}} ⊗ ψ^{−1}).)
items.note: Split from item 124; it is used separately in Theorems 9.3.1 and 9.3.4. The potential automorphy theorems it applies are a separate item planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2, and the lifting of projective representations is a separate missing item.

items.name: Lemmas 9.2.5 and 9.2.6: good primes have density one, and the auxiliary pair p, q
items.statement: Lemma 9.2.5. Let A/F be a challenging abelian surface. Then the set of rational primes which are good primes for A has relative density one in the set of primes which split completely in F. Lemma 9.2.6. Let A/F be a challenging abelian surface. Then there are distinct rational primes p, q such that p and q are both good primes for A, and for all places v|p of F, ρ̄_{A,q}(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues. (Proof of 9.2.5, following Sawin and Calegari–Geraghty Lem. A.7. By Lemma 9.2.2 it suffices that ρ̄_{A,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for a density one set of places v. Take a place of good reduction, split over p, with Frobenius polynomial x^4 − a_1x^3 + a_2x^2 − pa_1x + p^2. A is ordinary at v iff p ∤ a_2, and then the condition holds iff p ∤ a_1^2 − 4a_2. By the Weil bounds, p | a_1^2 − 4a_2 forces a_1^2 − 4a_2 = pc with c in a finite set. A Chebotarev argument then reduces the lemma to showing that the virtual representation (V^{⊗2} − 4∧^2V) ⊗ χ^{−1} has non-constant trace on each connected component of the Sato–Tate group: USp_4 for type A, and the normalizer of SU_2 × SU_2 in USp_4 for type B[C_2]. Proof of 9.2.6: for a good prime p the crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues on T_pA at each v|p are distinct, so ρ̄_{A,q}(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues for all but finitely many q of good reduction.)
items.locator: Lemmas 9.2.5 and 9.2.6 (§9.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 255 (Sawin, Ordinary primes for abelian surfaces)
items.note: Split from item 126, which keeps Definition 9.2.3. Lemma 9.2.5 is used only for Lemma 9.2.6, which is used in Lemma 9.2.7 and Theorem 9.2.8. No layer plans Sato–Tate groups of abelian surfaces or the density of ordinary primes.

items.name: Corollary 9.3.3: meromorphic continuation and functional equation for genus two curves
items.statement: Corollary 9.3.3 (corrected). Let C/F be a genus two curve over a totally real field. The completed Hasse–Weil L-function Λ(C,s) = ∏_{i=0}^{2}Λ_i(C,s)^{(−1)^i} is defined as for abelian varieties, with Λ_1(C,s) = Λ_1(Jac(C),s). It has a meromorphic continuation to the entire complex plane and satisfies a functional equation Λ(C,s) = εN^{−s}Λ(C,2−s) with ε ∈ R and N ∈ Q_{>0}. (Proof: Theorem 9.3.1 with A = Jac(C).) Both versions of the paper print Λ(C,3−s). For a curve, the completed Hasse–Weil function relates s and 1 + dim C − s = 2 − s: this is Corollary 2.8.7's formula with dimension 1, and Conjecture 1.1.1 with m = 1. The value 3 − s belongs to Λ(Jac(C),s), which is a different function.
items.note: Split from item 129 (Theorem 9.3.1), which is used separately. This is the genus two half of Theorem 1.1.2 (item 2). The printed 3 − s is a misprint and should be recorded as a source issue: Λ_0(C,s) and Λ_2(C,s) = Λ_0(C,s−1) are exchanged by s ↦ 2 − s, and Λ_1 is symmetric under s ↦ 2 − s, so no functional equation relates Λ(C,s) and Λ(C,3−s).

items.name: Theorem 10.1.4: modularity of elliptic curves over quadratic extensions via mod 5
items.statement: Theorem 10.1.4. Let F be a totally real field in which 5 splits completely, and let K/F be a quadratic extension in which 5 is unramified. Let E/K be an elliptic curve which has good ordinary reduction or semistable ordinary reduction at all places w|5 of K. Assume that ϱ̄_{E,5} : G_K → GL_2(F_5) has the following properties: (1) the projective image of ϱ̄_{E,5} is either S_5 = PGL_2(F_5) or S_4; (2) there is a representation r̄_5 : G_F → GL_2(F_5) with determinant ε^{−1} such that r̄_5|_{G_K} ≅ ϱ̄_{E,5}. Then E is modular. In particular, there exist infinitely many modular elliptic curves over K up to twist which are not CM and do not come from any subfield of K; for example, F = Q(√d) with d ≡ 1, 4 mod 5 and K = Q(d^{1/4}), a field of mixed signature. (Proof: Lemma 7.5.26 applied to r̄_5 gives ρ̄ = Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}(ϱ̄_{E,5} ⊗ δ_{M/K}) for an auxiliary quadratic character δ_{M/K}; it is vast, tidy and 5-distinguished weight 2 ordinary by Lemma 7.5.27. As in Proposition 10.1.3, r̄_5 comes from an ordinary Hilbert modular form over F. Its base change to K, twisted by δ_{M/K} and induced back to F, gives π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, unramified and ordinary above 5, with ρ̄_{π,5} ≅ ρ̄ and ρ_{π,5} pure. Theorem 8.4.1 then makes Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}(ϱ_{E,5} ⊗ δ_{M/K}) modular, and the argument of Theorem 9.3.4 makes ϱ_{E,5} ⊗ δ_{M/K}, hence E, modular.)
items.note: Split from item 133 (Proposition 10.1.3), where it had only been paraphrased. It is a separate result, not used later.

items.name: Koecher's principle for normal formal schemes, and the codimension of the boundary of the minimal compactification
items.statement: Koecher's principle in the form used in §8.2. If 𝔛 is a normal formal scheme, 𝔜 ⊆ 𝔛 an open formal subscheme whose complement has codimension ≥ 2, and ℒ a line bundle on 𝔛, then H^0(𝔛, ℒ) = H^0(𝔜, ℒ). The boundary of the minimal compactification of the Hilbert–Siegel variety has codimension ≥ 2, by an analysis of the blow-up in the boundary charts. Since ω^2 is pulled back from the minimal compactification, the cohomology groups of §8.2 may be computed on the good reduction loci 𝒴^{mult} ⊂ 𝒳^{mult}, 𝒴^{mult,‡} ⊂ 𝒳^{mult,‡} and 𝒴^{mult,†} ⊂ 𝒳^{mult,†}, on which forgetting level structure gives finite étale maps. The forms constructed there are cuspidal because they are obtained by descent of cuspidal forms.
items.locator: §8.2, the paragraph after Lemma 8.2.3, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 240. Koecher's principle is also invoked for Hilbert modular forms in §3 (p. 72), and, as Lan's Koecher principle (Thm. 8.7), in §6 (p. 141).
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications C6 plans the Koecher extension theorem for Hilbert modular varieties only. The extractions of Pilloni's higher Hida theory paper and of Calegari–Geraghty's non-regular GSp_4 paper record Koecher's principle for Siegel threefolds as missing and route it to ShimuraCompactifications. The general Hartogs statement for normal schemes is recorded as missing by the extractions of Česnavičius, Gille–Parimala and Kisin–Pappas, which route it to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0; it should be planned once there, and imported. The other uses on pp. 72 and 141 belong to other parts of this extraction and should cite this item rather than duplicate it.

items.name: Connectedness of tubes of connected components of the special fibre
items.statement: As used in the proof of Corollary 8.2.9: 𝒴^{mult,=_{v_2}1} and 𝒴^{mult,=_{v_2}2} are the tubes (the loci of points specialising into) of the special-fibre strata Y^{I,=_{v_2}1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1} and Y^{I,=_{v_2}2}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1}. Since all these spaces are smooth, the tube of a connected component of Y^{I,=_{v_2}i}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1} (i = 1, 2) is connected. The same proof uses that 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1=d^H_2=1} → 𝒴^{mult} induces an isomorphism on π_0, because both spaces have the same rank one points and every point of higher rank has a generalization to a rank one point.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 8.2.9 (§8.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 243
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII R2 plans formal schemes, the generic-fibre functor and the comparison with the good-reduction locus, and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3 defines tubes in frames, but no layer plans the connectedness of tubes. The paper states it without reference.

items.name: Poineau's theorem on connected components of shrinking neighbourhoods
items.statement: Poineau, Un résultat de connexité pour les variétés analytiques p-adiques: privilège et noethérianité, Compos. Math. 144 (2008), Theorem 2, as used in the proof of Lemma 8.2.5. With U_ε := 𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε,d^L_2>1}_{Iw(v_1,v_2)}, after possibly shrinking ε > 0 the natural map π_0(U_0 ×_{𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1=d^H_2=1}_{Iw(v_1)}} U_0) → π_0(U_ε ×_{𝒴^{mult,‡,d^H_1≥1−ε,d^H_2≥1−ε}_{Iw(v_1)}} U_ε) is surjective (8.2.6). In words: once ε is small, every connected component of the neighbourhood cut out by the relaxed inequalities meets the space cut out by the limiting equalities.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.2.5 (§8.2), equation (8.2.6), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 241
items.note: No layer plans results on connected components of analytic domains defined by inequalities on continuous functions.

items.name: The Ekedahl–Oort stratification of the Hilbert–Siegel variety and the affineness of its strata
items.statement: Let K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(O_{F_v}), with p split completely in F. The special fibre Y_{K^{p,Iw}K_p,1} has an Ekedahl–Oort stratification into 4^{[F:Q]} strata, according to the isomorphism class at geometric points of each 𝒢_w[p], w|p: ordinary μ_p^2 × (Z/pZ)^2; p-rank one μ_p × Z/pZ × G_{1,1}; supergeneral (connected-connected but not isomorphic to G_{1,1}^2); superspecial G_{1,1}^2. Here G_{1,1} = E[p] for a supersingular elliptic curve E. The stratification refines the p-rank stratification (the last two cases are p-rank 0), and the superspecial locus (𝒢_w[p] superspecial for all w|p) is the unique zero-dimensional stratum. Theorem (Boxer; Goldring–Koskivirta): the Ekedahl–Oort stratification extends to a stratification of the minimal compactification of Y_{K^{p,Iw}K_p,1} whose open strata are affine, and the superspecial locus does not meet the boundary. Hence every irreducible component of every Ekedahl–Oort stratum contains a superspecial point in its closure.
items.locator: §8.2, the paragraph before Lemma 8.2.10 and its proof, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 244 (Viehmann–Wedhorn; Boxer 2015; Goldring–Koskivirta, Strata Hasse invariants, Invent. Math. 217 (2019))
items.note: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2 plans Ekedahl–Oort/G-zip strata with their Hasse sections and the affineness of the minimal strata of partial minimal compactifications of leaves (citing Boxer's Theorem C). It does not plan the affineness of all Ekedahl–Oort strata of the minimal compactification of a Hilbert–Siegel variety. The Hasse invariants and p-rank strata are item 54.

items.name: The Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification at Iwahori level for GSp_4 and its canonical strata
items.statement: The special fibre Y_{K^{p,Iw}K_p^{Iw},1}, K_p^{Iw} = ∏_{v|p}Iw(v), and its local model M^{loc}_{K_p^{Iw},1} = ∏_{v|p}M^{loc}_{Iw(v),1} carry Kottwitz–Rapoport stratifications, that of the product being the product stratification. The strata of M^{loc}_{Iw(v)} are indexed by the admissible set Adm(μ), of cardinality 13, partially ordered by closure. By the theory of local models, if C is an irreducible component of the stratum labelled w ∈ Adm(μ)^{S_p}, then C̄ = ⨿_{w'≤w}C̄_{w'}, and if C̄_{w'} ≠ ∅ then C̄_{w''} ≠ ∅ for all w' ≤ w'' ≤ w. The Kottwitz–Rapoport invariant determines whether H_w and L_w/H_w are étale, multiplicative or connected-connected, hence the p-rank of 𝒢_w (Ngô–Genestier). Conversely, these determine the invariant when the p-rank is non-zero (Yu's table). In Yu's notation: s_2s_1s_2τ is the stratum where 𝒢_w is ordinary and L_w = 𝒢_w[F]; s_1s_2τ is the stratum where 𝒢_w has p-rank 1, H_w is multiplicative and L_w = 𝒢_w[F]; and τ, s_1τ and s_2τ are the canonical p-rank 0 strata (L_w = 𝒢_w[F]), which lie in the closure of both. For J ⊆ S_p the locus Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1,m-can} is a Kottwitz–Rapoport stratum: 𝒢_w ordinary with L_w = 𝒢_w[F] for w ∈ J^c, and 𝒢_w of p-rank 1 with H_w multiplicative and L_w = 𝒢_w[F] for w ∈ J. The projection to hyperspecial level maps this stratum finitely onto the p-rank stratum Y^{=_{J^c}2,=_J1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p,1}. For J ⊆ I, at level K_p(I), the canonical section L_w = 𝒢_w[F] (w ∈ I) identifies Y^{I,=_{J^c}2,=_J1}_{K^{p,Iw}K_p(I),1} with the corresponding m-can stratum.
items.locator: §8.2, between Lemmas 8.2.10 and 8.2.11, and the proof of Lemma 8.2.8, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 244–246 (Ngô–Genestier, Alcôves et p-rang des variétés abéliennes; Yu, Irreducibility and p-adic monodromies on the Siegel moduli spaces)
items.note: The local model diagram at parahoric level is item 42, routed to the Hilbert–Siegel Part II. The general Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification of local models (Adm(μ) and its closure relations) is also recorded as missing by the Kisin–Zhou extraction, which routes it to a proposed Part II of GeometricSatakeAndFusion on integral local models. The general stratification should be owned there, once. Only the GSp_4 Iwahori-level identifications used here (Yu's table, the canonical strata, the m-can strata at level K_p(I)) belong with the Hilbert–Siegel Part II.

items.name: The rank of the monodromy of rec_GT(π_v) and parahoric fixed vectors
items.statement: For an irreducible admissible representation π_v of GSp_4(F_v), v a finite place, let n(π_v) be the rank of the monodromy operator of rec_{GT}(π_v) (§2.3). An examination of Roberts–Schmidt, Local newforms for GSp(4), Table A.15 (whose column 'a' records n(π_v)) gives: n(π_v) ≥ 1 iff π_v^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} = 0; n(π_v) ≥ 2 iff π_v^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} = π_v^{Par(v)} = 0; n(π_v) = 3 iff π_v^{Kli(v)} = π_v^{Si(v)} = 0. Together with the semicontinuity of the rank of the nilpotent operator N in p-adic families (applied through Theorem 7.9.4 to regular-weight forms π'' with (π''_v)^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} ≠ 0) and Lemma 2.5.1, this gives the agreement of monodromy at the places v ∈ R in Corollary 8.2.2.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 8.2.2 (§8.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 238
items.note: Items 15–26 cover the Iwahori–Hecke algebra, ordinary representations and purity, but not the relation between the monodromy rank and the fixed vectors of the paramodular, Klingen and Siegel parahorics.

items.name: Cyclic base change, descent and automorphic induction for GL_n (Arthur–Clozel)
items.statement: Arthur–Clozel, Simple algebras, base change, and the advanced theory of the trace formula, Ch. 3, Thms. 4.2 and 5.1, as used. (a) Let F'/F be a cyclic extension of number fields of prime degree and Π' a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_{F'}) invariant under Gal(F'/F). Then there is an automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_F) with BC_{F'/F}(Π) = Π'; with the notation of §1, BC_{F'/F}(Π)_w = BC_{F'_w/F_v}(Π_v) at every place. This is used in Lemma 8.3.2 with n = 4. (b) Let K'/F' be a quadratic extension with character κ and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_4(A_{F'}) with Π ⊗ (κ∘Art_{F'}∘det) ≅ Π. Then Π is the automorphic induction of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_{K'}). This is used in Theorem 9.3.4. Both are iterated along solvable extensions.
items.locator: §1 (notation for base change along solvable extensions, p. 19) and the proofs of Lemma 8.3.2 and Theorem 9.3.4, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 19, 247 and 259–260
items.note: ML.5 registers cyclic base change and automorphic induction with exact hypotheses. The extractions of Newton–Thorne and of Boxer–Calegari–Gee record the same theorem as planned there.

items.name: Holomorphy and non-vanishing at s = 1 of twisted exterior square L-functions (Shahidi)
items.statement: Shahidi, On non-vanishing of twisted symmetric and exterior square L-functions for GL(n) (Pacific J. Math. 1997), as used in Lemma 8.3.2. Let F'/F be cyclic of prime degree and Π' = BC_{F'/F}(Π) cuspidal on GL_4(A_{F'}), with Π on GL_4(A_F). Then L^S(s, Π', ∧^2 ⊗ |·|^{−2}) = ∏_ψ L^S(s, Π, ∧^2 ⊗ |·|^{−2}ψ^{−1}), the product running over the characters ψ of A_F^×/F^×N_{F'/F}A_{F'}^×. By Shahidi's theorem, all but at most one factor on the right is holomorphic and non-vanishing at s = 1. The left side has a simple pole at s = 1 because Π' is the transfer of a representation of GSp_4 with central character |·|^2. Hence some L^S(s, Π, ∧^2 ⊗ |·|^{−2}ψ^{−1}) has a pole at s = 1, so Π is of symplectic type with multiplier |·|^2ψ.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.3.2 (§8.3), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 247
items.note: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors plans Tate, Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg factors (AL.1–AL.3) and unramified L-group factors without continuation (AL.4). No layer plans the Langlands–Shahidi exterior square L-function or the characterisation of symplectic type by its pole.

items.name: Solvable base change for GSp_4 with Iwahori-fixed vectors (Mok, Prop. 4.13)
items.statement: As used in Theorem 8.4.1 and in the proof of Corollary 7.9.6, from Mok, Galois representations attached to automorphic forms on GL_2 over CM fields, Compos. Math. 150 (2014), Prop. 4.13. Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 (in Theorem 8.4.1, as in its hypothesis (4)). For a suitable solvable extension of totally real fields F'/F, chosen with the local properties required there, there is an automorphic representation π' of GSp_4(A_{F'}) of parallel weight 2 which is a base change of π, in the sense that rec_{GT,p}(π'_w) = rec_{GT,p}(π_v)|_{W_{F'_w}} for each finite place w of F' above a place v of F. F' can be chosen so that moreover (π'_w)^{Iw(w)} ≠ 0 for all finite places w of F' (and π' is holomorphic at the infinite places, as required in Corollary 7.9.6).
items.locator: Proofs of Corollary 7.9.6 (§7.9) and Theorem 8.4.1 (§8.4), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 221 and 248
items.note: No layer plans base change for GSp_4. ML.5 registers cyclic base change for GL_n, and Theorem 2.9.3 (item 32) is the passage between GSp_4 and GL_4. The use in the proof of Corollary 7.9.6 belongs to another part of this extraction and should cite this item.

items.name: Auxiliary solvable totally real extensions with prescribed local behaviour
items.statement: As used in Theorem 8.4.1, and for the quadratic extensions in Theorem 8.5.2 and Lemma 9.2.7. Let F be a totally real field, F^{avoid}/F a finite extension, p a prime, and finitely many finite places of F with prescribed local requirements, such as ρ̄|_{G_{F'_w}} trivial, ρ|_{G_{F'_w}} unipotently ramified and q_w ≡ 1 mod p^2. Then there is a solvable Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F, linearly disjoint from F^{avoid} over F, in which p splits completely and the requirements hold at every place above the given ones.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 8.4.1, Theorem 8.5.2 and Lemma 9.2.7, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 248–249, 257
items.note: The paper uses this without proof. GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4 plans the local consequences of base change, not the choice of the fields. The Allen et al. extraction treats the corresponding field-extension step in its item on twisting to determinant ε_l^{−1}, and notes that another extraction routes the field-extension existence to R23.1.

items.name: Square roots of finite order characters and globalisation of quadratic characters
items.statement: As used in Theorem 8.5.2 and Lemma 9.2.7. (i) The obstruction to a square root of a finite order character χ of G_F is a class in the 2-torsion of the Brauer group of F. It is trivial at the places where χ is unramified and, for χ totally even, at the infinite places. So after a quadratic extension of totally real fields, in which p splits completely and which is linearly disjoint from a given field and of local degree 2 at the finitely many places where the class is non-zero, χ has a finite order square root. (ii) (Artin–Tate, Class field theory, Ch. X, Thm. 5.) Such a square root can be twisted by a quadratic character so as to be trivial at a prescribed finite set of places; this is used for ε̄ det r̄_q at the places dividing pq𝔯 in Lemma 9.2.7.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 8.5.2 and Lemma 9.2.7, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 249, 257
items.note: Tau Ceti's class field theory roadmap plans the Brauer sequence (Layer 10) and global existence (Layer 12), and states that the Grunwald–Wang theorem is outside it. The extractions of Allen et al. (twisting to determinant ε_l^{−1}) and of Boxer–Calegari–Gee et al. 2025 (Lemma 5.3.1 and Remark 5.3.2) record the same square-root and Grunwald–Wang arguments as missing and route them as a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality (R02.2, R02.4).

items.name: Twisted moduli spaces of principally polarized abelian surfaces with fixed torsion
items.statement: Let F' be a number field, and fix a prime, or a pair of distinct primes, together with symplectic Galois modules with inverse cyclotomic multiplier. The construction is the moduli space of principally polarized abelian surfaces with symplectic isomorphisms of their torsion onto the given modules. In Theorem 9.2.8, Y/F' parametrizes triples (B, ı_p, ı_q) with ı_p : B[p] ≅ A[p]|_{G_{F'}} and ı_q : B[q] ≅ ρ̄_q^∨ symplectic. In §10.2, B(ρ̄) parametrizes pairs (A, ı_3 : A[3] ≅ V(ρ̄)^∨). These spaces are smooth and geometrically connected, and over C (or Q̄) they are identified with the moduli space of principally polarized abelian surfaces with full level pq (resp. 3) structure. In Theorem 9.2.8, for each place v | pq∞ of F', the open set Ω_v = Y^{ord}(F'_v) (points with good ordinary reduction when v is finite) is non-empty: at v|∞ because det r̄_q^∨ = ε, at v|p because A itself gives a point (Lemma 9.2.7(5)), and at v|q through the canonical lift of A mod v.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.2.8 (§9.2) and §10.2, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 257, 268
items.note: PELModuli M5 plans Siegel moduli in every dimension and M6 the arithmetic moduli at every rigidifying level. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H6 plans the analogous twisted torsion moduli for Hilbert–Blumenthal varieties with their local points. The twisted Siegel version, with its geometric connectedness and local points, is not planned.

items.name: Potential automorphy of rank two compatible systems over totally real fields (Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor)
items.statement: Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, Potential automorphy and change of weight, as applied in Proposition 9.2.1 and Theorem 9.3.1. (a) Thm. 5.4.1: if 𝓡^1, 𝓡^2 are irreducible, odd, weight 0 weakly compatible systems of rank 2 l-adic representations of G_F, F totally real, there is a finite Galois extension of totally real fields F'/F such that 𝓡^1|_{G_{F'}} and 𝓡^2|_{G_{F'}} are automorphic and irreducible. (b) Prop. 5.3.2, applied to Sym^2 𝒮, which is irreducible by Lemma 9.1.10(2): for a strongly irreducible rank 2 weight 0 system 𝒮 over F', Sym^2 s̄_l|_{G_{F'(ζ_l)}} is irreducible for a density one set of primes l. (c) Thm. 4.5.1, applied to an odd r̃ : G_F → GL_2(Q̄_l): take r̃ crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights (0,1) at all places above l, where l > 7 is unramified in F and Sym^2 of the reduction of r̃ stays irreducible over F(ζ_l). Then r̃ is potentially automorphic. These are the applications made in the paper, not the full hypotheses of the cited results.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 9.2.1 and Theorem 9.3.1, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 254 and 258
items.note: ML.2 is the potential automorphy assembly with its regularity, polarization, residual-image, local and field-extension hypotheses. The extraction of Newton–Thorne records the potential automorphy theorem of Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor as planned there. The totally real rank two applications (a) and (c) must be among ML.2's exported statements. (b) is a residual-image statement for compatible systems of the same kind as Lemma 9.1.10(3) (Allen et al., Lemma 7.1.3). If ML.2's decomposition does not export it, it must be recorded as missing with that lemma's owner.

items.name: Lifting projective Galois representations with Hodge–Tate conditions (Tate, Patrikis)
items.statement: As used in Proposition 9.2.1, by Patrikis, Variations on a theorem of Tate, Lem. 2.3.17 and 2.7.4. Let F'/F be a quadratic extension of totally real fields and s_l : G_{F'} → GL_2(Q̄_l) a representation that is Hodge–Tate with weights (0,1) at the places above l. Suppose Proj s_l extends to a continuous projective representation G_F → PGL_2(Q̄_l). Then this extension lifts to a continuous r̃ : G_F → GL_2(Q̄_l) which is unramified at all but finitely many places and Hodge–Tate with weights (0,1) at all places dividing l, and r̃|_{G_{F'}} = s_l ⊗ ψ for a character ψ, of finite order since it is Hodge–Tate of weight 0. The underlying input is Tate's theorem H^2(G_F, Q/Z) = 0.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 9.2.1 (§9.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 254
items.note: Tau Ceti has projective representations and the Schur-multiplier obstruction for abstract groups, without topology (TauCeti.IsProjectiveRep.cohomologyClass_eq_zero_iff). No layer plans Tate's vanishing of H^2(G_F, Q/Z) or lifts with Hodge–Tate conditions.

items.name: Automorphic induction from GL_2 over a quadratic extension to GSp_4 (Roberts' theta lift)
items.statement: Roberts, Global L-packets for GSp(2) and theta lifts, Doc. Math. 6 (2001), Thm. 8.6, as used in Theorem 9.2.8. Let F_1F''/F'' be a quadratic extension of totally real fields and 𝛑 a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_{F_1F''}) of weight 0 and trivial central character (with ρ̄_{𝛑,q} ≅ r̄_q|_{G_{F_1F''}} as in Lemma 9.2.7). Then there is an automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_{F''}) of parallel weight 2 and trivial central character whose transfer to GL_4(A_{F''}) is the automorphic induction of 𝛑 ⊗ |·|. In particular ρ_{π,q} ≅ Ind_{G_{F_1F''}}^{G_{F''}} ρ_{𝛑,q}, and π is ordinary by construction when 𝛑 is q-ordinary.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.2.8 (§9.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 257–258
items.note: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 and MP.5 plan theta kernels and lifts for the dual pairs of their sources, not the GSO(4)–GSp_4 lift with its L-packets. Proposition 10.1.3 and Theorem 10.1.4 speak of 'the automorphic induction' of a Hilbert modular form from E to F without a reference. Presumably the same construction is meant, and this item should serve there too once that is checked.

items.name: Purity of Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms of parallel weight 2 (Blasius, Caraiani)
items.statement: For a totally real field L and a cuspidal automorphic representation 𝛑 of GL_2(A_L) of weight 0 (parallel weight 2), ρ_{𝛑,q}|_{G_{L_v}} is pure for every finite place v of L: away from q by Blasius (Hilbert modular forms and the Ramanujan conjecture), and at the places above q by Caraiani (Monodromy and local-global compatibility for l = p). It is used for the purity of ρ_{π,p} in Theorem 9.2.8, where ρ_{π,q} ≅ Ind ρ_{𝛑,q}, and in Proposition 10.1.3 and Theorem 10.1.4.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 9.2.8, Proposition 10.1.3 and Theorem 10.1.4, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 258, 266, 267
items.note: R19.2 constructs the representations of the cohomological Hilbert forms, including the parity cases. R19.3 proves purity through the weight theorem, R19.4 the Weil–Deligne compatibility with monodromy away from the coefficient prime, and R19.5 the comparison at the coefficient prime. In the uses here 𝛑 is unramified above p and q, so R19.5's crystalline comparison suffices at those places. The paper itself cites Blasius and Caraiani.

items.name: The Rankin–Selberg transfer GL_2 × GL_2 → GL_4 and the exterior square transfer GL_4 → GL_6
items.statement: As used in Theorem 9.3.1. (a) Ramakrishnan, Modularity of the Rankin–Selberg L-series, and multiplicity one for SL(2), Thm. M: for cuspidal automorphic representations π_1, π_2 of GL_2(A_K) there is an automorphic representation π_1 ⊠ π_2 of GL_4(A_K) with the tensor product parameters, so 𝓡^1 ⊗ 𝓡^2 is automorphic when 𝓡^1, 𝓡^2 are. (b) Kim, Functoriality for the exterior square of GL_4, with Henniart's refinement (Sur la fonctorialité, pour GL(4), donnée par le carré extérieur): for a cuspidal Π of GL_4(A_K) there is an automorphic representation ∧^2Π of GL_6(A_K) whose local components correspond to ∧^2 of the local parameters at every place. With Theorem 2.9.3 this makes ∧^2ρ_{A,p}|_{G_{F''}} automorphic.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.3.1 and Remark 9.3.2 (§9.3), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 258–259
items.note: ML.5 registers cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor and symmetric-power transfers with exact hypotheses; the Rankin–Selberg transfer is a tensor transfer. The extraction of Clozel–Thorne records Kim's and Ramakrishnan's transfers as planned there. The exterior square transfer, with Henniart's refinement at every place, must be named among ML.5's selected transfers when the layer is decomposed.

items.name: Serre's open image theorem for abelian surfaces with End = Z
items.statement: Serre (Lettre à Marie-France Vignéras du 10/02/1987, Collected Papers IV): if A is an abelian surface over a number field F with End_C(A) = Z, then ρ̄_{A,l}(G_F) = GSp_4(F_l) for all sufficiently large primes l. Used in Lemma 9.2.2, with Lemma 7.5.15, to show that ρ̄_{A,l} is vast and tidy for a density one set of l.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 9.2.2 (§9.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 254
items.note: No layer plans open image theorems for abelian surfaces, and FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.6 explicitly avoids Serre's theorem. The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty's non-regular GSp_4 paper records the same statement for A/Q and routes it to a proposed Part II of FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems on ℓ-adic and residual images of abelian varieties.

items.name: Continuation and functional equation of standard L-functions of GL_n (Godement–Jacquet)
items.statement: Godement–Jacquet, Zeta functions of simple algebras, Cor. 13.8, as used for (9.1.5). Let 𝓡 and Π be as in Definition 9.1.1, with Gamma factors L_v(Π,s) at v|∞. The completed L-function Λ_Π(𝓡,s) = L(𝓡,s)∏_{v|∞}L_v(Π,s), which is the standard L-function of the isobaric sum Π, admits a meromorphic continuation to C and satisfies Λ_Π(𝓡,s) = ε(Π)N(Π)^{−s}Λ_Π(𝓡^∨,1−s). With Remark 9.1.7 this gives the functional equation of Λ(𝓡_A,s) for automorphic A, and through Brauer induction the meromorphic continuation in Theorem 9.3.1.
items.note: AL.2 builds the Godement–Jacquet local factors and the adelic global integral for cuspidal GL_n representations, with Euler factorization, analytic continuation and functional equation. An isobaric sum is handled factor by factor.

items.name: Ordinary parallel weight 2 lifts of modular mod p representations of totally real fields (Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty)
items.statement: Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty, Congruences between Hilbert modular forms: constructing ordinary lifts, II (Math. Res. Lett. 20 (2013)), Thm. A, as used in Proposition 10.1.3, Theorem 10.1.4 and Theorem 10.2.6. Let E be a totally real field, p ∈ {3, 5} unramified in E, and ϱ̄ : G_E → GL_2(F̄_p) modular with determinant ε^{−1}. Suppose ϱ̄|_{G_{E(ζ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible (for p = 5 the determinant condition and the unramifiedness of E at 5 ensure that the projective image is not A_5), and ϱ̄ restricted to inertia at each w|p is an extension of ε^{−1} by 1. Then ϱ̄ arises from an ordinary Hilbert modular form of parallel weight 2 and trivial nebentypus.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 10.1.3 (§10.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 266
items.note: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting plans ordinary Hida theory and ordinary R = T (R21.1–R21.6), not the construction of ordinary lifts of a given modular residual representation.

items.name: Modularity of residual representations with solvable projective image over a totally real field (Tate, Langlands–Tunnell)
items.statement: As used in Proposition 10.1.3(1)–(2), and hence in Theorem 10.2.6, where ϱ̄ = ρ̄_{E,3} is surjective onto GL_2(F_3). Let E be a totally real field and ϱ̄ : G_E → GL_2(F̄_p) totally odd with solvable projective image; by the classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(k) the projective image is A_4, S_4 or dihedral, hence a subgroup of PGL_2(C). By a theorem of Tate (Serre, Modular forms of weight one and Galois representations, Thm. 4), ϱ̄ has a totally odd characteristic zero lift with finite solvable image. That lift is automorphic by the theorems of Langlands and Tunnell, so ϱ̄ is modular, as in §5 of Wiles.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 10.1.3 (§10.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 266
items.note: GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.5 plans automorphic induction and the solvable two-dimensional Artin modularity theorem with the projective and linear lifting steps, but states its weight-one interpretation over Q. The paper needs the conclusion over a totally real field.

items.name: Modularity of the non-solvable residual representations in Proposition 10.1.3
items.statement: As used in Proposition 10.1.3 and Theorem 10.1.4, for E totally real. (a) p = 3: the vast non-solvable ϱ̄ induced to GSp_4(F_3) come, by Lemma 7.5.21(4), from ϱ̄_3 : G_E → GL_2(F_9) with projective image A_5. These are modular by the odd Artin conjecture for totally real fields (Pilloni–Stroh, Surconvergence, ramification et modularité, Thm. 0.3), or alternatively by adapting Ellenberg's arguments. (b) p = 5: let ϱ̄ : G_E → GL_2(F_5) be surjective with determinant ε^{−1}, with 5 unramified in E (so [E(ζ_5):E] = 4). It has characteristic zero lifts of the required form by the method of Khare–Wintenberger (Snowden, Thm. 7.2.1), and such a lift is modular once ϱ̄ is (Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, and modularity). ϱ̄ itself is modular by realizing it as the 5-torsion of a modular elliptic curve over a solvable extension (Shepherd-Barron–Taylor; Taylor; Pilloni–Stroh, Prop. 2.1.3).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 10.1.3 (§10.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 266
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.1 organizes weight-one modularity in the proved cases, and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3 the Khare–Wintenberger lifts over Q; neither plans these statements over totally real fields. These inputs are needed only for Proposition 10.1.3(1)–(2) beyond the solvable case and for Theorem 10.1.4, not for Theorem 1.1.5.

items.name: Hilbert irreducibility with local conditions on a rational variety
items.statement: Serre, Lectures on the Mordell–Weil theorem, §§9.2 and 9.6, as used in the proof of Theorem 10.2.1. Consider the Galois cover R(ρ̄) = P(ρ̄) ×_{𝒜_2} 𝒜_2(5) → P(ρ̄), with group PSp_4(F_5), over the F-rational variety P(ρ̄). There are infinitely many x ∈ P(ρ̄)(F) such that the Galois group of the splitting field of any preimage y ∈ R(ρ̄) of x contains PSp_4(F_5). Moreover, x may be restricted to any non-trivial open subset of P(ρ̄)(F_v) for v in a finite set S of places.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 10.2.1 (§10.2), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 271
items.note: IG.2 plans Hilbert irreducibility over number fields and the specialization of regular Galois covers with full Galois group, with avoidance and linear-disjointness variants. The compatibility with v-adic open conditions (Hilbert sets of a rational variety are v-adically dense) must be included in it.

items.name: Theorem 2.7.2: ordinary Galois representations attached to ordinary cuspidal automorphic representations of GSp_4
items.statement: Theorem 2.7.2. Let F be a totally real field and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) of weight (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞}, where k_v ≥ l_v > 2 and k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2) for all v|∞, with central character |·|^2. Fix a prime p. Assume that π_v is unramified at all places v|p and that π is ordinary, with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v, β_v)_{v|p} (§2.4.23). Then there is a continuous semisimple representation ρ_{π,p} : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) such that: (1) ν ∘ ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1}; (2) for each finite place v ∤ p, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})^{ss}, and if furthermore ρ_{π,p} is irreducible then WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}); (3) for v|p, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is isomorphic to an upper triangular representation whose diagonal characters, in order, are λ_{α_v}ε^{(k_v+l_v)/2−2}, λ_{β_v}ε^{(k_v−l_v)/2}, λ_{β_v}^{−1}ε^{−1−(k_v−l_v)/2} and λ_{α_v}^{−1}ε^{1−(k_v+l_v)/2}, where λ_x is the unramified character taking Frob_v (geometric Frobenius) to x; (4) if ρ_{π,p} is irreducible, then ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is pure for each finite place v of F.
items.locator: Theorem 2.7.2 (§2.7), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 34; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 192
items.note: The proof deduces this from Theorem 2.7.1: part (3) is a standard consequence of p-adic Hodge theory, immediate from Geraghty 2019, Lem. 2.32, together with Proposition 2.4.6. The diagonal pairs (1,4) and (2,3) multiply to ε^{−1}, consistently with (1). Split from item 28 because it is cited on its own (arXiv pp. 219, 223, 233, 235 and 238; p. 247 invokes its proof). The convention for λ_x is stated on arXiv p. 28, and Frob_v is a geometric Frobenius by the conventions of §2.1. No layer plans Galois representations for GSp_4.

items.name: Weight (k_v, l_v) of an automorphic representation of GSp_4, and weight 0 for GL_2
items.statement: If K is a number field and 𝛑 an automorphic representation of GL_2(A_K), then 𝛑 has weight 0 if for each place v|∞ of K, 𝛑_v corresponds to the L-parameter φ_{0,1}. If F is a totally real field and π an automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F), then π has weight (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞} if for each place v|∞ of F, k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2, k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2), and π_v lies in the L-packet corresponding to φ_{(2; k_v−1, l_v−2)}. The congruence k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2) is imposed so that π is algebraic. π has parallel weight 2 if it has weight (2,2)_{v|∞}.
items.locator: §2.6, the definitions following Lemma 2.6.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 33; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 191
items.note: Theorems 2.7.1–2.7.3 and Definition 9.1.8 are stated in terms of these weights, and Lemma 2.9.1 uses the same parameters φ_{(2;k_v−1,l_v−2)} through their infinitesimal characters. Item 27 (Lemma 2.6.1) does not contain them. They rest on the archimedean parameters φ_{w,n} : W_R → GL_2(C) and φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)} : W_R → GSp_4(C), m_1 > m_2 ≥ 0, of §2.6, and on the archimedean L-packets {π^H_{(w;m_1,m_2)}, π^W_{(w;m_1,m_2)}} of GSp_4(R); weight (2,2) gives φ_{(2;1,0)}, whose packet consists (up to twist) of non-degenerate limits of discrete series. The paper remarks just before these definitions that the GSp_4(C)-parameter cannot in general be recovered from the GL_4(C)-parameter; φ_{(0;1,0)} is an example. No layer plans archimedean L-packets of GSp_4.

items.name: L-function, Gamma factors and conductor of a strictly compatible system, and the conjectural functional equation (2.8.4)–(2.8.5)
items.statement: For a strictly compatible system 𝓡 of G_F (F a number field), L(𝓡, s) := ∏_{v∤∞} L(WD_v(𝓡), s). If 𝓡 comes from an abelian variety, or more generally arises in a geometric setting where the Hodge structure is apparent ([Ser70]), there are Gamma factors L_v(𝓡, s) for v|∞, and Λ(𝓡, s) := L(𝓡, s) ∏_{v|∞} L_v(𝓡, s) (2.8.4). If 𝓡 arises from an abelian surface over a totally real field F, then L_v(𝓡, s) = Γ_C(s)^2 for all v|∞, where Γ_C(s) = (2π)^{−s}Γ(s). The conductor N(𝓡) is a product of local factors that depend only on the WD_v(𝓡). Conjecturally, for a strictly compatible system, Λ(𝓡, s) has a meromorphic continuation to the entire complex plane and satisfies Λ(𝓡, s) = ε(𝓡) N(𝓡)^{−s} Λ(𝓡^∨, 1 − s) for some factor ε(𝓡) (2.8.5).
items.locator: §2.8, (2.8.4) and (2.8.5) with the definitions around them, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 37; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 195–196
items.note: PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1 plans 'completed motivic L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data in admitted cases', with their archimedean factors, and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3 plans Artin and Swan conductors of l-adic representations, including the monodromy term; these supply L(𝓡, s), the Gamma factors and the conductor. No layer formulates the conjectural functional equation (2.8.5) as a predicate, so the item as a whole is missing. It is needed as one: Theorem 9.3.1 proves it for H^i of abelian surfaces, using ε(𝓡)ε(𝓡^∨) = N(𝓡) (Tate 1979, (3.4.7)), and (2.8.4)–(2.8.5) are cited on arXiv pp. 250, 251 and 258. The paper notes that ε(𝓡) cannot obviously be read off from the compatible system.

items.name: The completed Hasse–Weil zeta function Λ(A,s) of an abelian variety and its local factors
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field F. By Proposition 2.8.1, Λ_i(A, s) := Λ(H^i(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l), s) is well defined, and the completed Hasse–Weil zeta function of A is Λ(A, s) := ∏_{i=0}^{2 dim A} Λ_i(A, s)^{(−1)^i}. If v is a finite place of F at which A has good reduction, with reduction Ā, then the local factor L_v(A, s) := ∏_{i=0}^{2 dim A} L(WD(H^i(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l)), s)^{(−1)^i} (printed with exponent (−1)^s) equals exp(Σ_{m≥1} #Ā(k(v)_m)/m · #k(v)^{−ms}), where k(v) is the residue field of F_v and k(v)_m/k(v) its extension of degree m. For a curve C/F, Λ_i(C, s) and Λ(C, s) are defined in the same way, and Λ_1(C, s) = Λ_1(Jac(C), s) (§9.3).
items.locator: §2.8, the definitions of Λ_i(A,s), Λ(A,s) and L_v(A,s) before Conjecture 2.8.6, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 37 (and p. 259 for curves); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 196
items.note: Conjecture 2.8.6, Corollary 2.8.7, Theorem 9.3.1 and Corollary 9.3.3 are stated in terms of these functions. Item 1 defines the zeta function ζ_X by closed points, not these completed L-functions. The identity for the local factor is the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula Z(Ā, T) = ∏_i det(1 − Frob T | H^i)^{(−1)^{i+1}} with T = #k(v)^{−s}, transported by smooth proper base change. WeilConjectures:WC.1 plans the zeta function and determinant formula over a finite field, and WC.6 explicitly makes no assertion about global Hasse–Weil L-functions over number fields. No layer defines Λ(A, s). The printed exponent (−1)^s is a misprint for (−1)^i, in both versions; with (−1)^i the identity holds as stated.

items.name: Discrete automorphic representations of GSp_4, symplectic type, general type and transfer (§2.9)
items.statement: Let F be a totally real field. An automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) is discrete if it occurs in the discrete spectrum of the L^2 automorphic forms with fixed central character ω = ω_π; every cuspidal automorphic representation is discrete. Arthur's classification divides the discrete spectrum into six families. A cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_4(A_F) is of symplectic type with multiplier χ if the partial L-function L^S(s, Π, ∧^2 ⊗ χ^{−1}) has a pole at s = 1, S being any finite set of places of F; this implies Π ≅ Π^∨ ⊗ χ. A discrete automorphic representation π of GSp_4(A_F) is of general type (in the sense of Arthur) if there is a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_4(A_F) of symplectic type with multiplier ω_π such that, for each place v of F, the L-parameter obtained from rec_{GT}(π_v) by composing with the usual embedding GSp_4 ↪ GL_4 is rec(Π_v). Π is then called the transfer of π.
items.locator: §2.9, the definitions preceding Lemma 2.9.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 38; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 197 (Arthur, Art04; Gee–Taïbi)
items.note: Used throughout the paper: in the proof of Theorem 2.7.1(4), in Theorem 2.9.3 and Lemma 2.9.1, in §3.10 and §7.13 (only representations of general type contribute after localizing at a non-Eisenstein ideal), and in §9.1, where Remark 9.1.9 uses it to relate 'modular' and 'automorphic' abelian surfaces. Gee–Taïbi establish the compatibility of Arthur's classification with rec_GT. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 plans Arthur's classification for classical groups only as a register of proof sources; nothing plans the GSp_4 notions.

items.name: Lemma 2.9.1 and Remark 2.9.2: discrete representations not of general type have reducible Galois representations
items.statement: Lemma 2.9.1. Let F be totally real and π a discrete automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) such that, at each place v|∞, π_v has the same infinitesimal character as the representations in the L-packet corresponding to φ_{(2; k_v−1, l_v−2)}, with k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2) and k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2. Suppose that π is not of general type. Then there is a compatible system of reducible Galois representations ρ_{π,p} : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) such that, for all but finitely many places v of F, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})^{ss}. Remark 2.9.2. If π is of general type but otherwise satisfies the conditions of Lemma 2.9.1, the Galois representations constructed by Mok (see Theorem 2.7.1) form a compatible system which, unlike the one in Lemma 2.9.1, is expected always to be irreducible.
items.locator: Lemma 2.9.1 and Remark 2.9.2 (§2.9), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 38–39; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 197–198
items.note: Proof, following Calegari–Geraghty 2020, Thm. 7.11: π lies in one of Arthur's classes (b)–(f). In classes (e) and (f) its Hecke parameters are those of a sum of four algebraic idèle class characters. In class (d) they are those of λ|·|^{1/2} ⊞ λ|·|^{−1/2} ⊞ μ, with μ regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2 and ω_μ = λ^2 = ω_π. In class (b) they are those of μ_1 ⊞ μ_2, with μ_1 ≠ μ_2 cuspidal of central character ω_π (printed 'central character μ_π', a misprint present in both versions), which correspond to holomorphic Hilbert modular forms of paritious weight. In class (c) they are those of μ|·|^{1/2} ⊞ μ|·|^{−1/2}, with μ of orthogonal type, induced from a quadratic extension. The lemma is cited on its own on arXiv pp. 71, 221, 234 and 258–259.

items.name: Definition 2.10.1 and Lemma 2.10.2: the defect and balanced modules
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian local ring with residue field k and M a finitely generated S-module. The defect of M is d_S(M) := dim_k M/m_S M − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, k), and M is balanced if d_S(M) ≥ 0 (Definition 2.10.1). Lemma 2.10.2: if M is balanced, then there is a presentation S^d → S^d → M → 0 with d = dim_k M/m_S M. Conversely, if M admits a presentation S^r → S^r → M → 0 for some r ≥ 0, then M is balanced.
items.locator: Definition 2.10.1 and Lemma 2.10.2 (§2.10), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 39–40; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 199 (after Calegari–Geraghty 2018, §2.1)
items.note: The R03.5 decomposition node 'Balanced modules and Taylor–Wiles patching of modules' states the defect, the definition of balanced and the presentation S^d → S^d → M → 0 with d = dim_k M/m_S M. The converse direction should be added there. It follows from the exact sequence 0 → Tor_1^S(M,k) → K/m_SK → k^r → M/m_SM → 0, K being the image of S^r → S^r, which gives d_S(M) = r − dim_k K/m_SK ≥ 0. The forward direction uses a minimal free resolution. Mathlib has Tor as a derived functor on a monoidal abelian category (CategoryTheory.Tor), but no defect and no minimal resolutions. Split from item 150: Lemma 2.10.2 is cited on its own on arXiv pp. 216 and 226, separately from Proposition 7.10.1.

items.name: The groups Δ, Δ(Π_0), Δ(K^p), the quotient Y_K^{G_1} = Δ\Y_K, and Proposition 3.3.17
items.statement: With the notation of the unit action on Y_K, put Δ := (O_F)_(p)^{×,+}/O_F^{×,+}(K^p) (3.3.14), Δ(Π_0) := O_F^{×,+}(Π_0)/O_F^{×,+}(K^p) (3.3.15) and Δ(K^p) := O_F^{×,+}(ν(K^p))/O_F^{×,+}(K^p) (3.3.16); the last two are finite groups. Y_K^{G_1} := Δ\Y_K exists as a scheme, for the following reasons. Δ permutes the connected components of Y_K; the stabilizer of a connected component is the finite group Δ(Π_0), and that of a geometrically connected component is Δ(K^p). The action of Δ lifts to an ample line bundle on Y_K: for instance the tensor product of the line bundles det(Ω^1_{(A/C)/Y_K}) over the subgroups C = ∏_{v|p}C_v, where C_v is either 1 or one of the H_v, L_v in the level structure [Lan16, §6]. And Δ(Π_0) acts without fixed points by Lemma 3.3.13. Proposition 3.3.17: there is a canonical map 𝐘_K^{G_1} → Y_K^{G_1}, and Y_K^{G_1} is the coarse moduli space of 𝐘_K^{G_1}. There is a quasi-projective morphism Π_0 : Y_K^{G_1} → (O_F)_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1) with geometrically connected fibres, and the map Y_K → Y_K^{G_1} is étale and surjective. For c ∈ Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p), with associated morphism c : Spec C → Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p} ⊗ F)^×/ν(K^p)(1), let Y_{K,c} and Y^{G_1}_{K,c} be the fibres of Y_K and Y_K^{G_1} over c. Then there is a commutative square of analytic spaces whose horizontal maps are isomorphisms (Y_{K,c})^{an} ≅ Γ(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)} and (Y^{G_1}_{K,c})^{an} ≅ Γ_1(c,K)\𝓗^{Hom(F,R)}, and whose vertical maps are finite étale with group Δ(K^p) = Δ(K).
items.locator: (3.3.14)–(3.3.16) and Proposition 3.3.17 (§3.3), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 49; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 210
items.note: Split from item 41. The proposition follows from Proposition 3.3.9 and Lemma 3.2.3, and is used for Corollary 3.4.2 and for the compactification of Y_K^{G_1}. The integral model of G_1, which has no moduli interpretation of its own, is where automorphic forms on Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 live, so every later statement about G_1 goes through this quotient. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H3–H4 plan only the Hilbert analogue (Δ(N) and the unit-square comparison).

items.name: K-admissible rational polyhedral cone decompositions for G_1 (§3.5)
items.statement: Write V_F := V ⊗_{O_F} F and let 𝔆 be the set of totally isotropic F-subspaces W ⊂ V_F. For W ∈ 𝔆, consider the F ⊗ R-module of Q-bilinear forms φ : V_F/W^⊥ × V_F/W^⊥ → R with φ(λx, y) = φ(x, λy) for all λ ∈ F; C(V_F/W^⊥) is the cone of those forms that are positive semidefinite with radical defined over F. The conical complex 𝒞 is the quotient of ⊔_{W∈𝔆} C(V_F/W^⊥) by the equivalence relation induced by the inclusions C(V_F/W^⊥) ⊂ C(V_F/Z^⊥) for W ⊂ Z. A non-degenerate rational polyhedral cone of 𝒞 × G_1(A^∞) is a subset of C(V_F/W^⊥) × {γ}, for some (W, γ), of the form Σ_{i=1}^k R_{>0}s_i with s_i : V_F/W^⊥ × V_F/W^⊥ → Q. A rational polyhedral cone decomposition Σ is a partition 𝒞 × G_1(A^∞) = ⊔_{σ∈Σ} σ into non-degenerate rational polyhedral cones such that the closure of each cone is a union of cones. For W ∈ 𝔆, P_W ⊂ G_1 is the stabilizer of W, M_{W,l} the group of F-linear automorphisms of V_F/W^⊥, and M_{W,h} the group of symplectic similitudes of W^⊥/W (≅ Res_{F/Q}GSp_{4−2dim W}, non-trivial even when dim W = 2). M_W = M_{W,h} × M_{W,l} is the Levi quotient of P_W, P_{W,h} is the kernel of P_W → M_{W,l}, and there is a surjection P_{W,h} → M_{W,h}. G_1(Q)^+ acts on 𝔆 and on 𝒞: for γ ∈ G_1(Q)^+ ∩ P_W with image γ_l in M_{W,l} and φ ∈ C(V_F/W^⊥), (γφ)(x, y) = ν(γ)φ(γ_l x, γ_l y). The set 𝒞 × G_1(A^∞) has a diagonal left action of G_1(Q) and left and right actions of G_1(A^∞). For a compact open K ⊂ G_1(A^∞), Σ is K-equivariant if h.σ.k ∈ Σ for all h ∈ G_1(Q), k ∈ K and σ ∈ Σ. Σ is K-admissible if: (1) it is K-equivariant; (2) p.σ ∈ Σ for all σ ⊂ C(V_F/W^⊥) × {γ} and all p ∈ P_{W,h}(A^∞); (3) for every cone σ, with W ∈ 𝔆 such that σ ⊂ C(V_F/W^⊥) lies in the interior of C(V_F/W^⊥), if σ ∩ hpσu ≠ ∅ for some p ∈ P_{W,h}(A^∞), u ∈ K and h ∈ G_1(Q), then h ∈ P_{W,h}(A^∞); (4) G_1(Q)\Σ/K is finite. K-admissible decompositions exist, and any two have a common refinement. A cone σ ⊂ Hom_Q(Sym^2_{O_F} V_F/W^⊥, Q) is smooth with respect to a lattice L_W ⊂ Hom_Q(Sym^2_F V_F/W^⊥, Q) if the s_i can be taken to be part of a basis of L_W, and Σ is smooth with respect to lattices L_{W,γ} if every cone is. The K-admissible decompositions that are projective (in the sense of [AMRT10]) and smooth with respect to the lattices L_{W,K,γ} of the integral PEL datum (Theorem 3.5.1) form a cofinal subset, and the paper uses only these unless it says otherwise.
items.locator: §3.5, the combinatorial data before Theorem 3.5.1, Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 50–51; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 212–213 (after Pink 1990 and Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne 2016, §5.2 and App. B)
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications:C0 plans arithmetic-admissible collections of rational polyhedral cones (closure under faces, action of the arithmetic group, finiteness modulo that action, compatibility at the cusps), common refinements, and sufficiently fine smooth and projective refinements, after Ash–Mumford–Rapoport–Tai and Pink. C1 plans the rational boundary components with their parabolic subgroups, Levi quotients and positivity cones. This item is Pink's adelic formulation of that notion, specialized to G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4. The lattices L_{W,K,γ} come from Lan's integral theory, which ShimuraCompactifications:C5 plans only at good primes; for the paramodular choice V' ⊗ O_{F_v} = V_3 they belong with Theorem 3.5.1 (item 43). Condition (3) is the 'assumption on the cone decomposition' invoked in the proof of Lemma 3.5.3: it forces an element of Γ_{1,W}(c,K) stabilizing a cone to have trivial linear part.

items.name: Lemmas 3.5.2 and 3.5.3 and Proposition 3.5.4: the unit action on X_{K,Σ} and the toroidal compactification of Y_K^{G_1}
items.statement: Let K be reasonable and Σ as in Theorem 3.5.1. Lemma 3.5.2: the action of O_{F,(p)}^{×,+} on Y_K extends to X_{K,Σ} and factors through Δ = (O_F)_(p)^{×,+}/O_F^{×,+}(K^p). Lemma 3.5.3: the action of Δ on X_{K,Σ} is free. The quotient X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} of X_{K,Σ} by O_{F,(p)}^{×,+} exists, because on each connected component of X_{K,Σ} it is the quotient by a finite group and the component is projective, Σ being projective. It is called a toroidal compactification of Y_K^{G_1}. Proposition 3.5.4: X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} has a stratification indexed by G_1(Q)^+\Σ/K; the map X_{K,Σ} → X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} is étale and surjective; and if K is reasonable, X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} is a flat local complete intersection over Spec Z_(p), and is normal. The boundary divisor is written D, and the subscripts K and Σ are dropped when harmless.
items.locator: Lemmas 3.5.2 and 3.5.3 and Proposition 3.5.4 (§3.5), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 52–53; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) pp. 214–215
