items.note: Proof of Lemma 3.5.2: X_{K,Σ} is normal, so it is the normalization of Y_K in X_{K,Σ} × Spec C, and by [AMRT10] the component corresponding to c is Γ(c,K)\𝓗_Σ^{Hom(F,R)}, which carries the action of Γ_1(c,K)/Γ(c,K). Proof of Lemma 3.5.3: on Y_K this is Lemma 3.3.13. On the boundary, the stabilizer in Γ_1(c,K) of a cone of Σ_c \ {0} lies in Γ(c,K), by condition (3) of K-admissibility and because O_F^{×,+} is torsion free. Split from item 43: Proposition 3.5.4 is cited on its own (arXiv p. 76). No layer plans integral compactifications at parahoric level or for G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4. Printed slips, present in both versions: the sentence before Lemma 3.5.2 says Δ was defined in (3.3.15), which is Δ(Π_0), whereas Δ is (3.3.14); 'Γ(K, c)' in the proof of Lemma 3.5.2 should be Γ(c, K); and the set of non-trivial strata in the proof of Lemma 3.5.3 is written G^+(Q)\(Σ∖{0} × G(A^∞))/K, with G(A^∞) where G_1(A^∞) is meant.

items.name: §§3.6.1–3.6.2: prime-to-p change of level and the isomorphisms [g]
items.statement: Let K = K^pK_p and K' = (K^p)'K_p be compact open subgroups of G_1(A^∞) with K ⊂ K'. Forgetting the level structure, that is, replacing the K^p-orbit η by the (K^p)'-orbit containing it, gives finite étale maps Y_K → Y_{K'} and Y_K^{G_1} → Y_{K'}^{G_1}. For g ∈ G_1(A^{∞,p}), (A, ι, λ, η, η_p) ↦ (A, ι, λ, η∘g, η_p) defines an isomorphism [g] : Y_K → Y_{g^{−1}Kg}, which induces [g] : Y_K^{G_1} → Y_{g^{−1}Kg}^{G_1}. These maps extend to toroidal compactifications for suitable choices of cone decompositions.
items.locator: §§3.6.1 and 3.6.2, with the opening paragraph of §3.6; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 53–54, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Used to build the Hecke correspondences away from p (§3.9.3). The nearest atlas material is AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4, which constructs finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels and Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences, and ShimuraCompactifications C3, which extends Hecke translations to toroidal compactifications with compatible fans. Neither constructs these maps on the Hilbert–Siegel moduli problem of §3.3, with parahoric level at p.

items.name: Lemmas 3.6.9 and 3.6.10: the Siegel type correspondence p_1, p_2 at a place w|p
items.statement: Fix K^p and w|p. Let K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v ⊂ G_1(Z_p) be reasonable with K_w = GSp_4(O_{F_w}) (resp. K_w = Kli(w)). Let K'_p = ∏_{v≠w}K_v × Si(w) (resp. ∏_{v≠w}K_v × Iw(w)), also reasonable, and put K = K^pK_p, K' = K^pK'_p. Lemma 3.6.9: there are natural forgetful maps p_1 : Y_{K'} → Y_K and p_1 : Y^{G_1}_{K'} → Y^{G_1}_K, which forget L_w and are surjective and generically finite. Lemma 3.6.10: let x_w ∈ F^{×,+} be as in §3.6.3, a uniformizer in F_w and a unit at the other places above p. There is a map p_2 : Y_{K'} → Y_K, depending on x_w. It sends (A, ι, λ, η, η_p) to (A', ι', λ', η', η'_p), where: A' = A/L_w with π : A → A' the isogeny; ι'(x) = π∘ι(x)∘π^{−1}; λ' is obtained by descending x_w·λ from A to A'; η' = π∘η; η'_p is deduced from η_p through π : A[v] → A'[v] for v ≠ w; and, when K_w = Kli(w), H'_w = H_w^⊥/L_w ⊂ A'[w]. It induces a canonical map p_2 : Y^{G_1}_{K'} → Y^{G_1}_K. Remark 3.6.8: in this setting K, K' and p_2 do not mean what they mean in the Klingen setting of §3.6.3, where p_2 goes to paramodular level.
items.locator: §3.6.7 with Remark 3.6.8 and Lemmas 3.6.9 and 3.6.10; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 54–55, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 44. Used for T_{w,1} (§3.9.17). Its p-adic completion at hyperspecial level, pulled back to deep Klingen level, underlies U_{w,1} and U_{Kli(w),1} (§§4.5.1 and 5.3). The variant from Klingen to Iwahori level (the 'resp.' case) is not referred to again by section number. There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer plans it: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H4 and R18.4 treat GL_2 only.

items.name: Lemma 3.8.2: the coherent cohomology of ω^κ and ω^κ(−D) does not depend on Σ
items.statement: Let K be reasonable and κ a weight. The complexes RΓ(X_{K,Σ}, ω^κ), RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K,Σ}, ω^κ), RΓ(X_{K,Σ}, ω^κ(−D)) and RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K,Σ}, ω^κ(−D)) do not depend on the K-admissible projective cone decomposition Σ. For a refinement Σ' of Σ, pullback along π_{Σ',Σ} : X_{K,Σ'} → X_{K,Σ} identifies them. This is immediate from Theorem 3.5.1(3), which gives (Rπ_{Σ',Σ})_*O_{X_{K,Σ'}} = O_{X_{K,Σ}} and (Rπ_{Σ',Σ})_*I_{X_{K,Σ'}} = I_{X_{K,Σ}} for the invertible ideal sheaves of the boundary, together with the projection formula and π_{Σ',Σ}^*ω^κ = ω^κ (the semi-abelian scheme of Theorem 3.5.1(2), and with it the canonical extension of ω^κ, pulls back along π_{Σ',Σ}). The identity π_{Σ',Σ}^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} = I_{X_{K,Σ'}} that Theorem 3.5.1(3) also prints is false in general and is not needed. Any two admissible decompositions have a common refinement.
items.locator: Lemma 3.8.2 (§3.8.1), with Theorem 3.5.1(3); arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 51–52 and 56–57, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 46. It lets Σ be dropped throughout and is invoked in Remark 3.9.23. ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans refinement maps and the structure-sheaf pushforward, with higher direct images as a separate theorem. AutomorphicBundles B3 plans the independence of spaces of sections from the fan. Neither covers RΓ at parahoric level at p, which rests on Theorem 3.5.1(3) (item 43). Item 43's statement also asserts this independence as part of Theorem 3.5.1; that clause should be removed there so that the statement has one home.

items.name: Lemma 3.8.10: f^! commutes with restriction to the zero locus of a non-zero-divisor
items.statement: Let S be an affine Noetherian scheme and f : X → Y an embeddable morphism of embeddable S-schemes, each a local complete intersection of pure relative dimension n over S. Let h be a section of a line bundle 𝓛 on Y such that neither h nor f^*h is a zero-divisor. Let Y_{h=0} and X_{h=0} be the vanishing loci of h and f^*h, and f_0 : X_{h=0} → Y_{h=0} the restriction of f. Then for every locally free sheaf 𝓕 on Y, (f^!𝓕)|_{X_{h=0}} = f_0^!(𝓕|_{Y_{h=0}}). The paper calls this an equality of invertible sheaves; both sides are locally free of the rank of 𝓕, and invertible when 𝓕 is a line bundle. The proof uses [Har66, Prop. III.8.8], with O_{Y_{h=0}} represented by the perfect complex 𝓛^{−1} →^h O_Y.
items.locator: Lemma 3.8.10 (§3.8.8); arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 59, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, Prop. III.8.8)
items.note: Split from item 47. Used on its own throughout §4 (pp. 76, 79, 80, 82, 106 and 108), to reduce cohomological correspondences modulo p (h = p) and to restrict them to the vanishing loci of Hasse invariants. The printed 'equality of invertible sheaves' (the same in arXiv v3 and the published version) is accurate only when 𝓕 is a line bundle; for locally free 𝓕 both sides are locally free of the rank of 𝓕. There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer plans it. Routing: it goes as a source to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension, with item 47.

items.name: §§3.8.11–3.8.15: fundamental classes, their agreement, base change and boundary divisors
items.statement: Let S be affine Noetherian and f : X → Y an embeddable morphism of embeddable S-schemes. A fundamental class Θ : O_X = f^*O_Y → f^!O_Y is constructed in two situations. (a) The lci situation: X and Y are local complete intersections over S of the same relative dimension; X is normal; and there are an open V ⊂ X, smooth over S, whose complement has codimension at least 2 in X (printed 'of codimension 2'), and an open U ⊂ Y, smooth over S, with f(V) ⊂ U. Then f^!O_Y is invertible (Lemma 3.8.9) and f^!O_Y|_V = det Ω^1_{V/S} ⊗ f^*(det Ω^1_{U/S})^{−1}. Θ is the unique extension, by the algebraic Hartogs lemma, of the determinant of df : f^*Ω^1_{U/S} → Ω^1_{V/S}. (b) The finite flat situation: f is finite flat, f_*f^!O_Y = Hom_{O_Y}(f_*O_X, O_Y), and Θ(1) = tr_f, the trace f_*O_X → O_Y. Lemma 3.8.12 ([Pil20, Lem. 4.2.3.1]): if f is finite flat and X, Y are smooth over S, then L_{X/Y} ≅ [Ω^1_{Y/S} ⊗_{O_Y} O_X →^{df} Ω^1_{X/S}] and det(df) ∈ ω_{X/Y} = f^!O_Y is tr_f. §3.8.13: in a Cartesian square with i : Y' → Y an open immersion, j : X' → X and f' : X' → Y', if f is in either situation then so is f'; j^*f^! = (f')^!i^*, and j^*Θ is the fundamental class of f'. Lemma 3.8.15 ([Pil20, Lem. 4.2.4.1]): let D_X ⊂ X and D_Y ⊂ Y be effective reduced Cartier divisors relative to S such that f restricts to D_X → D_Y and D_X → f^{−1}(D_Y) is a homeomorphism. Assume f is in the finite flat situation, or in the lci situation with D_X ∩ X^sm and D_Y ∩ Y^sm normal crossings divisors, X^sm and Y^sm being the smooth loci. Then Θ restricts to a morphism O_X(−D_X) → f^!O_Y(−D_Y).
items.locator: §3.8.11, Lemma 3.8.12, §3.8.13, §3.8.14 and Lemma 3.8.15; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 60–61, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 47. §3.8.11 is cited on its own on pp. 100 and 103, and §3.8.13 on p. 79. These are Pilloni's Constructions 1 and 2, Lemma 4.2.3.1, Proposition 4.2.5.1 (open immersion case) and Lemma 4.2.4.1. Routing: they go as a source to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension, where the merged extraction of Pilloni's paper also sends them. Its item for Construction 1 reads the printed 'codimension 2' as 'codimension ≥ 2'. The statement here reads the printed 'of codimension 2' (the same in arXiv v3 and the published version) in the same way, since the Hartogs extension needs only codimension at least 2. There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer description plans fundamental classes.

items.name: Proposition 3.8.17: traces on canonical bundles and restriction to a divisor with ramification
items.statement: Let k be a field, f : X → Y a finite flat map of smooth k-varieties, and D ⊂ Y a smooth Cartier divisor with f^{−1}(D) = nD' for a smooth Cartier divisor D' ⊂ X. There are trace maps f_*K_X → K_Y and f_*K_{D'} → K_D, and adjunction isomorphisms K_D ≅ K_Y(D)|_D and K_{D'} ≅ K_X(D')|_{D'}. For a line bundle 𝓛 on Y the projection formula gives a twisted trace map f_*(K_X ⊗_{O_X} f^*𝓛) → K_Y ⊗_{O_Y} 𝓛, and similarly over D. Proposition 3.8.17: the following square commutes. Its top map is f_*(K_X(−(n−1)D')) → K_Y, the inclusion K_X(−(n−1)D') ⊂ K_X followed by the trace. Its vertical maps are restriction followed by adjunction, f_*(K_X(−(n−1)D')) → f_*(K_{D'} ⊗ O_X(−nD')|_{D'}) and K_Y → K_D ⊗ O_Y(−D)|_D. Its bottom map is the twisted trace for f : D' → D and the line bundle O_Y(−D)|_D, using f^*O_Y(−D)|_D = O_X(−nD')|_{D'} (printed O_X(−nD)|_{D'}).
items.locator: §3.8.16 and Proposition 3.8.17; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 61–62, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 47. Used on its own in §§5.6–5.7 (pp. 128 and 131). There f is the partial Frobenius F_w (with n = p) or its square, and D = D' is the rank-one locus Y_1^{I,=w 1}. The purpose is to compare U_{Iw(w),1} and U_{w,2} with traces of partial Frobenius. The printed O_X(−nD)|_{D'} should read O_X(−nD')|_{D'} (sourceIssues E38, a misprint that affects nothing, in both versions). There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer plans it.

items.name: §3.8.6: the abstract Hecke algebras H, H^S, H_s and H^p
items.statement: Let K = ∏_tK_t ⊂ G_1(A^∞) be compact open. H = C_c^∞(G_1(A^∞)//K, Z_p) is the convolution algebra of locally constant, bi-K-invariant, compactly supported Z_p-valued functions on G_1(A^∞). The Haar measure is the product of local Haar measures normalized by vol(K_t) = 1 at every finite place t of F. For a finite set S of places, H^S ⊂ H is the subalgebra of functions whose restriction to GSp_4(F_s) is the characteristic function of K_s for every s ∈ S. For each finite place s, H_s = C_c^∞(GSp_4(F_s)//K_s, Z_p), and H = ⊗'_sH_s. For K = K^pK_p reasonable, H^p = C_c^∞(G_1(A^{p,∞})//K^p, Z_p) is the Hecke algebra away from p; as a Z_p-module it is generated by the characteristic functions of the double cosets [K^pgK^p], g ∈ G_1(A^{∞,p}).
items.locator: §3.8.6 and the first paragraph of §3.9.3; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 58 and 62–63, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: SR.1 plans Hecke algebras over a coefficient ring A for locally profinite groups. It gives convolution by finite sums over open cosets and, where averaging is unavailable, integral double-coset operators following the Mathlib Hecke API. Its identification of corners e_U with bi-U-invariant algebras assumes compact opens of invertible pro-order in A, so it does not apply here (A = Z_p, with p-adic places). The bi-K-invariant algebras with vol(K) = 1 are the Hecke rings of the pairs (K, G_1(A^∞)) and (K_s, GSp_4(F_s)). Mathlib's HeckeRing (the finitely supported double-coset module of a Hecke pair) and Tau Ceti's HeckeCosetModule.instRingHeckeRing and HeckeCosetModule.mul_assoc (associativity at mixed levels, as in Remark 3.9.16) supply that ring once the pair is given. The group G_1(A^∞) itself is not in the libraries (item 35). AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.0 constructs complex-valued adelic test functions as restricted tensor products, which is the pattern of H = ⊗'_sH_s.

items.name: §3.9.3: the Hecke operators [K^pgK^p] on the coherent cohomology of X_K and X_K^{G_1}
items.statement: Let K = K^pK_p be reasonable and g ∈ G_1(A^{∞,p}). For suitable cone decompositions there is a correspondence X_K ←^{p_2} X_{K∩gKg^{−1}} →^{p_1} X_K. Here p_1 is induced by K ∩ gKg^{−1} ⊂ K (§3.6.1). p_2 is [g] : X_{K∩gKg^{−1}} → X_{K∩g^{−1}Kg} (§3.6.2) followed by the map X_{K∩g^{−1}Kg} → X_K induced by K ∩ g^{−1}Kg ⊂ K (printed K ∩ gKg^{−1} ⊂ K). There is a canonical isomorphism p_2^*ω^κ ≅ p_1^*ω^κ, because ω^κ depends only on the p-divisible group. For a cofinal set of cone decompositions, X_K and X_{K∩gKg^{−1}} are lci and smooth outside codimension 2. Hence there is a fundamental class p_1^*O_{X_K} → p_1^!O_{X_K} extending the trace of the finite étale map p_1 on the interior, and tensoring with p_1^*ω^κ gives p_1^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ = p_1^!O_{X_K} ⊗ p_1^*ω^κ. The composite Θ_g : p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ is a cohomological correspondence, and [KgK] is the composite RΓ(X_K, ω^κ) → RΓ(X_{K∩gKg^{−1}}, p_2^*ω^κ) →^{Θ_g} RΓ(X_{K∩gKg^{−1}}, p_1^!ω^κ) →^{Tr} RΓ(X_K, ω^κ), where Tr comes from the adjunction R(p_1)_*p_1^!ω^κ → ω^κ. The same construction works for ω^κ(−D). Everything commutes with (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}, which gives operators on RΓ(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ) and RΓ(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)). Remark 3.9.4: over Q_p, compatibility with the products of H^p follows from Harris [Har90b, Prop. 2.6], through the action of G_1(A_f^p) on the limit over K^p. Integrally this needs control of the cohomology of finite groups, but it already shows that H^p acts on the torsion-free part of the cohomology.

Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Harris, Automorphic forms of ∂̄-cohomology type as coherent cohomology classes, J. Differential Geom. 32 (1990), Prop. 2.6)
items.note: The composition law is Proposition 3.9.15 (item 50). AutomorphicBundles B5 plans pullback and trace along Hecke correspondences, and composition against the abstract Hecke algebra, for its bundles and sections. The integral action on RΓ over the toroidal compactification, through a fundamental class, is layer 3 of the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, from the merged extractions of Calegari–Geraghty and Pilloni, and is not yet an atlas layer. Misprint (affects nothing, in both versions): the inclusion defining the second map of p_2 is printed K ∩ gKg^{−1} ⊂ K for K ∩ g^{−1}Kg ⊂ K.

items.name: §3.9.5: the Cousin complex of a filtration and its terms
items.statement: Let X be a topological space. For a subset Z ⊆ X and an abelian sheaf 𝓕, Γ_Z(𝓕) is the subsheaf of sections supported on Z. For a filtration Z : Z_0 = X ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ Z_n ⊇ ⋯ by closed subsets, the Cousin complex Cous_Z(𝓕) [Kem78, p. 357] is a complex of abelian sheaves in degrees ≥ 0. Its degree-i term is 𝓗^i_{Z_i/Z_{i+1}}(𝓕), where 𝓗^k_{Z_i/Z_{i+1}} is the k-th derived functor of 𝒢 ↦ [U ↦ Γ_{Z_i∖Z_{i+1}}(U ∖ Z_{i+1}, 𝒢)] ([Kem78, Lem. 7.3]). Its differentials are induced by boundary maps, and it has an augmentation 𝓕 → Cous_Z(𝓕). For X a Noetherian scheme and 𝓕 quasi-coherent, Cous_Z(𝓕) is a complex of quasi-coherent sheaves. (3.9.8): if Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1} → X is affine, then 𝓗^k_{Z_i/Z_{i+1}}(𝓕) = (j_{i+1})_*R^kΓ_{Z_i∖Z_{i+1}}(𝓕|_{U_{i+1}}), where U_{i+1} = X ∖ Z_{i+1} and j_{i+1} is the inclusion ([Kem78, Lem. 8.5(e)], the spectral sequence degenerating by [Kem78, Thm. 9.6(c)]). For X Noetherian, 𝓕 quasi-coherent and Z closed with ideal sheaf I, R^iΓ_Z(𝓕) = colim_n 𝓔xt^i(O_X/I^n, 𝓕). The powers I^n may be replaced by any decreasing sequence of ideals J_n cofinal with them, that is, such that for every n there are k, k' with J_{k'} ⊂ I^n ⊂ J_k.
items.locator: §3.9.5 with (3.9.8); arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 63–64, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Kempf, The Grothendieck–Cousin complex of an induced representation, Adv. Math. 29 (1978), p. 357, Lemmas 7.3 and 8.5(e), Theorem 9.6(c))
items.note: Split from item 49. It is referred to on its own in §4.2 (p. 92), for the Cousin complex of the p-rank stratification. Mathlib's localCohomology defines H^i_I(M) = colim_n Ext^i(R/I^n, M) for modules over a commutative ring. For R Noetherian it compares this with the colimit over all ideals whose radical contains I (localCohomology.isoSelfLERadical) and proves invariance under ideals with the same radical (localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical). That is the affine, module-level form of the last formula; sheaf-level local cohomology and Cousin complexes are absent. No atlas layer plans them. Misprint (affects nothing, in both versions): 'Ekhedal–Oort' on p. 63.

items.name: §3.9.10: the Ekedahl–Oort filtration of the minimal compactification modulo p^n
items.statement: Assume K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(Z_p). Let X = X_{K,Σ}, X^* its minimal compactification and f : X → X^*. For n ≥ 1 let X_n = X × Spec Z/p^nZ and X_n^* = X^* × Spec Z/p^nZ. Let Z^* be the filtration of X_n^* whose term Z_i^* is the closure of the union of all Ekedahl–Oort strata of codimension i. Then ([Box15, Thm. 6.2.3]): (1) Z^* is a filtration; (2) Z_i^* ∖ Z_{i+1}^* is affine; (3) Z_i^* ∖ Z_{i+1}^* is a set-theoretic local complete intersection in U_{i+1}^* = X_n^* ∖ Z_{i+1}^*. For the pull-back Z of Z^* to X_n it follows that Z is a filtration, that Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1} ↪ X_n is affine, and that Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1} is a set-theoretic local complete intersection in U_{i+1} = X_n ∖ Z_{i+1}. The proofs of Proposition 3.9.11 and Lemma 3.9.13 also use the following. Each Ekedahl–Oort stratum in Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1} is the intersection in U_{i+1} of i Cartier divisors given by generalized Hasse invariants. These divisors may be taken pulled back from X_n^*, since a sufficiently large power of each generalized Hasse invariant lifts to X_n^*. Powers of them give a cofinal sequence of lci subschemes of U_{i+1} supported on Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1}. The Ekedahl–Oort stratification is invariant under prime-to-p isogenies and under (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}. Applying Theorem 3.9.6 to Z also needs codim_{X_n}(Z_i) ≥ i, which the paper does not state for the pull-back.
items.locator: §3.9.10 and the proofs of Proposition 3.9.11, Lemma 3.9.13 and Proposition 3.9.15; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 65–67, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501 (Boxer, Torsion in the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties and Galois representations, preprint 2015, Thm. 6.2.3)
items.note: This is the geometric input to the Cousin complex argument of item 50. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2 plans Ekedahl–Oort/G-zip strata, their Hasse sections and the affineness of minimal strata, citing Boxer's Theorem C. It does so for the unitary Shimura varieties of Caraiani–Scholze, not for all strata of the minimal compactification of Hilbert–Siegel varieties modulo p^n. No library. The minimal compactification X^* itself has no item in the extraction (it is defined in §6.2.1).

items.name: Lemma 3.9.22: the normalized Klingen type Hecke operator T_w at w|p
items.statement: Let K = K^pK_p with K_p = G_1(Z_p) and fix w|p. Let K' = K^pK'_p with K'_p = ∏_{v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) × Kli(w), and K'' = K^pK''_p with K''_p = ∏_{v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) × Par(w). Let p_1 : X_{K'} → X_K and p_2 : X_{K'} → X_{K''} be the Klingen type correspondence of §3.6.3, where p_2 depends on x_w. By Proposition 3.4.1: X_{K'}, X_{K''} and X_K are relative complete intersections over Spec Z_p of the same pure dimension; X_K is smooth; and X_{K'} and X_{K''} are normal and smooth over Z_p outside codimension 2. So p_1^!O_{X_K} and p_2^!O_{X_{K''}} are invertible and there are fundamental classes p_1^*O_{X_K} → p_1^!O_{X_K} and p_2^*O_{X_{K''}} → p_2^!O_{X_{K''}}. For κ with l_v ≥ 0, the differentials of the isogenies p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 and p_2^*𝒢 → p_1^*𝒢 give p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^*ω^κ and p_1^*ω^κ → p_2^*ω^κ, and hence cohomological correspondences Θ_1 : p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ and Θ_2 : p_1^*ω^κ → p_2^!ω^κ. Lemma 3.9.22 (details in [Pil20, Lem. 7.1.1, 7.1.2]): if l_w ≥ 2, Θ_1 is divisible by p^{2+l_w} and Θ_2 by p. Put T'_w = p^{−2−l_w}Θ_1, which gives RΓ(X_{K''}, ω^κ) → RΓ(X_K, ω^κ), and T''_w = p^{−1}Θ_2, which gives RΓ(X_K, ω^κ) → RΓ(X_{K''}, ω^κ). Then T_w := T'_w∘T''_w. The same definitions apply to cuspidal cohomology and over X^{G_1}; the operator is canonical on X^{G_1} and depends on x_w on X_K. Remark 3.9.21: T_w is not the double coset operator [GSp_4(O_{F_w}) diag(1, p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−2}) GSp_4(O_{F_w})]. The paper gives T_w = [GSp_4(O_{F_w}) diag(1, p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−1}) Par(w)][Par(w) diag(1, 1, 1, p^{−1}) GSp_4(O_{F_w})] = p[GSp_4(O_{F_w}) diag(1, p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−2}) GSp_4(O_{F_w})] + (1 + p + p^2 + p^3)p^{−2}[GSp_4(O_{F_w}) diag(p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−1}) GSp_4(O_{F_w})]. Remark 3.9.23: the action of T_w does not depend on the compactification ([Pil20, Prop. 7.2.1]).
items.locator: §3.9.20 with Remark 3.9.21, Lemma 3.9.22 and Remark 3.9.23; arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 68–69, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 51. Used on its own in §4.2 (pp. 82–83) and §4.5 (pp. 101, 103). The F = Q case is Pilloni's Lemmas 7.1.1–7.1.2 and T = T_1∘T_2, which the merged extraction of Pilloni's paper places in the proposed HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. This item is routed to the same roadmap, HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology). Its brief plans T_w = T'_w∘T''_w on Hilbert–Siegel varieties as Pilloni's T taken place by place, so the general statement and its F = Q case have one owner. The double-coset identity of Remark 3.9.21 is recorded as printed and was not checked. For the paper's J (§2.1.1, pairing e_1 with e_4 and e_2 with e_3), diag(a, b, c, d) is a similitude exactly when ad = bc. So diag(1, p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−1}) and diag(1, 1, 1, p^{−1}) are not in GSp_4(F_w), although their product diag(1, p^{−1}, p^{−1}, p^{−2}) is, and the displayed factors are not double cosets in GSp_4(F_w) as printed. The brief of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory asks for Remark 3.9.21 to be checked on this point. There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer plans the Hilbert–Siegel operator.

items.name: Corollary 3.10.5: dim H^1 = l_0·dim H^0 in the regular case
items.statement: Suppose we are in the setting of Theorem 3.10.1 and κ satisfies the hypothesis of part (2): for each v|∞, k_v − l_v > R and either l_v = 2 or l_v > R. Let l_0 be the number of infinite places v with l_v = 2. Then dim_Ē H^1(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2}_m ⊗ Ē = l_0·dim_Ē H^0(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2}_m ⊗ Ē.
items.locator: Corollary 3.10.5 (§3.10); arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 71, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 52 because it is used on its own (p. 216). Proof: since m is non-Eisenstein, the contributing π are of general type by Lemma 2.9.1. Each of the l_0 places with l_v = 2 gives the packet member that is generic there and holomorphic elsewhere, and Theorem 2.9.3 (item 32, conditional as recorded in item 33) finishes the argument. There are two Siegel threefold analogues. One is Calegari–Geraghty 2020's h1-h0-dimension-equality (proof of their Theorem 7.11), which their merged extraction routes to the proposed GSp4NonregularModularityLifting. The other is Pilloni's Proposition 15.2.4.1, that the holomorphic and generic members occur together with multiplicity one, which the merged extraction of Pilloni's paper places in the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer plans it.

items.name: Lemma 3.10.7: H^0 of the boundary vanishes after localizing at a non-Eisenstein ideal
items.statement: Let κ = (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞} be a weight with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 and k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2), let m be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, and let D be the boundary of X_K^{G_1}. Then H^0(D, ω^κ)_m ⊗ Ē = 0. Remark 3.10.6: this is essentially a special case of Harris–Zucker [HZ01], which cannot be cited directly because these Shimura varieties do not satisfy its hypotheses.
items.locator: Lemma 3.10.7 with Remark 3.10.6 (§3.10); arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 71–72, the final version; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. Inst. Hautes Études Sci. 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 52. It is the only place where the non-Eisenstein localization and i ≤ 1 enter the proof of Theorem 3.10.1. For F = Q the proof is Freitag, Siegelsche Modulfunktionen, IV Satz 4.4. For F ≠ Q, let π : X_K^{G_1} → X_K^{*,G_1} and write the boundary of the minimal compactification as ∂_0X^* ⊔ ∂_1X^*, with ∂_1X^* a union of Hilbert modular varieties and ∂_0X^* finitely many points. For parallel weight, π_*(ω^κ|_D) = ω^κ|_{∂X^*}, using π_*O = O, π_*I_D = I_{∂X^*} and R^1π_*I_D = 0. Otherwise sections vanish on π^{−1}(∂_0X^*) ([Lan13], [BR16, Prop. 1.5.8]), and π_*(ω^κ|_{π^{−1}(∂_1X^*)}) is zero unless the l_v are all equal, when it is ω^{(k_v)}. The remaining space is induced from Hilbert modular forms on M_W (Koecher's principle). The Satake transform H_{G_1} → H_{M_W} gives Galois representations ρ_π ⊕ (ρ_π ⊗ χ), which are Eisenstein. There is no library declaration, and no atlas layer plans it.

items.name: §3.10: the spherical Hecke ring T̃ away from S and non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: Let K = ∏_vK_v ⊂ GSp_4(A_F^∞) be open compact and S ⊃ S_p a finite set of places with K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S. Let O be the ring of integers of the coefficient field E (a finite extension of Q_p). T̃ = ⊗_{v∉S}O[GSp_4(F_v)//GSp_4(O_{F_v})] is the ring of spherical Hecke operators away from S. A maximal ideal m ⊂ T̃ is non-Eisenstein if two conditions hold. First, T̃/m is a finite extension of F_p. Second, for some (equivalently any) embedding T̃/m ↪ F̄_p, there is an irreducible representation ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F̄_p) such that for every v ∉ S, det(X − ρ̄(Frob_v)) ≡ X^4 − T_{v,1}X^3 + (q_vT_{v,2} + (q_v^3 + q_v)T_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^3T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + q_v^6T_{v,0}^2 (mod m), with the operators T_{v,i} of (2.4.8).

items.note: Used in Theorem 3.10.1, Corollary 3.10.5 and Lemma 3.10.7, and again in §6.6 (p. 167). IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3 plans the Hecke polynomial for GL_n only and warns against asserting it for other groups. The GSp_4 polynomial Q_v(X) of (2.4.8), with the operators T_{v,i} of §2.4.7, is item 163 of this extraction, and item 18 uses its roots. Both are routed, with most of the other §2.4 items, to GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations (Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: GSp_4, its local Langlands correspondence and Galois representations). This item is routed to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes), which imports T_{v,i} and Q_v(X) from that roadmap. There is no library declaration.

items.name: Harris's comparison: interior coherent cohomology and (Lie P^−_∞, K^h_∞)-cohomology of automorphic forms
items.statement: Let h : Res_{C/R}(G_m)(R) = C^× → GSp_4(R) send x + iy to [[xI_2, yS], [−yS, xI_2]], where S is the 2 × 2 block of J, so that h(i) = J. Let K^h, the centralizer of h, be identified with R^×U(2). Write g_C = g^{0,0} ⊕ g^{−1,1} ⊕ g^{1,−1}, with g^{0,0} = k_{h,C}, p^+ = g^{−1,1}, p^− = g^{1,−1} and 𝔓_h = k_{h,C} ⊕ p^−. Let P^− be the parabolic with Lie algebra 𝔓_h and P^− ∩ GSp_4(R) = K^h (P_h in [Har90a], Q^− in [BHR94], Q in [CG18]). Put P^−_∞ = ∏_{v|∞}P^−_v and K^h_∞ = ∏_{v|∞}K^h_v, and let V_κ = ⊗_{v|∞}V_{κ_v} be the representation of K^h_∞ whose automorphic vector bundle ([BHR94, Def. 1.3.2]) is ω^κ. Interior cohomology is H̄^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ) := im(H^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) → H^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ)). Let A_cusp(G_1) ⊂ A_(2)(G_1) be the cuspidal and the square-integrable automorphic forms with central character |·|^2, and m_*(π) the multiplicity of π in A_*(G_1). Then [Har90a, Thm. 2.7] gives inclusions ⊕_{π∈A_cusp(G_1)}((π^∞)^K ⊗ H^i(Lie P^−_∞, K^h_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_κ))^{⊕m_cusp(π)} ⊆ H̄^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ_C)^{|·|^2} ⊆ ⊕_{π∈A_(2)(G_1)}((π^∞)^K ⊗ H^i(Lie P^−_∞, K^h_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_κ))^{⊕m_(2)(π)}. By [Har90a, Prop. 2.7.2] the π contributing to H^0 are cuspidal. By Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4 [Art04, GT19], m_cusp(π) = m_(2)(π) = 1.

AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 plans relative Lie algebra cochains for (g, K) only, not (Lie P^−, K^h)-cohomology or Harris's comparison. The Siegel threefold form, Calegari–Geraghty 2020's Theorem 5.2 together with interior cohomology, is placed in layer 6 of the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes by the merged extractions. Differential Geom. 32) in Remark 3.9.4. Neither is among the extraction's prerequisites. There is no library declaration.

items.name: Archimedean inputs: temperedness under regularity, and (Lie P^−_v, K^h_v)-cohomology of (limits of) discrete series of GSp_4(R)
items.statement: (a) [BHR94, proof of Thm. 4.2.3, with Prop. 2.4.5]. Let π ∈ A_(2)(G_1) with H^i(Lie P^−_∞, K^h_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_κ) ≠ 0. If the infinitesimal character of π_∞ is far enough from all the root hyperplanes it does not lie on, then π_∞ is essentially tempered. Through the Casselman–Osborne relation between that infinitesimal character and κ, this is exactly the condition on κ in Theorem 3.10.1(2). (b) [Har90a, Thm. 3.5] (Mirković) and [BHR94, Thm. 3.2.1]. For such π with π_∞ essentially tempered, and each v|∞, H^j(Lie P^−_v, K^h_v; π_v ⊗ V_{κ_v}) = 0 except in three cases: l_v > 2, j = 0 and π_v the holomorphic discrete series of weight (k_v, l_v); l_v = 2, j = 0 and π_v the holomorphic limit of discrete series of weight (k_v, l_v); l_v = 2, j = 1 and π_v the generic limit of discrete series of weight (k_v, l_v). In each of these cases the space is one-dimensional. (c) Lowest weight theory ([PS09, §2.3]). If H^0(Lie P^−_v, K^h_v; π_v ⊗ V_{κ_v}) ≠ 0, then π_v is the holomorphic discrete series or holomorphic limit of discrete series of weight (k_v, l_v).

items.name: Wallach: a square-integrable automorphic representation with tempered archimedean component is cuspidal
items.statement: [Wal84, Thm. 4.3], as used. Let π be an automorphic representation of G_1(A_Q) = GSp_4(A_F) occurring in the space A_(2)(G_1) of square-integrable automorphic forms with central character |·|^2, and suppose π_∞ is essentially tempered. Then π occurs in the cuspidal spectrum: π ∈ A_cusp(G_1). In the proof of Theorem 3.10.1(2) this upgrades the two inclusions of Harris's comparison to equalities.

items.name: The p-rank strata X_1^{≤_I1,≥_J1,≥_K2} are Cohen–Macaulay local complete intersections
items.statement:
Let K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)} for all v|p, and let X_1 be the reduction modulo p of the toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ}. For any pairwise disjoint sets I, J, K of places above p (here K denotes a set of places, not the level), the scheme X_1^{≤_I1,≥_J1,≥_K2} is Cohen–Macaulay; indeed it is a local complete intersection over Spec F_p.

Reason given in the paper. X_1^{≤_I1,≥_J1,≥_K2} is open in X_1^{≤_I1}. X_1^{≤_I1} is a complete intersection in X_1, because it is given by the vanishing of the Hasse invariants Ha(𝓖_v), v ∈ I. And X_1 itself is a local complete intersection by Proposition 3.5.4.

Uses. The paper says it uses this repeatedly in order to apply Lemma 3.8.10, that is, to restrict cohomological correspondences to vanishing loci of Hasse invariants. At the levels of this statement it is used directly in three places:
- Lemma 4.2.8, for X_1^{≥_{J'}2};
- Lemma 4.2.25, for X_{K,1}^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J,≤_w1};
- the proof of Corollary 4.2.29, for X_1^{G_1,I'_{a,b},J}.
The paper also uses the same property, without separate comment, for the preimages of these strata at Siegel and Klingen level at w: X^{≥_{J'}2}_{K',1} and X^{I'_{a,b},J}_{K',1}. These uses are in Lemmas 4.2.7, 4.2.8, 4.2.15 and 4.2.22. There it serves to check identities between maps of locally free sheaves on a dense open subscheme, and, with the density of the ordinary locus, to show that Hasse invariants are not zero divisors.
items.locator: §4.1.1, the paragraph after the definition of the strata X_1^{∗(i)_{I_i}a_i}, arXiv p. 76
items.note: Item 54 previously contained this claim, stated for all strata rather than for these. Item 54 is a construction, while this is a theorem used on its own throughout §4.2. Neither library has Cohen–Macaulay rings or schemes (Mathlib at the pinned commit has none) or Hasse invariants. The commutative algebra of regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings and complete intersections is planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3. No atlas layer plans the mod p geometry of Hilbert–Siegel varieties.

items.name: Lemmas 4.2.6 and 4.2.7: the Siegel operator T_{w,1} commutes with the Hasse invariant
items.statement:
Setting of §4.2.3. K_p = G_1(Z_p); J = J' ⊔ {w}; K' = K^pK'_p with K'_p = ∏_{v≠w}K_v × Si(w). For a weight κ with l_w ≥ 2, T_{w,1}: p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ is a cohomological correspondence. By Lemma 3.8.10 and flatness of X_{K'} and X_K over Z_p, it reduces modulo p to T_{w,1}: p_2^*(ω^κ|_{X_1}) → p_1^!(ω^κ|_{X_1}), a map of locally free sheaves over (X_{K'})_1, which pulls back to X_1^{G_1,≥_{J'}2}.

Étale decomposition. The dense open subscheme (X_{K',1}^{≥_{J'}2})^{=_w2}, which is ordinary at w, is the union of two kinds of connected components. On the étale components (…)^{=_w2,et}, the kernel of the universal isogeny p_1^*𝓖_w → p_2^*𝓖_w contains no multiplicative group; the others are (…)^{=_w2,net}. Accordingly T_{w,1} = T^{et}_{w,1} + T^{net}_{w,1} over (X_{K',1}^{≥_{J'}2})^{=_w2}.

Lemma 4.2.6. T^{net}_{w,1} = 0 as soon as l_w ≥ 3. For all l_w ≥ 3, over (X_{K',1}^{≥_{J'}2})^{=_w2}, one has p_1^*Ha(𝓖_w)∘T^{et}_{w,1} = T^{et}_{w,1}∘p_2^*Ha(𝓖_w) as maps p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!(ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p−1}_{𝓖_w}). The first point comes from the proof of Lemma 3.9.18, since l_w + 1 > 3 and k_w + l_w > 3; the second from the compatibility of the Hasse invariant with étale isogenies.

Lemma 4.2.7. For l_w ≥ 3, p_1^*Ha(𝓖_w)∘T_{w,1} = T_{w,1}∘p_2^*Ha(𝓖_w) as maps of locally free sheaves on X_{K',1}^{≥_{J'}2}. Since this scheme is Cohen–Macaulay, it suffices to check on the dense open ordinary locus at w, where it is Lemma 4.2.6.
items.locator: Lemmas 4.2.6 and 4.2.7 with the decomposition T_{w,1} = T^{et}_{w,1} + T^{net}_{w,1} preceding them, §4.2.3, arXiv p. 79
items.note: Split from item 57, because §4.6 cites these lemmas directly: Lemma 4.2.7 in the paragraph before Proposition 4.6.9 (arXiv p. 109) and Lemma 4.2.6 in the proof of Lemma 4.6.14 (p. 110). Neither library has Hecke correspondences on Shimura varieties. No atlas layer plans Hecke correspondences at p on GSp_4-type varieties modulo p.

items.name: Lemmas 4.2.14, 4.2.15 and 4.2.19: the halves T'_w, T''_w of the Klingen operator commute with Ha and Ha'
items.locator: Lemmas 4.2.14, 4.2.15 and 4.2.19, with (4.2.17), (4.2.18) and the decompositions of T'_w and T''_w preceding them, §4.2.11, arXiv pp. 83–85
items.note: Split from item 58, because §4.6 cites Lemmas 4.2.15 and 4.2.19 directly: in the paragraph before Proposition 4.6.9 (p. 109), in the proof of Lemma 4.6.13 (p. 110) and in the proof of Corollary 4.6.15 (p. 111). Lemma 4.2.14 is used in the proof of Lemma 4.2.37. Pilloni's F = Q versions (his Proposition 7.4.1.1, Lemma 7.4.2.3 and Proposition 7.4.2.1) are proposed, but not planned, in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. Nothing in the libraries. The characteristic-zero display of T''_w on arXiv p. 82 prints X_{K'} for X_{K''}; the statement above uses X_{K''}, as §3.9.20 does.

items.name: Lemmas 4.2.36 and 4.2.37: T_{w,1} and T_w commute over the ordinary locus, and T̃^I is locally finite on X^{=_J1,=_{J^c}2}
items.statement:
Setting of §4.2.35: K_p = G_1(Z_p) and S_p = I ⊔ I^c. The commutativity of T_{w,1} and T_w is not proved in general. It is proved over the ordinary locus at w, where all the correspondences are finite flat over the interior, so that cohomological correspondences can be composed there.

Lemma 4.2.36. Suppose w ∈ I^c and l_w ≥ 2. Then T_{w,1}∘T_w = T_w∘T_{w,1} on RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D)). Proof: the two composites give the same cohomological correspondence over the interior. The same construction as the complex K^• of Proposition 4.2.33, applied to the interior Y_1^{G_1,I}, gives a complex K'^•, and T_w and T_{w,1} commute on each of its terms H^0(Y_1^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2}, ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w'∈J}(det 𝓖_{w'})^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w'∈J}Ha(𝓖_{w'})^n)). Hence they commute on the subcomplex K^•, and so on RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I},ω^κ(−D)).

Lemma 4.2.37. Fix J ⊂ I, and consider X_{K,1}^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2} = X_{K,1}^{=_J1,=_{J^c}2}: p-rank exactly 1 at the places of J, ordinary at the other places above p. The space is to be read over X^{G_1}, where §4.6 uses it; the paper omits the superscript G_1. There is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F and not on the tame level K^p, with the following property. If l_v ≥ 2 and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I, l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I^c, and l_v ≥ p+1 for all v ∈ J, then RΓ(X_{K,1}^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2},ω^κ(−D)) carries a locally finite action of T̃^I = ∏_{w|p}T_w ∏_{w∈I^c}T_{w,1}. The factors of T̃^I commute by Lemma 4.2.36.

Proof of Lemma 4.2.37. By Theorem 4.2.12, T^I acts locally finitely on RΓ(X^I_{K,1},ω^κ(−D)) with perfect ordinary part. Since T̃^I = T^I∏_{w∈I^c}T_w, T̃^I also acts locally finitely there. Then use the triangles induced by ω^κ →^{Ha(𝓖_w)} ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p−1}_{𝓖_w} → ω^κ ⊗ det ω^{p−1}_{𝓖_w}/Ha(𝓖_w) for w ∈ J, with Lemma 4.2.14. Finally pass to the limit over multiplication by Ha(𝓖_w) for w ∈ I ∖ J.
items.note:
Split from item 59, because §4.6 uses these lemmas separately. Proposition 4.6.9 applies e(T̃^I) to H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)), and the commutativity at Klingen level (Lemma 4.5.15, arXiv p. 104) is proved 'in the same way as Lemma 4.2.36'.

As printed (p. 95; published p. 266), Lemma 4.2.37 and its proof are written on X_{K,1}, not X^{G_1}_{K,1}. The paper itself warns (p. 78) that X_1 has infinitely many connected components, so finiteness is to be sought over X_1^{G_1}. Theorem 4.2.12, which the proof invokes, is stated over X_1^{G_1}, and §4.6 works over X^{G_1}_{K,1}.

Nothing in the libraries or the atlas.

items.name: §§4.3.4–4.3.5: the Igusa torsor IG^I over 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), the torus T_I, the Iwasawa algebra Λ̃_I and the sheaves Ω^{κ̃_I}
items.statement:
Standing assumption of §4.3: K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}. Fix a partition {v|p} = I ⊔ I^c.

§4.3.4, the loci. X_{K,1}^{≥_I1,Par-m-et,≥_{I^c}2} ⊂ X_{K,1}^{≥_I1,≥_{I^c}2} is the open subscheme where, for each v ∈ I with K_v = Par(v), the kernel of the quasi-polarization λ: 𝓖_v → 𝓖_v^D contains a multiplicative group. Away from the boundary, this kernel is an extension of an étale group of rank p by a multiplicative group of rank p. 𝔛^I_K := 𝔛_K^{≥_I1,Par-m-et,≥_{I^c}2} is the corresponding open formal subscheme, and 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) is the fibre of 𝔛^{≥1}_{K,Kli}(p^m) over 𝔛^I_K. Over 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞) there is, for v ∈ I, a Barsotti–Tate group H_{∞,v} ↪ 𝓖_v of height one and dimension one. For v ∈ I^c there is a rank 2 multiplicative Barsotti–Tate group 𝓖_v^m ↪ 𝓖_v, and H_{∞,v} ↪ 𝓖_v^m is a rank one sub-Barsotti–Tate group.

Spherical case. If K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for all v|p, set K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v). Then 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p) = 𝔛^I_{K_p(I)K^p}: at v ∈ I the Klingen level structure H_v is multiplicative, and at v ∈ I^c the multiplicative Klingen structure is extended to the canonical (ordinary) Iwahori level structure.

The Igusa torsor. IG^I → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞) is the profinite-étale torsor of trivializations ψ_v: Z_p ≃ T_p(H^D_{∞,v}) for v|p and φ_v: Z_p ≃ T_p((𝓖_v^m/H_{∞,v})^D) for v ∈ I^c. Here D is the Cartier dual and T_p the Tate module, a pro-étale sheaf. For v ∈ I, λ ∈ Z_p^× acts by ψ_v ↦ ψ_v∘λ; for v ∈ I^c, (λ,μ) ∈ (Z_p^×)^2 acts by (ψ_v,φ_v) ↦ (ψ_v∘λ, φ_v∘μ). The Galois group of the torsor is T_I := ∏_{v∈I}O_{F_v}^× ∏_{v∈I^c}(O_{F_v}^×)^2 ≃ ∏_{v∈I}Z_p^× ∏_{v∈I^c}(Z_p^×)^2.

§4.3.5, the sheaves.
- Λ̃_{1,v} = Z_p⟦O_{F_v}^×⟧ ≃ Z_p⟦Z_p^×⟧ and Λ̃_{2,v} = Z_p⟦(O_{F_v}^×)^2⟧ ≃ Z_p⟦(Z_p^×)^2⟧ are the one- and two-variable Iwasawa algebras.
- Λ̃_I = ⊗̂_{v∈I}Λ̃_{1,v} ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v∈I^c}Λ̃_{2,v} = Z_p⟦T_I⟧, and κ̃_I: T_I → Λ̃_I^× is the universal character.
- Ω_0^{κ̃_I} = ((π_*O_{IG^I}) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ̃_I)^{T_I}, where π: IG^I → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞) is the affine projection and T_I acts diagonally: naturally on π_*O_{IG^I} and through κ̃_I on Λ̃_I.
- Ω^{κ̃_I} = Ω_0^{κ̃_I} ⊗ ⊗_{v|p}det^2ω_{𝓖_v}. The twist is explained by Lemma 4.3.8. This is an invertible sheaf of O_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞)} ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ̃_I-modules.
items.locator: §4.3.4 (Igusa towers) and §4.3.5 (Sheaves of p-adic modular forms), arXiv pp. 96–97
items.note: Not covered by any item. Item 61 (§4.4) uses T_I, and every later p-adic complex (M_I^{pad,κ_I}, M_I, Theorem 4.6.1) is the cohomology of these sheaves. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T5 constructs Igusa torsors of trivializations of dual canonical subgroups over the ordinary locus, for the Hilbert route of Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O7 constructs ordinary Igusa forms in the Hilbert case. Neither covers this torsor over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus at Klingen level, with group T_I. The completed group ring Z_p⟦T_I⟧ is planned by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1. Pilloni's F = Q tower and sheaves (his §9: IG(p^m), 𝔍𝔊(p^∞), 𝔉^κ) are proposed in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.8 and Corollary 4.3.9: the comparison of Ω^κ with the classical sheaves ω^κ
items.statement:
§4.3.6 setting. Over 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), for all v|p, the differential of H_{∞,v} ↪ 𝓖_v gives a surjection ω_{𝓖_v} → ω_{H_{∞,v}}. Let κ = ((k_v,2)_{v∈I},(k_v,l_v)_{v∈I^c}) ∈ (Z^2)^{S_p} be an algebraic weight with k_v ≥ 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≥ l_v for v ∈ I^c.

(4.3.7), projection to the highest weight vector. By construction there is a surjection
ω^κ|_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞)} → (⊗_{v∈I}ω^{k_v−2}_{H_{∞,v}}) ⊗ (⊗_{v∈I^c}ω^{l_v−2}_{𝓖_v/H_{∞,v}} ⊗ ω^{k_v−2}_{H_{∞,v}}) ⊗ (⊗_{v|p}det ω^2_{𝓖_v}).

Hodge–Tate reductions. Over IG^I the Hodge–Tate maps Z_p →^{ψ_v} T_p(H^D_{∞,v}) →^{HT} ω_{H_{∞,v}} (v|p) and Z_p →^{φ_v} T_p((𝓖_v^m/H_{∞,v})^D) →^{HT} ω_{𝓖_v/H_{∞,v}} (v ∈ I^c) become isomorphisms after tensoring with O_{IG^I}. They give Z_p^×-reductions of the GL_1-torsors ω_{H_{∞,v}} and ω_{𝓖_v/H_{∞,v}}.

Classical weights as p-adic weights. A classical weight κ is identified with an element of Hom(Λ̃_I,Z_p) through the character ((x_v)_{v∈I},(x_v,y_v)_{v∈I^c}) ↦ ∏_{v∈I}x_v^{k_v−2}∏_{v∈I^c}x_v^{k_v−2}y_v^{l_v−2} of T_I. Set Ω^κ := Ω^{κ̃_I} ⊗_{Λ̃_I,κ} Z_p.

Lemma 4.3.8. For all such κ there is a canonical isomorphism
HT^*: (⊗_{v∈I}ω^{k_v−2}_{H_{∞,v}}) ⊗ (⊗_{v∈I^c}ω^{l_v−2}_{𝓖_v/H_{∞,v}} ⊗ ω^{k_v−2}_{H_{∞,v}}) ⊗ (⊗_{v|p}det ω^2_{𝓖_v}) ≃ Ω^κ.
It sends a rule g on triples (x,(a_v)_{v|p},(b_v)_{v∈I^c}) to the rule (x,(φ_v),(ψ_v)) ↦ g(x,(HT(ψ_v(1)))_{v|p},(HT(φ_v(1)))_{v∈I^c}).

Corollary 4.3.9. For all such κ there is a canonical surjection ω^κ|_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞)} → Ω^κ = Ω^{κ̃_I} ⊗_{Λ̃_I,κ} Z_p. It is the map (4.3.7), composed with Lemma 4.3.8.
items.locator: (4.3.7), Lemma 4.3.8 and Corollary 4.3.9, §4.3.6, arXiv pp. 97–98
items.note:
Split from item 60. Corollary 4.3.9 is used separately in §4.6: its kernel Kω^κ is defined from it on arXiv p. 115. The previous wording of Lemma 4.3.8 ('the relevant tensor product') was not a statement. The Hodge–Tate map it uses is item 145 (planned, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0). The extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) records the fact that HT ⊗ O is an isomorphism for a group étale-locally isomorphic to μ_{p^n} as a source item for T0. The comparison itself is planned nowhere.

In the proof as printed (p. 97; published p. 270), the transformation law of sections of Ω_0^κ reads f(x,(φ_v∘λ_v^{−1}),(ψ_v∘β_v^{−1})) = ∏_{v∈S_p}λ_v^{k_v−2}∏_{v∈I^c}β_v^{l_v−2}f(x,(φ_v),(ψ_v)). The indexing does not match: φ_v is indexed by I^c but λ_v by S_p, and ψ_v by S_p but β_v by I^c. Consistently with the T_I-action of §4.3.4, the λ_v (weights k_v − 2, all v|p) act on the ψ_v, and the β_v (weights l_v − 2, v ∈ I^c) act on the φ_v. On p. 98 (published p. 270), δ_v^{l_w−2} should be δ_v^{l_v−2}. The arguments of g in HT^*(g) are printed in the opposite order to the definition of g. The statements are unaffected.

items.name: Lan's vanishing of the higher direct images of subcanonical sheaves to the minimal compactification
items.statement:
Lan, Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions, IMRN 2017, Theorem 8.6, as the paper uses it. Setting: the Hilbert–Siegel variety with K_p = G_1(Z_p); a toroidal compactification X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} with projective cone decomposition; π its canonical map to the minimal compactification; ω^κ(−D) the subcanonical extensions of the automorphic vector bundles.

Statement as used: R^iπ_*𝓕 = 0 for i > 0, for the following sheaves 𝓕:
- 𝓕 = ω^κ(−D), also modulo p;
- 𝓕 = ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝓖_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝓖_w)^n), modulo p and over the open X_1^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2}, that is, over an open of the minimal compactification.
In the proof of Proposition 4.2.33 the paper applies Lan's theorem directly to the second family of sheaves. The start of §6.2 invokes the same fact: the higher derived pushforwards of the cuspidal sheaves from the toroidal to the minimal compactification vanish. The exact hypotheses are those of Lan's Theorem 8.6, which the paper cites without restating.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.2.33, §4.2.30, arXiv p. 94 (also §6.2.1, arXiv p. 143), citing Lan, IMRN 2017, Theorem 8.6
items.note: A key external input, not covered by any item. Item 143 covers the pushforward to the minimal compactification as a construction, not this vanishing. Neither library has it. AutomorphicBundles B3 defines the pushforward of the canonical and subcanonical extensions to the minimal compactification as a coherent sheaf, but does not plan the vanishing of its higher direct images. ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans only the higher direct images along refinements of toroidal compactifications. ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans the integral minimal compactification for good-prime PEL data, which covers the PEL model at K_p = G_1(Z_p). The extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) records the same theorem, for the Siegel threefold, and routes Lan's vanishing to the proposal IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, asking that it be stated once in Lan's generality and also locally on the minimal compactification. Lan's IMRN 2017 paper is already among this extraction's prerequisites. That entry should name Theorem 8.6, and also Theorem 8.7 (the Koecher principle, used in §6.1.4).

items.name: The Artin–Rees lemma
items.statement:
Let R be a Noetherian ring, I ⊆ R an ideal, M a finitely generated R-module and N ⊆ M a submodule. There is k ≥ 0 such that I^nM ∩ N = I^{n−k}(I^kM ∩ N) for all n ≥ k.

Use in the paper. The proof of Lemma 4.2.10 applies it on the Noetherian scheme X_{K'} to the locally free sheaf p_1^*ω^κ. The map Θ(κ) factors through p^3p_1^*ω^κ ∩ ⋂_x I(x)^{l_w}p_1^*ω^κ, where x runs over the generic points of V(𝓘) (finitely many up to the action of (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}) and I(x) is the ideal of the closure of x. Artin–Rees shows that Θ(κ) then factors through p^3𝓘p_1^*ω^κ once l_w exceeds a constant C.

items.name: §4.5.8 with Lemmas 4.5.9, 4.5.10 and 4.5.13: the Klingen-type operator U_{w,2} = U'_w∘U''_w
items.statement:
Let w|p and let K = K^pK_p be reasonable with K_p = G_1(Z_p). Put K' = K^pK'_p with K'_p = ∏_{v|p,v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) × Kli(w), and K'' = K^pK''_p with K''_p = ∏_{v|p,v≠w}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) × Par(w). Let p_1 : 𝔛_{K'} → 𝔛_K and p_2 : 𝔛_{K'} → 𝔛_{K''} be the p-adic completion of the Klingen-type Hecke correspondence of §3.9.20, for suitable cone decompositions. Here p_2 depends on a choice of x_w ∈ F^{×,+}, and there are natural isogenies p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 → p_1^*𝒢 whose composite is multiplication by x_w. Fix m ≥ 1.
Let 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m) be the formal subscheme of 𝔛_{K'} ×_{p_1,𝔛_K} 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) where Ker(p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢) ∩ p_1^*H_m = 0. Lemma 4.5.9: 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m) is open and closed in this fibre product. The projection r_1 : 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) and the lift r_2 : 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^m) of p_2 form a correspondence; r_2 is defined using p_2^*H_m, the image of p_1^*H_m, onto which p_1^*H_m maps isomorphically.
Lemma 4.5.10: there is a normalized trace map “p^{−2}Tr_{r_1}” : (r_1)_*O_{𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m)} → O_{𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m)}. The proof shows that dr_1 on top differentials is divisible by p^2. Let x be a closed point of the interior that is ordinary at w. The fibre of r_1 over x parametrizes L = Ker(p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢) ⊂ 𝒢_w[p] of étale rank 2 and multiplicative rank 1 with L ∩ H_m = 0. The map r_1 has degree p^3, with p points in the fibre and inseparability degree p^2. By Serre–Tate theory the map of completed local rings ⊗_{v|p}W(k(x))[[T_{1,v},T_{2,v},T_{3,v}]] → ⊗_{v|p}W(k(x'))[[T_{1,v},T_{2,v},T_{3,v}]] is T_{i,v} ↦ T_{i,v} if v ≠ w or i = 1, and T_{i,w} ↦ (1+T_{i,w})^p − 1 for i = 2, 3. One concludes by Grothendieck duality modulo p^n (§3.8.11) and a limit over n.
The isogeny induces r_2^*ω^κ → r_1^*ω^κ. Zariski locally on Spf R, over the identity of r^*ω_{H_{m,w}} = R, it is given on r^*ω_{𝒢_w} = R^2 by the matrix diag(p, 1) (4.5.12). It is normalized by dividing by p^{l_w}. For m = ∞ the isogeny gives an isomorphism r_1^*H_{∞,w} ≅ r_2^*H_{∞,w}, hence an isomorphism r_2^*Ω^{κ_I} ≅ r_1^*Ω^{κ_I}. With Lemma 4.5.10 this defines U'_w ∈ Hom(RΓ(𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}), RΓ(𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I})).
Let 𝔠_{w,2,2}(p^m) be the open and closed formal subscheme of 𝔛_{K'} ×_{p_2,𝔛_{K''}} 𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^m) where Ker(p_2^*𝒢 → p_1^*𝒢) has trivial connected component. Let s_2 : 𝔠_{w,2,2}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^m) be induced by p_2, and let s_1 : 𝔠_{w,2,2}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) lift p_1. The lift exists because H_m is connected, so p_2^*𝒢 → p_1^*𝒢 maps p_2^*H_m isomorphically onto its image p_1^*H_m. Lemma 4.5.13: there is a normalized trace map p^{−1}Tr_{s_2} : R(s_2)_*O_{𝔠_{w,2,2}(p^m)} → O_{𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^m)}. At a closed point x of the interior, the fibre of s_2 parametrizes the étale subgroups of rank p of the kernel of the quasi-polarization 𝒢_w → 𝒢_w^D. That kernel is finite flat of rank p^2, an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative one. The map s_2 is totally inseparable of degree p at x, and by Serre–Tate theory the map of completed local rings is T_{i,v} ↦ T_{i,v} if v ≠ w or i = 1, 2, and T_{3,w} ↦ (1+T_{3,w})^p − 1.
The étale isogeny s_2^*𝒢 → s_1^*𝒢 gives isomorphisms s_1^*ω^κ → s_2^*ω^κ and s_1^*Ω^{κ_I} → s_2^*Ω^{κ_I}. These define U''_w ∈ Hom(RΓ(𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}), RΓ(𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I})). Define U_{w,2} := U'_w∘U''_w.
items.note: Missing. The declaration index has no Hida or Igusa declaration and none about Siegel modular varieties. No atlas stage plans Hecke operators at p for GSp_4 or mentions its Klingen or paramodular levels or higher Hida theory. This is split from the §4.5 item because §4.5.8 is cited on its own in §5.7 (pp. 128, 130), where U_{w,2} is analysed on the w-non-ordinary locus and identified with the square of the partial Frobenius, and its normalization p^{−3−l_w} is taken from here. The Serre–Tate computations use the Serre–Tate theorem (planned at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4) and the Serre–Tate local coordinates, which are planned nowhere; Lemma 4.5.9 uses the rigidity of groups of multiplicative type (a separate item). Misprints, the same in both versions: on p. 104 (published p. 278) 's_1 : 𝔠_{w,1,2}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m)' should read 𝔠_{w,2,2}(p^m); on p. 103 the base of the fibre product defining 𝔠_{w,2,2}(p^m) is printed 𝔛''_K for 𝔛_{K''}.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.15: the Hecke operators at p commute
items.statement: By §4.5.14, U_{v,1} means U_{Iw(v),1}. Lemma 4.5.15: the operators {U_{Kli(v),1}, U_{v,2}}_{v∈I} and {U_{v,1}, U_{v,2}}_{v∈I^c} commute with each other on RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli(p^∞)}, Ω^{κ_I}(−D)). Proof, as for Lemma 4.2.36: RΓ is computed by a complex L^• with L^k = lim_t L^k_t, where L^k_t = ⊕_{J⊂I,#J=k} colim_{×∏_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)} H^0(𝔛^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli(p^∞)}, Z/p^tZ ⊗ Ω^{κ_I}(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)^n)) (4.5.16). Here Ha(𝒢_w)^n lifts canonically to Z/p^tZ whenever p^{t−1} divides n, and such n are cofinal. Each term (4.5.16) is stable under the Hecke action and embeds into the corresponding colimit over the interior. There all the correspondences are finite flat, and commutativity follows from standard properties of the Iwahori and Klingen Hecke algebras.
items.note: Missing, for the same reasons as the operators themselves: no library or atlas stage has Hecke operators at p for GSp_4. This is split from the §4.5 item because it is cited separately in the proof of Lemma 5.8.2 (p. 133). The Cousin-type complex is that of §4.2.30 and Proposition 4.2.33.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.17: U_{Iw(w),1}(U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1}) = U_{w,2} on the ordinary locus at w
items.statement: If w ∈ I, then U_{Iw(w),1}(U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1}) = U_{w,2} as Hecke operators on RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I,=_w2}_{K,Kli(p^∞)}, Ω^{κ_I}(−D)), where =_w2 denotes the locus where 𝒢_w has p-rank 2. Proof: using a Cousin complex as in Lemma 4.5.15, one reduces to comparing the underlying correspondences away from the boundary. The correspondence of U_{Iw(w),1} parametrizes triples (𝒢, H_m, L) with L ⊂ 𝒢_w[p] étale, totally isotropic of degree p^2 and L ∩ H_m = 0. The correspondence of Z_w = U_{Kli(w),1} − U_{Iw(w),1} parametrizes triples (𝒢, H_m, M) with M ⊂ 𝒢_w[p] of multiplicative rank 1, totally isotropic of degree p^2 and M ∩ H_m = 0. As in [Pil20, Prop. 10.2.1], the correspondence of U_{w,2} parametrizes triples (𝒢, H_m, N) with N ⊂ 𝒢_w[p^2] totally isotropic of degree p^4, N[p] of degree p^3 and N ∩ H_m = 0. On the level of correspondences pU_{w,2} = U_{Iw(w),1}Z_w. The normalization factors of U_{w,2}, U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w are p^{−5}, p^{−3} and p^{−3}, and 5 + 1 = 3 + 3.
items.note: Missing: no library or atlas stage has these operators. This is split from the §4.5 item because it is cited separately three times: in the proof of Lemma 5.8.1 (p. 133), which gives U_{Iw(w),1}Z_w = U_{w,2} on the ordinary locus at w and underlies the doubling map of §5.8; in §7.9 (p. 217), where it gives (7.9.2) (U_{v,1} − c̃_v)(U_{v,1} − c̃'_v) = 0; and in §8.1 (p. 236). The decomposition U_{Kli(w),1} = U_{Iw(w),1} + p^{l_w−2}Z_w of §5.4 (p. 121, for l_w ≥ 2) is not this lemma: it follows from the definitions of U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w as the normalized étale and multiplicative parts of the correspondence of U_{Kli(w),1} over the ordinary locus at w. The lemma refers forward to U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w, which are defined in §§5.3–5.4.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1(3): the Hida complex specializes to Klingen-level ordinary cohomology
items.statement: Setting of Theorem 4.6.1(1)–(2): p ≠ 2 splits completely in F; K = K^pK_p is reasonable with K_p = G_1(Z_p); U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2}; M_I = e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)). Theorem 4.6.1(3): let κ = ((k_v,l_v)_{v|p}) be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 when v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1) for all v|p. Then there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} Z_p. Here K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v), so that 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K_p(I)K^p} = 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p) (§4.3.4), and ⊗_{Λ_I,κ} is base change along f_κ : Λ_I → Z_p. Proof: Lemma 4.6.25, together with Lemma 4.6.21, which shows that e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p), ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), ω^κ(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.locator: Theorem 4.6.1(3), §4.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 105, proof on p. 116 (published pp. 280 and 293)
items.note: Missing: nothing in the libraries or the atlas builds Hida complexes for GSp_4. This part is split from the theorem because it is used on its own. In §6.6 (p. 164), after inverting p, it gives M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p = e(U^I)RΓ(X^{G_1,mult}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)), which Propositions 6.6.1 and 6.6.2 use. The old item stated it only as 'a canonical isomorphism comparing the specialization of M_I with the ordinary part of the classical coherent cohomology'. For F = Q it is part of Pilloni's Theorem 11.3.1.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1(4): comparison with classical cohomology at spherical level in large weight
items.statement: Setting of Theorem 4.6.1(1)–(2). Theorem 4.6.1(4): there is a universal constant C, depending only on p (and on the fixed field F) but not on the tame level K^p, with the following property. Let κ = ((k_v,l_v)_{v|p}) be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 when v ∈ I, k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p − 1) for all v|p, k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v|p, and l_v ≥ C for all v ∈ I^c. Then the map e(∏_{v|p}T_v ∏_{v∈I^c}T_{v,1}) H^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) → H^i(M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} Z_p) is an isomorphism for i = 0 and injective for i = 1. Here T_v is the normalized Klingen-type Hecke operator at v|p (§3.9.20, Lemma 3.9.22) and T_{v,1} the normalized Siegel-type one (§3.9.17, Lemma 3.9.18). Proof: Theorem 4.2.1, together with Proposition 4.6.19 and Lemma 4.6.25.
items.locator: Theorem 4.6.1(4), §4.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 106, proof on p. 116 (published pp. 280 and 293)
items.note: Missing: nothing in the libraries or the atlas builds Hida complexes for GSp_4. The old item omitted this part entirely. It is used in the proof of Proposition 6.6.2 (p. 166): 'it follows from Theorem 4.6.1 that the map e(T^I)RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ(−D)) → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p is an isomorphism on H^0 and is injective on H^1'. The paper prints 'depending only on p'. The results the part is deduced from (Theorem 4.2.1, Propositions 4.6.9 and 4.6.19) say 'depending only on p and F'. Since F is fixed throughout, the two agree.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.9 with Lemmas 4.6.12–4.6.17: T-ordinary and U-ordinary H^0 on the p-rank strata agree
items.statement:
(§4.6.8) Fix J ⊂ I, and let J^c be its complement in S_p. The map X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1 → X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1} forgets the multiplicative subgroups H_v of order p at v ∈ J^c. It is finite étale of degree (p+1)^{#J^c}, and gives an injection H^0(X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)) → H^0(X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)). Standing assumptions of §4.6.8: l_v ≥ 3 for v ∈ I^c; k_v ≥ 3 and l_v ≥ 2 for v ∈ I; and l_v ≥ p+1 and k_v ≥ 2p+3 for v ∈ J. Then T_w (w|p) and T_{w,1} (w ∈ I^c) act on the source, and U_{w,2} (w|p) and U_{w,1} (w ∈ I^c) act on the target.
Proposition 4.6.9 (under these standing assumptions): there is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F but not on K^p, such that the following hold whenever l_w ≥ 2 for all w, k_w − l_w ≥ C for all w|p, and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ I^c. (1) U^I = ∏_{w|p}U_{w,2}∏_{w∈I^c}U_{w,1} is locally finite on H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)). (2) With T̃^I = ∏_{w|p}T_w∏_{w∈I^c}T_{w,1}, the map e(T̃^I)H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)) is an isomorphism. (3) This isomorphism is equivariant for T_{w,1} on the left and U_{w,1} on the right for all w ∈ I^c, and for T_w and U_{w,2} for all w ∈ J. Remark 4.6.10: the ordinarity condition prevents 'newforms' of Klingen level.
Ingredients. For w ∈ J^c, X_w parametrizes totally isotropic L_w ⊂ 𝒢_w[p^2] of étale rank p^3 and multiplicative rank p. The maps x_1 : X_w → (X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_K)_1 (forgetful, finite flat) and x_2 : 𝒢 ↦ 𝒢/L_w define T̃_w ∈ End H^0((X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_K)_1, ω^κ(−D)). This is promoted to T̃'_w and T̃''_w at the level Kli_w, which is Klingen at w only, in the commutative diagram (4.6.11). Lemma 4.6.12 ([Pil20, Lem. 11.1.1.1, 11.1.1.3]): if k_w − l_w ≥ 1, then (1) T̃_w = T_w and (2) U_{w,2}∘T̃''_w = U_{w,2}∘U_{w,2}. Lemma 4.6.13: for w ∈ J, the canonical map H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)) → H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)) intertwines T_w and U_{w,2}. Lemma 4.6.14: for w ∈ I^c, the same map intertwines T_{w,1} and U_{w,1}. Corollary 4.6.15: suppose l_w ≥ 2 and k_w − l_w ≥ 1 for all w ∈ J^c. Then ∏_{w∈J^c}U_{w,2} is locally finite on H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)), ∏_{w∈J^c}T̃_w is locally finite on H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)), and the map e(∏_{w∈J^c}T̃_w)H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)) → e(∏_{w∈J^c}U_{w,2})H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)) is surjective.
Let 𝔛^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_K and 𝔛^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p) be the formal completions of 𝔛^{G_1,I,=_{J^c}2}_K and 𝔛^{G_1,I,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p) along these strata of the special fibres. Their ideal of definition 𝓘 satisfies p ∈ 𝓘 and 𝓘/p = (Ha(𝒢_w) det ω_{𝒢_w}^{1−p}, w ∈ J). Their H^0 of ω^κ(−D) are 𝓘-adically complete, separated and Z_p-flat, and reduce modulo 𝓘 to the spaces above; higher cuspidal cohomology vanishes because these strata have affine image in the minimal compactification. The operator T̃_w lifts to them, and Tr is the trace of the finite étale map. Lemma 4.6.16: for n ≥ 1 and f ∈ H^0(𝔛^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_K, ω^κ(−D)), Tr∘(∏_{w∈J^c}U_{w,2})^n∘ι(f) ≡ p^{#J^c}(∏_{w∈J^c}T̃_w)^n(f) mod p^{inf_{w∈J^c}(k_w−l_w)}. Lemma 4.6.17: if k_w − l_w > p^{#J^c} for all w ∈ J^c, then the map e(∏_{w∈J^c}T̃_w)H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)) → e(∏_{w∈J^c}U_{w,2})H^0(X^{G_1,I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)) is bijective. Proposition 4.6.9 follows from Corollary 4.6.15, Lemma 4.6.17 and Lemmas 4.6.12–4.6.14.
items.note: Missing. No library or atlas stage has Hecke operators or Hasse-invariant strata for GSp_4. The old item gave only a summary of these results, without their hypotheses. The standing assumptions of §4.6.8 ask l_v ≥ p+1 and k_v ≥ 2p+3 for v ∈ J; this does not conflict with l_v = 2 on I in Theorem 4.6.1, because the proof of Proposition 4.6.19 applies the proposition to the twists by ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{n(p−1)}, whose weights at w ∈ J are (k_w + n(p−1), l_w + n(p−1)) with n ≥ 1. In Lemma 4.6.17 the hypothesis k_w − l_w > p^{#J^c} is stronger than the proof needs: the proof uses only inf_w(k_w − l_w) − #J^c ≥ 1, so k_w − l_w > #J^c suffices. The lemma as printed is true, so this is not a mistake. A subscript slip on p. 109 (published p. 283), the same in both versions: the space is printed X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K_p,Kli}(p)_1 for X^{I,=_J1,=_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1. The F = Q case is Pilloni's Corollaries 11.1.1.1–11.1.1.2.

items.name: Proposition 4.6.19: the T̃-ordinary and U-ordinary cohomology modulo p agree
items.statement: Proposition 4.6.19: there is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F but not on K^p, with the following property. If l_w ≥ 2 for all w, k_w − l_w ≥ C for all w|p, and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ I^c, then U^I is locally finite on RΓ(X^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)), and there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism e(T̃^I)RΓ(X^{I,G_1}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)RΓ(X^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D)), where T̃^I = ∏_{w|p}T_w∏_{w∈I^c}T_{w,1}. Proof: the complex K^• of §4.2.30 computes RΓ(X^{I,G_1}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D)), with K^k = ⊕_{J⊂I,#J=k} colim_{×∏_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)} H^0(X^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2}_{K,1}, ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)^n)). The analogous complex L^• computes the cohomology at level Kli(p). It therefore suffices to prove two things for each J ⊂ I and n ≥ 1: that U^I is locally finite on H^0(X^{G_1,I,≥_{J^c}2}_{K,Kli}(p)_1, ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)^n)), and that e(T̃^I) of the corresponding level-one term maps isomorphically to e(U^I) of it. The case n = 1 is Proposition 4.6.9. The general case follows by induction on n, using the exact sequences 0 → ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{(n−1)(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)^{n−1}) → ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)^n) → ω^κ(−D) ⊗ ⊗_{w∈J}(det 𝒢_w)^{n(p−1)}/(Σ_{w∈J}Ha(𝒢_w)) → 0 and the acyclicity of these sheaves (proof of Proposition 4.2.33).
items.note: Missing: no library or atlas stage has this. The old item mentioned it only by number. It is used in Lemma 4.6.23 and in the proof of Theorem 4.6.1(4).

items.name: Lemma 4.6.21: U^I lowers the Klingen level from p^n to p^{n−1}
items.statement: Let κ = ((k_v,l_v)_{v|p}) be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 when v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1) for all v|p. Then for each n ≥ 2 there is a map U^I : RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{Kli}(p^n), ω^κ(−D)) → RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{Kli}(p^{n−1}), ω^κ(−D)) (the diagonal of the square whose rows are U^I at levels p^n and p^{n−1} and whose columns are the pullbacks from level p^{n−1} to level p^n) such that: the pullback from level p^{n−1} followed by this map is U^I at level p^{n−1}, and this map followed by the pullback is U^I at level p^n. The proof is a computation in the Hecke algebra, as in the proof of [Pil20, Thm. 11.3.1]. Consequently, as the proof of Theorem 4.6.1 notes, the natural map e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p), ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), ω^κ(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.locator: Lemma 4.6.21 (§4.6.20), §4.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 114; its consequence is in the proof of Theorem 4.6.1, p. 116 (published pp. 291 and 293)
items.note: Missing: no library or atlas stage has this. The old item listed it by number only. It is needed for Theorem 4.6.1(3) and for Lemma 4.6.23.

items.name: Lemma 4.6.22, with Nakayama's lemma for maps: perfectness and amplitude of complexes of complete flat modules
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian ring with maximal ideal m. Lemma 4.6.22: let M^• be a bounded complex of m-adically complete and separated flat R-modules such that the cohomology groups of M^• ⊗_R R/m are finite-dimensional and concentrated in degrees [a, b]. Then M^• is a perfect complex concentrated in degrees [a, b]. Proof: [Pil20, Prop. 2.2.1] shows that M^• is perfect, and [KT17, Lem. 2.3, Cor. 2.7] shows that it is concentrated in degrees [a, b]. The paper uses it together with Nakayama's lemma for maps ([Pil20, Prop. 2.2.2], used in the proof of Lemma 4.6.23): a map f : M^• → N^• of bounded complexes of m-adically complete and separated flat R-modules is a quasi-isomorphism if f ⊗_R R/m is.
items.locator: Lemma 4.6.22 and the paragraph before it (§4.6.20), and the proof of Lemma 4.6.23, §4.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 114–115 (published pp. 291–292)
items.note: Planned. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 says: 'Define perfectness through local finite-projective resolutions; construct minimal representatives over local rings … Prove derived Nakayama and specialization/extension results under explicit derived completeness and finiteness hypotheses. Distinguish the amplitude of a chosen complex, Tor-amplitude and the degrees of nonzero cohomology.' DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 plans derived completeness and 'conservativity of reduction on derived complete objects'. A bounded complex of complete flat modules is derived complete, so Lemma 4.6.22 and Nakayama for maps are instances. The extraction of Pilloni's Duke 2020 paper records his Propositions 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 as planned at the same two layers. Neither library has perfect complexes: the declaration index has no perfect-complex, pseudo-coherent or amplitude declaration. The lemma is an item of its own because it is cited again in the proof of Proposition 7.8.11 (p. 215), over Λ_I[∏_{v∈Q∪R}T(k(v))], via its 'straightforward extension to the semi-local situation' (cf. [Nak84, Prop. 2]). That ring is finite over Λ_I, hence a finite product of complete local rings, so the extension follows factor by factor; the design job should state it in that form.

items.name: Lemmas 4.6.23–4.6.27: the integral comparison, the kernel Kω^κ, and perfectness in fixed weight and over Λ_I
items.statement:
Every complex below can be represented, via a Čech complex for a finite affine cover, by a bounded complex of flat, complete and separated Z_p-modules (resp. Λ_I-modules), so Lemma 4.6.22 applies.
Lemma 4.6.23: let κ = ((k_v,l_v)_{v|p}) be a classical algebraic weight with l_w ≥ 2 for all w, k_w − l_w ≥ C for all w|p and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ I^c, where C is as in Proposition 4.6.19. Then U^I is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), ω^κ(−D)), and there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism e(T̃^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_K, ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), ω^κ(−D)). The proof uses Proposition 4.6.19, [Pil20, Prop. 2.2.2, Prop. 2.3.1] and Lemma 4.6.21.
For a classical algebraic weight κ, let Kω^κ be the kernel of the surjection ω^κ → Ω^κ of Corollary 4.3.9 over 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), so that 0 → Kω^κ → ω^κ → Ω^κ → 0 is exact. Lemma 4.6.24: for any w|p, U_{w,2} ∈ p·End(RΓ(𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Kω^κ)); this follows from (4.5.12).
Lemma 4.6.25: let κ = ((k_v,l_v)_{v|p}) be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 when v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1) for all v|p. Then U^I is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), ω^κ(−D)) and on RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^κ(−D)), and the map e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p), ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^κ(−D)) is a quasi-isomorphism. In the proof, U^I is topologically nilpotent on the Kω^κ term of the exact triangle, by Lemma 4.6.24. Local finiteness holds in large weight by Lemma 4.6.23, and it is transported to all weights of the congruence class by [Pil20, Prop. 2.3.1].
Lemma 4.6.26: let κ be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 when v ∈ I, k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1) for all v|p, l_w ≥ 2 for all w, k_w − l_w ≥ C for all w|p (printed: for all w ∈ I; see the note) and l_w ≥ C for all w ∈ I^c. Then e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^κ(−D)) is a perfect complex of Z_p-modules concentrated in degrees [0, #I]. This follows from Lemmas 4.6.25 and 4.6.23 and Theorem 4.2.1, noting that T^I divides T̃^I, so that e(T̃^I)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^κ(−D)) is a direct summand of e(T^I)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^κ(−D)).
Lemma 4.6.27: U^I is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)), and e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K,Kli}(p^∞), Ω^{κ_I}(−D)) is a perfect complex of Λ_I-modules concentrated in degrees [0, #I]. This follows from Lemma 4.6.26 by Nakayama's lemma in the form of Lemma 4.6.22, together with [Pil20, Prop. 2.3.1].
items.note: Missing: no library or atlas stage has this. The old item listed these lemmas by number only. [Pil20, Prop. 2.3.1] characterizes local finiteness of an endomorphism of a bounded complex of complete flat modules by local finiteness on the cohomology of its reduction modulo the maximal ideal (§2.11 of the paper); since the weights of the congruence class have the same reduction modulo p, this carries local finiteness from one weight to all of them and to the family. Two points in the text, both the same in the published version. (a) The proof of Lemma 4.6.25 treats only level Kli(p^∞); the passage from Kli(p) to Kli(p^∞) in its displayed map is supplied by Lemma 4.6.21, as the proof of Theorem 4.6.1 says, so the printed '(p)' in that display may be intended as '(p^∞)'. The statement is correct either way. (b) Lemma 4.6.26 (p. 116; published p. 293) assumes k_w − l_w ≥ C only for w ∈ I, but its proof uses Lemma 4.6.23, which needs k_w − l_w ≥ C for all w|p, as do Proposition 4.6.19 and Theorem 4.6.1(4). The hypothesis should read 'for all w|p'. This appears to affect nothing: Lemma 4.6.27 uses Lemma 4.6.26 in a single weight, which can be chosen with k_w − l_w ≥ C at every w|p, and the printed statement is then recovered from Lemma 4.6.27 by specialization along f_κ.

items.name: Serre–Tate local moduli at points ordinary at w, and the local form of the p-isogeny correspondences
items.statement: Serre–Tate local moduli (N. Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli, LNM 868 (1981), §2, Theorem 2.1). Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and A_0/k an ordinary abelian variety of dimension g. For every artinian local W(k)-algebra R with residue field k and every deformation A/R of A_0, there is a Z_p-bilinear form q(A/R; −, −) : T_pA_0(k) × T_pA_0^t(k) → Ĝ_m(R) = 1 + m_R. The construction A ↦ q(A/R) identifies the deformation functor of A_0 with Hom_{Z_p}(T_pA_0(k) ⊗ T_pA_0^t(k), Ĝ_m), so the formal deformation space is a formal torus of dimension g^2 over W(k). A homomorphism f_0 : A_0 → B_0 lifts to A → B if and only if q(A; α, f_0^t(β)) = q(B; f_0(α), β) for all α ∈ T_pA_0(k) and β ∈ T_pB_0^t(k). Hence the deformations of A_0 with a lift of a principal polarization form the formal subtorus Hom(Sym^2 T_pA_0(k), Ĝ_m) of dimension g(g+1)/2.
items.locator: Used in the proofs of Lemma 4.5.4, Lemma 4.5.10 and Lemma 4.5.13, §4.5, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 100, 103 and 104 (published pp. 273, 276 and 278); external: N. Katz, 'Serre–Tate local moduli', Lecture Notes in Math. 868 (1981), §2
items.note: Missing. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4 plans only the Serre–Tate equivalence ('Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration'). It does not plan the canonical coordinates or the formal-torus structure. Tau Ceti ModularCurves 7F plans Serre–Tate theory only for elliptic curves (ST-1, Katz Theorem 1.2.1), and no stage plans Serre–Tate coordinates. Neither library has anything: the declaration index has no Serre–Tate declaration. The extractions of Pilloni's Duke 2020 paper and of Boxer–Pilloni 2026 record the same input as missing and route it to A4. The paper gives the computation for Lemma 4.5.13 only as 'a calculation in Serre–Tate theory which is similar to the proof of Lemma 4.5.10'. That lemma is at paramodular level at w, where the polarization is not principal at w, so the design job needs the version of the coordinates for the paramodular polarization type (as in Pilloni's (X, pZ; Z, Y) chart). Moreover its proof fixes an arbitrary interior point of 𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^m), not one ordinary at w: when w ∈ I such a point may have p-rank one at w, where 𝒢_w is not ordinary and Katz's coordinates do not apply as stated. The design job must supply the computation there, for example through a Serre–Tate parameter for the extension of the étale part of the kernel of the quasi-polarization by its multiplicative part, or by reducing to points ordinary at w.

items.name: Rigidity of finite groups of multiplicative type: the open and closed loci of the correspondences of §4.5
items.statement: Let S be a scheme or a p-adic formal scheme, H a finite locally free commutative group scheme of multiplicative type over S (étale locally a product of groups μ_{p^m}) and N a finite locally free commutative group scheme over S. By Cartier duality, Hom_S(H, N) = Hom_S(N^D, H^D) with H^D étale. Hence homomorphisms H → N lift uniquely along nilpotent thickenings, and hence over the completed local ring at a point, and the locus of S where a given homomorphism H → N vanishes is open and closed. The paper uses this, without a reference, for the correspondences of §4.5: the loci of the fibre products where the kernel of the canonical isogeny p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢 has trivial multiplicative part (𝔠_{w,1}(p^m), §4.5.1) or meets the multiplicative group p_1^*H_m trivially (𝔠_{Kli(w),1}(p^m), §4.5.6, and 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m), Lemma 4.5.9) are open and closed. In the proof of Lemma 4.5.9, the locus where L = p_1^*H_m ∩ Ker(p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢) is zero is open because L is finite over the fibre product, and closed because a non-trivial map p_1^*H_m|_x → Ker(p_1^*𝒢 → p_2^*𝒢)|_x at a point x extends over the completed local ring at x.
items.locator: §4.5.1 (p. 100), §4.5.6 (p. 101) and the proof of Lemma 4.5.9 (p. 102), arXiv:1812.09269v3 (published pp. 272–275); the paper cites no source (a standard one is SGA 3, Exp. IX–X)
items.note: Missing. Tau Ceti has Cartier duality for finite locally free bicommutative Hopf algebras over a commutative ring (TauCeti.FiniteLocallyFreeBicommutativeHopfAlgCat.cartierDuality, an anti-equivalence whose inverse is again finite dualization), and groups of multiplicative type only over a field (TauCeti.multiplicativeTypeCommHopfAlgProperty is defined over a field); neither library has rigidity in families. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 plans Cartier duality and finite flat subgroup constructions over general bases but does not name this rigidity. The extraction of Pilloni's Duke 2020 paper records the same input (used in his Lemma 10.2.1, the F = Q case of Lemma 4.5.9) as missing and routes it to R07.1. Every Hecke operator at p of §4.5 depends on it, so it is a key input rather than a proof step.

items.name: §5.4 and Lemma 5.4.1: the operators U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w on the w-ordinary locus and their relation to U_{Kli(w),1}
items.statement: With 𝔠_{Kli(w),1}, v_1, v_2 and Θ_κ as in Lemmas 5.3.1–5.3.2: let 𝔠^{=_w2}_{Kli(w),1} be the open formal subscheme where v_1^*𝒢_w (equivalently v_2^*𝒢_w) is ordinary; it restricts to a correspondence over 𝔛^{I,=_w2}. There the multiplicative rank of ker(v_1^*𝒢_w → v_2^*𝒢_w) is 0 or 1 (not 2, since H_w meets the kernel trivially), so 𝔠^{=_w2}_{Kli(w),1} = 𝔠^{=_w2,et}_{Kli(w),1} ⊔ 𝔠^{=_w2,m-et}_{Kli(w),1}, the loci where the isogeny v_1^*𝒢 → v_2^*𝒢 is étale, respectively where its kernel has multiplicative rank 1. Correspondingly the restriction of Θ_κ to 𝔛^{I,=_w2} is Θ_κ = Θ_κ^{et} + Θ_κ^{m-et}, and one defines the normalized cohomological correspondences U_{Iw(w),1} = p^{−3}Θ_κ^{et} and Z_w = p^{−l_w−1}Θ_κ^{m-et}.
