Lemma 5.4.1: U_{Iw(w),1} and Z_w are p-integral. Over the ordinary locus at w: U_{Kli(w),1} = U_{Iw(w),1} + p^{l_w−2}Z_w if l_w ≥ 2, and U_{Kli(w),1} = p^{2−l_w}U_{Iw(w),1} + Z_w if l_w ≤ 2. In particular U_{Kli(w),1} ≡ U_{Iw(w),1} mod p if l_w > 2, and U_{Kli(w),1} ≡ Z_w mod p if l_w < 2.
items.locator: §5.4 with Lemma 5.4.1 and the identities after it, together with the decomposition of 𝔠^{=_w2}_{Kli(w),1} after Lemma 5.3.1, arXiv pp. 120–121 (published pp. 298–299)
items.note: Split from item 66. §5.4 feeds Proposition 5.4.2, Corollary 5.4.5 and §5.8, while Lemma 5.3.2 is also used on its own in §4.5.6. No stage of the atlas, no decomposition and no draft roadmap plans parahoric-level Hecke correspondences for Hilbert–Siegel varieties. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 120–121. The decomposition of 𝔠^{=_w2} is on published p. 298, and §5.4 on p. 299.

items.name: §6.1.2: admissible formal schemes over O_{C_p} and formal Banach sheaves (flat, small)
items.statement: An admissible O_{C_p}-algebra is a flat O_{C_p}-algebra which is a quotient of a converging power series ring O_{C_p}⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ by a finitely generated ideal; an admissible formal scheme is a quasi-compact separated p-adic formal scheme over Spf O_{C_p} admitting an open covering by formal spectra of admissible algebras (a special case of the usual notion, as the paper notes). Following Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni, Def. A.1.1.1: a formal Banach sheaf on an admissible formal scheme 𝔖 is a family (𝔉_n)_{n≥0} of quasi-coherent sheaves such that (1) 𝔉_n is a sheaf of O_𝔖/p^n-modules, (2) 𝔉_n is flat over O_{C_p}/p^n, and (3) for all 0 ≤ m ≤ n there are isomorphisms 𝔉_n ⊗_{O_{C_p}} O_{C_p}/p^m ≅ 𝔉_m. It is identified with 𝔉 = lim_n 𝔉_n, since 𝔉_n = 𝔉 ⊗_{O_{C_p}} O_{C_p}/p^n. It is flat if every 𝔉_n is a flat O_𝔖/p^n-module. It is small if there is a coherent O_𝔖/p-module 𝔊 such that 𝔉_1 = colim_{j∈N}𝔉_{1,j} is an inductive limit of coherent sheaves whose successive quotients 𝔉_{1,j+1}/𝔉_{1,j} are direct summands of 𝔊.
items.locator: §6.1.2 (Recollections about formal Banach sheaves), arXiv pp. 139–140 (published p. 321); after Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), Def. A.1.1.1
items.note: Used in Theorem 6.1.3, in the definitions of 𝔊^{κ_A,w} and 𝔉^{κ_A,w} (§6.1.9) and in the proof of Theorem 6.2.6. AdicSpacesPartII R2 plans admissible formal schemes, admissible blow-ups and generic fibres, and R3 plans coherent sheaves and finite traces. Neither plans formal Banach sheaves or smallness. The extraction of Pilloni's paper (Duke Math. J. 169, 2020; merged, not yet reviewed) records the same definitions as missing and routes them by source to AdicSpacesPartII (R0, R2, R3). Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 139–140.

items.name: §6.1.4: the Hodge–Tate map at full level p^n on the toroidal formal model, Fargues' cokernel bound, and the modified model 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)} with ω^mod
items.statement: For a finite flat group scheme H → S, the Hodge–Tate map HT_H : H → ω_{H^D} (of fppf sheaves) sends x ∈ H(T), viewed through Cartier duality as a homomorphism H^D_T → G_{m,T}, to x^*(dt/t). Let K = K_pK^p be neat with K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(O_{F_v}). Let 𝔜_K and 𝔛_K be the p-adic formal schemes over O_{C_p} of Y_K and of a toroidal compactification X_K, and 𝒴_K ⊂ 𝒳_K their analytic adic spaces over Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}). For n = (n_v) ∈ Z_{≥0}^{S_p}, let K(p^n) = K_p(p^n)K^p with K_p(p^n) = ∏_v ker(GSp_4(O_{F_v}) → GSp_4(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v})). The map 𝒳_{K(p^n)} → 𝒳_K of analytic toroidal compactifications is finite flat, and 𝔛_{K(p^n)} and 𝔜_{K(p^n)}, the normalizations of 𝔛_K and 𝔜_K in 𝒳_{K(p^n)} and 𝒴_{K(p^n)}, are admissible formal schemes. Over 𝔜_{K(p^n)} there is a universal O_F-linear map ∏_v(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v})^4 → ∏_v 𝒢_v[p^{n_v}], symplectic up to a similitude factor and an isomorphism on analytic adic spaces. Composing it with HT (the quasi-polarization identifies 𝒢_v with 𝒢_v^D) gives HT : ∏_v(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v})^4 → ∏_v ω_{𝒢_v}/p^{n_v}. This map extends over 𝔛_{K(p^n)}: for F = Q by Pilloni–Stroh, Prop. 1.2, and in general by the Koecher principle of Lan, Thm. 8.7. By Fargues (Thm. 7; see also Pilloni–Stroh, Thm. 1.5) the cokernel of its linearization is killed by p^{1/(p−1)}. Let 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)} → 𝔛_{K(p^n)} be the normalization of the blow-up of the following ideal: locally, after trivializing ω_𝒢, it is the product over v|p of the ideals generated by the 2 × 2 minors of the 2 × 4 matrix of local lifts to ω_𝒢 of the Hodge–Tate classes at v. This is an admissible formal scheme. Let ω^mod_𝒢 ⊂ ω_𝒢 be the subsheaf generated by p^{1/(p−1)}ω_𝒢 and local lifts of the image of HT; it becomes locally free after pullback to 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)}. Then: (1) ω^mod_𝒢 is a locally free O_F ⊗ O_{𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)}}-module of rank 2; (2) p^{1/(p−1)}ω_𝒢 ⊂ ω^mod_𝒢 ⊂ ω_𝒢; (3) HT factors through ∏_v ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{n_v−1/(p−1)}ω^mod_{𝒢_v}, and its linearization ∏_v(O_{F_v}/p^{n_v})^4 ⊗ O → ∏_v ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{n_v−1/(p−1)} is surjective.
items.locator: §6.1.4 (Recollections about the Hodge–Tate period map), arXiv pp. 140–141 (published pp. 322–323); Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), Thm. 7; Pilloni–Stroh, Ann. Math. Qué. 40 (2016), Prop. 1.2, Thm. 1.5 and §1.4; Lan, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2017, Thm. 8.7
items.note: Split from item 77, whose statement described 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) as defined by degrees of canonical subgroups. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 plans the finite-level Hodge–Tate map through Cartier duality and semi-abelian degeneration charts, but no estimate for the cokernel and no modified lattice. T5 plans the Hilbert lattice ω^int of Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, not this lattice on the normalized blow-up of the ideal of 2 × 2 minors. ShimuraCompactifications C6 plans Koecher only for Hilbert sections. Item 145 (outside this cluster) claims that T2 and T5 plan ω^mod, and that claim should be revisited. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 140–141.

items.name: §6.1.4 and Lemma 6.1.5: the neighbourhoods 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) and the canonical filtration Fil^can_v
items.statement: Notation of the item on the Hodge–Tate map at level p^n and ω^mod. Let e_{v,1}, …, e_{v,4} be the canonical basis of O_{F_v}^4 and ε = (ε_v) ∈ ∏_{v|p}([0, n_v − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q). The admissible formal scheme 𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε) → 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)}, an open subscheme of an admissible blow-up of 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)}, is defined by the conditions HT(e_{v,1}) ∈ p^{ε_v}ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{n_v−1/(p−1)} for all v|p and HT(e_{v,2}) ∈ p^{ε_v}ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{n_v−1/(p−1)} for all v ∈ I^c. On it, for v ∈ I^c, HT ⊗ 1 : (O/p^{ε_v})e_{v,3} ⊕ (O/p^{ε_v})e_{v,4} → ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{ε_v} is an isomorphism (O = O_{𝔛_{K(p^n)}(ε)}). For all v|p let Fil^can_v ⊂ ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{ε_v} be the submodule generated by HT(e_{v,2}) and HT(e_{v,3}). Lemma 6.1.5: Fil^can_v is a locally free O/p^{ε_v}-module of rank one and locally a direct factor of ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/p^{ε_v}ω^mod_{𝒢_v}. With Gr^can_v = ω^mod_{𝒢_v}/(p^{ε_v}ω^mod_{𝒢_v} + Fil^can_v), HT ⊗ 1 : (O/p^{ε_v})e_{v,4} → Gr^can_v is an isomorphism for all v|p, and HT ⊗ 1 : (O/p^{ε_v})e_{v,3} → Fil^can_v is an isomorphism for v ∈ I^c.
items.locator: §6.1.4 (end) with Lemma 6.1.5, arXiv pp. 141–142 (published pp. 323–324); Pilloni, Lem. 12.2.2.1
items.note: Split from item 77. These are cut out by Hodge–Tate conditions, not by degrees of canonical subgroups. No stage plans formal neighbourhoods of this kind on Hilbert–Siegel varieties or the filtration Fil^can. The Pilloni extraction records the Siegel versions (𝔛(p^n, ε), Fil^can and Lemma 12.2.2.1) as missing. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 141–142.

items.name: §6.2.1 and Remark 6.2.2: the minimal compactification at level p^n, the descent of Λ^2HT and the modified model 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} with det ω^mod
items.statement: Take n_v = n for all v. Let 𝔛^*_K be the minimal compactification of 𝔜_K, to which det ω_𝒢 descends as an invertible sheaf, and 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)} the Stein factorization of 𝔛_{K(p^n)} → 𝔛^*_K, a normal admissible formal scheme. (i) (Pilloni–Stroh, Cor. 1.4.) The determinant of the Hodge–Tate map on 𝔛_{K(p^n)}, Λ^2HT : ⊗_{v|p}Λ^2(O_{F_v}/p^nO_{F_v})^4 → ⊗_{v|p}det ω_{𝒢_v}/p^n, is the pullback of a map of the same form defined over 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}. Remark 6.2.2: literally, the determinant of HT is Λ^{2[F:Q]}(O_F/p^n)^4 → det ω_𝒢/p^n; using the O_F-action it factors through the direct factor ⊗_{v|p}Λ^2(O_{F_v}/p^n)^4. (ii) (Pilloni–Stroh §1.4 for F = Q, and the same construction in general.) There is a normal admissible formal scheme 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} → 𝔛^*_{K(p^n)}. It is the normalization of the blow-up of the ideal which is locally the product over v|p of the ideals generated by the coefficients at v of a local lift ⊗_vΛ^2(O_{F_v}^4) ⊗ O → ⊗_v det ω_{𝒢_v} of Λ^2HT. It carries a locally free modification det ω^mod_𝒢 ⊂ det ω_𝒢 such that (1) p^{2[F:Q]/(p−1)}det ω_𝒢 ⊂ det ω^mod_𝒢 ⊂ det ω_𝒢, and (2) Λ^2HT factors into a surjection ⊗_vΛ^2(O_{F_v}/p^n)^4 ⊗ O → det ω^mod_𝒢/p^{n−2[F:Q]/(p−1)}. By the universal properties of blow-ups and normalizations there is a map 𝔛^mod_{K(p^n)} → 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)}.
items.locator: §6.2.1 with Remark 6.2.2, arXiv pp. 143–144 (published p. 326); Pilloni–Stroh, Ann. Math. Qué. 40 (2016), Cor. 1.4 and §1.4
items.note: Part of the external input to Lemma 6.2.3 and Theorem 6.2.6 (item 78), split from the proposed §6.2.1 item. No stage plans the Stein factorization at level p^n with the descent of Λ^2HT, or the modified determinant on the minimal compactification. The Pilloni extraction records the Siegel versions as missing: the minimal compactification 𝔛(p^n)^⋆ with the descent of Λ^2HT, and 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} with det ω^mod. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 143–144.

items.name: §6.2.1: the models 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)} with ample det ω^mod and sections approximating ⊗HT(e_{v,i})∧HT(e_{v,j}) (Scholze; Pilloni–Stroh)
items.statement: (Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties, proof of Thm. 4.3.1, pp. 1029–30, as cited; Pilloni–Stroh, Thm. 1.16.) Notation of the item on 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)}. There is an integer N such that for all n ≥ N there are a normal admissible formal scheme 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)} and a projective map 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} → 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}, an isomorphism on the associated analytic spaces, with the following properties. (1) det ω^mod_𝒢 descends to an ample invertible sheaf on 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}. (2) For every rational ε > 0 there is n(ε) ≥ N such that, for n ≥ n(ε), there are sections s_{(i_v,j_v)_{v|p}} ∈ H^0(𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}, det ω^mod_𝒢) with s_{(i_v,j_v)} = ⊗_{v|p}HT(e_{v,i_v}) ∧ HT(e_{v,j_v}) in det ω^mod_𝒢/p^ε, for all 1 ≤ i_v, j_v ≤ 4.
items.locator: §6.2.1, arXiv pp. 144–145 (published p. 327); Scholze, Ann. of Math. 182 (2015), Thm. 4.3.1 and pp. 1029–30; Pilloni–Stroh, Ann. Math. Qué. 40 (2016), Thm. 1.16
items.note: Split from the proposed §6.2.1 item. PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S1 plans Scholze's Siegel construction up to the minimal compactification, and S3 plans the extension of the Hodge–Tate period map to compactifications. Neither describes these finite-level models with an ample det ω^mod and sections approximating the Plücker coordinates of HT, and neither treats the Hilbert–Siegel case. The Pilloni extraction records the Siegel model 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} as missing. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 144–145.

items.name: §§6.3.9–6.3.12, Remark 6.3.10 and Lemmas 6.3.13–6.3.14: the operators U_{v,2}, U_{v,1} and U_{v,1}U_{v,2} on overconvergent cohomology and the compactness of U^I
items.statement: For v ∈ I: s_1 : 𝒞_{v,2} → 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) parametrizes isogenies A → A' whose kernel on p-divisible groups is a totally isotropic M_v ⊂ 𝒢_v[p^2], locally isomorphic to (O_{F_v}/p)^2 ⊕ O_{F_v}/p^2, with M_v ∩ H_{v,n_v} = 0. The map s_2 : 𝒞_{v,2} → 𝒳_{K(I,p^{n'})}(ε') (n'_v = n_v + 1, ε'_v = ε_v + 1, other entries unchanged) sends (A, A') to A' with the images of H_{v',n_{v'}} (v' ≠ v) and of L_{v',n_{v'}} (v' ∈ I^c) and with H'_{v,n_v+1} = Im(p^{−1}H_{v,n_v}); that s_2 lands there is checked as in Pilloni, Lem. 13.2.1.1. U_{v,2} on RΓ(𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ (det ω_𝒢)^2(−D)) is the composite of three steps. First, restriction from level (n', ε', w'), where w'_v = w_v + 1. Second, the natural map s_2^*ℱ^{κ_A,w'} → s_1^*ℱ^{κ_A,w} (Pilloni, Lem. 13.2.2.1), tensored with p^{−2} times the natural map on (det ω_𝒢)^2(−D). Third, p^{−3}Tr_{s_1}. For v ∈ I^c, work étale-locally in a symplectic isomorphism 𝒢_v[p^∞] ≅ (F_v/O_{F_v})^4 with H_{v,n_v} = ⟨p^{−n_v}e_{v,1}⟩ and L_{v,n_v} = ⟨p^{−n_v}e_{v,1}, p^{−n_v}e_{v,2}⟩. For U_{v,2}, s_1 : 𝒞_{v,2} → 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) parametrizes isogenies whose kernel M_v ⊂ 𝒢_v[p^2] is totally isotropic, locally isomorphic to (O_{F_v}/p)^2 ⊕ O_{F_v}/p^2 and generated by p^{−1}e_{v,2}, p^{−1}e_{v,3}, p^{−2}e_{v,4}. Here s_2 lands at the same level 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε): H'_{v,n_v} is generated by the image of p^{−n_v}e_{v,1}, and L'_{v,n_v} by the images of p^{−n_v}e_{v,1} and p^{−n_v−1}e_{v,2}, and these depend only on M_v, H_{v,n_v} and L_{v,n_v}. U_{v,2} is again built from the natural map on ℱ^{κ_A,w} tensored with p^{−2} times the map on (det ω_𝒢)^2(−D), followed by p^{−3}Tr_{s_1}, with no change of level. U_{v,1} (v ∈ I^c) comes from t_1 : 𝒞_{v,1} → 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), parametrizing isogenies with totally isotropic kernel M_v ⊂ 𝒢_v[p], isomorphic to (O_{F_v}/p)^2 and meeting L_{v,n_v} trivially. Here t_2 lands at the same level, the map on (det ω_𝒢)^2(−D) is not renormalized, and the trace is p^{−3}Tr_{t_1}. Remark 6.3.10: for v ∈ I^c, U_{v,2} alone does not improve analyticity and convergence in the v-direction, as it visibly does for v ∈ I, but U_{v,1}U_{v,2} does. The composite comes from the correspondence u_1 : 𝒞_v → 𝒳_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) of isogenies whose kernel M_v ⊂ 𝒢_v[p^3] is totally isotropic, locally isomorphic to O_{F_v}/p ⊕ O_{F_v}/p^2 ⊕ O_{F_v}/p^3 and generated by p^{−1}e_{v,2}, p^{−2}e_{v,3}, p^{−3}e_{v,4}. The map u_2 sends (A, A') to A', with H'_{v,n_v+1} generated by the image of p^{−n_v−1}e_{v,1} and L'_{v,n_v+1} by the images of p^{−n_v−1}e_{v,1} and p^{−n_v−2}e_{v,2}. The normalizations are p^{−2} on (det ω_𝒢)^2(−D) and p^{−6}Tr. Lemma 6.3.13: the image of u_2 lies in 𝒳_{K(I,p^{n'})}(ε'), where n'_v = n_v + 1 and ε'_v = ε_v + 1. Set U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2}. Lemma 6.3.14: U^I acting on C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) is compact. Moreover, with n+1 = (n_v + 1), ε+1 = (ε_v + 1) and w+1 = (w_v + 1), there is a map Ũ^I : C_cusp(G_1, n+1, ε+1, w+1, …) → C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, …) with the following property: U^I on C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, …) is Ũ^I composed with restriction, and U^I on C_cusp(G_1, n+1, ε+1, w+1, …) is restriction composed with Ũ^I. The restriction map is compact by a Čech argument, as in Pilloni, Lem. 13.2.4.1.
items.locator: §§6.3.9–6.3.12 with Remark 6.3.10 and Lemmas 6.3.13 and 6.3.14, arXiv pp. 149–152 (published pp. 332–336)
items.note: Split from item 79. Lemma 6.3.14 is used on its own: in §6.3.15 (finite-dimensionality of e(U^I)H^i_cusp and Theorem 6.3.16), in Lemma 6.5.4 and in §6.6. The atlas plans a compact U_p on overconvergent Hilbert modular forms (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O6). It does not plan these correspondences for GSp_4 over F with Klingen reduction at I and Borel reduction at I^c. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 149–152.

items.name: Proposition 6.3.7: overconvergent locally analytic cuspidal cohomology vanishes outside [0, #I]
items.statement: Proposition 6.3.7. For A a normal admissible O_{C_p}-algebra and κ_A a w'-analytic character as in §6.1.9, H^i_cusp(†, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) = colim_{n,ε,w}H^i(C_cusp(n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p})) vanishes for i ∉ [0, #I]. It follows from Theorem 6.2.6. Hence the same holds for the direct factor H^i_cusp(G_1, †, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}), the form used in Proposition 6.6.2.
items.locator: Proposition 6.3.7 (§6.3.5), arXiv p. 148 (published p. 331)
items.note: Split from item 79. It is used on its own in the proof of Proposition 6.6.2, the equality of Euler characteristics (arXiv p. 165). The last sentence is an immediate consequence and is not printed. No stage plans the proposition.

items.name: §6.1.1: compact endomorphisms of perfect complexes of projective Banach modules, their characteristic series, and Coleman's local constancy of slope-zero dimensions
items.statement: (§6.1.1, second paragraph.) Let A be a C_p-Banach algebra; in the applications it is an affinoid algebra of weight space. An endomorphism U of a perfect complex of A-modules is compact if it has a representative Ũ, an endomorphism of a bounded complex M^• of projective Banach A-modules, which is compact in each degree. The product over i of the characteristic power series det(1 − XŨ | M^i) defines the spectral variety of Ũ (Coleman). The input to Theorem 6.3.16 is Coleman [Col97, §A5], used as in Pilloni §13.4: over affinoids of weight space, the dimensions of the slope-zero parts of the terms of such a complex are locally constant in the weight.
items.locator: §6.1.1, second paragraph, arXiv p. 139 (published p. 320), and the proof of Theorem 6.3.16, arXiv p. 153 (published p. 337); Coleman, Invent. Math. 127 (1997), Part A and §A5; Pilloni, §13
items.note: Split from item 147 and from the proposed single item on complexes. LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 plans compact operators and Fredholm determinants on a single (Pr) Banach module. It does not plan compact endomorphisms of bounded complexes of projective Banach modules up to homotopy. The Pilloni extraction records K^proj(A) with compact endomorphisms, and Coleman's local constancy of slope dimensions, as missing. It routes both by source to L4 and treats the product characteristic series as planned there. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 139 and 153.

items.name: §6.1.1 and the proof of Theorem 6.3.16: the spectral variety of a compact endomorphism of a perfect complex, its slope decompositions, and the interpolating perfect complex
items.statement: (§6.1.1, second paragraph, and the proof of Theorem 6.3.16.) Let U, Ũ and M^• be as in the item on compact endomorphisms of perfect complexes. M^• determines a complex of coherent sheaves ℳ^• over the spectral variety of Ũ. The spectral variety of U is defined to be the support of the cohomology sheaves H^•(ℳ^•). It does not depend on the choice of M^• and Ũ, and over it the sheaves H^•(ℳ^•) admit slope decompositions (Urban §2; Pilloni §13). The proof of Theorem 6.3.16 applies this to U^I acting on C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ_A ⊗ (2,2)_{v|p}) over affinoids of weight space. A perfect complex C^• over the spectral variety interpolates the complexes C_cusp(G_1, n, ε, w, κ), and together with the local constancy of the slope-zero dimensions of the C^i this gives Theorem 6.3.16 (item 80).
items.locator: §6.1.1, second paragraph, arXiv p. 139 (published p. 320), and the proof of Theorem 6.3.16, arXiv p. 153 (published p. 337); Urban, Ann. of Math. 174 (2011), §2; Pilloni, §§13.1 and 13.4
items.note: Split from item 147 and from the proposed single item on complexes. PadicFamilies L2a plans the Fredholm hypersurface of a compact operator on one module and its admissible cover by slope blocks. It does not plan the spectral variety as the support of the cohomology of a complex, its independence of the representative, or the local constancy of slope Euler characteristics. The Pilloni extraction records these (its spectral varieties Z̃ and Z, and Proposition 13.1.3.1) as missing and routes them by source to PadicFamilies (L0a, L2a). Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 139 and 153.

items.name: §6.5.2: the degree functions deg_v and the neighbourhoods 𝒳(J) of the multiplicative locus
items.statement: §6.5.2. Let K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v) and 𝒳_{K^pK_p(I)} the analytic space of X_{K_p(I)K^p}. For each v|p there is an isogeny 𝒢 → 𝒢' whose kernel is a quasi-finite group scheme H_v of order p away from the boundary. For each v ∈ I^c there is also an isogeny whose kernel L_v is of order p^2 away from the boundary. Let x be a rank one point, with valuation v_x normalized by v_x(p) = 1, and let δ be as in §6.5.1 (item 144). Set deg_v(x) = v_x(δ_{H_v}) ∈ [0,1] for v ∈ I, deg_v(x) = v_x(δ_{L_v}) ∈ [0,2] for v ∈ I^c, and deg = (deg_v)_v : 𝒳^{rk1}_{K^pK_p(I)} → [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c}. For each rational interval J ⊂ [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c} there is a unique quasi-compact open 𝒳_{K^pK_p(I)}(J) whose rank one points are deg^{−1}(J). The multiplicative locus is 𝒳^mult = 𝒳({1}^I × {2}^{I^c}). For (ε_v) ∈ ([0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c}) ∩ Q^{S_p}, set 𝒳((ε_v)) = 𝒳(∏_{v∈I}[1 − ε_v, 1] × ∏_{v∈I^c}[2 − ε_v, 2]). Then 𝒳^mult = 𝒳((0)_v), and the spaces 𝒳((ε_v)) with all ε_v → 0^+ form a fundamental system of strict neighbourhoods of 𝒳^mult. All these spaces are stable under the action of (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} on the polarization, and they descend to open subspaces of 𝒳^{G_1}_{K^pK_p(I)}.
items.locator: §6.5.2 (Neighbourhoods of the ordinary locus), arXiv pp. 154–155 (published pp. 339–340)
items.note: Split from the proposed item 144, so that the general degree (§6.5.1) and these Hilbert–Siegel neighbourhoods are each routed once. No stage plans them. §6.5 then studies how the Hecke correspondences move these degrees (item 83). A lead for the review of §6.5, outside this cluster: §6.5.2 defines 𝒳((ε_v)) through the upper intervals [1 − ε_v, 1] and [2 − ε_v, 2]. But §6.5.3 and Lemma 6.5.4 use tuples (ε_v) ∈ [1 − 1/p, 1)^I × [2 − 1/p, 2)^{I^c}, and entries tending to 1 and 2, as lower degree bounds. Checked on the page images of arXiv pp. 154–155.

items.name: The sheaf 𝓕^{κ,w^-} (§6.4)
items.statement: For a weight κ and an analyticity radius w as in §6.3, 𝓕^{κ,w^-} := colim_{w'<w} 𝓕^{κ,w'}. This is the direct limit, over w' < w, of the sheaves 𝓕^{κ,w'} of w'-analytic sections on the spaces 𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) of §6.3.
items.locator: §6.4, the sentence before Proposition 6.4.2, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 153 (published version p. 337)
items.note: The proof of Proposition 6.4.2 explains why the sheaf is needed. The BGG resolution of Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni §7.2 contains 'a minor error', which is corrected by replacing 𝓕^{κ,w} with 𝓕^{κ,w^-}. The sheaf is used in Proposition 6.4.2, in the Hecke-action paragraph after it and in the proof of Corollary 6.4.3. Since w'-analytic sections are w-analytic for w' < w, there are inclusions ω^κ ⊂ 𝓕^{κ,w^-} ⊂ 𝓕^{κ,w}. Status missing: there is no locally analytic sheaf of this kind in the libraries or the atlas, and PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (ℱ^{k,w^-}) as missing.

items.name: Proposition 6.4.2: the relative analytic BGG resolution
items.statement:
Proposition 6.4.2. Let κ = ((k_v,l_v))_{v|p} be a dominant algebraic weight with l_v = 2 if v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p − 1); the print has 'k_v = l_v = 2 mod (p−1)'. There is a relative analytic BGG resolution, an exact sequence of sheaves
  0 → ω^κ(−D) → 𝓕^{κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) → ⊕_{s∈W^{(1)}} 𝓕^{s•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) → ⋯ → ⊕_{s∈W^{(d)}} 𝓕^{s•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) → 0.
Here:
- W is the Weyl group of GL_2(F ⊗_Q Q_p). Since p splits completely in F, it equals ∏_{v|p}{1_v, w_v} with ℓ(w_v) = 1.
- W^{(i)} is the set of elements of length i, and d = #S_p is the maximal length.
- • is the twisted (dot) Weyl action.
The sheaves live on the spaces 𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε) of §6.3, where Corollary 6.4.3 uses the resolution.
items.locator: Proposition 6.4.2, §6.4, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 153 (published version p. 338)
items.note:
Proof in the paper: it is a relative version of the main result of Jones, An analogue of the BGG resolution for locally analytic principal series, J. Number Theory 131 (2011). It is proved in Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni, p-adic families of Siegel modular cuspforms, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), §7.2, after replacing 𝓕^{κ,w} there by 𝓕^{κ,w^-}.
Status missing:
- Tau Ceti has Verma modules (TauCeti.VermaModule) but no BGG resolution and no locally analytic induction.
- Layer 6 of the Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight roadmap says explicitly: 'Do not invoke a full BGG resolution'.
- No atlas layer plans a locally analytic BGG resolution.
- PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q case (its Prop. 13.3.2.1) as missing.

items.name: Hecke actions on the BGG resolution and the twist of U_{v,2} by p^{k_v−l_v+1}
items.statement:
Let κ be as in Proposition 6.4.2.
(a) From the paragraph between Proposition 6.4.2 and Corollary 6.4.3: the actions of U_{v,1} and U_{v,2} by cohomological correspondences on 𝓕^{κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) restrict to actions on the subsheaf ω^κ(−D), and the action of U^I on the cohomology is compact.
(b) From the proof of Corollary 6.4.3, citing Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni §7.3. For J ⊂ S_p let w_J = ∏_{v∈J}w_v. The differential from ⊕_{s∈W^{(i)}} to ⊕_{s∈W^{(i+1)}} in Proposition 6.4.2 is the product of the maps θ_{s,s'} : 𝓕^{s•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D) → 𝓕^{s'•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D), for s = w_J with #J = i and s' = w_{J∪{v}} with v ∉ J.
- On cohomology, θ_{s,s'} is equivariant for U_{w,i} (w ≠ v) and for U_{v,1}.
- θ_{s,s'} ∘ U_{v,2} = p^{(k_v−l_v)+1} U_{v,2} ∘ θ_{s,s'}. The print has U_{v,2} ∘ θ_{s,s'} = p^{(k_v−l_v)+1} θ_{s,s'} ∘ U_{v,2}; see the note.
Equivalently, the spectral sequence of the resolution is Hecke-equivariant when the standard action of U_{v,2} on H^i(𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), 𝓕^{w_J•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D)) is multiplied by p^{k_v−l_v+1} for v ∈ J.
items.locator: §6.4, the paragraph after Proposition 6.4.2 and the proof of Corollary 6.4.3, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 153–154 (published version pp. 338–339)
items.note:
Why the order of composition is corrected: the printed relation does not fit the sentence that follows it. With the printed relation, θ_{s,s'} is equivariant only if the target action is multiplied by p^{−(k_v−l_v+1)}, not by p^{k_v−l_v+1}. Only the corrected relation gives the conclusion used, that on the terms with s ≠ 1 the twisted slopes are raised by k_v − l_v + 1. A one-variable model confirms it: a (k+1)-st derivative D satisfies D(f(pz)) = p^{k+1}(Df)(pz).
PAPER-PILLONI-20/E119 records the same slip in Pilloni 2020, Prop. 13.3.3.1. There the exponent is printed with the wrong sign, which is equivalent to the reversed order here.
Status missing: nothing in the libraries, and no layer plans the Hecke equivariance of analytic BGG differentials. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q case as missing.

items.name: Corollary 6.4.3: ordinary classical and ordinary locally analytic cohomology agree in degree 0 (and in degree 1 in regular weight)
items.statement:
Corollary 6.4.3. Let κ = ((k_v,l_v))_{v|p} be a dominant algebraic weight with l_v = 2 if v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 mod (p − 1). Consider the natural map
  e(U^I)H^i(𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)H^i(𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), 𝓕^{κ,w} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D)),
where U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2} and e(U^I) is its ordinary projector.
- It is an isomorphism for i = 0 and injective for i = 1.
- It is an isomorphism for i = 1 if moreover k_v − l_v ≥ 3 for all v|p.
items.locator: Corollary 6.4.3, §6.4, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 153–154 (published version pp. 338–339)
items.note:
Proof in the paper:
- Proposition 6.4.2 gives the spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = ⊕_{s∈W^{(p)}} H^q(𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), 𝓕^{s•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_𝓖)^2(−D)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), ω^κ(−D)).
- The Hecke twist of the preceding item makes it equivariant.
- Under the stated hypotheses the ordinary projector kills E_1^{p,q} for p ≥ 1, by Proposition 6.4.1. The print says 'for p > 1' (sourceIssues E84, a misprint that affects nothing), but E_1^{1,0} must also be killed for the H^0 isomorphism and the H^1 injectivity.
The corollary is used in Proposition 6.6.2 and Theorem 6.6.4.
On sourceIssues E2 (𝓕^{κ,w} for 𝓕^{κ,w^-}): the spectral sequence in the proof must be the w^- one. The printed statement with 𝓕^{κ,w} is not evidently wrong: the map factors through 𝓕^{κ,w^-}, and the usual improvement of analyticity (Lemma 6.3.14) identifies the finite slope parts of w^-- and w-analytic cohomology. sourceIssues E83 records a gap in the proof of the i = 1 isomorphism. Proposition 6.4.1 bounds the slopes of each factor of U^I separately, and U^I has N = #I + 2#I^c factors, so the argument gives the i = 1 isomorphism only when k_v − l_v ≥ 3N. The threshold 3 would need a slope bound for U^I itself. Proposition 6.6.2 can take its constant C ≥ 3N.
Status missing: nothing in the libraries or the atlas. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (its Cor. 13.3.3.1) as missing.

items.name: §6.5.1: Fargues' degree and the section δ_H of an isogeny
items.statement:
§6.5.1, after Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010) and Ann. Sci. ÉNS 44 (2011). Let K be a complete valued extension of Q_p whose valuation v is normalized by v(p) = 1.
- Let M be a finitely presented torsion O_K-module, M ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^r O_K/x_i. Then deg M := Σ_{i=1}^r v(x_i). The print has Σ v(x_i mod p) with v : O_K/pO_K → [0,1]; see the note.
- For a group scheme H over O_K, ω_H is the conormal sheaf along the identity section. If H is finite flat, then ω_H is finitely presented and torsion, and deg H := deg ω_H.
More generally, let A → A' be an isogeny of semi-abelian schemes over an analytic adic space S, with p-divisible groups 𝓖 → 𝓖'.
- ω_𝓖 and ω_{𝓖'} are the conormal sheaves along the unit sections.
- ω^+_𝓖 and ω^+_{𝓖'} are the subsheaves of integral differentials, those that locally on S come from a formal model.
- H is the kernel of 𝓖 → 𝓖', a quasi-finite group scheme.
Attached to the isogeny is a section δ_H of det ω_{𝓖'} ⊗ det ω_𝓖^{−1}, lying in (det ω_{𝓖'})^+ ⊗ (det ω_𝓖^{−1})^+. For x ∈ S the norm |δ_H|_x, computed in a local trivialization of that integral sheaf, does not depend on the trivialization. Suppose x is a rank one point with v_x(p) = 1, and H_x ⊂ 𝓖_x extends to a finite flat group scheme on a formal model 𝔊_x of 𝓖_x over Spec k(x)^+. Then v_x(δ_H) = deg H_x.
items.locator: §6.5.1 (Fargues' degree function), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 154 (published version p. 339)
items.note:
On the printed truncation 'v(x_i mod p)': the paper applies deg to groups that p does not kill. In Lemma 6.5.12 it applies it to M_{1,w} ⊂ 𝓖_w[p^2], where 'deg M_w ≤ 3 − 2ε' is a real condition. In the proof of Proposition 6.5.22 it applies it to M_{w,n} ⊂ 𝓖_w[p^n] and uses deg M_{w,n} = Σ_i deg M_{w,i}/M_{w,i−1} ≤ n(1 − ε''). The truncated sum is at most the number of cyclic summands of ω_M, which is at most 2 here, and it is not additive. With it, Lemma 6.5.12(6) at ε = 1/2 would hold at every point. The meaning is Fargues' degree Σ v(x_i).
Status missing:
- No Mathlib or Tau Ceti declaration defines the degree of a finite flat group scheme.
- HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0, T3 and T4 do not mention it. Item 144 of this extraction says the degree is 'the measure used' in T3 and T4, but their descriptions do not plan it.
- PAPER-PILLONI-20 records Fargues' degree as missing and routes it as a source to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0.

items.name: §6.5.2: degree functions and the neighbourhoods 𝓧(J), 𝓧^{mult}, 𝓧((ε_v)) of the multiplicative locus
items.statement:
§6.5.2. Let K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v) and let 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)} be the analytic space attached to X_{K_p(I)K^p}.
- For each v|p there is an isogeny 𝓖 → 𝓖' whose kernel H_v is a quasi-finite group scheme of order p away from the boundary.
- For each v ∈ I^c there is an isogeny 𝓖 → 𝓖' whose kernel L_v is quasi-finite of order p^2 away from the boundary.
Degree functions: let 𝓧^{rk1}_{K^pK_p(I)} be the set of rank one points, each x carrying its valuation v_x with v_x(p) = 1.
- For v ∈ I, deg_v(x) = v_x(δ_{H_v}) ∈ [0,1].
- For v ∈ I^c, deg_v(x) = v_x(δ_{L_v}) ∈ [0,2].
- deg = (deg_v)_v : 𝓧^{rk1} → [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c}.
Neighbourhoods:
- For each product J of rational intervals in [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c} there is a unique quasi-compact open 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}(J) with 𝓧(J)^{rk1} = deg^{−1}(J).
- The multiplicative locus is 𝓧^{mult}_{K^pK_p(I)} = 𝓧({1}^I × {2}^{I^c}).
- For (ε_v) ∈ ([0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c}) ∩ Q^{S_p}, 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}((ε_v)_{v∈S_p}) := 𝓧(∏_{v∈I}[1−ε_v,1] × ∏_{v∈I^c}[2−ε_v,2]).
- 𝓧^{mult} = 𝓧((0)_v), and {𝓧((ε_v))}_{ε_v→0+} is a fundamental system of strict neighbourhoods of 𝓧^{mult}.
All these spaces are stable under the action of (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} on the polarization. They descend to open subspaces of 𝓧^{G_1}_{K^pK_p(I)}, written with a superscript G_1.
items.locator: §6.5.2 (Neighbourhoods of the ordinary locus), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 154–155 (published version pp. 339–340)
items.note:
AdicSpacesPartII:R2 plans the general mechanism: 'rational subdomains cut out by a section of a line bundle and a valuation bound'. The degree functions, these neighbourhoods and the fundamental-system property are planned nowhere. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε as missing.
Notation clash: §6.5.3 and Lemma 6.5.4 write 𝓧((a_v)) with a_v the lower bound of the degree interval, not the ε_v of this definition (see the next two items). §8 (arXiv p. 239) uses this section's reading.

items.name: §6.5.3: comparison of the neighbourhoods 𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}((ε_v)) with the degree neighbourhoods
items.statement:
§6.5.3. Take parallel n ∈ Z_{≥1} and (ε_v) ∈ ([0, n − 1/(p−1)] ∩ Q)^{S_p}, and let 𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}((ε_v)) be the space of §§6.1.4 and 6.3.1.
(a) This part is Pilloni 2020, Lem. 14.1.1, for v ∈ I, extended trivially to v ∈ I^c. The forgetful map 𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}((ε_v)) → 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p} factors through the open subspace on which
- deg_v ≥ 1 − (2/n)(n − ε_v + 1/(p−1)) for v ∈ I, and
- deg_v ≥ 2 − (2/n)(n − ε_v + 1/(p−1)) for v ∈ I^c.
A bound ≤ 0 imposes no condition. For ε_v = n − 1/(p−1) and n → ∞ these bounds tend to 1 and 2.
(b) This part is Pilloni 2020, Lem. 14.1.2. Let ε_v ≥ 1 − 1/p for v ∈ I and ε_v ≥ 2 − 1/p for v ∈ I^c. Then the open subspace of 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p} on which deg_v ≥ ε_v for all v|p is contained in 𝓧_{K(I,p)}((1 − 1/(p−1))_{v∈S_p}).
items.locator: §6.5.3 (Comparison between spaces of overconvergent cohomology), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 155 (published version p. 340)
items.note:
The paper writes both subspaces as 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}((a_v)), with a_v the lower bound of the degree interval. The §6.5.2 definition would instead give 𝓧(∏[1−a_v,1] × ∏[2−a_v,2]). Two things force the lower-bound reading. First, the text remarks that the bounds tend to 1 and 2 ('both types of spaces are neighbourhoods of the multiplicative locus'). Second, the cited Lemma 14.1.2 of Pilloni 2020 is about 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε = {deg H ≥ ε}. This is sourceIssues E85, a misprint that affects nothing: the tuples of §6.5.3 and Lemma 6.5.4 are read as lower bounds on the degrees, as in Pilloni 2020 §14.1, with max{0, ·}. For n = 1, 𝓧_{K(I,p)}((ε_v)) is an open subspace of 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p} (§6.3.1), so (b) is an inclusion of opens. The max{0, ·} of Pilloni is left implicit here.
Status missing: no layer compares these neighbourhoods, and PAPER-PILLONI-20 records its Lemmas 14.1.1 and 14.1.2 as missing.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.4: Hecke action, compactness and comparison with the §6.3 neighbourhoods
items.statement:
Lemma 6.5.4. Let κ be a classical algebraic weight and let (ε_v) ∈ ([1 − 1/p, 1)^I × [2 − 1/p, 2)^{I^c}) ∩ Q^{S_p}. Let 𝓨 be the open subspace of 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)} on which deg_v ≥ ε_v for all v|p (the paper writes it 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}((ε_v)_{v∈S_p}); see the note), and let 𝓨^{G_1} be its G_1-variant.
(1) RΓ(𝓨, ω^κ) carries an action of the operators U_{v,1} and U_{v,2}.
(2) The operator ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1} is compact on RΓ(𝓨^{G_1}, ω^κ).
(3) The restriction map between RΓ(𝓨^{G_1}, ω^κ) and RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K(I,p)}((1 − 1/(p−1))_{v∈S_p}), ω^κ), along the inclusion of §6.5.3(b), induces a quasi-isomorphism on the finite slope parts for ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}.
(4) The same holds for cuspidal cohomology, with ω^κ(−D).
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.4, §6.5.3, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 155–156 (published version pp. 340–341)
items.note:
Printed (3): 'The canonical map RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K^pK_p(I)}((ε_v)), ω^κ) → RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K(I,p)}((1−1/(p−1))), ω^κ)'. For ε_v in the stated range, the sentence just before the lemma, citing Pilloni 2020 Lem. 14.1.2, includes the first space in the second as an open subspace. The canonical restriction map therefore runs the other way. On finite slope parts the two sides are identified whichever way the comparison is made (sourceIssues E85, a misprint that affects nothing; the same entry records that the tuple (ε_v) is read as the lower bounds deg_v ≥ ε_v).
Proof in the paper:
- the operators are defined by a routine computation;
- compactness holds because the operators improve the degrees (Pilloni 2011, Prop. 2.3.6), parallel to Lemma 6.3.14;
- the quasi-isomorphism is analytic continuation as in Lemma 6.5.18.
The lemma is used to define the dagger complex (6.5.5). Through that complex it enters Proposition 6.6.2 and Theorem 6.6.4, where it links e(U^I)H^i(𝓧_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), ω^κ(−D)) in Corollary 6.4.3 to the dagger complex.
Status missing: nothing in the libraries or the atlas.

items.name: (6.5.5): the dagger space 𝓧^{mult,†} and the complex e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}, ω^κ(−D))
items.statement: (6.5.5). The dagger space is 𝓧^{mult,†}_{K^pK_p(I)} := lim_{ε_v→0+} 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}((ε_v)_{v∈S_p}). It is the multiplicative locus together with its fundamental system of strict neighbourhoods 𝓧((ε_v)) = 𝓧(∏_{v∈I}[1−ε_v,1] × ∏_{v∈I^c}[2−ε_v,2]) of §6.5.2, and it has a G_1-variant. Let κ be a classical algebraic weight, and let 𝓨^{G_1} be the space of Lemma 6.5.4: the open subspace where deg_v ≥ ε_v, for any (ε_v) in the range of that lemma. It is one of the neighbourhoods above, with parameters 1 − ε_v for v ∈ I and 2 − ε_v for v ∈ I^c. Using Lemma 6.5.4, the complex e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) is defined to be e(U^I)RΓ(𝓨^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)); by Lemma 6.5.4(3), (4) this does not depend on the choice. Here U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2} acts compactly, and e(U^I) is its ordinary projector.
items.locator: (6.5.5) and the sentence after it, §6.5.3, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 156 (published version p. 341)
items.note:
The right-hand side is printed with ω^κ rather than ω^κ(−D). The cuspidal version (Lemma 6.5.4(4)) is what is meant. The printed right-hand side writes 𝓧^{G_1}_{K^pK_p(I)}((ε_v)) in the lower-bound notation of §6.5.3 and Lemma 6.5.4, not in the §6.5.2 notation of (6.5.5) itself. The statement above makes the space explicit.
AdicSpacesPartII:F1 plans the general dagger formalism: dagger affinoids, 'cofinal systems of strict neighborhoods' and gluing to dagger spaces. This particular space and complex are planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.6: the ordinary overconvergent complex is perfect in degrees [0,#I]
items.statement: Lemma 6.5.6. For a classical algebraic weight κ, the complex e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) is a perfect complex (of C_p-vector spaces) supported in degrees [0, #I].
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.6, §6.5.3, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 156 (published version p. 341)
items.note: Proof in the paper: the cohomology vanishes outside [0, #I] 'as usual by pushing forward to the minimal compactification' (compare Theorem 6.2.6), and it is finite because U^I is compact. The lemma is used in Proposition 6.6.2. Status missing: nothing in the libraries or the atlas.

items.name: §6.5.11: the correspondences C_w^{(n)} for U_{w,2}^n (w ∈ I) and U_{w,1}^n (w ∈ I^c), with integral bounds
items.statement:
§6.5.11.
(a) Let w ∈ I and n ≥ 1. The correspondence t_{w,n,1}, t_{w,n,2} : C_w^{(n)} → 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p} parametrizes tuples (𝓖, {H_v}_{v∈I}, {H_v ⊂ L_v}_{v∈I^c}, 𝓖 → 𝓖_n). Here the isogeny 𝓖 → 𝓖_n has kernel M_{n,w} ⊂ 𝓖_w[p^{2n}], totally isotropic, locally isomorphic to (O_{F_w}/p^n)^2 ⊕ O_{F_w}/p^{2n}, with M_{n,w} ∩ H_w = {0}.
- t_{w,n,1} forgets the isogeny.
- t_{w,n,2} sends the tuple to (𝓖_n, {H'_v}_{v∈I}, {H'_v ⊂ L'_v}_{v∈I^c}), the images in 𝓖_n.
- There are cohomological correspondences (t_{w,n,1})_*t_{w,n,2}^*ω^κ → ω^κ and (t_{w,n,1})_*t_{w,n,2}^*ω^κ(−D) → ω^κ(−D). They give U_{w,2}^n, the n-th iterate of U_{w,2}.
- They restrict to (t_{w,n,1})_*t_{w,n,2}^*(ω^κ)^{++} → p^{−3n}(ω^κ)^{++} and (t_{w,n,1})_*t_{w,n,2}^*(ω^κ(−D))^{++} → p^{−3n}(ω^κ(−D))^{++}, and induce maps on cohomology.
(b) Let w ∈ I^c. The same holds with kernel M_{n,w} ⊂ 𝓖_w[p^n], totally isotropic, locally isomorphic to (O_{F_w}/p^n)^2, with M_{n,w} ∩ L_w = {0}. The resulting operator is U_{w,1}^n, with the same bounds p^{−3n}.
items.locator: §6.5.11 (Hecke correspondences again), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 156–157 (published version pp. 342–343)
items.note:
The paper uses (ω^κ)^{++} without defining it (its first occurrence is here, on p. 157). As in Pilloni 2020 §14.4.2, it is the integral structure of topologically nilpotent sections relative to the lattice (ω^κ)^+ built from ω^+_𝓖. PAPER-PILLONI-20 notes the same omission there.
Misprint: in both formulas for t_{w,n,1} the family is printed {H_w ⊂ L_v}_{v∈I^c}, for {H_v ⊂ L_v}_{v∈I^c}.
Status missing: there are no Hilbert–Siegel Hecke correspondences in the libraries or the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.12: degrees under the U_{w,2}-correspondence for w ∈ I
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.12, §6.5.11, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 157 (published version p. 343)
items.note:
(6) is printed with 'deg M_w' for deg M_{1,w} in both versions (a trivial misprint). With Fargues' degree, (6) follows from (4), (5) and additivity: deg M_{1,w} ≥ 1 + 2 deg M_{1,w}/M_{1,w}[p].
Proof in the paper: (1) and (2) hold because the maps are isomorphisms; the rest is Pilloni 2020, Lem. 14.3.1 and Cor. 14.3.1. The lemma is used in Corollary 6.5.15 and, by analogy, Lemma 6.5.19. Status missing: see item 83. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records its Lemma 14.3.1 as missing.

items.name: Corollary 6.5.14: a power of U_{w,1} contracts towards the multiplicative locus (w ∈ I^c)
items.statement:
Corollary 6.5.14. Let w ∈ I^c and 1 > ε' ≥ ε > 0. There exists n ∈ Z_{≥0} such that for every product of intervals ∏_{v≠w}J_v ⊂ [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c∖{w}},
  U^n_{w,1}(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [1+ε, 2])) ⊂ 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [1+ε', 2]).
Here U^n_{w,1}(Y) = t_{w,n,2}(t_{w,n,1}^{−1}(Y)) is the image of Y under the correspondence C_w^{(n)}.
items.locator: Corollary 6.5.14, §6.5.11, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 158 (published version p. 343)
items.note: Proof in the paper: Lemma 6.5.13(3) and the maximum principle (Pilloni 2011, Prop. 2.3.6). The corollary is used in Lemma 6.5.18 and, through it, in Lemma 6.5.4. Status missing: AdicSpacesPartII does not state the maximum principle on adic spaces. The Iwahori-level model, Pilloni 2011 Prop. 2.3.6, has no extraction. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records only the Klingen-level analogue (its Cor. 14.3.2, the model for Corollary 6.5.15) as missing.

items.name: Corollary 6.5.15: a power of U_{w,2} contracts towards the multiplicative locus (w ∈ I)
items.statement:
Corollary 6.5.15. Let w ∈ I and 1 > ε' ≥ ε > 0. There exists n ∈ Z_{≥0} such that for every product of intervals ∏_{v≠w}J_v ⊂ [0,1]^{I∖{w}} × [0,2]^{I^c},
  U^n_{w,2}(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [ε, 1])) ⊂ 𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [ε', 1]).
The print has U^n_{w,1}; see the note.
items.locator: Corollary 6.5.15, §6.5.11, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 158 (published version p. 344)
items.note: Printed 'U^n_{w,1}' in both versions. For w ∈ I no operator U_{w,1} is defined: the correspondence of §6.5.11 is that of U_{w,2}. The proof is 'the same way as Corollary 6.5.14, using Lemma 6.5.12 (3)', and Lemma 6.5.12 is a statement about C_w^{(1)} for w ∈ I, which gives U_{w,2}. This is sourceIssues E86, a misprint that affects nothing. The corollary is used in Lemma 6.5.20 (its proof is left to the reader). PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q model (its Cor. 14.3.2) as missing.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.17 and the finite slope subspace for U_{w,1}
items.statement:
Lemma 6.5.17. Let J = ∏_{v|p}J_v ⊂ [0,1]^I × [0,2]^{I^c} be a product of intervals, let w ∈ I^c, and assume J_w = [2 − ε, 2]. The correspondence C_w^{(1)} restricts to t_{w,1,2} : C_w^{(1)} ×_{t_{w,1,1}, 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}} 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}(J) → 𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}(J), so U_{w,1} acts on H^i(𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}(J), ω^κ).
Definition: the finite slope subspace H^i(𝓧(J), ω^κ)^{fs−U_{w,1}} is the subspace generated by the classes annihilated by a polynomial in U_{w,1} with non-zero constant term.
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.17 and the definition after it, §6.5.16, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 158 (published version p. 344)
items.note: Proof in the paper: Lemma 6.5.13(3). The finite slope subspace is defined for an arbitrary endomorphism, not only a compact one, so it is not the slope decomposition planned in LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.18: restriction is an isomorphism on U_{w,1}-finite slope parts (w ∈ I^c)
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.18, §6.5.16, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 158–159 (published version pp. 344–345)
items.note: Proof in the paper: take n as in Corollary 6.5.14. If P(U_{w,1})f = 0 with a_0 ≠ 0, put Q(X) = −a_0^{−1}(P(X) − a_0), so that Q(U_{w,1})^n f = f. The operator Q(U_{w,1})^n factors through the larger domain, which gives the extension; injectivity is proved the same way. The proof calls the lemma 'the corollary'. The lemma is used in Corollary 6.5.23, in Lemma 6.5.4 and in the proof of Theorem 8.2.1 (arXiv p. 240). PAPER-PILLONI-20 records its Klingen-level analogue (Prop. 14.5.2) as missing.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.19 and the finite slope subspace for U_{w,2}
items.statement:
Lemma 6.5.19. Let w ∈ I and let J = ∏_{v|p}J_v with J_w = [1 − ε, 1]. Then U_{w,2} acts on H^i(𝓧_{K^pK_p(I)}(J), ω^κ).
Definition: H^i(𝓧(J), ω^κ)^{fs−U_{w,2}} is the subspace generated by the classes annihilated by a polynomial in U_{w,2} with non-zero constant term.
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.19 and the definition after it, §6.5.16, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 159 (published version p. 345)
items.note: The proof is left to the reader as the analogue of Lemma 6.5.17, using Lemma 6.5.12(3).

items.name: Lemma 6.5.20: restriction is an isomorphism on U_{w,2}-finite slope parts (w ∈ I)
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.20, §6.5.16, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 159 (published version p. 346)
items.note: The proof is left to the reader as the analogue of Lemma 6.5.18, using Corollary 6.5.15. The lemma plays the role that Lemma 6.5.18 plays in Corollary 6.5.23 for the omitted proof of Corollary 6.5.25.

items.name: Proposition 6.5.22: factorization of U_{w,1}^n modulo p^{n(l_w(1−ε')−3)} (w ∈ I^c)
items.locator: Proposition 6.5.22 with §6.5.21, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 159–161 (published version pp. 346–347)

items.name: Corollary 6.5.23: integral extension of U_{w,1}-small-slope classes (w ∈ I^c)
items.statement:
Corollary 6.5.23. Let w ∈ I^c, let J_v (v ≠ w) be intervals, and let 0 < ε ≤ 1. Let P = X^m + a_{m−1}X^{m−1} + ⋯ + a_0 be a polynomial all of whose roots a satisfy v(a) < l_w − 3. Then there is a map
  ext : H^i(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [1+ε,2]), ω^κ)[P(U_{w,1}) = 0] → (lim_n H^i(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [0,2]), ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++}))[P(U_{w,1}) = 0]
with two properties:
- ext followed by restriction to 𝓧(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [1+ε,2]) is the map induced by ω^κ → ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++};
- the restriction H^i(𝓧(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [0,2]), ω^κ)[P(U_{w,1}) = 0] → H^i(𝓧(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [1+ε,2]), ω^κ)[P(U_{w,1}) = 0] followed by ext is the map induced by ω^κ → ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++}.
items.locator: Corollary 6.5.23, §6.5.21, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 161–162 (published version pp. 347–349)

items.name: Proposition 6.5.24: factorization of U_{w,2}^n modulo p^{n(l_w+k_w−3−2ε'k_w)} (w ∈ I)
items.locator: Proposition 6.5.24, §6.5.21, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 163 (published version p. 350)
items.note: The diagram prints the exponent as n(l_w+k_w−3−2ε'k_v) in the upper entry and n(l_w+k_w−3−2ε'k_w) in the middle one. It also prints the bottom-left restriction as '∏J_v × [1,0]', for [0,1]. Both are recorded in sourceIssues E89 (read k_w and [0,1]), as misprints that affect nothing. The exponent agrees with Pilloni 2020 Prop. 14.6.1, N = n(2r + k − 3 − 2ε'(r+k)), under (k, r) = (k_w − l_w, l_w). The proof is left to the reader (compare Pilloni 2020, Prop. 14.6.1).

items.name: Corollary 6.5.25: integral extension of U_{w,2}-small-slope classes (w ∈ I)
items.statement:
Corollary 6.5.25. Let w ∈ I, let J_v (v ≠ w) be intervals, and let 1 > ε ≥ 0. Let P = X^m + a_{m−1}X^{m−1} + ⋯ + a_0 be a polynomial all of whose roots a satisfy v(a) < k_w + l_w − 3. Then there is a map
  ext : H^i(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [ε,1]), ω^κ)[P(U_{w,2}) = 0] → (lim_n H^i(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [0,1]), ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++}))[P(U_{w,2}) = 0]
with two properties:
- ext followed by restriction to 𝓧(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [ε,1]) is the map induced by ω^κ → ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++};
- the restriction H^i(𝓧(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [0,1]), ω^κ)[P(U_{w,2}) = 0] → H^i(𝓧(∏_{v≠w}J_v × [ε,1]), ω^κ)[P(U_{w,2}) = 0] followed by ext is the map induced by ω^κ → ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++}.
items.locator: Corollary 6.5.25, §6.5.21, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 163 (published version p. 350)
items.note: The proof is left to the reader, from Proposition 6.5.24 and Lemma 6.5.20, as for Corollary 6.5.23 (compare Pilloni 2020, Cor. 14.6.1).

items.name: §6.5.26: the domains J(S,ε) and finite slope classes
items.statement:
§6.5.26. For S ⊂ S_p and a rational number ε with 0 < ε < 1, put
  J(S,ε) = ∏_{v∈S∩I}[0,1] × ∏_{v∈S∩I^c}[0,2] × ∏_{v∈S^c∩I}[ε,1] × ∏_{v∈S^c∩I^c}[1+ε,2].
A class f ∈ H^i(𝓧_{K_p(I)K^p}(J(S,ε)), ω^κ) is of finite slope if, for every v|p, there is a polynomial P_v all of whose roots are non-zero such that P_v(U_{v,1})f = 0 when v ∈ I^c and P_v(U_{v,2})f = 0 when v ∈ I.
items.locator: §6.5.26 (Proof of the main classicality theorem), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 163 (published version pp. 350–351)
items.note: The range of ε is not printed. 0 < ε < 1 is the range in which both Corollary 6.5.23 (0 < ε ≤ 1) and Corollary 6.5.25 (1 > ε ≥ 0) apply.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.27: rational cohomology surjects onto the integral limit, isomorphically on finite slope parts
items.statement:
Lemma 6.5.27. For S ⊂ S_p and ε as in §6.5.26, the canonical map
  H^i(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}(J(S,ε)), ω^κ) → lim_n H^i(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}(J(S,ε)), ω^κ/p^n(ω^κ)^{++})
is surjective and induces an isomorphism on the finite slope parts.
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.27, §6.5.26, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 164 (published version p. 351)
items.note: Proof in the paper: surjectivity is Pilloni 2020, Prop. 3.2.1, and injectivity is proved as in Pilloni 2020, Lem. 14.7.1. The G_1 superscript is needed for a finiteness property used in the injectivity. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records its Proposition 3.2.1 and Lemma 14.7.1 as missing.

items.name: Lemma 6.5.28: restriction J(T,ε) → J(S,ε) is an isomorphism on small slope eigenspaces
items.locator: Lemma 6.5.28, §6.5.26, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 164 (published version p. 351)
items.note: Proof in the paper: by induction reduce to T = S ∪ {w}, then combine Lemma 6.5.27 for S and T with Corollaries 6.5.23 and 6.5.25. With S = ∅ and T = S_p this gives Theorem 6.5.8. The lemma is stated for ω^κ, and the theorem uses its cuspidal version and Lemmas 6.5.18 and 6.5.20 to pass from J(∅,ε) to the dagger space. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records its analogue (Thm. 14.7.1) as missing.

items.name: §6.6: 𝓧^{mult} is the generic fibre of the formal ordinary locus, and M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p = e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult}, ω^κ(−D))
items.statement:
(§6.6, from Theorem 4.6.1(3).) The multiplicative locus 𝓧^{mult}_{K_p(I)K^p} of §6.5.2 is the rigid analytic generic fibre of the formal scheme 𝔛^I_{K_p(I)K^p} of §4.3.4. That formal scheme is the open formal subscheme where:
- for v ∈ I, 𝓖_v has p-rank ≥ 1 and H_v is multiplicative;
- for v ∈ I^c, 𝓖_v is ordinary with its canonical Iwahori level structure.
For every classical algebraic weight κ with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p − 1) for all v|p,
  M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p = e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)).
items.locator: §6.6, the paragraph before Proposition 6.6.1 and the proof of Proposition 6.6.1, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 164–165 (published version pp. 352–353)
items.note: The paper states the identification of 𝓧^{mult} with the generic fibre in parentheses. It rests on v_x(δ_H) = deg H_x (§6.5.1) and on Fargues' fact that a finite flat group scheme of order p^h has degree h exactly when it is multiplicative. Passing to the generic fibre after ⊗C_p is the formal-to-rigid comparison for coherent cohomology, whose general form is in AdicSpacesPartII:R2 ('comparison of a model's formal generic fibre'). PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (Lemma 14.8.1(2)) as missing.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 6.6.1: the two-affinoid Čech description and the density of overconvergent classes
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.6.1, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 165 (published version pp. 352–353)
items.note: The paper asserts the two-affinoid cover without proof. For F = Q it is in Pilloni 2020, proof of Lem. 14.8.2 (footnote 25), where Hasse-invariant lifts cut the p-rank ≥ 1 locus of the minimal compactification into two affines; PAPER-PILLONI-20 records it as missing. AdicSpacesPartII:F1 plans the general strict-neighbourhood formalism but not this cover.

items.name: Proof of Proposition 6.6.2: T-ordinary classical cohomology at hyperspecial level equals U-ordinary cohomology at level K_p(I)
items.statement:
(Claim in the proof of Proposition 6.6.2.) Let #I ≤ 1 and let κ be a classical algebraic weight with:
- l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p − 1);
- l_v ≥ C for v ∈ I^c and k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v|p, C a sufficiently large constant (at least that of Theorem 4.6.1(4)).
The natural map RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ(−D)) → RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)), from hyperspecial level K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(O_{F_v}) to level K_p(I), induces a quasi-isomorphism
  e(T̃^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ(−D)) → e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)),
where T̃^I = ∏_{v|p}T_v∏_{v∈I^c}T_{v,1} (Lemma 4.2.37). This is the operator whose ordinary projector appears in Theorem 4.6.1(4). The paper writes e(T^I); see the note.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.6.2 with Remark 6.6.3, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 166–167 (published version pp. 354–355)
items.note:
Why T̃^I: the proof and Remark 6.6.3 print e(T^I), and Theorem 4.2.1 defines T^I = ∏_{w∈I}T_w∏_{w∈I^c}T_{w,1}, which has only T_{w,1} at w ∈ I^c. But Remark 6.6.3 says that at v ∈ I^c ordinarity holds 'essentially by definition since the two Hecke operators at v|p occur in the projector'. The last step of the proof also applies Theorem 4.6.1(4), whose projector is e(∏_{v|p}T_v∏_{v∈I^c}T_{v,1}) = e(T̃^I).
Proof in the paper: Theorem 3.10.1(2) computes both sides in terms of automorphic representations. The claim then follows from Proposition 2.4.26, once every π_v (v|p) contributing to either side is ordinary. Remark 6.6.3 explains why: ordinarity holds by definition at v ∈ I^c, and at v ∈ I it needs the Katz–Mazur inequality (separate item).
Theorem 3.10.1(1)–(2) assume localization at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal m, and only part (3), for H^0, is stated without it. Here it is applied to unlocalized cohomology in degrees 0 and 1. Sections 7–8 use the consequences only after such a localization. This item is routed to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology), which plans Proposition 6.6.2, and with it this claim, after localizing both sides at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal m.
Status missing: nothing in the libraries or the atlas.

items.name: Remark 6.6.3: the Katz–Mazur inequality for Hecke parameters at v ∈ I
items.statement:
(Remark 6.6.3.) Let v ∈ I, and let π_v be a local representation contributing, in degree 0 or 1, to e(T̃^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ(−D)) or to e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)). Here T̃^I is as in the preceding item; at v ∈ I it contributes only T_v, and the paper writes T^I. Let the Hecke parameters of π_v be [α_v p^{1−k_v/2}, β_v p^{1−k_v/2}, β_v^{−1}p^{k_v/2}, α_v^{−1}p^{k_v/2}]. The Katz–Mazur inequality says that the Newton polygon lies above the Hodge polygon with the same initial and terminal points. Here this means that α_v and β_v are p-adic integers.
Consequence: U_{v,2}-ordinarity of π_v (α_vβ_v a p-adic unit) implies ordinarity (α_v and β_v both p-adic units).
items.locator: Remark 6.6.3, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 166–167 (published version pp. 354–355)

items.name: Proposition 6.6.2: the ordinary overconvergent complex and the specialized Hida complex have equal Euler characteristics
items.statement:
Proposition 6.6.2. Suppose that #I ≤ 1. Let κ be a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p − 1) for all v|p; the congruence is not printed, see the note. Then
  EC(e(U^I)RΓ(𝓧^{G_1,mult,†}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D))) = EC(M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p).
Here EC(C) = Σ_i (−1)^i dim_{C_p} H^i(C), and both complexes are perfect in degrees [0,1]. The proof also shows that both equal EC(e(U^I)H^•_cusp(G_1,†,κ)), which is what Theorem 6.6.4 uses.
items.locator: Proposition 6.6.2, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 165–166 (published version pp. 353–354)

items.name: Theorem 6.6.4: for #I ≤ 1 the ordinary overconvergent complex is the specialized Hida complex
items.locator: Theorem 6.6.4, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 167 (published version p. 355)
items.note:
Proof in the paper: let d_i = dim H^i(M_I ⊗^L C_p) and d_i^† = dim e(U^I)H^i_cusp(G_1,†,κ). The equality of Euler characteristics gives d_1 − d_1^† = d_0 − d_0^†. Proposition 6.6.1 together with Corollary 6.4.3 makes the first difference non-positive and the second non-negative. The composite through e(U^I)H^i_cusp(G_1,†,κ) is then an isomorphism.
The proof uses a map e(U^I)H^i_cusp(G_1,†,κ) → H^i(M_I ⊗^L C_p) that §6 does not construct. Dimension counts alone suffice. Let a_i = dim e(U^I)H^i(mult,†). Then:
- a_0 ≤ d_0 and a_1 ≥ d_1 (Proposition 6.6.1);
- a_0 = d_0^† and a_1 ≤ d_1^† (Corollary 6.4.3 with Lemma 6.5.4(3));
- d_0^† − d_1^† = d_0 − d_1 (proof of Proposition 6.6.2).
These force a_i = d_i, so the injective (i = 0) and surjective (i = 1) maps of Proposition 6.6.1 are isomorphisms.
The theorem is used in the proof of Theorem 8.2.1 ('ordinary implies overconvergent if #I ≤ 1'). Status missing: PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (Thm. 14.8.1 and Lemma 14.8.4) as missing.

items.name: Theorem 6.6.5: ordinary classicity for #I ≤ 1
items.statement:
Theorem 6.6.5. Suppose that #I ≤ 1 and that κ is a classical algebraic weight with l_v = 2 if v ∈ I, l_v ≥ 4 if v ∉ I, and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p − 1) for all v|p (the congruence is not printed; see Proposition 6.6.2). Then the canonical map
  e(U^I)RΓ(X^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D))[1/p] → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} Q_p
is a quasi-isomorphism. Here X^{G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p} is the toroidal compactification over Z_p, and the map is restriction to the formal ordinary locus followed by Theorem 4.6.1(3).
items.locator: Theorem 6.6.5, §6.6, arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 167 (published version p. 355)
items.note:
Proof in the paper: 'This follows from Theorem 6.6.4 and Theorem 6.5.8'; descent from C_p to Q_p is by flat base change. Applying e(U^I) to Theorem 6.5.8 needs the U^I-ordinary part to lie in its small slope range. That holds when the individual operators U_{v,2} (v ∈ I) and U_{v,1}, U_{v,2} (v ∈ I^c) have non-negative slopes on the classes concerned. Then slope 0 for U^I forces slope 0 for each factor, and 0 < k_v + l_v − 3 for v ∈ I and 0 < l_v − 3 for v ∉ I (this is where l_v ≥ 4 enters). The paper does not discuss the individual slopes. They are ≥ 0 on H^0 (Proposition 6.4.1), and §7 localizes at p-adically integral eigenvalues (Remark 6.6.3).
The theorem is used in §7.8 (Remark 7.8.9 and the end of §7.8), §7.9 and §7.13, always after localizing at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra. Status missing: PAPER-PILLONI-20 records the F = Q analogue (its Thm. 14.8.1) as missing.

items.name: Definition 7.1.4: local deformation problems for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}
items.statement: Definition 7.1.4. A local deformation problem for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is a subfunctor 𝓓_v of 𝓓_v^□ (Definition 7.1.2) such that 𝓓_v is represented by a quotient R_v of R_v^□, and, for all A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}, ρ ∈ 𝓓_v(A) and a ∈ ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k)), one has aρa^{-1} ∈ 𝓓_v(A).
items.locator: Definition 7.1.4 (§7.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 170 (published p. 358); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 85. It is cited separately in §7.3, where the ordinary problems 𝓓_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} and 𝓓_v^P are shown to be local deformation problems by Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 2.4.6. It is also used by every local condition of §7.4. Missing: no layer description of the atlas mentions GSp_4-valued deformation functors or deformations with fixed similitude. GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.3 and LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 are for representations with fixed determinant; GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 is for polarized GL_n over a CM field. Neither library has Galois deformation rings.

items.name: Definition 7.1.5: global deformation problems, deformations of type 𝓢, T-framed deformations and their representing rings
items.statement:
Definition 7.1.5. A global deformation problem is a tuple 𝓢 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, ψ, {𝓓_v}_{v∈S}), with ρ̄, S, {Λ_v} and ψ as in §7.1, and 𝓓_v a local deformation problem for ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} for each v ∈ S.
A lift of ρ̄ is a continuous ρ : G_{F,S} → GSp_4(A), with A a CNL_Λ-algebra, such that ρ mod m_A = ρ̄ and ν∘ρ = ψ. Lifts ρ_1, ρ_2 are strictly equivalent if ρ_2 = aρ_1a^{-1} for some a ∈ ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k)). A deformation of ρ̄ is a strict equivalence class of lifts.
A lift ρ is of type 𝓢 if ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∈ 𝓓_v(A) for each v ∈ S; this is a property of its strict equivalence class. 𝓓_𝓢 is the functor on CNL_Λ of deformations of type 𝓢.
For T ⊆ S, a T-framed lift of type 𝓢 is a tuple (ρ, {γ_v}_{v∈T}), with ρ of type 𝓢 and γ_v ∈ ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k)). Two T-framed lifts (ρ_1, {γ_v}) and (ρ_2, {γ'_v}) are strictly equivalent if there is a ∈ ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k)) with ρ_2 = aρ_1a^{-1} and γ'_v = aγ_v for each v ∈ T. 𝓓_𝓢^T is the functor of T-framed deformations of type 𝓢.
Since ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible, 𝓓_𝓢 and 𝓓_𝓢^T are representable, by R_𝓢 and R_𝓢^T. If T = ∅ then R_𝓢 = R_𝓢^T. Otherwise R_𝓢 → R_𝓢^T is formally smooth of relative dimension 11#T − 1, because 𝓓_𝓢^T → 𝓓_𝓢 is a torsor under (∏_{v∈T} ĜSp_4)/Ĝ_m (completions along the identity). 𝓣 denotes the coordinate ring of (∏_{v∈T} ĜSp_4)/Ĝ_m over Λ, a power series algebra over Λ in 11#T − 1 variables.
items.locator: Definition 7.1.5 and the paragraphs following it (§7.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 170 (published pp. 358–359); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note:
Split from item 85. Misprints, all also in the published version (p. 358):
- The paper prints 'ρ∘ν = ψ' for the global lifts; ν∘ρ = ψ is meant.
- It writes the domain of a lift of type 𝓢 as G_F; lifts are of G_{F,S}.
- It describes 𝓓_𝓢(A) as 'the set of lifts ρ : G_F → GSp_4(A) of type 𝓢', where strict equivalence classes (deformations) are meant. The next paragraph shows this, since it identifies R_𝓢 with R_𝓢^T for T = ∅.
Missing: no layer description of the atlas mentions GSp_4-valued deformation functors or deformations with fixed similitude. GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.3 and LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 are for representations with fixed determinant; GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 is for polarized GL_n over a CM field. Neither library has Galois deformation rings.

items.name: Lemma 7.1.6: the T-framed global ring is R_𝓢 ⊗̂_Λ 𝓣
items.statement: Lemma 7.1.6. Let 𝓢 be a global deformation problem and T ⊆ S. The choice of a representative ρ_𝓢 : G_{F,S} → GSp_4(R_𝓢) of the universal deformation of type 𝓢 determines a splitting of the torsor 𝓓_𝓢^T → 𝓓_𝓢, and a canonical isomorphism R_𝓢^T ≅ R_𝓢 ⊗̂_Λ 𝓣, where 𝓣 is the coordinate ring of (∏_{v∈T} ĜSp_4)/Ĝ_m over Λ.
items.locator: Lemma 7.1.6 (§7.1), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 171 (published p. 359); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note: Split from item 85. It is cited separately in §7.11 (arXiv p. 225), where representatives of the universal deformations, identified modulo λ, are fixed. The paper's proof is 'This is obvious.' Missing: no layer description of the atlas mentions GSp_4-valued deformation functors or deformations with fixed similitude, and neither library has Galois deformation rings.

items.name: Closed points of R_v^□[1/p]: Kisin's comparison of completed local rings, and smooth points
items.statement: Let x ∈ Spec R_v^□[1/p] be a closed point. Its residue field is a finite extension E'/E (Taylor, Automorphy … II, Lemma 1.6). Let ρ_x : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(E') be the corresponding specialization of the universal lift. By Kisin's argument, (R_v^□[1/p])^∧_x is the universal lifting ring of ρ_x. (For GL_n this is Allen, Deformations of polarized automorphic Galois representations and adjoint Selmer groups, Theorem 1.2.1; for GSp_4 the argument is identical.) That is: for every Artinian local E'-algebra A with residue field E', and every continuous lift ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) of ρ_x (with similitude character ψ, left implicit in the paper), there is a unique continuous map of E'-algebras (R_v^□[1/p])^∧_x → A through which the universal lift pushes forward to ρ. The point x is smooth if (R_v^□[1/p])^∧_x is regular. ad^0ρ_x denotes the Lie algebra 𝔤^0(E') = Lie Sp_4(E'), with the adjoint action of G_{F_v} through ρ_x.

items.name: The ordinary local deformation problems 𝓓_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} and 𝓓_v^P at v | p, with the weight algebras Λ_{v,1}, Λ_{v,2}
items.statement:
Keep the assumptions of §7.3: p splits completely in F, and ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary with a fixed labelling ᾱ_v, β̄_v.

Weight algebras. Let O_{F_v}^×(p) = 1 + pO_{F_v} be the pro-p completion of O_{F_v}^×. Put Λ_{v,1} = O[[O_{F_v}^×(p)]] and Λ_{v,2} = O[[(O_{F_v}^×(p))²]]; both are formally smooth over O since F_v = Q_p. Let Λ_v be one of them. Using the character I_{F_v} → O_{F_v}^×(p) given by Art_{F_v}^{-1}, define characters θ_{v,1}, θ_{v,2}: if Λ_v = Λ_{v,1}, then θ_{v,1} = θ_{v,2} = θ_v, the natural character; if Λ_v = Λ_{v,2}, then θ_{v,i} corresponds to the i-th copy.

Subgroups. Let 𝔠̄_v be ᾱ_v or β̄_v, and let 𝔠̄'_v = ᾱ_vβ̄_v/𝔠̄_v be the other. B ⊂ GSp_4 is the upper triangular Borel subgroup, and P ⊂ B is the subgroup of matrices with zero (1,2) and (3,4) entries.

(B, 𝔠̄_v)-ordinary lifts. For A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}, a lift ρ_A : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is (B, 𝔠̄_v)-ordinary if there is an increasing filtration 0 = Fil^0 ⊂ Fil^1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Fil^4 = A^4 by free A-submodules stable under G_{F_v}, with G_{F_v} acting on Fil^i/Fil^{i−1} by a character χ_i, where χ̄_1 = λ_{𝔠̄_v}, χ̄_2 = λ_{𝔠̄'_v}, χ_1|_{I_{F_v}} = θ_{v,1}, χ_2|_{I_{F_v}} = θ_{v,2}, χ_3 = ε^{-1}χ_2^{-1} and χ_4 = ε^{-1}χ_1^{-1}. Such a filtration is unique (Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 2.4.6), and ρ_A is then ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k))-conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal χ_1, χ_2, ε^{-1}χ_2^{-1}, ε^{-1}χ_1^{-1}.

P-ordinary lifts. If Λ_v = Λ_{v,1}, ρ_A is P-ordinary if it is both (B, ᾱ_v)- and (B, β̄_v)-ordinary; equivalently, if it is ker(GSp_4(A) → GSp_4(k))-conjugate to [[χ_1, 0, *, *], [0, χ_2, *, *], [0, 0, ε^{-1}χ_2^{-1}, 0], [0, 0, 0, ε^{-1}χ_1^{-1}]].

The functors. For Λ_v = Λ_{v,2}, 𝓓_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} is the subfunctor of (B, 𝔠̄_v)-ordinary lifts; for Λ_v = Λ_{v,1}, 𝓓_v^P is the subfunctor of P-ordinary lifts. These are local deformation problems (Definition 7.1.4), represented by CNL_{Λ_v}-algebras R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} and R_v^P.

items.name: Definition 7.3.11 and Lemma 7.3.12: B- and P-framed deformation rings, and formal smoothness of R^B and R^P over them
items.statement:
Keep §7.3 with F_v = Q_p, writing ρ̄ for ρ̄|_{G_{Q_p}}, R^B = R_v^{B,𝔠̄_v} and R^P = R_v^P. These are framed with respect to GSp_4, so they are also written R^{B,□} and R^{P,□}.

Definition 7.3.11. 𝓓^{B,◹} and 𝓓^{P,◹} are the subfunctors of deformations that land inside B, resp. P, with representing rings R^{B,◹} and R^{P,◹}. (The framing takes place in the upper right corner; ◹ stands for the paper's corner symbol.)

Further notation:
- R^{B,◹} is the universal B-framed deformation ring of ρ̄ with fixed similitude character.
- R^{P,univ} = R^{P,univ,□} is the ring of deformations to GSp_4 with fixed similitude character that can be conjugated into P, without the inertial condition that defines R^P. R^{P,univ,◹} is the universal P-framed deformation ring with fixed similitude character.
- There are tautological maps R^B → R^{B,◹} and R^P → R^{P,◹}.
- ad_{GSp_4}, ad_B and ad_P denote the adjoint representations of ρ̄ on the Lie algebras of GSp_4, B and P. For p odd, ad^0_{GSp_4}, ad^0_B and ad^0_P are their direct factors for fixed similitude character, of dimensions 10, 6 and 5.

Lemma 7.3.12. Suppose ρ̄ is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary.
(1) There is a splitting R^{B,◹} → R^{B,□} → R^{B,◹} which realizes R^B = R^{B,□} as formally smooth over R^{B,◹} of relative dimension dim ad^0_{GSp_4} − dim ad^0_B = 10 − 6 = 4.
(2) There are splittings R^{P,univ,◹} → R^{P,univ,□} → R^{P,univ,◹} and R^{P,◹} → R^{P,□} → R^{P,◹} which realize R^P and R^{P,univ} as formally smooth over R^{P,◹} and R^{P,univ,◹} respectively, of relative dimension dim ad^0_{GSp_4} − dim ad^0_P = 10 − 5 = 5.

Proof:
- The unique filtration of Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Lemma 2.4.6, is split by a symplectic matrix congruent to 1.
- p-distinguishedness makes H^0(Q_p, ad^0_P) → H^0(Q_p, ad^0_B) → H^0(Q_p, ad^0_{GSp_4}) isomorphisms, which gives the tangent-space count.
- The obstruction groups of the B-framed and GSp_4-framed ordinary problems are both H^2(Q_p, ad^0_B).

items.name: Proposition 7.3.16: the P-ordinary rings R^{P,univ} and R^P are complete intersections with irreducible generic fibres of dimensions 15 and 14
items.statement: Proposition 7.3.16. Suppose ρ̄|_{G_{Q_p}} is p-distinguished (weight 2 ordinary). Then R^{P,univ} and R^P are complete intersections. They are connected in characteristic zero, and their non-smooth locus in characteristic zero has codimension at least two. In particular, the generic fibres R^{P,univ}[1/p] and R^P[1/p] are irreducible, of dimensions 15 and 14 over Q_p respectively.
items.locator: Proposition 7.3.16 (§7.3.13), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 183–185 (published pp. 375–377); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501

Proof. By Lemma 7.3.15, reduce to R^{P,univ,◹} and R^{P,◹} (dimensions 10 and 9). The explicit presentations of Lemma 7.3.7 show that these are one of:
- formally smooth;
- a power series ring modulo one nonzero relation;
- a power series ring modulo a height-two prime not contained in (λ), which happens only when ᾱ² = β̄² = 1 and η_{α²} = η_{β²} = 0.
Connectedness, and codimension two of the non-smooth locus, use Lemma 7.3.9 and a separate treatment of the case ᾱβ̄ = 1.

items.name: The O[Δ_v]-algebra structure on R_v^□ at a Taylor–Wiles place
items.statement: Keep the set-up of §7.4.3 (Lemma 7.4.4). Let Δ_v = k(v)^×(p)², where k(v)^×(p) is the maximal p-power quotient of k(v)^×, and let ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(R_v^□) be the universal lift. By Lemma 7.4.4, ρ is GSp_4(R_v^□)-conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ψγ_2^{-1} ⊕ ψγ_1^{-1}. For i = 1, 2, the character γ_i ∘ Art_{F_v}|_{O_{F_v}^×} factors through k(v)^×(p), which gives a canonical local O-algebra map O[Δ_v] → R_v^□. This map depends on the ordering ᾱ_1, …, ᾱ_4, and it is formally smooth of relative dimension 10.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.7: the Ihara avoidance ring R_v^1 is equidimensional of dimension 11, with generic points of characteristic zero and uniquely lifted special-fibre generic points
items.statement: Keep the set-up of §7.4.5: v is a finite place of F with q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial, ψ|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified with trivial reduction modulo λ, and Λ_v = O. Let R_v^1 represent 𝓓_v^χ for χ_1 = χ_2 = 1, that is, the lifts ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} (with ν∘ρ = ψ|_{G_{F_v}}) such that ρ(σ) has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^4 for all σ ∈ I_{F_v}. Proposition 7.4.7. (1) Spec R_v^1 is equidimensional of dimension 11, and every generic point has characteristic zero. (2) Every generic point of Spec R_v^1/(λ) is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_v^1.

items.name: Propositions 7.4.17 and 7.4.18: the spaces 𝓜(x, y; q), their components, flatness and connectedness
items.statement:
For x, y ∈ O^× and q a positive integer not divisible by p, 𝓜(x, y; q) is the closed subscheme of GSp_4²/O of pairs (Φ, Σ) such that Σ has characteristic polynomial (X − x)(X − y)(X − y^{-1})(X − x^{-1}) and ΦΣΦ^{-1} = Σ^q; the order of x and y does not matter. The map (Φ, Σ) ↦ (Φ, log_2(Σ)) is an isomorphism 𝓜(1, 1; q) ≅ 𝓝(q).

Proposition 7.4.17. Let q be a positive integer with q ≡ 1 mod p.
(1) Let the 𝓜_i be the irreducible components of 𝓜(1, 1; q), with their reduced structure. Then the special fibres 𝓜_{i,𝐅} are distinct, generically reduced and irreducible, and their reductions are precisely the irreducible components of 𝓜(1, 1; q)_𝐅.
(2) Suppose either that q ≠ 1 and x, y are nontrivial (q − 1)st roots of 1 in 1 + λO with x ≠ y^{±1}, or that q = 1 and x, y are arbitrary elements of 1 + λO. Then 𝓜(x, y; q)^red is flat over O.

Proposition 7.4.18. Let q > 1 with q ≡ 1 mod p, and let x, y be nontrivial (q − 1)st roots of 1 in 1 + λO with x ≠ y^{±1}. If R is the completed local ring of 𝓜(x, y; q) at the point (1, 1) of the special fibre, then Spec R[1/p] is connected.

items.name: §7.4.19 with Propositions 7.4.20 and 7.4.21: R̃_v^χ ≅ R_v^χ[[T]] is the completed local ring of 𝓜(x, y; q_v) at (1, 1)
items.statement:
Keep the set-up of §7.4.5 (q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial). Let χ = (χ_1, χ_2), with χ_i : O_{F_v}^× → O^× continuous and trivial mod λ.
- 𝓓̃_v^χ is the functor on CNL_O of continuous homomorphisms ρ : G_{F_v} → GSp_4(A) that are trivial mod m_A and such that, for σ ∈ I_{F_v}, the characteristic polynomial of ρ(σ) is (X − χ_1(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ)))(X − χ_2(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ)))(X − χ_2(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{-1})(X − χ_1(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{-1}).
- 𝓓_v^χ ⊂ 𝓓̃_v^χ is the subfunctor with ν∘ρ = ε^{-1}.
- These are represented by R̃_v^χ and R_v^χ.
- 𝓓_1 is the functor of continuous unramified characters G_{F_v} → A^× that are trivial mod m_A. It is represented by O[[T]], with universal character sending Frob_v to 1 + T.
For A ∈ CNL_O and p > 2, t ↦ t² is a bijection of 1 + m_A; write x ↦ √x for its inverse.

Proposition 7.4.20. (ρ, ψ) ↦ ρ ⊗ ψ is an isomorphism of functors 𝓓_v^χ × 𝓓_1 → 𝓓̃_v^χ, with inverse ρ ↦ (ρ ⊗ √(ε·(ν∘ρ))^{-1}, √(ε·(ν∘ρ))). Consequently R_v^χ[[T]] ≅ R̃_v^χ.

Proposition 7.4.21. Let σ be a chosen topological generator of the tame inertia subgroup of G_{F_v}, and put x = χ_1(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ)) and y = χ_2(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ)). Then R̃_v^χ ≅ Ô_{𝓜(x,y;q_v),(1,1)}.

Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501

Proof of Proposition 7.4.21. Every lift of the trivial ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} factors through T_v = G_{F_v}/P_{F_v}, where P_{F_v} is the maximal pro-prime-to-p subgroup of I_{F_v}. T_v is topologically generated by a Frobenius φ and σ, subject to σ generating a pro-p group and φσφ^{-1} = σ^{q_v}.

Uses:
- Proposition 7.4.7 follows from Propositions 7.4.17(1), 7.4.21, Taylor's Lemma 2.7 and Proposition 7.4.20.
- Proposition 7.4.8 follows from Propositions 7.4.17(2), 7.4.18, 7.4.21 and Lemma 7.4.6, as in Taylor's Proposition 3.1.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.12: an absolutely irreducible subgroup with centre of order at least 3 is tidy
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.12. If H ⊂ GSp_4(k) is absolutely irreducible and the centre Z of H has order at least 3, then H is tidy.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.13: groups containing Δ are tidy for p ≥ 5

items.name: Lemma 7.5.18: SL_2(k) ≀ Z/2Z is weakly enormous, and enormous if #k ≠ 5
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.18. Let k have characteristic p ≥ 3, and let G = SL_2(k) ≀ Z/2Z = (SL_2(k) × SL_2(k)) ⋊ Z/2Z, the semi-direct product swapping the two copies of SL_2(k), viewed as a subgroup of Sp_4(k) as in §2.2. Then G is weakly enormous, and G is enormous if #k ≠ 5.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.18 (§7.5), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 202–203 (published p. 398); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note:
Split from item 99. Cited in Lemma 7.5.19, Lemma 7.5.21 (case (3a)) and Lemma 7.5.22. (E1) reduces by inflation–restriction to H^1(SL_2(k), Sym²(k²)) = 0 for #k ≠ 5 (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Lemma 2.48). (E3) follows from Lemma 7.5.17 once G ∖ (SL_2(k) × SL_2(k)) has an element whose order neither divides 4 nor is divisible by p.

Error in the proof (not recorded by the extraction). The paper asserts that, since 8 | p² − 1, SL_2(k) has an element a of order exactly 8, and takes g = (a, a)σ. This fails whenever #k ≡ ±3 mod 8: then 16 ∤ (#k)² − 1, and the Sylow 2-subgroup of SL_2(k) is the quaternion group of order 8, which has no element of order 8. Examples are k = F_3, F_5, F_11, F_13; a brute-force count of element orders in these groups confirms it. The conclusion survives: take a ∈ SL_2(k) of order 4 (for instance [[0, 1], [−1, 0]]) and g = (a, 1)σ. Then g² = (a, a) has order 4, so g has order 8, which neither divides 4 nor is divisible by p. The same text is in the published version (p. 398). It affects the proof only, and does so in cases the paper uses: k = F_3 in Lemmas 7.5.21(3a) and 7.5.22, and k = F_5 in Lemma 7.5.19.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.19: the substitute for p = 5
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.19. Let H/F be a quadratic extension, and let r̄ : G_H → GL_2(F_5) be a surjective representation with determinant ε̄^{-1}. Let ρ̄ : G_F → GSp_4(F_5) be the induction of r̄ to F. Assume that the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_5)}} is G = SL_2(F_5) ≀ Z/2Z, and that 5 is unramified in F. Then ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{5^N})}) is weakly enormous for all N ≥ 1, and ζ_5 does not lie in the fixed field of ad^0ρ̄; in particular, ρ̄ is vast.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.19 (§7.5), arXiv:1812.09269v3 p. 203 (published p. 398); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501

The image Γ of ρ̄ is the full preimage of G in GSp_4(F_5), with [Γ : G] = 4. The image of Γ in PGSp_4(F_5) has abelianization (Z/2Z)², which does not surject onto Gal(F(ζ_5)/F) = Z/4Z.
