items.name: Lemma 7.5.22 and Remark 7.5.23: inductions from a quadratic extension are vast and tidy
items.statement: Lemma 7.5.22. Suppose p ≥ 3, K/F is a quadratic extension with K unramified at p, and r̄ : G_K → GL_2(k) restricted to G_{K(ζ_p)} has image SL_2(k). Choose σ ∈ G_F ∖ G_K, and assume Proj r̄^σ ≇ Proj r̄ but det r̄^σ = det r̄ = ε̄^{-1}. Let ρ̄ := Ind_{G_K}^{G_F} r̄ : G_F → GSp_4(k). If p = 3, assume that the fixed fields of the kernels of Proj r̄ and Proj r̄^σ are disjoint. Then ρ̄ is vast and tidy. Remark 7.5.23: for p = 3, it suffices (by Lemmas 7.5.21 and 7.5.5) that the image of ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_27)}} is SL_2(F_3) ≀ Z/2Z or one of its subgroups of index three and order 384 from Lemma 7.5.21. The hypothesis Proj r̄ ≇ Proj r̄^σ alone does not force this: the image over F(ζ_3) may be the subgroup of order 384 with abelianization Z/6Z, and the image over F(ζ_9) may then be its Sylow 2-subgroup, of order 128. The paper's further assertion that this subgroup of order 128 is not enormous is false; see the note.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.22 and Remark 7.5.23 (§7.5), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 204–205 (published pp. 400–401); Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, arXiv:1812.09269v3 (final version); Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501
items.note:
Split from item 99. Cited in Lemma 9.2.2 and in §§9–10 (arXiv pp. 254, 257, 272).

Proof:
- For #k > 3, PSL_2(k) is simple, and Goursat's lemma gives image SL_2(k)² over K(ζ_p), hence SL_2(k) ≀ Z/2Z over F(ζ_{p^N}); Lemmas 7.5.18–7.5.19 then apply.
- For k = F_3, use the disjointness hypothesis and Lemma 7.5.21.
- Tidiness is Lemma 7.5.13 for p ≥ 5. For p = 3, take an element of order 8 with ν = −1 and eigenvalues (ζ, −ζ^{-1}, ζ, −ζ^{-1}).
The PGL_2 facts used (automorphisms of PSL_2(k)) are of the kind ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 plans for GL_2.

Two mistakes, not recorded by the extraction. Both texts are the same in the published version (p. 401).

(a) Error in the proof for k = F_3 (arXiv p. 205). The paper says: 'The abelianization of this group has order prime to 3, so the image of ρ̄ restricted to F(ζ_{3^N}) is also of this form.' This is false: (A, B)σ^e ↦ χ(A) + χ(B) is a surjection SL_2(F_3) ≀ Z/2Z → Z/3Z, and the abelianization is Z/6Z. The conclusion survives. For N ≥ 2, the image over F(ζ_{3^N}) is either SL_2(F_3) ≀ Z/2Z, or its unique normal subgroup of index 3, K = {(A, B) : χ(A) = −χ(B)} ⋊ ⟨σ⟩. K is the enormous group H of Lemma 7.5.21(3)(b). K has no quotient of order 3, because σ inverts the Z/3Z quotient of {(A, B) : χ(A) = −χ(B)}. So the image is enormous for all N ≥ 2. This affects the proof only.

(b) Error in Remark 7.5.23. The subgroup of order 128 is a Sylow 2-subgroup of Sp_4(F_3), namely Q_8 ≀ Z/2Z, and it is enormous. Checks:
- (E1) holds, since its order is prime to 3.
- (E2): the natural representation restricts to Q_8 × Q_8 as V_A ⊕ V_B, non-isomorphic irreducibles swapped by σ.
- Decomposition: ad^0 = Sym²W = Ind(χ_1) ⊕ Ind(χ_2) ⊕ Ind(χ_3) ⊕ As(V), where χ_j runs over the nontrivial characters of Q_8/{±1}.
- (E3): the elements with four distinct eigenvalues are g = (a, b)σ with ab of order 4, and their eigenvalues are the primitive 8th roots of unity. Such g acts on Ind(χ_j) with eigenvalues ±√χ_j(ab), which include 1 when ab ∈ ker χ_j, and acts on As(V) with eigenvalues 1, −1, i, −i.
A machine check on a characteristic-zero model agreed: the group has order 128; the natural character and the four constituents all have norm 1; 48 elements have distinct eigenvalues; and 16, 16, 16 and 48 of them have eigenvalue 1 on the respective constituents. This is consistent with the enormous class of order 128 listed in §7.5.20. It affects nothing, since the remark only motivates the p = 3 hypothesis. With that image, ρ̄ would in fact be vast.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles data for GSp_4, the augmented problem S_Q, Δ_Q and the Λ[Δ_Q]-structure
items.statement:
Fix a global deformation problem S = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, ψ, {D_v}_{v∈S}) for GSp_4 (Definition 7.1.5; p > 2).
A Taylor–Wiles datum is a tuple (Q, (ᾱ_{v,1},…,ᾱ_{v,4})_{v∈Q}) consisting of:
- a finite set Q of finite places of F, disjoint from S, with q_v ≡ 1 mod p for each v ∈ Q;
- for each v ∈ Q, an ordering ᾱ_{v,1}, ᾱ_{v,2}, ᾱ_{v,3} = ψ̄(Frob_v)ᾱ_{v,2}^{−1}, ᾱ_{v,4} = ψ̄(Frob_v)ᾱ_{v,1}^{−1} of the eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_v), which are assumed k-rational and pairwise distinct.
The augmented problem is S_Q = (ρ̄, S ∪ Q, {Λ_v}_{v∈S} ∪ {O}_{v∈Q}, ψ, {D_v}_{v∈S} ∪ {D_v^□}_{v∈Q}).
Let Δ_v = k(v)^×(p)^2, where k(v)^×(p) is the maximal p-power quotient of k(v)^×, and Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q}Δ_v. The orderings determine a Λ[Δ_Q]-algebra structure on R^T_{S_Q} for every T ⊆ S, through the homomorphisms O[Δ_v] → R_v^□ of §7.4.3. (Those come from Lemma 7.4.4: the universal lift at v is conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ψγ_2^{−1} ⊕ ψγ_1^{−1}, and γ_i∘Art_{F_v}|_{O_{F_v}^×} factors through k(v)^×(p).) With a_Q = ker(Λ[Δ_Q] → Λ) the augmentation ideal, the natural surjection R^T_{S_Q} → R^T_S has kernel a_Q R^T_{S_Q}.
items.locator: §7.6 (Taylor–Wiles primes), the definitions before Lemma 7.6.1, arXiv p. 208, with §7.4.3, arXiv p. 189; published pp. 404–405

The GL_n analogues are planned (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 and G7; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.4); the GSp_4 version with ordered symplectic pairs of eigenvalues is not. items.name: Definition 7.8.2: the tame levels K^p, K_0^p(Q), K_1^p(Q) and K_0^p(Q,R)
items.statement:
Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, with v_0 chosen as in §7.8.
- K^p = ∏_v K_v ⊂ GSp_4(A_F^{∞,p}) is the open compact subgroup with K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S_p ∪ R ∪ {v_0}, and K_v = Iw_1(v) for v ∈ R ∪ {v_0}. Here Iw(v) and Iw_1(v) are the preimages in GSp_4(O_{F_v}) of B(k(v)) and U(k(v)) (§2.4), so Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) ≅ T(k(v)).
- For a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q, (ᾱ_{v,i})_{v∈Q}): K_0^p(Q)_v = K_1^p(Q)_v = K^p_v for v ∉ Q, and K_0^p(Q)_v = Iw(v), K_1^p(Q)_v = Iw_1(v) for v ∈ Q.
- K_0^p(Q,R)_v = K^p_v for v ∉ Q ∪ R, and K_0^p(Q,R)_v = Iw(v) for v ∈ Q ∪ R.
- K_1^p(Q,R) := K_1^p(Q), which is already Iw_1(v) at v ∈ R.
Thus K_1^p(Q) ⊂ K_0^p(Q,R).
items.locator: Definition 7.8.2 (§7.8), arXiv pp. 211–212; published pp. 408–409
items.note: Split from item 101; used in Propositions 7.8.10, 7.8.11 and 7.9.8. Neither library has GSp_4, Iwahori or pro-v Iwahori subgroups. No atlas layer plans these levels: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H4 plans Iwahori levels for Hilbert varieties only.

items.name: Lemma 7.8.3: a level with pro-v Iwahori component at an absolutely unramified place of residue characteristic > 5 is neat
items.statement:
Let K = ∏_v K_v ⊂ GSp_4(A_F^∞) be an open compact subgroup. Suppose some place v of F is absolutely unramified, of residue characteristic greater than 5, with K_v = Iw_1(v). Then K is neat (Definition 3.2.1). Applied with v = v_0, the lemma shows that K_pK_0^p(Q) and K_pK_1^p(Q) are neat for every compact open K_p ⊂ GSp_4(F ⊗ Q_p).
Proof. Let ζ be an eigenvalue of an element of Iw_1(v) that is a root of unity. The characteristic polynomial reduces to (X − 1)^4, so v(1 − ζ) ≥ 1/4. If ζ ≠ 1, then v(1 − ζ) is 0 or at most 1/(l − 1) < 1/4, since l > 5.
items.locator: Lemma 7.8.3 (§7.8), arXiv p. 212; published p. 409
items.note: Split from item 101; used in §7.7, §7.8 and, through Definition 7.13.4, in §7.13. ShimuraData D5 defines neatness, and ShimuraVarieties V0 proves that neat congruence subgroups exist; neither states this criterion. Neither library has neat subgroups of GSp_4(A_F).

items.name: The Hecke algebras T̃^I and T̃^{I,Q}, the maximal ideals m̃^{I,𝔠} (7.8.4), and the modules M^{χ,I,𝔠}, M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} with their Hecke algebras T^{χ,I,𝔠}, T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}
items.statement:
Assume Hypothesis 7.8.1, with v_0 and K^p as in Definition 7.8.2.
Spherical Hecke algebras. T̃ = ⊗'_{v∉S_p∪R∪{v_0}} O[GSp_4(F_v)//GSp_4(O_{F_v})], and T̃^Q is the same over v ∉ S_p ∪ R ∪ {v_0} ∪ Q.
The maximal ideal of ρ̄. m̃^{an} ⊂ T̃ is the maximal ideal of ρ̄: it contains λ, and det(X − ρ̄(Frob_v)) ≡ Q_v(X) modulo m̃^{an} for all v ∉ S_p ∪ R ∪ {v_0}. Here Q_v(X) = X^4 − T_{v,1}X^3 + (q_vT_{v,2} + (q_v^3 + q_v)T_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^3T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + q_v^6T_{v,0}^2 ∈ T̃[X] (cf. (2.4.8)). m̃^{an,Q} ⊂ T̃^Q is defined likewise.
Adding the operators at p. For I ⊆ S_p, T̃^I = T̃[{U_{v,0}, U_{Kli(v),1}, U_{v,2}}_{v∈I}, {U_{v,0}, U_{v,1}, U_{v,2}}_{v∈I^c}], and T̃^{I,Q} = T̃^Q[the same operators]. For a choice 𝔠, m̃^{I,𝔠} = (m̃^{an}, {U_{v,0} − 1, U_{v,2} − ᾱ_vβ̄_v}_{v∈S_p}, {U_{Kli(v),1} − ᾱ_v − β̄_v}_{v∈I}, {U_{v,1} − 𝔠_v}_{v∈I^c}) ⊂ T̃^I (7.8.4), where ᾱ_v, β̄_v, 𝔠_v stand for any lifts to O. m̃^{I,𝔠,Q} ⊂ T̃^{I,Q} is defined in the same way from m̃^{an,Q}.
The modules. Let χ = (χ_{v,1}, χ_{v,2})_{v∈R} be characters of I_{F_v} of p-power order, viewed as characters of T(k(v)) through Art_{F_v}. Then:
- M^{χ,I,𝔠} = RHom^0_{Λ_I}(M^{•,I}_{K^p}, Λ_I)_{m̃^{I,𝔠},χ,|·|^2}, a Λ_I-module;
- M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} = RHom^0_{Λ_I}(M^{•,I}_{K_1^p(Q)}, Λ_I)_{m̃^{I,𝔠,Q},m̃_Q,χ,|·|^2}, a Λ_I[Δ_Q]-module.
The notation is as follows. M^{•,I}_{K^p} is the complex M_I^• of Theorem 4.6.1 at tame level K^p. m̃_Q is localization at the maximal ideals m̃_v (v ∈ Q) of the subalgebras O[T(F_v)/T(O_{F_v})_1] of the pro-v Iwahori Hecke algebras H_1(v) (§2.4.29), where λ, U_{v,0} − 1 ∈ m̃_v and U_{v,1}, U_{v,2} ≡ ᾱ_{v,1}, ᾱ_{v,1}ᾱ_{v,2} mod m̃_v. The subscript χ means χ-coinvariants for ∏_{v∈R}T(k(v)). The subscript |·|^2 means coinvariants under T_{v,0} − q_v^{−2} for all v ∉ S_p ∪ R ∪ {v_0}.
The Hecke algebras on the modules. T^{χ,I,𝔠} (resp. T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}) is the Λ_I-subalgebra of End_{Λ_I}(M^{χ,I,𝔠}) (resp. End_{Λ_I}(M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q})) generated by the image of T̃^I (resp. T̃^{I,Q}). None of these objects depends on 𝔠_v for v ∈ I. For v ∈ I, Hensel's lemma and ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v give X^2 − U_{Kli(v),1}X + U_{v,2} = (X − α̃_v)(X − β̃_v), with α̃_v, β̃_v ∈ T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} lifting ᾱ_v, β̄_v.
items.locator: §7.8 between Lemma 7.8.3 and Lemma 7.8.5, including (7.8.4), arXiv pp. 212–213; and the opening paragraph of §7.9, arXiv p. 216; published pp. 409–410 and 415
items.note:
No item covered this construction. Item 103 wrongly attributed the modules to Definition 7.8.8 and gave RHom^0 into Λ_I[Δ_Q]. The construction depends on Theorem 4.6.1 (item 63, higher Hida theory) and on Lemma 7.8.5. No atlas layer or library has GSp_4 Hecke algebras over Λ_I.
Notation: (7.8.4) is printed with α_vβ_v and α_v + β_v without bars; since λ ∈ m̃^{an}, any lifts of ᾱ_v, β̄_v give the same ideal. The sentence before Lemma 7.8.5 refers to 'M^{χ,I,𝔠,W}', a misprint for M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} (in both versions).

items.name: Proposition 7.8.10: the covers at Taylor–Wiles and Ihara-avoidance places extend finite étale over the toroidal compactification
items.statement:
Setting. Let K_p be a reasonable level at p (for example K_p(I)), and Σ a good polyhedral cone decomposition. Let X_{K_pK_0^p(Q,R),Σ} and X_{K_pK_1^p(Q,R),Σ} be the toroidal compactifications for the same Σ. Over the interior Y_{K_pK_0^p(Q,R)}, for each v ∈ Q ∪ R, there is a flag 0 ⊂ H_v ⊂ L_v ⊂ H_v^⊥ ⊂ A[v] whose graded pieces are étale k(v)-group schemes of rank 1.
Proposition 7.8.10. (1) For all v ∈ Q ∪ R, the groups H_v, L_v/H_v, H_v^⊥/L_v and A[v]/H_v^⊥ extend to finite étale k(v)-group schemes of rank 1 over X_{K_pK_0^p(Q,R),Σ}. (2) The map X_{K_pK_1^p(Q,R),Σ} → X_{K_pK_0^p(Q,R),Σ} is finite étale with group ∏_{v∈Q∪R}T(k(v)), and X_{K_pK_1^p(Q,R),Σ} identifies with the torsor of trivializations of H_v, L_v/H_v, H_v^⊥/L_v and A[v]/H_v^⊥ compatible with duality.
Proof outline. Work in the completion along a σ-stratum, using Mumford's construction A = B/X_σ. Each subquotient either extends as a subquotient of B[v], or maps isomorphically to X_σ ⊗_{O_F} k(v) and is constant. The torsor of trivializations is normal, finite flat, and generically equal to X_{K_pK_1^p(Q,R),Σ}.
items.locator: Proposition 7.8.10 (§7.8), arXiv pp. 214–215; published pp. 412–413
items.note: Split from item 104. It is used in the proofs of Propositions 7.8.11 and 7.9.8. For F = Q it is Stroh [Str15, §2.4.5]. ShimuraCompactifications C4 plans the comparison of level structures across boundary charts in general, not these prime-to-p Iwahori covers. The proof prints 'compatible with duality for all v|p'; it should read v ∈ Q ∪ R.

items.name: Corollary 7.9.6: Galois representations for ordinary cuspidal representations of GSp_4 of parallel weight 2
items.statement:
Corollary 7.9.6. Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 with central character |·|^2. Fix a prime p > 2, and assume that π is ordinary. Then there is a continuous semisimple representation ρ_{π,p} : G_F → GL_4(Q̄_p) such that:
(1) for each finite place v ∤ p at which π_v is unramified, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and det(X − ρ_{π,p}(Frob_v)) = Q_v(X).
Suppose further that ρ̄_{π,p} is vast and tidy, and that for each v | p the ordinary Hecke parameters α_v, β_v of π_v satisfy ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v. Then ρ_{π,p} can be conjugated into GSp_4(Q̄_p), and:
(2) ν∘ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1};
(3) for each finite place v ∤ p, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})^{ss};
(4) for each v | p, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} ≅ [[λ_{α_v}, 0, *, *], [0, λ_{β_v}, *, *], [0, 0, λ_{β_v}^{−1}ε^{−1}, 0], [0, 0, 0, λ_{α_v}^{−1}ε^{−1}]] (rows).
Proof outline.
- If π is not of general type: GL_1 and GL_2 results give a reducible ρ_{π,p} satisfying (1), and (2)–(4) are vacuous.
- If π is of general type: Mok [Mok14, Thm. 4.14] gives (1) and (3) with GL_4 values. Then base change to a solvable totally real F'/F, linearly disjoint from the fixed field of ker ρ̄_{π,p}, with p split and Iwahori-fixed vectors everywhere [Mok14, Prop. 4.13], and apply Theorem 7.9.4 with I = S_p, χ = 1 and Q = ∅.
items.locator: Corollary 7.9.6 (§7.9), arXiv pp. 220–221; published pp. 420–421
items.note:
Split from item 106. It is used in the proofs of Corollary 8.2.2 and Lemma 8.3.2 (arXiv pp. 238 and 247). It extends Theorems 2.7.1–2.7.2 (item 28) to parallel weight 2.
Gap in the proof (not yet recorded as a source issue). The proof takes ρ̄ := ρ̄_{π,p} and asserts that Hypothesis 7.8.1 holds after the base change, having arranged only that p splits completely in F' and that Π has Iwahori-fixed vectors at every finite place. Two conditions are not checked.
(a) Conditions (4)(a) and (5)(c) need a set R containing every place where Π is ramified, at which ρ̄ is trivial and q_w ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3). A place where Π is ramified with Iwahori-fixed vectors, and where ρ̄ is nontrivial or q_w ≢ 1 mod p, violates them. This is repaired by also requiring F' to trivialize ρ̄ and to make q_w ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3) at the places above the ramification of π, as the proof of Theorem 8.4.1 does (arXiv p. 248).
(b) Condition (3), that ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary for v | p, is conclusion (4) reduced modulo λ, and §7.3 assumes it before defining the local problems D_v^P and D_v^{B,𝔠_v} that Theorem 7.9.4 uses. The corollary assumes only ᾱ_v ≠ β̄_v for the Hecke parameters, and the proof gives no argument for (3).
In both later uses ρ_{π,p} ≅ ρ for a ρ that is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary by hypothesis, so (b) holds there, and (a) is repaired as above; the results of §8 are not affected.

items.name: Lemma 7.9.7: Nakayama's lemma for bounded complexes of complete flat modules
items.statement: Lemma 7.9.7. Let Λ ∈ CNL_O, and let f^• : C^• → D^• be a morphism of bounded complexes of m_Λ-adically complete and separated flat Λ-modules. Suppose that the induced morphism C^• ⊗^L_Λ Λ/m_Λ → D^• ⊗^L_Λ Λ/m_Λ is a quasi-isomorphism. Then f^• is a quasi-isomorphism. ([Pil20, Prop. 2.2].)
items.locator: Lemma 7.9.7 (§7.9), arXiv p. 222; published p. 421
items.note:
Split from item 107.
Why planned: DD.1 plans conservativity of reduction on derived complete objects. A bounded complex of m_Λ-adically complete separated flat modules over the Noetherian ring Λ is derived m_Λ-complete, so applying that conservativity to the cone of f^• gives the lemma. P7 plans derived Nakayama for complexes over complete Noetherian local O-algebras. The extraction of Pilloni's 2020 paper records the same statement (its Proposition 2.2.2) as planned at these two stages.
Neither library has derived Nakayama.
Misprint: the paper prints Λ/m_λ for Λ/m_Λ, in the published version too.

items.name: §7.11: the patching construction (S_∞, R_∞^{1,I,𝔠}, R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}, M_∞^{1,I,𝔠}, M_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}) and the dimension identity (7.11.1)
items.locator: §7.11 (The patching construction) with (7.11.1), arXiv pp. 224–226; published pp. 424–426
items.note: No item covered this construction. Item 150 (Proposition 7.10.1, planned at DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5, P8 and P9) is its abstract input, and item 108 (Proposition 7.11.2) its first consequence. Misprint: the paper prints R^1_N := R_N^{1,∞,𝔠}⊗̂_Λ T and R^χ_N := R_N^{χ,∞,𝔠}⊗̂_Λ T; the superscript ∞ should be I (the same in the published version).

items.name: §7.12: top-dimensional cycles Z(R), the cycle Z(M, R) of a module, the special-fibre cycles η̄, and the maximal O-flat quotient R'
items.statement:
This follows Emerton–Gee [EG14, §2].
- Cycles. For an equidimensional Noetherian local ring R of dimension d, a d-cycle on Spec R is a formal Z-linear combination of the generic points of Spec R. The d-cycles form the group Z^d(R), also written Z(R).
- The cycle of a module. For a finite R-module M, Z(M, R) = Σ_η len_{R_η}(M_η)·η, the sum over the generic points η of Spec R.
- Special-fibre cycles. If R is an equidimensional flat Noetherian O-algebra of dimension d + 1 and η is a generic point of Spec R, then R^η is the quotient of R by the corresponding minimal prime, and η̄ := Z(R^η/(λ), R/(λ)) ∈ Z^d(R/(λ)).
- The maximal O-flat quotient. For R ∈ CNL_O, R' is its maximal O-flat (p-torsion free) quotient, namely the image of R in R[1/p]. An O-flat R-module is naturally an R'-module.
items.locator: §7.12, the recollections before Lemma 7.12.2, arXiv pp. 226–227; published pp. 426–427 (R' is introduced in §7.11 before (7.11.1))
items.note: Mathlib has Module.length and minimal primes, but no cycle groups. No atlas layer plans cycles of modules over local deformation rings; the extraction of Le–Le Hung–Levin–Morra 2020 also records [EG14, Lemma 2.2.14] as missing.

items.name: §7.12: cycles of O-flat modules modulo λ, and cycles of completed tensor products (Emerton–Gee Prop. 2.2.13 and Lem. 2.2.14; Thorne Lems. 1.3–1.4)
items.statement:
(a) [EG14, Prop. 2.2.13]. Let R be an equidimensional flat Noetherian O-algebra of dimension d + 1 and M a finite O-flat R-module. Then Z(M/λM, R/(λ)) = Σ_η len_{R_η}(M_η)·η̄, the sum over the generic points η of Spec R.
(b) [Tho15, Lem. 1.3]. For R_1, R_2 ∈ CNL_O, the natural map R_1⊗̂R_2 → R_1'⊗̂R_2' induces (R_1⊗̂R_2)' ≅ R_1'⊗̂R_2'. (The kernel is p-power torsion and R_1'⊗̂R_2' is O-flat.)
(c) [Tho15, Lem. 1.4]. Let R_1, R_2 ∈ CNL_O be O-flat and equidimensional of dimensions d_1 + 1 and d_2 + 1, with all irreducible components of Spec R_i and Spec R_i/(λ) geometrically irreducible. Then R = R_1⊗̂_O R_2 is O-flat and equidimensional of dimension d_1 + d_2 + 1. For generic points η_i of Spec R_i, the kernel of R → R_1^{η_1}⊗̂R_2^{η_2} is a minimal prime, giving a generic point (η_1, η_2), and every generic point arises this way. For minimal primes 𝔭_i of R_i/(λ), (𝔭_1, 𝔭_2) = ker(R/(λ) → R_1/(λ,𝔭_1)⊗̂R_2/(λ,𝔭_2)) is a minimal prime of R/(λ), and every minimal prime arises this way. Hence Z^{d_1}(R_1/(λ)) ⊗ Z^{d_2}(R_2/(λ)) ≅ Z^{d_1+d_2}(R/(λ)), η_1⊗η_2 ↦ (η_1, η_2).
(d) [EG14, Lem. 2.2.14]. For finite R_i-modules M_i and M = M_1⊗̂_O M_2, Z(M_1/λM_1, R_1/(λ)) ⊗ Z(M_2/λM_2, R_2/(λ)) = Z(M/λM, R/(λ)) (7.12.1). In particular R^η ≃ R_1^{η_1}⊗̂R_2^{η_2} and η̄ = η̄_1 ⊗ η̄_2 for η = (η_1, η_2).
items.locator: §7.12, the recollections before Lemma 7.12.2, including (7.12.1), arXiv pp. 226–227; published pp. 427–428
items.note: These are cited results; the paper does not prove them. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 plans completed tensor products over O and when they remain Noetherian and local, but not their dimension, minimal primes or cycles. Neither library has these results.

items.name: §7.13: the primes p_x, p̃^{an}_{x'}, p̃^{I,𝔠}_{x'} (7.13.3), smooth points, and the spaces S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)} and S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(I),χ}
items.statement:
Points and primes.
- Let x be a closed point of Spec R^{1,I,𝔠}[1/p] or Spec R^{χ,I,𝔠}[1/p], with E enlarged to contain its residue field; x gives ρ_x : G_F → GSp_4(O). p_x is the prime ideal that is the kernel of R^{1,I,𝔠} → E (resp. R^{χ,I,𝔠} → E), so that the quotient by p_x has dimension one (the paper says 'height one'; see the note). The same symbol denotes its pullbacks along R^{·,I,𝔠,loc} → R_∞^{·,I,𝔠} → R^{·,I,𝔠}.
- x is smooth if R^{1,I,𝔠,loc}_{p_x} (resp. R^{χ,I,𝔠,loc}_{p_x}) is regular.
- Let ρ' : G_F → GSp_4(O) give a point x' of R^{1,I,𝔠} or R^{χ,I,𝔠}. p̃^{an}_{x'} ⊂ T̃ is the prime generated by the coefficients of Q_v(X) − det(X − ρ'(Frob_v)) for v ∉ R ∪ S_p ∪ {v_0}.
- p̃^{I,𝔠}_{x'} = (p̃^{an}_{x'}, {U_{v,0} − 1, U_{v,2} − α'_vβ'_v}_{v∈S_p}, {U_{Kli(v),1} − α'_v − β'_v}_{v∈I}, {U_{v,1} − 𝔠'_v}_{v∈I^c}) ⊂ T̃^I (7.13.3). Here α'_v ≡ ᾱ_v and β'_v ≡ β̄_v (mod λ), and 𝔠'_v ∈ {α'_v, β'_v} is the lift of 𝔠_v; all are determined by ρ'|_{G_{F_v}} as in §7.3.
Spaces of p-adic forms. Fix I ⊆ S_p, 𝔠, a classical algebraic weight κ, and K^{p,Iw} as in Definition 7.13.4.
- S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)} is the subspace of (e(U^I)H^0(𝔛^{I,G_1}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D))_{m̃^{I,𝔠}}) ⊗_O E annihilated by {U_{v,0} − 1}_{v∈S_p}, {U_{v,0} − q_v^{−2}}_{v∈R} and {T_{v,0} − q_v^{−2}}_{v∉S_p∪R∪{v_0}}.
- S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(I),χ} := (S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(I)})^{∏_{v∈R}Iw(v)/Iw_1(v)=χ}, the subspace with nebentypus χ.
Duality with the patched modules. By Lemma 7.8.5 (2):
- (M^{1,I,𝔠}/p_κM^{1,I,𝔠})[1/p] ≃ (S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)})^∨, and (M^{χ,I,𝔠}/p_κM^{χ,I,𝔠})[1/p] ≃ (S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(I),χ})^∨;
- for ρ' of weight κ (that is, Λ_I → R^{·,I,𝔠} → E equals κ), (M_∞^{1,I,𝔠}/p_{x'}M_∞^{1,I,𝔠})[1/p] ≃ (M^{1,I,𝔠}/p_{x'}M^{1,I,𝔠})[1/p] ≃ (S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃^{I,𝔠}_{x'}])^∨;
- likewise (M_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}/p_{x'}M_∞^{χ,I,𝔠})[1/p] ≃ (M^{χ,I,𝔠}/p_{x'}M^{χ,I,𝔠})[1/p] ≃ (S^{I,𝔠}_{κ,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(I),χ}[p̃^{I,𝔠}_{x'}])^∨.
items.locator: §7.13, between Remark 7.13.2 and Proposition 7.13.5, including (7.13.3) and Definition 7.13.4, arXiv pp. 230–231; published pp. 431–433
items.note:
No item covered these definitions. Theorem 7.13.6 and Theorem 8.2.1 are stated in terms of them.
Misprint: the paper's second display has M^{1,I,𝔠} as its middle term where M^{χ,I,𝔠} is meant (the same in the published version).
Wording: the paper calls p_x (and, on arXiv p. 234, p̃^{I,𝔠}_π) a 'height one' prime. As the kernel of a map to E it has one-dimensional quotient; its height is in general larger than one, and for the patched rings R_∞, along which the same symbol is pulled back, it is far larger. 'Dimension one' is meant; nothing depends on it.
Notation: in (7.13.3) 𝔠'_v is the lift of 𝔠_v determined by ρ', whereas in §7.3, (7.9.2) and Proposition 7.13.9 the symbol 𝔠'_v denotes the other eigenvalue ᾱ_vβ̄_v/𝔠_v (or its lift).

items.name: Lemma 7.13.8: a maximal Cohen–Macaulay patched module is free at smooth points (Diamond–Fujiwara)
items.statement:
Lemma 7.13.8. Let R be (R_∞^{1,I,𝔠})' or (R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠})' for some I and 𝔠, and let M be a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module. Let x ∈ Spec R[1/p] be a smooth closed point with residue field E, and p_x ⊂ R the corresponding prime ideal. Then M_{p_x} is a free R_{p_x}-module. Hence, if η is the unique generic point of Spec R specializing to x, dim_{R_η} M_η = dim_E(M/p_xM)[1/p].
Proof: a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over a regular local ring is free.
items.locator: Lemma 7.13.8 (§7.13), arXiv p. 232; published p. 434
items.note:
Split from item 112; used only in the proof of Theorem 7.13.6.
Why planned: the content is general. A maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring, localized at a prime where the ring is regular, is free, with rank read off at the generic point. R03.3 plans regular sequences, depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings and modules, projective dimension, Auslander–Buchsbaum, and depth and dimension formulas under the maps used. The lemma is their standard corollary together with Serre's theorem that finite modules over a regular local ring have finite projective dimension, which R03.3 does not name and must include.
Libraries: Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing, regular sequences, Rees's theorem relating regular sequences to the vanishing of Ext, and projective dimension (including its change under quotient by a regular element), but no depth invariant, no Auslander–Buchsbaum formula and no Cohen–Macaulay modules.

items.name: Proposition 7.13.9: the doubling injection (U_{w,1} − 𝔠'_w) from Klingen to Iwahori level at w
items.statement:
Proposition 7.13.9. Let ρ = ρ_x, as in Hypothesis 7.13.1. For any I ⊆ S_p, w ∈ I^c, K^p as in Definition 7.13.4 and choice 𝔠, there is an injection (U_{w,1} − 𝔠'_w) : S^{I∪{w},𝔠}_{κ_2,K^pK_p(I∪{w})}[p̃_x^{I∪{w},𝔠}] → S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^pK_p(I)}[p̃_x^{I,𝔠}]. Here 𝔠'_w is the unit eigenvalue of ρ_x at w that does not reduce to 𝔠_w, as in (7.9.2).
Proof: the statement reduces to O-coefficients, and hence to the injectivity of (7.9.3) with w = v. That injectivity was proved in the proof of Proposition 7.9.1, from Theorem 5.8.6.
items.locator: Proposition 7.13.9 (§7.13), arXiv p. 233; published p. 434
items.note:
Split from item 112. It is used in the proof of Theorem 7.13.6, and again in §8 (arXiv pp. 236, 238 and 240), including the proof of Theorem 8.2.1. It depends on the doubling Theorem 5.8.6 (item 73).
Notation: 𝔠'_w here has the meaning of §7.3 and (7.9.2), not that of (7.13.3), where 𝔠'_v is the lift of 𝔠_v. Only this reading makes the map land in the target: by (7.9.2), the image of U_{w,1} − 𝔠'_w is killed by U_{w,1} minus the lift of 𝔠_w.

items.name: Proposition 7.13.11: dimensions of the ρ_reg- and π-eigenspaces in regular weight and in weight κ_2
items.statement:
Setting: the notation of the proof of Theorem 7.13.6.
- ρ_reg : G_F → GSp_4(O) is a point of weight κ_reg in the support of M^{1,∅,𝔠}/p_{κ_reg}M^{1,∅,𝔠}, on the same component of R_∞^{1,∅,𝔠} as ρ.
- ρ^χ_reg is a point of weight κ_reg in the support of M^{χ,∅,𝔠}/p_{κ_reg}M^{χ,∅,𝔠}.
- π is the representation of Hypothesis 7.13.1 (6), and p̃_π^{I,𝔠} its prime.
Proposition 7.13.11. dim_E S^{∅,𝔠}_{κ_reg,K^{p,Iw}K_p(∅)}[p̃^{∅,𝔠}_{x_reg}] = 8d_ρ; dim_E S^{∅,𝔠}_{κ_reg,K^{p,Iw_1}K_p(∅),χ}[p̃^{∅,𝔠}_{x^χ_reg}] = 8; and dim_E S^{I,𝔠}_{κ_2,K^{p,Iw}K_p(I)}[p̃^{I,𝔠}_π] ≥ 8d_{ρ_{π,p}} (7.13.10). Moreover there are automorphic representations π_reg and π^χ_reg of GSp_4(A_F), of weight κ_reg and central character |·|^2, with ρ_{π_reg,p} ≅ ρ_reg and ρ_{π^χ_reg,p} ≅ ρ^χ_reg.
Proof outline.
- By Theorems 6.6.5 and 3.10.1, the first dimension is Σ_π dim_{Ē}(π^∞)^{K^{p,Iw}K_p(∅), {U_{v,1} = 𝔠_v^{reg}, U_{v,2} = α_v^{reg}β_v^{reg}}_{v∈S_p}}. The sum runs over cuspidal π of weight κ_reg, with central character |·|^2, holomorphic at infinity, and with ρ_{π,p} ≅ ρ_reg.
- Such π are of general type (Lemma 2.9.1). By strong multiplicity one for GL_4 (Jacquet–Shalika) and Arthur's classification (Theorem 2.9.3), the sum equals (Σ_{π_{v_0}∈L(ρ_reg|G_{F_{v_0}})} dim π_{v_0}^{Iw_1(v_0)}) · ∏_{v∈R}(Σ_{π_v∈L(ρ_reg|G_{F_v})} dim π_v^{Iw(v)}).
- Away from R ∪ S_p ∪ {v_0}, the hyperspecial invariants are 1-dimensional. At v ∈ S_p the contribution is 1-dimensional (Propositions 2.4.24 and 2.4.26).
- dim π_{v_0}^{Iw_1(v_0)} = 8, by Propositions 2.4.6, 2.4.3 and 2.4.4 and the choice of v_0.
- Proposition 7.13.5 applies at v ∈ R: purity holds by Theorem 2.7.2 (4), and genericity by Lemma 7.1.3 and Proposition 2.4.22.
- For ρ^χ_reg, Σ_{π_v∈L(ρ^χ_reg|G_{F_v})} dim π_v^{Iw_1(v),χ} = 1 by Proposition 2.4.28.
- The last inequality is the contribution of π, which occurs by Theorem 3.10.1.
items.locator: Proposition 7.13.11 (§7.13), arXiv pp. 234–235; published pp. 436–437
items.note: Split from item 112. It is used only in the proof of Theorem 7.13.6, but it carries that theorem's dependence on Arthur's classification for GSp_4 (Theorem 2.9.3; its conditional status is recorded in items 32–33) and on the Roberts–Schmidt tables through Proposition 7.13.5. No atlas layer or library has these counts.

items.name: Definition 2.8.2 and Remark 2.8.3: the GSp_4-valued compatible system 𝓡_A of an abelian surface
items.statement: Definition 2.8.2. If A/F is an abelian surface over a number field F, then ρ_{A,l} := H^1(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l) and 𝓡_A := {ρ_{A,l}}; ρ_{A,l} is regarded as a representation ρ_{A,l} : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_l) with multiplier ε_l^{−1}, and the paper does so without comment. Remark 2.8.3. A set of GSp_4-valued representations is said to form a compatible system when the corresponding GL_4-valued representations form a compatible system; in particular the ρ_{A,l} : G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_l) of Definition 2.8.2 form a compatible system in this sense. No compatibility between the symplectic structures is required: every representation the paper considers has the inverse cyclotomic character as multiplier.
items.locator: Definition 2.8.2 and Remark 2.8.3 (§2.8), arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 36–37; Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) p. 195
items.note: Split from item 30, which keeps Proposition 2.8.1, a general theorem about abelian varieties routed to its general owner. These are the paper's conventions for abelian surfaces and are used throughout §§9–10: Definitions 9.1.6 and 9.1.8, Lemma 9.2.2, Theorem 9.3.1 and Proposition 10.1.1. The symplectic structure comes from the Weil pairing of a polarization (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 plans the pairing induced by a polarization); strict compatibility and purity of 𝓡_A are Proposition 2.8.1. Checked against the text of arXiv v3 pp. 36–37 and the published p. 195. Neither library has compatible systems of Galois representations.

items.name: Serre–Tate coordinates at interior points of the Hilbert–Siegel formal models and the local form of the p-isogeny correspondences of §4.5
items.statement: Let p split completely in F and let x be a closed point in the interior of one of the formal models 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) or 𝔛^I_{K'',Kli}(p^m) of §4.5. Then the completed local ring at x is Ô_x ≅ ⊗̂_{v|p}W(k(x))[[T_{1,v},T_{2,v},T_{3,v}]], and at a place w where 𝒢_{x,w} is ordinary the T_{i,w} can be taken to be Serre–Tate coordinates for the polarization type at w. A correspondence given by an isogeny that is an isomorphism at every v ≠ w, and at w divides out a subgroup of the étale part, acts on completed local rings by T_{i,v} ↦ T_{i,v} for v ≠ w and T_{i,w} ↦ (1+T_{i,w})^p − 1 on the coordinates it affects: (1) for u_1 : 𝔠_{w,1}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) (proof of Lemma 4.5.4, w ∈ I^c, so 𝒢_w is ordinary), on all three coordinates T_{1,w}, T_{2,w}, T_{3,w}, so u_1 is totally inseparable and p^{−3}du_1 is integral; (2) for r_1 : 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m) → 𝔛^I_{K,Kli}(p^m) (proof of Lemma 4.5.10, at interior points ordinary at w), on T_{2,w} and T_{3,w} only, giving inseparability degree p^2; (3) for s_2 at the paramodular level K'' (proof of Lemma 4.5.13), on T_{3,w} only, s_2 being totally inseparable of degree p at every interior point, since its fibre parametrizes the étale subgroups of rank p in the kernel of the quasi-polarization 𝒢_w → 𝒢_w^D, a finite flat group scheme of rank p^2 which the paper describes as an extension of an étale by a multiplicative subgroup.
items.note: Split from item 247, which keeps Katz's general Serre–Tate local moduli, routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 as the Pilloni (2020) and Boxer–Pilloni (2026) extractions route the same input. What stays here is the application at points of the formal schemes of the higher Hida theory, whose only use is the normalized traces of Lemmas 4.5.4, 4.5.10 and 4.5.13. It imports the product decomposition of the p-divisible group over v|p and the local structure of the Hilbert–Siegel models (Proposition 3.4.1). Two gaps for the design job: at paramodular level the polarization at w is not principal, so the coordinates must be those of the paramodular polarization type (as in Pilloni's chart (X, pZ; Z, Y)); and Lemma 4.5.13 fixes an arbitrary interior point, which for w ∈ I may have p-rank one at w, where Katz's coordinates do not apply as stated. The paper gives Lemma 4.5.13 only as 'a calculation in Serre–Tate theory which is similar to the proof of Lemma 4.5.10'. Checked against the text of arXiv v3 pp. 100–104.

prerequisites.citation: Kai-Wen Lan, "Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties", London Math. Soc. Monographs 36, Princeton (2013); "Compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties in ramified characteristics", Forum Math. Sigma 4 (2016), e1; "Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions", IMRN 2017, 3237–3280
prerequisites.why: The source of Theorem 3.5.1: the existence of integral toroidal compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties with their stratifications, boundary divisors, semi-abelian extensions and functoriality in the cone decomposition, including the ramified and parahoric-level cases which the atlas's ShimuraCompactifications C5 explicitly excludes. Also the source of neatness (Definition 1.4.1.8), of the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism (Theorem 6.4.1.1) and of the boundary charts used in §5.9.

prerequisites.citation: Wee Teck Gan and Shuichiro Takeda, "The local Langlands conjecture for GSp(4)", Ann. of Math. (2) 173 (2011), 1841–1882
prerequisites.why: The local Langlands correspondence rec_{GT} for GSp_4, its L-packets, and the characterization of the generic member of a packet by holomorphy of the adjoint L-factor at s = 1, which is part (vii) of their main theorem and is what Proposition 2.4.22 and Proposition 7.13.5 rest on. Every statement of local–global compatibility in the paper is phrased through it.

prerequisites.citation: James Arthur, "The endoscopic classification of representations: orthogonal and symplectic groups", AMS Colloquium Publications 61 (2013), and "Automorphic representations of GSp(4)", in Contributions to automorphic forms, geometry, and number theory (2004), 65–81, with Toby Gee and Olivier Taïbi, "Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4 and restriction to Sp_4", J. Éc. polytech. Math. 6 (2019), 469–535
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2.9.3, the transfer between GSp_4 and GL_4 with Arthur's multiplicity formula, on which the whole passage between the Galois representations and the automorphic forms depends. §1.4.1 of the paper states carefully that the Gee–Taïbi proof is only as unconditional as Arthur's book and the stabilisation of the twisted trace formula, and in particular depends on cases of the twisted weighted fundamental lemma whose proofs had not appeared; that dependency must be carried explicitly by any roadmap that consumes this.

prerequisites.citation: Richard Taylor, "Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations II", Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), 183–239
prerequisites.why: Ihara avoidance: the comparison of the patched modules over the deformation rings R^1 and R^χ at a place where the residual representation is trivial and q_v ≡ 1 mod p, through the cycles they define. §§7.4 and 7.12 follow it closely, and Propositions 7.4.7 and 7.4.8 are the GSp_4 analogues of its results for GL_n, with Remark 7.4.11 recording exactly where GSp_4 is harder.

prerequisites.citation: Fabrizio Andreatta, Adrian Iovita and Vincent Pilloni, "p-adic families of Siegel modular cuspforms", Ann. of Math. (2) 181 (2015), 623–697
prerequisites.why: The construction of the overconvergent locally analytic sheaves 𝓕^{κ_A,w} from the Hodge–Tate map and the canonical filtration, the analytic BGG resolution of §7.2 and the Hecke operators of §6.2, all of which §6 takes over with the modification recorded in the proof of Proposition 6.4.2. Also the vanishing theorem for the cohomology of a projective formal scheme with an affine analytic model, Theorem 6.1.3.

prerequisites.citation: Laurent Moret-Bailly, "Groupes de Picard et problèmes de Skolem I, II", Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. 22 (1989), 161–179 and 181–194; "Extensions de corps globaux à ramification et groupe de Galois donnés", C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 311 (1990), 273–276
prerequisites.why: The rational point theorem that turns the twisted moduli spaces of §§9.1 and 10.2 into elliptic curves and abelian surfaces with prescribed torsion and prescribed local behaviour. It is used three times: in Proposition 9.1.11, in the proof of Theorem 9.2.8 and in Theorem 10.2.1.

prerequisites.citation: Richard Taylor, "Remarks on a conjecture of Fontaine and Mazur", J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 1 (2002), 125–143
prerequisites.why: Potential modularity for GL_2 over totally real fields by the Moret-Bailly method. It is the residual modularity input of §9: the elliptic curve produced over the auxiliary totally real field is potentially modular by this theorem, and its induction to GSp_4 gives the residually modular representations to which Theorem 8.4.1 applies.

prerequisites.citation: Haruzo Hida, "p-adic automorphic forms on Shimura varieties", Springer Monographs in Mathematics (2004)
prerequisites.why: Classical Hida theory for GSp_4 and more general groups: the ordinary projector, the control theorems and the projective module over the full 2[F:Q]-dimensional weight space. It is the I = ∅ end of the family of theories constructed in §4, and the point of comparison for what higher Hida theory adds.

prerequisites.citation: George Kempf, "The Grothendieck–Cousin complex of an induced representation", Adv. Math. 29 (1978), 310–396
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.9.6 and Remark 3.9.7: for a filtration by closed subschemes of the right codimension with affine successive differences, the Cousin complex of a maximal Cohen–Macaulay sheaf resolves it by acyclic sheaves. This is the mechanism by which the Hecke operators are made to act on the coherent cohomology of the compactification in Proposition 3.9.15, and it is used again for the complex K^• of Proposition 4.2.33.

prerequisites.citation: Stéphane Bijakowski, Vincent Pilloni and Benoît Stroh, "Classicité de formes modulaires surconvergentes", Ann. of Math. (2) 183 (2016), 975–1014, and Vincent Pilloni, "Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel", Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), 167–222
prerequisites.why: The classicality of small slope overconvergent forms by analytic continuation and the dynamics of the Hecke correspondences on the degrees of the level subgroups, with Fargues' degree function. Theorem 6.5.8 is the higher-degree generalisation for GSp_4 over a totally real field, and Remark 6.5.10 records that the I = ∅ case in degree 0 is their theorem.

prerequisites.citation: George Boxer, "Torsion in the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties and Galois representations", arXiv:1507.05922, and Wushi Goldring and Jean-Stefan Koskivirta, "Strata Hasse invariants, Hecke algebras and Galois representations", Invent. math. 217 (2019), 887–984
prerequisites.why: The generalised Hasse invariants attached to the Ekedahl–Oort stratification, of which the secondary Hasse invariant Ha'(𝓖_v) of §4.1 is a special case, and the fact that the Ekedahl–Oort strata of the minimal compactification are affine, which is what Lemma 8.2.10 uses to show that every irreducible component of a p-rank stratum meets the supersingular locus.

prerequisites.citation: Robert Coleman, "p-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms", Invent. math. 127 (1997), 417–479, and Éric Urban, "Eigenvarieties for reductive groups", Ann. of Math. (2) 174 (2011), 1685–1784
prerequisites.why: Fredholm theory for compact operators on Banach modules, slope decompositions, and their extension to perfect complexes, which is what Lemma 6.3.14, Theorem 6.3.16 and the finite slope arguments of §6.5 rest on. Theorem 6.3.16 in particular is Coleman's local constancy of the Euler characteristic in the weight.

prerequisites.citation: Alain Genestier and Jacques Tilouine, "Systèmes de Taylor–Wiles pour GSp(4)", Astérisque 302 (2005), 177–290, and "Geometry of the Siegel modular threefold with paramodular level structure", Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 139 (2011), 3181–3190
prerequisites.why: The earlier Taylor–Wiles systems for GSp_4 in regular weight, the local models at Klingen, Siegel, Iwahori and paramodular level used in Proposition 3.4.1, the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification which gives the density of the rank one locus, and the computation of the Klingen-level U-eigenvectors reproved as Proposition 2.4.17.

prerequisites.citation: Chung Pang Mok, "Galois representations attached to automorphic forms on GL_2 over CM fields", Compos. Math. 150 (2014), 523–567
prerequisites.why: The archimedean L-parameters of §2.6 and the construction of the Galois representations of Theorems 2.7.1 and 2.7.3, whose §§5.1–5.3 the paper says go over unchanged to the case of general totally real fields. Together with Taylor, Laumon, Weissauer and Sorensen it is the source of the GSp_4 Galois representations in regular weight.

prerequisites.citation: Nicholas Shepherd-Barron and Richard Taylor, "mod 2 and mod 5 icosahedral representations", J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997), 283–298, and Igor Dolgachev and David Lehavi, "On isogenous principally polarized abelian surfaces", Contemp. Math. 465 (2008), 51–69
prerequisites.why: The twisting argument which shows that a twist of a rational moduli space of abelian varieties with prescribed torsion is itself rational, and the odd theta map Th^- realising the degree six cover of the Burkhardt quartic as a rational variety equivariantly for PSp_4(F_3). Theorem 10.2.1 is their argument applied not to A_2(3) itself but to that cover.

prerequisites.citation: Armand Brumer and Kenneth Kramer, "Paramodular abelian varieties of odd conductor", Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 366 (2014), 2463–2516
prerequisites.why: The paramodular conjecture, its prescription of the optimal level for an abelian surface, and the computation that the smallest prime conductor of an abelian surface is 277. §10.4 reproduces it as Conjecture 10.4.3 in the modified form which includes fake abelian surfaces, and explains why the original statement needs that modification.

prerequisites.citation: Christian Johansson, "On the Sato–Tate conjecture for non-generic abelian surfaces", Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 369 (2017), 6303–6325, with an appendix by Francesc Fité
prerequisites.why: The classification of abelian surfaces over a number field by their endomorphism algebras into the types A, B[C_i], C, D, E and F, and the reduction of all but two of them to lower rank functoriality. Proposition 9.2.1 takes this classification over wholesale, and what is left is the notion of a challenging abelian surface.

prerequisites.citation: Chandrashekhar Khare and Jack Thorne, "Potential automorphy and the Leopoldt conjecture", Amer. J. Math. 139 (2017), 1205–1273, and Mark Kisin, "Moduli of finite flat group schemes, and modularity", Ann. of Math. (2) 170 (2009), 1085–1180
prerequisites.why: The bookkeeping of the Taylor–Wiles patching argument in the modern framed form: the presentation of the global deformation ring over the local ones which Proposition 7.2.1 follows from Kisin §3.2, and the descent from level Q to level 1 which Proposition 7.9.8 follows from Khare–Thorne Lemma 6.25.

prerequisites.citation: Richard Taylor and Teruyoshi Yoshida, "Compatibility of local and global Langlands correspondences", J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007), 467–493, and Rutger Noot, "The system of representations of the Weil–Deligne group associated to an abelian variety", Algebra Number Theory 7 (2013), 243–281
prerequisites.why: Purity of Weil–Deligne representations with the monodromy filtration and the uniqueness of the monodromy operator (Lemma 2.5.1), and the strict compatibility of the system attached to an abelian variety including at the places of bad reduction (Proposition 2.8.1). Purity is a hypothesis in Theorem 8.4.1 and is what makes the local deformation rings smooth at the relevant points.

routes.title: Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field
routes.brief:
Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field (HilbertSiegelModularVarieties). First prerequisite: Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves). Where the parent stops: for Res_{F/Q}GL_2 over a totally real field F it builds the two groups (H0), Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli and integral models (H1–H2), the unit action and arithmetic quotient (H3), p-level structures, Iwahori level included (H4), and the F = Q tests (H5). R18 is its quaternionic strand, and its compactifications are ShimuraCompactifications C6. It plans nothing for GSp_4 and no coherent cohomology. This Part II starts there and builds the GSp_4 analogues of H0–H5: the Hilbert–Siegel varieties of G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 and of its subgroup G with similitude in G_m, integrally at parahoric level at p and compactified, with level maps, automorphic bundles and mod p strata. The notation is reversed: the parent's G* ⊂ Res_{F/Q}GL_2 corresponds to G ⊂ G_1 here.

Source: Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni, "Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular", Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501, arXiv:1812.09269v3. Sections used: §2.1.1 (the matrix J), §§3.1–3.8.1, §3.9.10 with the proofs that follow it, Proposition 7.8.10 and §8.2 (arXiv pp. 15–16, 41–58, 65–67, 214–215, 244–246; published pp. 169, 201–221, 229–232, 412–413, 448–450).

Method. Specialize, as the parent's R18 does: prove only what the O_F-structure, the product over the places v | p and the passage from G to G_1 add.

Setting.
- V = O_F^4 with the form ⟨,⟩_1 of matrix J = (0 s; −s 0), where s = (0 1; 1 0). So ⟨e_1,e_4⟩_1 = ⟨e_2,e_3⟩_1 = 1, and e_i, e_j pair to 0 for the other i < j. Put ⟨,⟩ = Tr_{F/Q}∘⟨,⟩_1.
- ν : G_1 → Res_{F/Q}G_m is the similitude, and G = G_1 ×_{ν,Res_{F/Q}G_m} G_m.
- From §3.3 on, p is totally split in F, so F_v = Q_p for every v | p.
- The lattice chain at v | p: V_0 = V ⊗ O_{F_v} and V_j = ⟨p^{-1}e_1, …, p^{-1}e_j, e_{j+1}, …, e_4⟩. GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Si(v), Kli(v) and Iw(v) are the stabilizers of V_0, of V_1 → V_3, of V_0 → V_2, of V_0 → V_1 → V_3 → V_0 and of V_0 → V_1 → V_2 → V_3 → V_0 (§3.3.1). They are taken from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3.
- Fix one lattice convention, shared with ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 and with the Siegel-threefold moduli imported from ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII. That roadmap may use lattices conjugate to these by the element e_1 ↦ e_4, e_4 ↦ −e_1 (fixing e_2 and e_3) of Sp_4(Z), which carries pV_3 = ⟨e_1,e_2,e_3,pe_4⟩ to ⟨pe_1,e_2,e_3,e_4⟩. The F = Q acceptance test depends on this choice.
- A level K = K^pK_p ⊂ G_1(A^∞) is reasonable if two conditions hold:
  - K^p ⊂ G_1(A^{∞,p}) is neat, in the sense of ShimuraData D5. Definition 3.3.3 prints G(A^{∞,p}); this is a recorded misprint.
  - K_p = ∏_{v|p}K_v with each K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v), Si(v), Kli(v), Iw(v)}.

Final theorems as printed, with the recorded corrections.

(1) Shimura data and complex uniformization.
- Plan the data: (G, X) of Hodge type through (O_F, V, ⟨,⟩) (PELModuli M0, ShimuraData D4–D5), and (G_1, X_1) of abelian type (ShimuraVarieties V6), both with reflex field Q.
- K ⊂ G_1(A^∞) is neat. H is the Siegel upper half-space of degree 2, and G_1(R)/Z(R)^0K_∞^0 = (H ∪ −H)^{Hom(F,R)}. Here Z(R)^0 is the identity component of the centre of G_1(R), and K_∞^0 that of a maximal compact subgroup.
- S^{G_1}_K(C) = G_1(Q)\(G_1(R) × G_1(A^∞))/Z(R)^0K_∞^0K and S^G_K(C) = G(Q)\(G(R) × G_1(A^∞))/R_{>0}K_∞^0K.
- G_1(Q)^+ = ν^{-1}(F^{×,+}) and G(Q)^+ = G(Q) ∩ G_1(Q)^+. Write Γ_1(c,K) = G_1(Q)^+ ∩ cKc^{-1} and Γ(c,K) = G(Q)^+ ∩ cKc^{-1}.
- S^{G_1}_K(C) = ⊔_c Γ_1(c,K)\H^{Hom(F,R)}, with c running over the strict class group F^{×,+}\(A^∞⊗F)^×/ν(K).
- S^G_K(C) = ⊔_c Γ(c,K)\H^{Hom(F,R)}, with c running over Q^{×,+}\(A^∞⊗F)^×/ν(K). This index set is infinite if and only if F ≠ Q. For F = Q it is the finite strict class group; the paper calls it infinite, a recorded error that affects nothing. S^G_K(C) is not the PEL Shimura variety of G.
- O_F^×(K) is the centre of Γ_1(c,K), a subgroup of finite index in O_F^×. Put Δ(K) = Γ_1(c,K)/⟨O_F^×(K), Γ(c,K)⟩ ≅ (O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K))/ν(O_F^×(K)).
- Lemma 3.2.2: "ν(Γ_1(c,K)) = O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K)".
- Lemma 3.2.3: "The map Γ(c,K)\H^{Hom(F,R)} → Γ_1(c,K)\H^{Hom(F,R)} is finite étale with group Δ(K)".

(2) Proposition 3.3.9. Let K be reasonable. Over Noetherian Z_(p)-algebras, 𝐘_K classifies tuples (A, ι, λ, η, η_p):
- ι : O_F → End(A) ⊗ Z_(p), with Lie A locally free of rank 2 over O_F ⊗ R.
- λ is O_F-linear and a Z_(p)^{×,+}-multiple of a polarization. Its kernel on A[v^∞] is trivial if K_v ≠ Par(v), and of order p^2 if K_v = Par(v). The paper prints "Z_(p)^×-polarization", which is wrong at paramodular places.
- η is a K^p-orbit of pairs (η_1, η_2), with k acting by (η_1k, ν(k)η_2).
- η_p consists of H_v ⊂ A[v] of order p at Kli(v), a totally isotropic L_v of order p^2 at Si(v), and a flag H_v ⊂ L_v at Iw(v).
- Morphisms are O_F-linear prime-to-p quasi-isogenies f with λ = r·f^*λ′, r ∈ Z_(p)^{×,+}. The paper prints f^*λ = rλ′.

The statement: "The groupoid 𝐘_K is representable by a quasi-projective scheme Π_0 : Y_K → Z_(p)^{×,+}\(A^{∞,p}⊗F)^×/ν(K^p)(1). The morphism Π_0 has geometrically connected fibres". Moreover (Y_{K,c})^an ≅ Γ(c,K)\H^{Hom(F,R)}.

Proof route: Y_K is a disjoint union, over G(A^{∞,p})\G_1(A^{∞,p})/K^p, of Kottwitz PEL spaces for G. The paper cites only Kottwitz, which covers hyperspecial level (import PELModuli M2 with ShimuraCompactifications C5). The other levels need more:
- at Kli, Si and Iw places, relative Hilbert schemes of finite flat subgroups;
- at Par places, the lattice-chain construction or Zarhin's trick;
- at non-hyperspecial levels, geometric connectedness of the characteristic-p fibres, which is not in Kottwitz. Prove it, for example by Zariski connectedness from the normal, flat, proper X_{K,Σ} (Theorem 3.5.1(4)) over each component of the finite étale base, together with an argument that the boundary divisor does not disconnect the special fibre; or cite a source. Record a gap if neither is found.

(3) Unit action. An element x ∈ (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)} (totally positive, prime to p) sends λ ↦ xλ and η_2 ↦ xη_2. The subgroup Z_(p)^{×,+} acts trivially.
- Lemma 3.3.12: O_F^{×,+}(K^p) := {x^2 : x ∈ O_F^× ∩ K^p} acts trivially, through a canonical natural transformation.
- Lemma 3.3.13, corrected: the stabilizer of a geometric point is Z_(p)^{×,+}·O_F^{×,+}(K^p); the paper prints O_F^{×,+}(K^p). So (3.3.14) should read Δ = (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}/(Z_(p)^{×,+}·O_F^{×,+}(K^p)).
- The last case of the proof of Lemma 3.3.13 (A isogenous to A_1^2) assumes End^0(A_1) is commutative. This fails at supersingular points (a recorded gap). Use the ℓ-adic eigenvalue argument with neatness instead.
- Two finite groups: Δ(Π_0) = (O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K^p)∏_{ℓ≠p}Z_ℓ^×)/O_F^{×,+}(K^p), the stabilizer of a component, and Δ(K^p) = (O_F^{×,+} ∩ ν(K^p))/O_F^{×,+}(K^p).
- Proposition 3.3.17:
  - Y_K^{G_1} := Δ\Y_K is the coarse moduli space of [Y_K/((O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}/Z_(p)^{×,+})];
  - Π_0 : Y_K^{G_1} → (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}\(A^{∞,p}⊗F)^×/ν(K^p)(1) is quasi-projective with geometrically connected fibres;
  - Y_K → Y_K^{G_1} is étale and surjective;
  - over C, Γ(c,K)\H → Γ_1(c,K)\H is finite étale with group Δ(K^p) = Δ(K).
- Recorded misprints in (1)–(3) and their proofs, which must not be copied:
  - proof of Lemma 3.2.2: take h close to γg^{-1} and use hg (the printed version, with h close to gγ^{-1} and hγ, does not work);
  - condition (2) of 𝐘_K: End(A) (printed End(G));
  - proof of Proposition 3.3.9: η̃_2 : A^{∞,p} ≃ H_1(G_m, A^{∞,p}) (printed with an extra factor A^{∞,p} ⊗);
  - proof of Lemma 3.3.12: x ∈ O_F^× ∩ K^p (printed O_F^{×,+} ∩ K^p).

(4) Local geometry.
- Proposition 3.4.1: "The scheme Y_K is flat over Spec Z_(p), normal, and a local complete intersection (so in particular Cohen–Macaulay) of pure relative dimension 3[F:Q]. If K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for all v|p, then it is smooth, while in general it is smooth away from codimension 2."
- Corollary 3.4.2: Y_K^{G_1} is normal, flat and lci.
- Y_K is étale locally isomorphic to ∏_{v|p}M^loc_{K_v}. §3.4 prints Y^G_K for Y_K here (a recorded misprint).

Kottwitz–Rapoport strata. Since F_v = Q_p, each M^loc_{K_v} is a genus-two local model.
- Imported at each place: the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification of M^loc_{K_v} and its closure relations, and the Iwahori-level special-fibre strata of the Siegel threefold with Yu's table (see Imports). At Iwahori level the strata are indexed by Adm(μ), with #Adm(μ) = 13. The invariant at a place w | p decides whether H_w and L_w/H_w are étale, multiplicative or connected–connected, and so decides the p-rank of 𝒢_w (Genestier–Ngô). Conversely, these data determine the invariant when that p-rank is non-zero (Yu). The stratum s_2s_1s_2τ (𝒢_w ordinary, L_w = 𝒢_w[F]) and the stratum s_1s_2τ (p-rank 1, H_w multiplicative, L_w = 𝒢_w[F]) both contain the canonical p-rank-0 strata τ, s_1τ and s_2τ in their closures.
- Planned here, at every reasonable level: the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification of the special fibre of Y_K, as the product over v | p of the strata of M^loc_{K_v}, through the étale-local comparison. At Klingen, Siegel-parahoric and paramodular places, the strata of M^loc_{K_v} are the images of the Iwahori strata; plan this, with their p-rank description at Klingen and paramodular level (for paramodular level, see also Yu, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 139 (2011)). HigherHidaAndColemanTheory imports these strata for its density statement, which stays there.
- Planned here: the closure argument at level ∏_{v|p}Iw(v), where the strata are labelled by u ∈ Adm(μ)^{S_p}. Let C be an irreducible component of the stratum u. Then C̄ = ⊔_{u′≤u}C̄_{u′}, where C̄_{u′} = C̄ ∩ (stratum u′), and if C̄_{u′} ≠ ∅ then C̄_{u″} ≠ ∅ for every u′ ≤ u″ ≤ u.
- Planned here: the m-can loci. For J ⊆ S_p, the m-can locus at level ∏Iw(v) is where, for w ∉ J, 𝒢_w is ordinary and L_w = 𝒢_w[F], and, for w ∈ J, 𝒢_w has p-rank 1, H_w is multiplicative and L_w = 𝒢_w[F]. It is a stratum, and it maps finitely onto the corresponding p-rank locus at hyperspecial level.
- Planned here: the identification at K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∉I}Iw(v). Let Y^I_1 be the locus of geometric points of the special fibre at level K^pK_p(I) where H_w is multiplicative for w ∈ I and where, for w ∉ I, 𝒢_w is ordinary and H_w ⊂ L_w = 𝒢_w[F] (the canonical Iwahori structure). This is the paper's Y^I (§4.3.4); HigherHidaAndColemanTheory identifies its own open subscheme with this locus. For J ⊆ I, adjoining L_w = 𝒢_w[F] for w ∈ I identifies the locus of Y^I_1 where 𝒢_w has p-rank 1 for w ∈ J and p-rank 2 for w ∉ J with the m-can locus for J. The proof of Lemma 8.2.8, where this is done, drops the superscript I (a recorded misprint).

(5) Compactifications.
- Choose V′ with V′ ⊗ O_{F_v} = V_3 at Par(v) and V ⊗ O_{F_v} elsewhere, and K^p stabilizing V′ ⊗ Ẑ^p. The paper prints V′ ⊗ A^{∞,p}.
- Σ is K-admissible, projective, and smooth for the lattices L_{W,K,γ}.

Theorem 3.5.1:
1. X_{K,Σ} exists, stratified by G(Q)^+\Σ/K, and its boundary is a relative Cartier divisor.
2. The universal abelian scheme A extends to a semi-abelian scheme.
3. For a refinement Σ′, the map π : X_{K,Σ′} → X_{K,Σ} is projective with (Rπ)_*O = O and (Rπ)_*I_{X_{K,Σ′}} = I_{X_{K,Σ}}. The printed identity π^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} = I_{X_{K,Σ′}} is false for Σ′ ≠ Σ and must not be proved.
4. For K reasonable, X_{K,Σ} is flat, normal and Cohen–Macaulay. It is lci if Σ is smooth, and smooth if moreover every K_v is hyperspecial.

Proof route. Build it here for the integral PEL datum (O_F, V′, ⟨,⟩) at all five levels (Lan, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2017, Thm. 6.1, with the construction by normalization of Lan, Forum Math. Sigma 4 (2016), §2):
- If K_p = G_1(Z_p), use Lan's 2013 book (ShimuraCompactifications C5).
- If every K_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)}, take a closed subscheme of a toroidal compactification of a Siegel moduli space with prime-to-p polarization, by Zarhin's trick (PELModuli M5).
- In general, take the normalization of the closure of Y_K in the product of the compactifications at the levels K′_v ∈ {GSp_4(O_{F_v}), Par(v)} reached by the degeneracy maps, with a blow-up or blow-down at the boundary where needed.
- Part (4) follows from Proposition 3.4.1 and Lan's description of the formal completions along boundary strata (Thm. 6.1(4)). The printed proof cites Proposition 3.5.4 instead, which is itself deduced from the theorem (a recorded misprint).
- The rank-one boundary strata are built from Hilbert–Blumenthal abelian schemes, which in some Klingen cases carry Iwahori (Γ_0-type) level at places above p. Import these from the parent (H1–H2, H4, with ShimuraCompactifications C6).
- For F = Q, the Klingen and paramodular cases must be the imported ones.

Lemmas 3.5.2–3.5.3: the unit action extends to X_{K,Σ}, factors through Δ and is free. The printed proof of Lemma 3.5.2 reduces to C by normality, which is not enough (a recorded gap). Prove it over Z_(p), using an invariant ample bundle on the projective components or working on the boundary charts. The sentence before Lemma 3.5.2 cites (3.3.15) for Δ; read (3.3.14) (a recorded misprint).

Proposition 3.5.4: X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} = Δ\X_{K,Σ} is stratified by G_1(Q)^+\Σ/K, and X_{K,Σ} → X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} is étale and surjective. For K reasonable, X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} is a normal, flat local complete intersection over Z_(p).

Minimal compactifications. At hyperspecial level, X^*_K is C5's minimal compactification for (O_F, V, ⟨,⟩), with f : X_{K,Σ} → X^*_K. Δ acts on it, and X^{G_1,*}_K = Δ\X^*_K. Plan here the boundary strata of both: points and Hilbert–Blumenthal varieties on X^*_K, and points and Hilbert modular varieties for Res_{F/Q}GL_2 on X^{G_1,*}_K (ShimuraCompactifications C6, with the parent's H3). IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (Lemma 3.10.7) and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (§6.2) use them.

Proposition 7.8.10, for any finite set S of places v ∤ p (the paper takes S = Q ∪ R).
- Setting. K_p is reasonable. K_0^p(S) ⊃ K_1^p(S) are tame levels with Iw(v) (resp. Iw_1(v)) at v ∈ S and equal elsewhere, and K_0^p(S) is neat; the paper secures neatness with Iw_1(v_0) at an auxiliary place, by the criterion of Lemma 7.8.3. One good cone decomposition Σ is used at both levels. Over the interior at level K_pK_0^p(S), the Iw(v)-structure is a flag 0 ⊂ H_v ⊂ L_v ⊂ H_v^⊥ ⊂ A[v] whose graded pieces are étale of rank 1 over k(v). Iw(v) and Iw_1(v) come from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3, and T is the diagonal maximal torus of GSp_4.
1. These graded pieces extend to finite étale k(v)-group schemes of rank 1 over X_{K_pK_0^p(S),Σ}.
2. X_{K_pK_1^p(S),Σ} → X_{K_pK_0^p(S),Σ} is finite étale with group ∏_{v∈S}T(k(v)). It is the torsor of trivializations of these graded pieces compatible with duality. The printed proof says "for all v|p" where it means v ∈ S (a recorded misprint).

(6) Level maps (§3.6).
- Away from p: the forgetful finite étale maps, and [g] : Y_K → Y_{g^{-1}Kg} for g ∈ G_1(A^{∞,p}).
- Fix w | p and x_w ∈ F^{×,+}, a uniformizer at w and a unit at the other v | p.

Klingen type (levels GSp_4 ← Kli → Par at w):
- Lemma 3.6.4: p_1 forgets H_w and is "proper surjective, generically finite étale".
- Lemma 3.6.5: p_2 sends A ↦ A/H_w^⊥, with λ′ descended from x_w^2λ. It is "proper, surjective, generically finite étale" and depends on x_w; the induced map on G_1-models is canonical.

Siegel type (levels GSp_4 ← Si, resp. Kli ← Iw, at w):
- Lemma 3.6.9: p_1 forgets L_w and is "surjective and generically finite".
- Lemma 3.6.10: p_2 sends A ↦ A/L_w, with λ′ descended from x_wλ, and H′_w = H_w^⊥/L_w at Kli(w). It depends on x_w, and the induced map on G_1-models is canonical.

Extend all these maps to compactifications for suitable Σ. Import ShimuraCompactifications C3, and, for F = Q, the Siegel-threefold p_1, p_2 of Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary), with the interior maps from ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII.

(7) Bundles (§3.7, over Z_p).
- ω_𝒢 = ∏_{v|p}ω_{𝒢,v}, each factor of rank 2.
- For κ = (k_v,l_v) with k_v ≥ l_v (classical if l_v ≥ 2), ω^κ = ⊗_v Sym^{k_v−l_v}ω_{𝒢,v} ⊗ det^{l_v}ω_{𝒢,v}. The paper writes ∏_v for this tensor product.
- A weight for G_1 adds an even integer w_0 ≡ k_v − l_v mod 2 (the paper calls it w; later w_0 = 2).
- x acts on ω^κ_{(A,x^{-1}λ)} = ω^κ_{(A,λ)} by ∏_v v(x)^{(k_v+l_v−w_0)/2}. This is compatible with O_F^{×,+}(K^p) because N_{F/Q}(ε)^{w_0} = 1, and it gives an effective descent datum along Y_K → Y_K^{G_1}.
- As printed, the scalar is r^{Σ_v(k_v+l_v−w_0)/2} ≠ 1 for r ∈ Z_(p)^{×,+}, although r acts through id_A. This is a misprint that affects nothing, the same omission of Z_(p)^{×,+} as in Lemma 3.3.13 and (3.3.14), and it is recorded with them (§3.7.2, arXiv pp. 55–56, published p. 218). Define the datum on unit representatives through Δ(Π_0) instead.
- Also plan Remark 3.7.3 (over F_p with k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 0 mod p−1, the tautological datum) and the canonical extensions e^*Ω^1.

(8) §3.8.1.
- Lemma 3.8.2: RΓ of ω^κ and of ω^κ(−D) on X_{K,Σ} and on X^{G_1}_{K,Σ} "are independent of Σ". This follows from (Rπ)_*O = O and (Rπ)_*I_{X_{K,Σ′}} = I_{X_{K,Σ}} (the corrected Theorem 3.5.1(3)), from π^*ω^κ ≅ ω^κ (AutomorphicBundles B3, compatibility with refinements) and the projection formula, and, on X^{G_1}, from the Δ-equivariance of π.
- Proposition 3.8.3 prints that the pull-backs RΓ(X^{G_1}_K, ω^κ) → RΓ(X_K, ω^κ) and RΓ(X^{G_1}_K, ω^κ(−D)) → RΓ(X_K, ω^κ(−D)) "split in the derived category of Z_p-modules". This is false in general (a recorded error; counterexample F = Q(√7), p = 3, Δ(K^p) ≅ Z/36).
- Prove Proposition 3.8.3 when p ∤ #Δ(K^p). The rest of Δ(Π_0) only moves the base, where the trace is surjective. Consumers inherit the hypothesis.
- Lemma 3.8.5 states f_*O_T = O_S ⊕ I_G ⊗_{Z[G]} f_*O_T for a finite étale G-Galois cover. It needs #G invertible on S.

(9) Ekedahl–Oort strata at hyperspecial level.

From §8.2:
- There are 4^{[F:Q]} strata, given by the type of each 𝒢_w[p]: ordinary μ_p^2 × (Z/pZ)^2; p-rank 1 μ_p × Z/pZ × G_{1,1}; supergeneral; or superspecial G_{1,1}^2. Here G_{1,1} = E[p] for a supersingular elliptic curve E.
- The stratification refines the p-rank stratification, and the superspecial locus is the unique zero-dimensional stratum.
- It extends to the minimal compactification X^*_K of (5) with affine open strata, and the superspecial locus misses the boundary. Hence every component of every stratum has a superspecial point in its closure.

From §3.9.10 (Boxer, Theorem 6.2.3): let X_n^* = X^*_K ⊗ Z/p^n, X_n = X_{K,Σ} ⊗ Z/p^n, and Z_i^* ⊂ X_n^* the closure of the codimension-i strata.
- Z^* is a filtration. Z_i^* \ Z_{i+1}^* is affine, and is a set-theoretic local complete intersection in X_n^* \ Z_{i+1}^*.
- For the pull-back Z = f^{-1}Z^* to X_n: Z is a filtration; the inclusion Z_i \ Z_{i+1} → X_n is an affine morphism, being the base change of Z_i^* \ Z_{i+1}^* → X_n^*, although Z_i \ Z_{i+1} itself need not be affine (strata meeting the boundary contain positive-dimensional proper fibres of f); and Z_i \ Z_{i+1} is a set-theoretic local complete intersection in X_n \ Z_{i+1}.
- Each stratum in Z_i \ Z_{i+1} is set-theoretically the intersection, in X_n \ Z_{i+1}, of i Cartier divisors given by powers of generalized Hasse invariants that lift to X_n^*. These are the generalized (G-zip) Hasse sections of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2, specialized here. At a single place w, the sections cutting out the codimension-1 and codimension-2 conditions on 𝒢_w have the same vanishing loci (p-rank ≤ 1 and p-rank 0 at w) as the Hasse invariants Ha(𝒢_w) and Ha′(𝒢_w) used by HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. That roadmap imports Ha and Ha′ from their owners and proves that their loci are the p-rank loci planned here; neither roadmap builds a second copy of these sections.
- The strata are stable under prime-to-p isogenies and under (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}.
- Also prove codim_{X_n} Z_i ≥ i, which the paper uses without stating it.

Imports:
- Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves) H0–H5: H1–H2 and H4 for the Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli and their Iwahori-level integral models that appear as abelian parts of the rank-one boundary strata (with ShimuraCompactifications C6), and H0, H3 and H5 for the groups, the unit action and the F = Q comparisons.
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M0–M3, M5.
- Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D0, D4, D5.
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties) V0, V6, V8.
- Adelic algebraic groups and arithmetic quotients (AdelicAlgebraicGroups) AA.4.
- Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A1–A4.
- Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1, R07.2.
- Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) R09.2, R09.5.
- Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.0a, RG2.3, including Iw_1(v) at v ∤ p.
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII): genus-two lattice-chain moduli, local models and the Siegel-threefold maps p_1, p_2; and the Iwahori-level special-fibre strata of the Siegel threefold, with the étale, multiplicative or connected–connected types of H and L/H and Yu's table matching them with the Kottwitz–Rapoport strata (C.-F. Yu, Adv. Math. 218 (2008), p. 1276). Pilloni's joined brief already asks that roadmap to recover these strata (Pilloni, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), pp. 186–189). Yu's table must live there too, since that roadmap is upstream of this one.
- Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models and residue-field curves (GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII; the joined briefs use several subtitles): the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification of local models and its closure relations.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C0–C6, including C5's minimal compactification at hyperspecial level.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary): Lan's integral toroidal compactifications of the Siegel threefold at Klingen and paramodular level, their boundary charts, the compactified Siegel-type correspondence and the extensions of p_1, p_2. It plans nothing for the O_F-linear datum and nothing at Iwahori level, so the compactifications of Theorem 3.5.1 are built here.
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms (AutomorphicBundles) B2–B3.
- Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration) IG.2: Ekedahl–Oort/G-zip strata and their Hasse sections. The affineness of all strata of X_n^* is planned here, using those sections.

Mathlib and Tau Ceti have none of this.

Owned elsewhere. These roadmaps import this one:
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes): cohomological correspondences, the prime-to-p Hecke action through the Ekedahl–Oort Cousin complex, and Theorem 3.10.1 with Lemma 3.10.7.
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory): the operators at p; the Hasse-invariant and p-rank strata as subschemes, with Ha(𝒢_w) and Ha′(𝒢_w) imported there from their owners, and the density statements; and the formal models.
- Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular (AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity): the Taylor–Wiles levels, Lemmas 8.2.7, 8.2.8, 8.2.10 and 8.2.11 with Corollary 8.2.9, and the twisted moduli, which are the GSp_4 analogue of the parent's H6.

Upstream owners:
- Coherent duality: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension.
- Cousin complexes: Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.2.
- The neatness criterion of Lemma 7.8.3: ShimuraData D5.

Every statement must say which side it lives on:
- the G side carries the moduli, and its maps depend on x_w;
- the G_1 side carries the automorphic forms, and its maps are canonical.
Here, p-rank loci are sets of geometric points.

Acceptance tests:
- For F = Q (G = G_1, Δ = 1, x_w = p), with the lattice convention fixed in the setting, every object and map that ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII or ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary also builds is the imported Siegel-threefold one.
- The element e_1 ↦ e_4, e_4 ↦ −e_1 (fixing e_2, e_3) preserves J.
- For a real quadratic F, compute Δ(K), Δ(Π_0) and Δ(K^p), including F = Q(√7).
- In the blow-up of a smooth two-dimensional cone, with boundary ideals I below and I′ above, check that π^*I ≠ I′ but (Rπ)_*I′ = I.
- List Adm(μ) and check the closure claims of (4).
routes.reason:
§3 of the paper builds for G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 what Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves) builds in H0–H5 for Res_{F/Q}GL_2. So do §3.9.10, Proposition 7.8.10 and the stratification paragraphs of §8.2. Together they give:
- the Shimura data of G_1 and of a subgroup G with rational similitude, with a PEL moduli problem for G;
- integral models at parahoric level at p;
- the action of the totally positive elements prime to p;
- the arithmetic quotient for G_1;
- toroidal and minimal compactifications and level maps;
- descended automorphic bundles and mod p strata.
These are new layers in the parent's direction, so they form a Part II.

Nothing in the atlas or in the other proposals builds the Hilbert–Siegel case:
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) and ShimuraCompactifications C5 stop at good level.
- Two proposed Part IIs work at parahoric level, but only for the Siegel threefold over Q. Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII) supplies the genus-two lattice-chain moduli, their local models, the maps between levels and the Iwahori-level special-fibre strata. Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary) supplies Lan's compactifications at Klingen and paramodular level and the compactified Siegel-type correspondence.
- Neither builds the O_F-linear problem, its compactifications at all five parahoric levels, the passage to G_1 or the descent.

This roadmap imports those inputs, together with the Kottwitz–Rapoport stratification of local models from Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models and residue-field curves (GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII), and the Ekedahl–Oort/G-zip strata with their Hasse sections from Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration) IG.2. It proves the specialization, and it builds the compactifications of the O_F-linear datum, which nothing else plans.

It holds 19 items: the groups and complex uniformization, the moduli problem, the unit action and G_1-models, local geometry and Kottwitz–Rapoport strata, the compactifications with the covers of Proposition 7.8.10, the level maps, the bundles, Lemma 3.8.2 and Proposition 3.8.3, and the Ekedahl–Oort strata and filtration.

Three other roadmaps own the neighbouring material, and all three import this one:
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes) owns coherent cohomology with its Hecke action.
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory) owns the operators at p and the Hasse-invariant geometry.
- Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular (AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity) owns the Taylor–Wiles levels and the component lemmas of §8.2.

The parahoric subgroups belong to Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.3, and neatness to Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D5.

routes.title: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology
routes.brief:
Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory; parent PadicFamilies; area padic).

This route joins the proposal of this roadmap made from V. Pilloni, "Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights", Duke Math. J. 169 (2020). The extractions of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2025) and of Boxer–Pilloni, "Higher Hida theory for Siegel modular forms" (Invent. Math. 2026), also join it. All four share id, parent, title and area, and the design job merges their briefs into one roadmap. It is the higher Coleman roadmap that the maintainer's guide for this paper asks for.

Source: G. Boxer, F. Calegari, T. Gee and V. Pilloni, "Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular", Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501, arXiv:1812.09269v3. Statement numbers agree in both versions. "p. N" is a page of arXiv v3, and E-numbers are this paper's sourceIssues. Read the misprints recorded there as corrected. The other corrections below are stated in corrected form, saying what the paper prints wherever a reader checking the page would otherwise see a misquotation. They are not yet among the recorded sourceIssues; cite each by its number once it is recorded.

WHERE IT STARTS

Pilloni's brief (layers 1–9) treats the Siegel threefold over Q at K_p = GSp_4(Z_p). Boxer–Pilloni's adds genus g at Iwahori level. This paper carries Pilloni's layers to a totally real F in which p splits completely, one place above p at a time. In the paper's words, "traditional Hida theory considers the case I = ∅, while the higher Hida theory of [Pil20] is the case F = Q and I = {p}" (p. 74), and many arguments are "simply the product over the places v|p" (pp. 73, 138). The paper also adds a doubling layer (§5).

Plan each statement on its Siegel counterpart. Prove each computation that is local at v (O_{F_v} = Z_p) only once. Prove that F = Q, I = {p} recovers Pilloni's objects, in the precise sense of the first acceptance test. Layer numbers below are Pilloni's.

SETTING

- G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4 contains G, the subgroup with similitude in G_m. Every statement says whether it concerns X or X^{G_1}. Operators depend on x_w on X and are canonical on X^{G_1}.
- p ≠ 2 from §4.4 on. S_p = I ⊔ I^c.
- A weight is κ = (k_v,l_v)_v with k_v ≥ l_v and k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2).
- K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∈I^c}Iw(v).
- T_I = ∏_{v∈I}Z_p^×∏_{v∈I^c}(Z_p^×)^2 = T_I^f × T_I^0, with T_I^0 pro-p, and Λ_I = Z_p[[T_I^0]]. A classical κ with l_v = 2 on I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1) gives f_κ: Λ_I → Z_p.
- T^I = ∏_{w∈I}T_w∏_{w∈I^c}T_{w,1} and U^I = ∏_{v∈I}U_{v,2}∏_{v∈I^c}U_{v,1}U_{v,2}. e(·) is the ordinary projector (PadicFamilies L0a).
- X_1^{G_1,I} = X_1^{G_1,≥_I1,≥_{I^c}2}. In §4.2 it is taken at K_p = G_1(Z_p), where the superscripts are p-rank conditions. In §5 it is taken at K_p(I), with w ∈ I fixed (§5.2). Theorem 4.2.1 (p. 77). Let K_p = G_1(Z_p). There is a universal constant C, depending only on p and F and not on K^p, with the following property. Suppose l_w ≥ 2 for all w, k_w − l_w ≥ C for w ∈ I, and l_w ≥ C for w ∈ I^c. Then RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^κ(−D)) carries a locally finite action of T^I, and:
(1) e(T^I)RΓ(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^κ(−D)) is perfect of amplitude [0,#I];
(2) e(T^I)H^0(X_1^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) → e(T^I)H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^κ(−D)) is an isomorphism;
(3) the same map on H^1 is injective;
(4) if furthermore l_w ≥ 3 for all w ∈ I, the map on RΓ is a quasi-isomorphism.
Parts (2)–(4) also hold for non-cuspidal cohomology.

Theorems 4.2.4, 4.2.12 and 4.2.13 (pp. 78–82) lead to Theorem 4.2.1. They are the Siegel and Klingen vanishing theorems on the strata X_1^{G_1,≤_{I_a}1,≥_{I_b}1,≥_J2}.

(2) M_I := e(U^I)M_I^{p-ad,κ_I} is a perfect complex of Λ_I-modules concentrated in [0,#I].
(3) For all classical algebraic κ with l_v = 2 for v ∈ I and k_v ≡ l_v ≡ 2 (mod p−1) for all v|p, there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism e(U^I)RΓ(𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K_p(I)K^p}, ω^κ(−D)) → M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} Z_p.
(4) There is a universal C, "depending only on p" (read "on p and F") and not on K^p, with the following property. For such κ with k_v − l_v ≥ C for all v|p and l_v ≥ C for v ∈ I^c, the map e(∏_{v|p}T_v∏_{v∈I^c}T_{v,1})H^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) → H^i(M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} Z_p) is an isomorphism for i = 0 and injective for i = 1.

Remark 5.8.7 gives the form that §7.9 uses. Let M ⊂ e(U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)) ⊗ F̄_p be finite-dimensional and stable under U_{Kli(w),1} and U_{w,2}. Suppose there are distinct α_w, β_w ∈ F̄_p^× such that U_{Kli(w),1} − (α_w+β_w) and U_{w,2} − α_wβ_w are nilpotent on M. Then M injects into the localization of the target (with coefficients in F̄_p) at U_{Iw(w),1} − ξ_w, both for ξ_w = α_w and for ξ_w = β_w. Then f ↦ (1 − β̃_wU_{Iw(w),1}^{−1})f and f ↦ (1 − α̃_wU_{Iw(w),1}^{−1})f, which are the doubling map composed with f ↦ (f, −α̃_w^{−1}f) and with f ↦ (f, −β̃_w^{−1}f), are injective maps from M into e(U_{Iw(w),1}U_{w,2})H^0(X_1^{G_1,I,=_w2}, ω^2(−D)) ⊗ F̄_p, localized at U_{Iw(w),1} − α_w and at U_{Iw(w),1} − β_w respectively.
