  - 𝒳^mult_{K_p(I)K^p}, the rigid generic fibre of 𝔛^I_{K_p(I)K^p} (p. 165): for v ∈ I, 𝒢_v has p-rank ≥ 1 and H_v is multiplicative; for v ∈ I^c, 𝒢_v is ordinary with its canonical Iwahori structure. At v ∈ I it is not an ordinary locus;
  - the identification M_I ⊗^L_{Λ_I,κ} C_p = e(U^I)RΓ(𝒳^{G_1,mult}, ω^κ(−D)) stated before Proposition 6.6.1, from Theorem 4.6.1(3). It needs a formal–rigid comparison of coherent cohomology on a non-proper formal scheme: use that of Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII) R2–R3, as in Pilloni's Lemma 14.8.1;
  - the two-affinoid Čech cover, which the paper asserts without proof. For F = Q and I = {p} it is Pilloni's Klingen two-affine covering of §14.8, already planned in this roadmap. Plan the Hilbert–Siegel cover as its generalization: descend Ha(𝒢_v) (v|p) and Ha′(𝒢_w) (w ∈ I) to the minimal compactification and lift them, as SiegelModularFormsModPn does for its spherical covering. Build it once, and do not rebuild the spherical covering. The same proof uses R^iπ_*ω^κ(−D) = 0 (i > 0) for the projection π to the minimal compactification at level K_p(I); request Lan's vanishing in that form from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes;
  - Proposition 6.6.1: for #I = 1, injective on H^0 and surjective on H^1. It is also used for I = ∅;
  - Proposition 6.6.2 (equal Euler characteristics), with Remark 6.6.3, localized as DEPENDENCIES AND GAPS says;
  - Theorems 6.6.4–6.6.5, localized likewise. The printed proof of 6.6.4 uses a map out of H^i_cusp that is never constructed. Instead, count dimensions using the restriction map of Proposition 6.6.1. For Theorem 6.6.5, add rigid GAGA (AdicSpacesPartII R3) and descent from C_p to Q_p, to pass from the analytic 𝒳^{G_1} over C_p to the algebraic X^{G_1}[1/p] over Q_p.

OPERATORS AT p AND THE PRIME-TO-p ACTION

On Hilbert–Siegel varieties this roadmap owns T_{w,1}, T_w, T′_w, T″_w, U_{w,1}, U_{w,2}, U_{Kli(w),1}, U_{Iw(w),1}, Z_w, U^I (integral and overconvergent), F_w and their projectors. This matches the merged brief's ownership of Pilloni's T and Klingen operators. For F = Q, T_{w,1} over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus is SiegelModularFormsModPn's T_{p,2}, and only the comparison is proved here (layer 2).

The correspondences and the operators on representations are imported. The prime-to-p Hecke action on the p-adic and overconvergent complexes is planned here, as the Hilbert–Siegel form of Pilloni's Proposition 15.1.1. Plan it as one construction with that proposition and with Boxer–Pilloni's spherical Hecke action on their Igusa complexes, both already planned in this roadmap.
- Build the prime-to-p correspondences on 𝔛^{G_1,I}_{K,Kli(p^∞)} and on the §6 spaces from the maps [g] of Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field (HilbertSiegelModularVarieties) and the cohomological correspondences of IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.
- Prove that the spherical operators away from S_p and the central operators U_{v,0} (v|p) act on M_I^{p-ad,κ_I}, on M_I, on e(U^I)RΓ(𝒳^{G_1,mult,†}, ω^κ(−D)) and on H^0(X_1^{G_1,I}, ω^2(−D)) at level K_p(I).
- Prove that they commute with one another and with U^I, U_{Kli(w),1} and Z_w, and that they satisfy the Hecke relations, through the Cousin complex of Lemma 4.5.15.
- Prove that they are compatible with the maps of Theorems 4.6.1(3)–(4), 6.5.8, 6.6.4 and 6.6.5 and with the restriction map of §5.8.
The paper uses this action in §§5.8 and 7.8 without constructing it. IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes supplies it only on classical coherent cohomology (integrally at hyperspecial level, Proposition 3.9.15, and in characteristic 0).

IMPORTS FROM PROPOSALS (all upstream; none imports this roadmap)

- Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field (HilbertSiegelModularVarieties):
  - G, G_1 and Y_K;
  - Propositions 3.4.1 and 3.5.4, and Theorem 3.5.1 (also for the boundary charts behind Proposition 5.9.3);
  - the (O_F)^{×,+}_{(p)}-action and Δ (Proposition 3.3.17, Lemmas 3.5.2–3.5.3), and Lemma 3.8.2;
  - the §3.6 correspondences and the maps [g];
  - ω^κ and its descent;
  - Proposition 3.8.3 in its corrected form;
  - the Ekedahl–Oort and Kottwitz–Rapoport strata, and, at K_p(I), the identification of the canonical Kottwitz–Rapoport locus with the p-rank locus.
- Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: GSp_4, its local Langlands correspondence and Galois representations (GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations): Propositions 2.4.24 and 2.4.26; T_{v,i}; the normalized U_{Iw(v),i}, U_{Kli(v),i} and the projectors e_reg, e_irreg, e(I) on representations; and Remark 2.4.18, the representation-theoretic form of Lemmas 4.5.17 and 5.8.3(3).
- Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n (SiegelModularFormsModPn): Ha′, and the normalized T_{p,2} over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus (for the comparison in layer 2).
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes):
  - cohomological correspondences, and the general form of Lemma 3.9.13 (correspondences of Cousin complexes), used for Lemmas 4.2.36, 4.5.15 and 4.5.17;
  - the prime-to-p Hecke action on classical coherent cohomology;
  - Lan's vanishing, for Proposition 4.2.33, §6.2.1 and the proof of Proposition 6.6.1;
  - Theorem 3.10.1, with (2) at level K_p(I) in its localized form.

IMPORTS FROM THE ATLAS

- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies): L0a, L2a.
- Locally analytic distributions, growth, and character spaces (LocallyAnalyticDistributions): L3, L4.
- P-adic measures, completed group algebras, and characteristic ideals (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras): L1.
- Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and p-adic automorphic coefficients (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms): O1, O4, O8.
- Hodge–Tate theory, canonical subgroups, and automorphic period maps (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups): T0, T5.
- Shimura towers and perfectoid representability (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties): S1, S3.
- Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII): F1, R2, R3.
- Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli): A2, A4.
- Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory): R07.1.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications): C4, C5, C6.
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms (AutomorphicBundles): B5.
- Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry): A0-extension.
- Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations): SF.2.
- Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra): P7, R03.3.
- Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves): H1, H2, H3.
- Modular Curves PartII (ModularCurvesPartII): R13.2, R13.5.
- Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights): R15.3.
- Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions): ML.0, ML.4.

CONSUMERS

- Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular (AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity) uses Theorem 4.6.1, Lemmas 4.5.17 and 6.5.18, Theorem 5.8.6 with Remark 5.8.7, and Theorems 6.5.8, 6.6.4 and 6.6.5, in their localized forms. It also uses the prime-to-p Hecke action on M_I, through the algebra T̃^I of §7.8.
- Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting) may import Theorem 5.8.6; this roadmap never imports it.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- For F = Q and I = {p}: T_w is Pilloni's T, and U^I = U_{p,2} is Pilloni's U after matching normalizations. Λ̃_I = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] is Pilloni's Λ, and Λ_I = Z_p[[1+pZ_p]] is its factor on which the torsion μ_{p−1} ⊂ Z_p^× acts trivially. The paper's ω^{(k,2)} = Sym^{k−2}ω ⊗ det^2ω is Pilloni's Ω^{(k−2,2)}, and f_{(k,2)}, which is x ↦ x^{k−2} through κ_I = κ_1 ⊗ (2,2) and the (det ω)^2 twist in Ω^{κ̃_I}, is Pilloni's specialization z ↦ z^{k−2} on that factor. So M_I is the summand of Pilloni's M over that factor (his weights k ≡ 0 mod p−1, the paper's k ≡ 2 mod p−1), not all of M.
- For I = ∅, M_I is classical Hida theory.
- T_I^0 ≅ Z_p^{#I+2·#I^c}, so weight space has relative dimension #I + 2·#I^c over Z_p (Λ_I has Krull dimension one more), and the amplitude is [0,1] when #I = 1.
- Over the w-ordinary locus, U_{Kli(w),1} ≡ U_{Iw(w),1} mod p if l_w > 2, and U_{Kli(w),1} ≡ Z_w mod p if l_w < 2 (p. 121).
- F_w is finite flat of degree p^3, and of degree p^2 on the rank-one locus.
- On the modular curve over F_p, a U_p-eigenform in H^0(X, ω) with non-zero eigenvalue vanishes for p > 2 and is a multiple of Ha for p = 2 (§5.1).

routes.title: Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular
routes.brief:
AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity, "Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular" (new roadmap; area langlands).

Joined proposal. This route joins the maintainer's route for this paper: the new roadmap AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity, built by the queued design job DESIGN-BCGP18, with the same id, title and area. When the queue is next generated, the maintainer attaches this brief to the queued job DESIGN-BCGP18 as additional instructions and does not create a design job named after the roadmap id. DESIGN-BCGP18 merges the maintainer's brief and this one into one roadmap. Modularity of abelian surfaces (AbelianSurfacesModularity; design job DESIGN-BCGP25, from Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, "Modularity theorems for abelian surfaces", arXiv:2502.20645) builds on it. The maintainer's brief asks for the whole paper on existing roadmaps, with missing self-contained theories proposed separately. The review of this paper gives each part one owner:
- Hilbert–Siegel varieties, integral models, compactifications, bundles, level maps and mod p strata: Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field (HilbertSiegelModularVarieties).
- Higher Hida and higher Coleman theory, the separate roadmap the maintainer asked for: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory).
- Integral coherent cohomology and its Hecke action: Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes).
- GSp_4 local representation theory and Galois representations in regular weight: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: GSp_4, its local Langlands correspondence and Galois representations (GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations; "the GSp_4 Part II" below).
- Deformation rings, residual-image conditions and patching algebra: the existing layers named below.
This roadmap plans what remains: the argument of §§7.7–10 and the paper's final theorems.

Source: G. Boxer, F. Calegari, T. Gee and V. Pilloni, Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 153–501. Pages are those of arXiv:1812.09269v3; statement numbers agree in both versions. F is totally real and p ≥ 3 splits completely in F. ε is the cyclotomic character, ν the similitude, and rec_GT,p is Gan–Takeda's correspondence normalized as in §2.3. "Pure" is as in §2.5. Everything depends on Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp_4 (§1.4.1), whose conditional status this extraction routes, as a source, to be recorded at Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.0 and ML.4. Carry that dependence explicitly.

Final theorems, as printed (checked on page images), with the corrections the review confirmed.
- Theorem 8.4.1 (pp. 247–248). Suppose that p ≥ 3 splits completely in the totally real field F/Q, and that ρ: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) satisfies:
  (1) ν∘ρ = ε^{−1};
  (2) ρ̄ is vast and tidy (Definitions 7.5.6, 7.5.11);
  (3) for all v|p, ρ|G_{F_v} is p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary (Definition 7.3.1);
  (4) there exists π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary at all v|p, with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄;
  (5) for all finite v, ρ|G_{F_v} and ρ_{π,p}|G_{F_v} are pure.
  Then ρ is modular. More precisely, there is an ordinary automorphic representation π′ of GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 with ρ_{π′,p} ≅ ρ, and WD(ρ|G_{F_v})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_GT,p(π′_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) for every finite v.
- Theorem 8.5.2 (pp. 248–249), with Definition 8.5.1 (twisted means an unramified twist). It has the same statement with these changes:
  - (1) becomes ν∘ρ = χε^{−1}, with χ totally even, of finite order and unramified above p;
  - (3) and (4) require the twisted notions;
  - π has no central-character condition;
  - the conclusion gives a twisted ordinary π′.
  The paper only sketches the proof. Write out its "obvious generalization" of Lemma 8.3.2. In the sketch, read ρ|G_{F′} ⊗ ψ^{−1} for the printed ρ|G_{F′} ⊗ ψ.
- Theorem 9.2.8 (p. 257). A challenging abelian surface A over a totally real F (type A, End_C A = Z, or type B[C_2]) is potentially modular. More precisely, there are a finite Galois extension of totally real fields F′/F and a prime p splitting completely in F′ such that ρ_{A,p}|G_{F′} is modular and irreducible.
- Theorem 9.3.1 (p. 258). For every abelian surface A/F, 𝓡_A is potentially automorphic, and Conjecture 2.8.6 holds for A for each 0 ≤ i ≤ 4. With Corollary 9.3.3 it gives:
  - Theorem 1.1.2: Conjecture 1.1.1 (Serre's form of the Hasse–Weil conjecture) holds for every genus two curve and every abelian surface over a totally real field.
  - Theorem 1.1.3: each such variety is potentially automorphic in the sense of Definition 9.1.1.
- Corollary 9.3.3 (p. 259). For a genus two curve C/F, Λ(C,s) continues meromorphically to C, and Λ(C,s) = εN^{−s}Λ(C,3−s) with ε ∈ R and N ∈ Q_{>0}. Both versions print 3 − s; the correct form has Λ(C,2−s), since 2 − s = 1 + dim C − s.
- Theorem 9.3.4 (p. 259; Theorem 1.1.4). Let K/F be a quadratic extension of a totally real field, and E/K a genus one curve or an elliptic curve. Then E is potentially modular. More precisely, there are a Galois extension of totally real fields F′/F and a weight 0 cuspidal 𝛑 on GL_2(A_{KF′}) with trivial central character such that ρ_{E,l}|G_{KF′} ≅ ρ_{𝛑,l} for each l. In fact WD_v(ρ_{E,l}|G_{KF′_v})^{F-ss} ≅ rec(𝛑_v|det|_v^{−1/2}) at each finite v. Conjecture 2.8.6 holds for E. Correction: the "more precisely" clause fails when E has CM defined over K. There ρ_{E,l}|G_K is a sum of two characters coming from algebraic Hecke characters, and the first sentence still holds.
- Proposition 10.1.1 (pp. 264–265; Theorem 1.1.7). Hypotheses:
  - p > 2 splits completely in F;
  - A/F has good ordinary reduction at all v|p, with unit root crystalline eigenvalues distinct mod p at each v|p;
  - A has a polarization of degree prime to p;
  - ρ̄_{A,p}: G_F → GSp_4(F_p), the dual of A[p], is vast and tidy;
  - ρ̄_{A,p} is ordinarily modular: some π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2, ordinary (the printed "unramified and" is deleted; see Proposition 10.1.3) at all v|p, has ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄_{A,p}, with ρ_{π,p}|G_{F_v} pure for all finite v.
  Then A is modular: some ordinary π′ of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 has ρ_{π′,p} ≅ ρ_{A,p}.
- Proposition 10.1.3 (pp. 265–266). Let p > 2 split completely in F. Let ρ̄_p: G_F → GSp_4(F_p) be absolutely irreducible with similitude ε^{−1}, vast and tidy, and p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary. Suppose one of the following:
  (1) p = 3 and ρ̄_3 is induced from a 2-dimensional representation with inverse cyclotomic determinant over a totally real quadratic E/F in which 3 is unramified;
  (2) p = 5 and ρ̄_5 is induced in the same way from a GL_2(F_5)-valued representation, with 5 unramified in E;
  (3) ρ̄_p is induced from a character of a quartic CM extension H/F in which p splits completely.
  Then ρ̄_p is ordinarily modular.
  Correction: delete "unramified" here, in the hypothesis of Proposition 10.1.1 (Theorem 1.1.7 omits it) and in the proof of Theorem 10.1.4. In cases (1)–(2) the form may be ramified at p, and Theorem 8.4.1 needs only ordinarity.
- Theorem 10.1.4 (p. 267). Let 5 split completely in F, let K/F be quadratic with 5 unramified, and let E/K have good ordinary or semistable ordinary reduction at all w|5. Suppose that:
  (1) the projective image of ρ̄_{E,5} is S_5 = PGL_2(F_5) or S_4;
  (2) some r̄_5: G_F → GL_2(F_5) with determinant ε^{−1} has r̄_5|G_K ≅ ρ̄_{E,5}.
  Then E is modular. In particular, there are infinitely many modular elliptic curves over K, up to twist, which are not CM and do not come from any subfield of K.
- Theorem 10.2.1 (p. 269). Fix ρ̄: G_F → GSp_4(F_3) with similitude ε^{−1}. Then:
  - B(ρ̄), the moduli of pairs (A, ı_3) below, is unirational over F;
  - infinitely many principally polarized A/F, up to twist, have End_C(A) = Z and ı_3: A[3] ≃ V(ρ̄)^∨, and they may be taken to be Jacobians of curves y^2 = f(x) with f quintic;
  - if ρ̄|G_{F_v} arises, for all v|3, as the 3-torsion of an abelian surface over F_v with good ordinary reduction, the A may be taken good ordinary at all v|3.
  The proof of the last clause has a gap: it needs an ordinary point of the degree six cover P(ρ̄)(F_v), not of B(ρ̄)(F_v). The image of P(ρ̄)(F_v) is open and closed in B(ρ̄)(F_v), and nothing in the paper shows that it meets the ordinary locus. Plan the last clause with the hypothesis that for each v|3 there is an ordinary point of P(ρ̄)(F_v) (an ordinary principally polarized surface with A[3] ≅ V(ρ̄)^∨ and an F_v-rational odd theta characteristic). Derive it from the printed hypothesis only when F_v = Q_3, through Lemma 9.3.7 of the 2025 paper (see Boundaries). Do not state the printed form for other F_v, where it remains unproved.
- Theorem 10.2.6 (pp. 271–272; Theorem 1.1.5 over Q). If 3 splits completely in F, there are infinitely many modular A/F, up to twist, with End_C(A) = Z that do not come from any proper subfield: for each p, no twist of ρ_{A,p} extends to the absolute Galois group of a proper subfield of F. In the proof:
  - H/F must be totally real, for example F(√2);
  - read A[3] ≅ V(ρ̄)^∨ for the printed A[3] ≅ ρ̄;
  - do not use Res_{H_v/F_v}(E) as the local point at v|3: it has no F_v-rational odd theta characteristic, so it lies outside the image of P(ρ̄)(F_v). Since F_v = Q_3, take the ordinary local point from Lemma 9.3.7 of the 2025 paper.
- §§10.3–10.4:
  - Lemma 10.3.1: every A/Q satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.1 satisfies the paramodular conjecture.
  - Lemma 10.3.2 is conditional on the Fontaine–Mazur, Standard, Hodge and Tate conjectures (the Tate conjecture is used three times in the sketch, on p. 275, but is missing from the printed hypotheses; state it as a hypothesis) and on compatible systems for cuspidal Π on GL_4 of type φ_{2;1,0}. For such a symplectic Π with multiplier |·|^2 and rational eigenvalues it gives a motive that is an abelian surface or a quaternionic ("fake") abelian fourfold, and proves a converse (that direction uses standard automorphy conjectures and the known Mumford–Tate conjecture for type II).
  - §10.4.2 (type II fourfolds A = Res_{K/Q}(B ⊗ χ)), as exposition, with ∧^2V ≅ χ_{K/Q}·(χ∘Ver) for the printed ∧^2V ≅ χ_{K/Q}; the conclusion stands.
  - Conjecture 10.4.3 is Brumer–Kramer's modified paramodular conjecture, and Expected Lemma 10.4.4 is proved only in sketch.
  - Lemma 10.4.6:
    - correct End_C(A) ⊗ Q to D × D (printed M_2(D));
    - 𝒮 is a system of G_{Q(√−6)} (printed G_Q);
    - read a_5 = 2^4·η^2·3 = −240 − 96√−6 (printed 2^4·η·3). The printed discriminant 2^90·3^6·(1−√−6)^30·(2−√−6)^6 holds only for the corrected value;
    - in the proof, read "If B were not autochthonous" for the printed "If B were autochthonous".
  Record the status of each.

Additions, layer by layer.
1. Statements (§§1.2, 1.4.2, 2.8, 9.1).
   - Definition 2.8.2 and Remark 2.8.3: ρ_{A,l} = H^1(A_F̄, Q̄_l), GSp_4-valued with multiplier ε_l^{−1}.
   - Definition 9.1.1 as printed. Π = ⊞Π_i with C-algebraic cuspidal Π_i on GL_{n_i}, M_Π is a number field, and WD_v(𝓡) = ⊕rec(Π_{i,v}|det|_v^{(1−n_i)/2}); there is no infinitesimal-character condition. With it go Remarks 9.1.2–9.1.4 and (9.1.5).
   - Definition 9.1.6 and Remark 9.1.7.
   - Definition 9.1.8, read with WD(ρ|G_{F_v}) where WD(ρ_{π,p}|G_{F_v}) is printed, and Remark 9.1.9.
   - As exposition only: §1.2 (defect, reduction to two degrees, and the local–global compatibility carried by the Hida complexes, made precise by Theorem 7.9.4) and §1.4.2 (genus ≥ 3).
   Imports:
   - Proposition 2.8.1 from Néron models and semistable abelian varieties (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties) R11.5.
   - Λ(𝓡,s), Λ(A,s) and Conjectures 1.1.1 and 2.8.6 from Periods, motivic L-values and special-value conjectures (PeriodsAndSpecialValues) PS.1.
   - Godement–Jacquet from Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.2.
   - rec for GL_n from Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.6, and for GL_2 from GL₂ Automorphic Representations And Transfer (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer) R16.2–R16.3 (Definition 9.1.1, Theorem 9.3.4).
   - Compatible systems from Potential Modularity And Compatible Systems (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems) R24.5:operations.
   - Lemma 9.1.10, with (3) corrected to SL_2(F_l), from Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) PA.5.
2. Taylor–Wiles set-up (§§7.7–7.8).
   - Hypotheses 7.7.1 and 7.8.1, and v_0, absolutely unramified.
   - The problems 𝓢^{I,𝔠}_χ and 𝓢^{I,𝔠}_{χ,Q}: 𝔠 picks ᾱ_v or β̄_v at each v|p, and a Taylor–Wiles datum has four eigenvalues (printed n).
   - The levels of Definition 7.8.2.
   - T̃^I, m̃^{I,𝔠} (7.8.4) and the modules M^{χ,I,𝔠} = RHom^0_{Λ_I}(M^{•,I}_{K^p}, Λ_I)_{m̃^{I,𝔠},χ,|·|^2} and M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}, with their Hecke algebras.
   - Definition 7.8.8 and Proposition 7.8.11.
   Imports:
   - Global Galois deformation rings (GlobalGaloisDeformations) G7 and R04.1–R04.5: Definitions 7.1.2–7.1.5, Proposition 7.2.1, Corollary 7.6.3, S_Q and Δ_Q.
   - Local Galois deformation rings and their components (LocalGaloisDeformationRings) L7, L8, R08.1 and R08.2: Definition 7.3.1, 𝒟_v^P, 𝒟_v^{B,𝔠_v}, 𝒟_v^χ and Propositions 7.3.4, 7.3.16 and 7.4.2–7.4.8.
   - Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations) G7: vast, tidy and enormous, §7.5 through Lemma 7.5.23, §2.2, and Lemmas 2.1.3 and 8.3.1.
   - Lemma 7.8.3 from Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D5.
   - Proposition 7.8.10 from HilbertSiegelModularVarieties.
   - Theorem 4.6.1 and Theorem 6.6.5 (ordinary classicity for #I ≤ 1, used in Proposition 7.8.11) from HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.
   - From Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra): Lemmas 7.8.5–7.8.6 and 4.6.22 at P7, and balanced modules at R03.5.
   - Theorem 3.10.1 and Corollary 3.10.5 from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.
   - Q_v(X) and Lemmas 2.4.33–2.4.37 from the GSp_4 Part II.
3. Galois representations over Hida–Hecke algebras (§7.9).
   - Proposition 7.9.1 comes from Theorem 5.8.6, Remark 5.8.7 and Lemma 4.5.17 of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.
   - Theorem 7.9.4 is glued as in Clozel–Harris–Taylor, with reconstruction from determinants at Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.1. It uses Theorem 2.7.2 and Propositions 2.4.13, 2.4.26, 2.4.28 and 2.4.30 of the GSp_4 Part II, and Theorem 6.6.5 of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

In Proposition 7.11.2 for #I = 1, prove M_∞ O-flat first. Defect 0 and defect 1 are different theorems, and only §8's doubling relations give classical forms.
5. Multiplicities (§§7.12–7.13).
   - Hypothesis 7.13.1 and Definition 7.13.4.
   - The primes 𝔭_x, 𝔭̃ (7.13.3), of dimension one (the paper prints "height one"), and the spaces S^{I,𝔠}.

   Imports: Theorem 6.6.5 of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (Proposition 7.13.11); Lemmas 7.12.2–7.12.3 at P9, whose proof needs unit cycle coefficients; cycles at R03.6; Lemma 7.13.8 at R03.3; Theorem 2.9.3 and Lemma 2.9.1 at ML.4.

Lemma 2.5.1 is imported from Automorphic Galois Representations PartII (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII) AG2.5, in its corrected form: a pure N maximises rank(N^j) for every j and is the unique Weil–Deligne structure doing so; maximising the rank of N alone characterises it when dim V = 4 and N is symplectic, the case used here.

7. Potential automorphy (§9).
   - Galois types, challenging surfaces and Proposition 9.2.1.
   - Lemma 9.2.2. Its type B[C_2] case must treat separately a surface with real multiplication by a real quadratic field M defined over K but not over F, at primes l inert in M. There s̄_l^σ is the Frobenius twist of s̄_l, and ρ̄_{A,l}(G_{F(ζ_l)}) = SL_2(F_{l^2}) ⋊ Z/2 ⊂ Sp_4(F_l) (the printed argument would give SL_2(F_{l^2}) ≀ Z/2, which is too large to lie in Sp_4(F_l)). This group is enormous for l ≥ 11 (Lemmas 7.5.14 and 7.5.17) and tidy by Lemma 7.5.12 (Lemma 7.5.13 does not apply). The containment SL_2(O_M/λ) ⊂ s̄_λ(G_K) for almost all λ comes from Ribet's large-image theorem for abelian varieties with real multiplication, since s_l and s_l^σ never become isomorphic over a finite extension of K, so there are no potential inner twists. Import it from Faltings finiteness, semisimplicity and isogeny theorems, Part II: ℓ-adic and residual images of abelian varieties (Serre's open-image theorems) (OpenImageTheoremsForAbelianVarieties) if that Part II is accepted; otherwise plan it here. In the proof, read "some finite place v of K" for the printed "of F". The false step is the sentence "Aut(PSL_2(k)) = PGL_2(k)" in the proof of Lemma 7.5.22: it is PΓL_2(k) = PGL_2(k) ⋊ Gal(k/F_p). That lemma comes from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, where it must be restricted to k = F_p, or corrected by treating the Frobenius-twisted case separately.
   - Definition 9.2.3 and Lemmas 9.2.5–9.2.6.
   - Lemma 9.2.7. As printed, conclusion (5) needs F_q-rational local data that the choice of q does not provide, and the proof does not fix the determinant over F_q. Repair it as follows.
     - Choose q good and with t^2 − a_1(v)t + (a_2(v) − 2p) split mod q at every v|p (Chebotarev: a positive-density condition, compatible with Lemma 9.2.6).
     - At w|q, use φ̄_{w1} = λ_a ⊕ ε̄^{−1}λ_a^{−1} and φ̄_{w2} = λ_b ⊕ ε̄^{−1}λ_b^{−1}, with a ≠ b in F_q^× the unit roots of two ordinary elliptic curves over F_q, instead of A's data, and change the first bullet of (5) to match. F_q-rationality of A's unit roots at w|q is not a Chebotarev condition, and the paper gives no argument for it.
     - Fix det r̄_q = ε̄^{−1} from the start: apply Moret-Bailly to the twisted form classifying GL_2(F_q)-extensions with determinant ε̄^{−1}, or make ε̄·det r̄_q a square first and then use the paper's Brauer argument. The Brauer obstruction only controls F̄_q-valued square roots.
     - In Theorem 9.2.8, take the local point at v|q to be the canonical lift of the product of those two elliptic curves. In its proof, read "central character |·|^2" for "trivial central character" and ρ_{π,q} for ρ_{π,p}.
   - The twisted moduli of principally polarized abelian surfaces with symplectic torsion isomorphisms, geometrically connected, with ordinary local points: the GSp_4 analogue of Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves) H6.
   - Theorem 9.2.8; Theorem 2.7.3 (GL_2 over a quadratic extension); Theorem 9.3.1; Corollary 9.3.3; Theorem 9.3.4; Proposition 9.4.1 and Definition 9.4.2.
   Imports:
   - Serre's open image theorem from Faltings finiteness, semisimplicity and isogeny theorems (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems) R28.4, or from its proposed Part II (OpenImageTheoremsForAbelianVarieties), if that is accepted.
   - Moret-Bailly (R23.1); Proposition 9.1.11 (R23.2, R23.3, R23.5).
   - Proposition 9.1.12 in its corrected form (R23.1, R24.5:operations): there are a finite Galois extension K/E and a finite Galois extension L′/K′, K′ = KE′, with (1) Gal(L′/K′) ≅ G; (2) K/E linearly disjoint from E′F^(avoid)/E; (3) and (5) as printed; (4) L′_w/K′_w = H′_v/E′_v, the diagram's top-left entry being Gal(L′_w/K′_w). No descent of L′ to an extension L/K is asserted. Keeping L/K and reading (2) with L/E is itself false: the two places above a split auxiliary place would get isomorphic local extensions, so the asymmetric choice at the auxiliary place in Lemma 9.2.7 (φ̄_{w1} unramified, Proj φ̄_{w2} ramified) could not be realised.
   - Brauer's induction theorem from Induction, restriction, and Mackey theory for finite groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction) layer 6, cited and never re-planned, applied to compatible systems at R24.5. For Proposition 9.4.1, Artin L-functions continued by Brauer's theorem, with Hecke L-functions from Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.1.
   - Rank-two potential automorphy (ML.2); Ramakrishnan, Kim–Henniart and Arthur–Clozel (ML.5); Roberts' theta lift (the GSp_4 Part II).
   - Patrikis's lifting (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1).
   - Purity from Galois representations attached to modular and Hilbert modular forms (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations) R19.3–R19.5.
   - Siegel moduli from Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M5–M6.
   - Polarizations and Weil restriction from Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A2, A3 and A6.
   - For Proposition 10.1.1 (good ordinary reduction with distinct unit roots gives p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary) and Lemma 9.2.5 (the conditions p ∤ a_2 and p ∤ a_1^2 − 4a_2): p-divisible groups and connected–étale sequences from Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1 via AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4; D_cris from P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) R06.2; the crystalline comparison from Cohomology comparisons: integral diagrams and rational period realizations (CohomologyComparisons) CP.2. The equality of the crystalline and ℓ-adic Frobenius polynomials of an abelian variety over a finite field (Katz–Messing) is planned in no atlas layer, and the brief of Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups from modularity lifting (AdjointSelmerGroupsFromModularityLifting) plans it "unless a layer owns it". Give it one owner: request it at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4, beside the Tate module and the p-divisible group, and import it from there. Neither roadmap plans it.
8. Modularity (§10).
   - Propositions 10.1.1 and 10.1.3, and Remark 10.1.2. Imports:
     - ordinary lifts from Ordinary automorphic forms and ordinary modularity lifting (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting) R21.2;
     - Langlands–Tunnell, base change and automorphic induction from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4–R17.5;
     - the odd Artin conjecture and the mod 5 argument from ML.1.
   - Lemmas 7.5.25–7.5.27 and Theorem 10.1.4, with embedding problems from Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups) IG.4.
   - §10.2:
     - 𝒜_2(3), the Burkhardt quartic;
     - 𝒜_2(6), with S_6 ≅ Sp_4(F_2) through Weierstrass points;
     - P = 𝒜_2(3)^−, and the locus of Jacobians with a marked rational Weierstrass point;
     - Proposition 10.2.3 and Lemma 10.2.4, with the Schur multiplier from Induction, restriction, and Mackey theory for finite groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction) layer 7;
     - Theorems 10.2.1 and 10.2.6, with Hilbert irreducibility from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2, and Lemma 9.3.7 of the 2025 paper (see Boundaries).
   - The paramodular statements, with local newform theory from the GSp_4 Part II.
   - Tau Ceti roadmaps, cited and never re-planned: Algebraic curves — function fields, divisors, and Riemann–Roch (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves) layer 10; The Jacobian challenge (Christian Merten's AG version) (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge) layers D–F; The Chebotarev density theorem (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev) layer 10.

Boundaries.
- Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting, from Calegari–Geraghty 2020) is not used here, and neither roadmap imports the other. The statement they share is planned once: for a Hecke-equivariant O[Δ_Q]-perfect complex computing coherent cohomology of the Taylor–Wiles covers, localisation at m_Q followed by Δ_Q-coinvariants recovers the level-K^p complex, in all degrees. Its owner is IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. That roadmap already owns the Hecke-equivariant Hochschild–Serre descent and imports Q_v(X) from the GSp_4 Part II; for this statement it also imports Lemmas 2.4.33–2.4.37 from there. Proposition 7.9.8 here is its application to the Hida complexes M^{•,I}, and GSp4NonregularModularityLifting applies it to its own complexes. The Calegari–Geraghty (2020) statements that Proposition 7.9.8 is planned in GSp4NonregularModularityLifting only because its "natural owner, DESIGN-BCGP18, is pending", and that "AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity should import this roadmap", are superseded and must be re-pointed.
- The density argument of Lemma 9.2.5 (Chebotarev on the Zariski closure of ρ_{A,l}(G_F) after Sawin, with the Weil-bound reduction to finitely many polynomial non-vanishing conditions on the unit roots, over a totally real field) is planned once. It goes in OpenImageTheoremsForAbelianVarieties if that Part II is accepted, since both consumers already import it; otherwise it goes here. AdjointSelmerGroupsFromModularityLifting must then import it instead of planning it: its "planned here" for Calegari–Geraghty's Lemmas A.7(2) and A.8 is to be re-pointed.
- AbelianSurfacesModularity imports from here: P(ρ̄) and the marked-Weierstrass locus, the rationality of P(ρ̄), the S_6 ≅ Sp_4(F_2) dictionary, the twisted moduli, Lemmas 9.3.6–9.3.7 of the 2025 paper with their seed curves, Lemma 10.3.1 and Conjecture 10.4.3. The extraction of the 2025 paper currently routes these statements (its §9.2.1 twisted odd-theta moduli, Lemmas 9.3.6–9.3.7 and the seed curves) to AbelianSurfacesModularity, and its brief designs layers for them. DESIGN-BCGP25 must import them from here instead.
- Plan here, with the 2025 paper as source, its Lemma 9.3.7: every ordinary ρ̄: G_{Q_3} → GSp_4(F_3) with multiplier ε̄^{−1} and finite flat dual is ρ̄_{Jac(X),3} for a genus two X/Q_3 with a rational Weierstrass point, Jac(X) good ordinary and 3-distinguished. Plan with it that paper's Lemma 9.3.6 and the explicit scalar and non-scalar seed curves. Import Lemmas 9.3.4–9.3.5 of that paper from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1–A5. Theorem 10.2.1 needs it at each v|3 with F_v = Q_3, and so does Theorem 10.2.6, where every such F_v is Q_3; this roadmap cannot import AbelianSurfacesModularity.
- The maintainer's one-line target, "every abelian surface over a totally real field is potentially modular", is Theorem 1.1.3, potential automorphy. Potential modularity is proved only for challenging surfaces.
routes.reason:
The maintainer routed this paper to a new roadmap, AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity, "Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular", in area langlands, built by the queued design job DESIGN-BCGP18. The extractions of Pilloni (2020), Calegari–Geraghty (2020), Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2025) and Boxer–Pilloni (2026) all name it under that id, and Modularity of abelian surfaces (AbelianSurfacesModularity, DESIGN-BCGP25) builds on it. This route therefore joins the maintainer's route under the same id, title and area. Its brief is an addition that DESIGN-BCGP18 merges with the maintainer's brief, not a second design job. An accepted new route would otherwise become a design job named after its roadmap id, a second job writing the same roadmap. So when the queue is next generated, the maintainer attaches this brief to DESIGN-BCGP18 as additional instructions and does not create a design job named after the roadmap id.

A new roadmap is right because nothing in the atlas goes in its direction:
- GL₂ Modularity Lifting (GL2ModularityLifting), Ordinary automorphic forms and ordinary modularity lifting (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting) and Potential Modularity And Compatible Systems (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems) are rank-two theories.
- Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure), the only lifting in the atlas with positive defect, treats polarized GL_n over CM fields in Betti cohomology, which cannot see weight-two Siegel forms.
- Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) registers endpoints without proving them.
- No layer plans GSp_4 modularity lifting, patching of coherent cohomology, or abelian surfaces as such.

The route keeps 60 items:
- the argument of §§7.7–10 (Taylor–Wiles set-up, Galois representations on Hida–Hecke algebras, patching in defect 0 and 1, Ihara-avoidance multiplicities, étale descent, the lifting theorems, potential automorphy and the modularity applications);
- the paper's final theorems;
- the GSp_4 conventions for abelian surfaces (Definition 2.8.2);
- Theorem 2.7.3 and Corollary 7.9.6, which need parallel weight two and so come after the Hida families.

What the paper develops in other directions goes to its owners:
- the Hilbert–Siegel varieties, higher Hida and Coleman theory, integral coherent Hecke complexes and GSp_4 local Langlands go to the four Part IIs named in the brief;
- the deformation rings, image conditions, patching algebra, L-function conjectures and potential-modularity inputs go to existing stages, as sources.

Several statements were planned twice, here and in sibling proposals. The brief gives each one owner, which needs these changes elsewhere:
- The descent of Proposition 7.9.8, in all degrees, belongs to Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes). That roadmap's brief from this paper must add it, with Lemmas 2.4.33–2.4.37 of the GSp_4 Part II. The Calegari–Geraghty (2020) brief of Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting) must drop "natural owner DESIGN-BCGP18" and "AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity should import this roadmap".
- The density argument of Lemma 9.2.5 (Calegari–Geraghty's Lemmas A.7(2) and A.8) goes to Faltings finiteness, semisimplicity and isogeny theorems, Part II: ℓ-adic and residual images of abelian varieties (Serre's open-image theorems) (OpenImageTheoremsForAbelianVarieties) if that Part II is accepted, and otherwise here. Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups from modularity lifting (AdjointSelmerGroupsFromModularityLifting) imports it rather than planning it. The Katz–Messing identification of Frobenius polynomials is requested at Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A4, and both roadmaps import it from there.
- The 2025 extraction must route P(ρ̄), the marked-Weierstrass locus, the S_6 ≅ Sp_4(F_2) dictionary, the twisted odd-theta moduli, its Lemmas 9.3.6–9.3.7 with the seed curves, Lemma 10.3.1 and Conjecture 10.4.3 as imports from here, not as AbelianSurfacesModularity's own layers. Its join of GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations must use this brief's title, "Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: GSp_4, its local Langlands correspondence and Galois representations". Its own title misquotes the parent's atlas title. It must also use the same area as this paper's route for that Part II.

The route that carries Proposition 9.1.12 must state its corrected form, with no descent of L′ to L/K; its proposed repair "clause (2) must read L/E" is itself false. The route that sends Lemma 7.5.22 to Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations) G7 must record that Aut(PSL_2(k)) = PΓL_2(k), and either restrict the lemma to k = F_p or treat the Frobenius-twisted case separately.

routes.title: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: GSp_4, its local Langlands correspondence and Galois representations
routes.brief:
Scope. This Part II starts where Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) stops. The parent registers normalizations and conditional status (ML.0), owns Arthur's classification for GSp_4 with the transfer to GL_4 (this paper's Lemma 2.9.1, Theorem 2.9.3) and Gan–Takeda's rec_GT with its L-packets and Definition 2.3.1 (ML.4), and registers cyclic base change, automorphic induction and other known transfers (ML.5), which this Part II imports for GL_n; it plans nothing else for GSp_4. Building on rec_GT, this Part II is the single owner of the explicit local representation theory of GSp_4 used in Siegel and Hilbert–Siegel arithmetic, the archimedean parameters and weights, the Galois representations of regular-weight cuspidal representations over totally real fields, and the GSp_4 transfers of Layer 9 (base change along a solvable totally real extension, the lift into GSp_4 from GL_2 over a quadratic extension, and solvable descent to GSp_4 over Q). Those transfers are specific to GSp_4 and are planned only here; ML.5 does not register them. In the title, 'GSp_4' and 'its local Langlands correspondence' refer to this explicit local theory built on rec_GT. The group and its parahorics (PELModuli M0, ShimuraData D5, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3) and Gan–Takeda's correspondence with its L-packets (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4) are imported, not planned here.

Joined proposal. Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Modularity theorems for abelian surfaces (arXiv:2502.20645) routes items to this id with the same parent, title and area (langlands). The design job merges the two briefs into one roadmap. Where they differ, the final ownership governs: Gan–Takeda, Arthur's transfer and multiplicities come from ML.4; ET.6 supplies only rec for GL_n. The 2025 paper follows this paper's conventions (its §1.8.12: Art sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius; the cyclotomic character has Hodge–Tate weight −1). Its Theorem 1.8.13 lists the same Hodge–Tate weights as Theorem 2.7.1(3), in the order of its display (1.8.14). That display exchanges the ε-powers on α and α^{−1} (αε^{1−(k_v+l_v)/2} first, α^{−1}ε^{(k_v+l_v)/2−2} last). This contradicts the paper's own weight-2 display (1.8.19), which it derives from (1.8.14) by interpolation, and the Theorem 2.7.2 it cites. It is a misprint affecting nothing, to be recorded against the 2025 extraction. Plan Theorem 2.7.2(3) as printed here, register its normalization at ML.0, and cite the 2025 statement in corrected form. The layers give this paper's additions and place the 2025 items.

Notation: q_v = #k(v), Frob_v geometric, ε cyclotomic (Hodge–Tate weight −1), ν the similitude, λ_x unramified with Frob_v ↦ x, β_{v,0} = diag(ϖ_v,ϖ_v,ϖ_v,ϖ_v), β_{v,1} = diag(ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1,1), β_{v,2} = diag(ϖ_v^2,ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1). Throughout Layers 1–5, as in §2.4 (arXiv p. 20): p > 2 is prime, p splits completely in the totally real field F, E/Q_p is finite with ring of integers O and residue field k, and q_v^{1/2} ∈ E is fixed; Lemma 2.4.34 uses p > 2. Statements follow arXiv:1812.09269v3 (numbering of Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021)), with the corrections listed after the layers.

Layer 1: principal series and the spinor polynomial (§§2.4.5–2.4.11). χ_1 × χ_2 ⋊ σ is n-Ind_B^{GSp_4(F_v)} of diag(a,b,cb^{−1},ca^{−1}) ↦ χ_1(a)χ_2(b)σ(c). Proposition 2.4.6: (1) it is irreducible iff none of χ_1, χ_2, χ_1χ_2^{±1} is |·|_v^{±1}; (2) each irreducible constituent π has rec_{GT,p}(π)^{ss} = σ∘Art^{−1} ⊗ ((χ_1χ_2)∘Art^{−1} ⊕ χ_1∘Art^{−1} ⊕ χ_2∘Art^{−1} ⊕ 1); (3) if it is irreducible, its parameter has N = 0. (2.4.8): for unramified π, with t_{v,i} the eigenvalue of T_{v,i} = [GSp_4(O_{F_v})β_{v,i}GSp_4(O_{F_v})], rec_{GT,p}(π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial Q_v(X) = X^4 − t_{v,1}X^3 + (q_vt_{v,2} + (q_v^3+q_v)t_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^3t_{v,0}t_{v,1}X + q_v^6t_{v,0}^2. Prove its conversion to the GL_4 conventions of IHG.3 and to the Hecke polynomials of the re-pointed items: Calegari–Geraghty's Q_x(X) (Duke Math. J. 169 (2020), Definition 6.7), Pilloni's reciprocal Q_ℓ(X) (Duke Math. J. 169 (2020), §5.1.3, with differently indexed operators), and the 2025 paper's Q_ℓ and dual-spin P_ℓ (§§1.8.27–1.8.28: Q_ℓ is the geometric-Frobenius characteristic polynomial of ρ_{π,p}, P_ℓ that of ρ_{π,p}^∨ε^{−3}). Definitions 2.4.9, 2.4.11: the Hecke parameters [α_v, β_v, γ_vβ_v^{−1}, γ_vα_v^{−1}] are the roots of Q_v, ordered so that pairs (1,4) and (2,3) multiply to the similitude γ_v at Frob_v, unique up to D_8; π(χ) is general if they are pairwise distinct and no ratio of them is q_v, and then π(χ) is irreducible with |W·χ| = 8.

Layer 2: the Iwahori–Hecke algebra (§§2.4.29–2.4.38, Remark 2.4.18). The GSp_4 instance of the imported Bernstein presentation (2.4.32) and of the centre O[X_*(T)]^W ≅ spherical algebra, x ↦ e_{Sph(v)}x, in the coordinates x_0: t ↦ diag(t,t,1,1), x_1: t ↦ diag(1/t,1,1,t), x_2: t ↦ diag(1,1/t,t,1). Here x_0^2x_1x_2 is t ↦ diag(t,t,t,t) and O[X_*(T)] = O[x_0, x_1, x_2, (x_0^2x_1x_2)^{−1}]. The involutions s_1, s_2, s_1s_2s_1 ∈ W send (x_0, x_1, x_2) to (x_0, x_2, x_1), (x_0x_2, x_1, x_2^{−1}), (x_0x_1, x_1^{−1}, x_2), which defines the triples wγ below. With the e_i the coefficients, (X − x_0)(X − x_0x_1)(X − x_0x_2)(X − x_0x_1x_2) = Σ_{i=0}^{4} e_iX^i as printed, and Σ e_iX^i maps to q_v^{−6}Q_v(q_v^{3/2}X) = X^4 − q_v^{−3/2}T_{v,1}X^3 + (q_v^{−2}T_{v,2} + (1 + q_v^{−2})T_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^{−3/2}T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + T_{v,0}^2. From here on the paper ignores the powers of q_v^{1/2}, which are ±1 modulo λ when q_v ≡ 1 mod p (see Layer 5). Remark 2.4.18: e_{Kli(v)} sends U^naive_{Iw(v),1} + q_v(U^naive_{Iw(v),1})^{−1}U^naive_{Iw(v),2}, U^naive_{Iw(v),2}, U^naive_{Iw(v),0} to U^naive_{Kli(v),1}, U^naive_{Kli(v),2}, U^naive_{Kli(v),0}. For q_v ≡ 1 mod p: Lemma 2.4.33, H ⊗ k ≅ k[X_*(T) ⋊ W]. Lemma 2.4.34 and Corollary 2.4.35: for smooth O[GSp_4(F_v)]-modules, [GSp_4(O_{F_v}) : Iw(v)]^{−1}e_{Sph(v)} splits M^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} ⊂ M^{Iw(v)} (the index is ≡ |W| = 8 mod p, a unit since p > 2); and M^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} = (M^{Iw(v)})^W for smooth k-modules. Then e_{Sph(v)}M ≠ 0. If n is unique, then for each maximal ideal m ⊂ k[X_*(T)] in the support of M, the maps k[W] ⊗_k M_m → M, w ⊗ x ↦ w·x, and M_m → e_{Sph(v)}M, x ↦ e_{Sph(v)}·x, are isomorphisms. Remark 2.4.38: U^naive_{v,0} = x_0^2x_1x_2, and when this is 1, U^naive_{v,1} = x_0 and U^naive_{v,2} = (s_1s_2s_1)(x_1) = x_1^{−1}; so under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.4.36, (U_{v,0} − 1, U_{v,1} − α_1, U_{v,2} − α_1α_2) lies in the support of M. The 2025 paper's §7.4 statements at q ≡ 1 mod p join this layer. First, the Bernstein centre is localized in the coordinates x_0, x_1, x_2 with multiplier x_0^2x_1x_2. Second, once the multiplier is included, a regular residual orbit has eight distinct torus eigenideals whose localizations split a finite module; the coefficients of Σ e_iX^i alone need not fix the multiplier when the trace vanishes. Third, §7.4.12: let R be complete local Noetherian and N a smooth R[GSp_4(Q_q)]-module with N^{K_2} finite projective over R[K_1/K_2] for every normal compact open pair K_2 ⊂ K_1. At a regular residual character with roots α_1, α_2, α_2^{−1}, α_1^{−1}, projection from the localized spherical invariants to any chosen Iwahori eigensummand is an isomorphism, by a proof that does not divide by #W = 8.

Layer 3: Iwahori and Klingen eigenvalues. Propositions 2.4.12, 2.4.17: for a general unramified principal series with Hecke parameters [α_v, β_v, q_vβ_v^{−1}, q_vα_v^{−1}], π^{Iw(v)} is a sum of 8 one-dimensional simultaneous eigenspaces of U^naive_{Iw(v),i} = [Iw(v)β_{v,i}Iw(v)], with eigenvalues q_v^{−2}, α_v, q_v^{−1}α_vβ_v for each ordered (α_v, β_v); π^{Kli(v)} is a sum of 4 for U^naive_{Kli(v),i}, with q_v^{−2}, α_v + β_v, q_v^{−1}α_vβ_v for each {α_v, β_v}. Propositions 2.4.13, 2.4.20: an irreducible admissible π with such an Iwahori (resp. Klingen) eigenvector, no ratio of a pair of the four parameters being q_v, is the unramified principal series with those Hecke parameters. Proposition 2.4.22: for unipotent r (r^{ss} unramified), its L-packet contains a generic representation iff ad(r)(1) has no invariants.

Layer 4: ordinary representations (§2.4.23; v | p, F_v = Q_p). For k ≥ l ≥ 2, k ≡ l mod 2: U_{•,i} = p^{n_i}U^naive_{•,i} with (n_0, n_1, n_2) = (2, (k+l)/2−2, k−1) for • = Iw(v), Kli(v), and U_{Si(v),1} = p^{n_1}U^naive_{Si(v),1}. π with central character |·|^2 is ordinary of weights k ≥ l ≥ 2 if π^{Iw(v)} has a U_{Iw(v),i}-eigenvector with unit eigenvalues u_{v,i}; α_v = u_{v,1}, β_v = u_{v,2}/u_{v,1}; π is then a constituent of the unramified principal series with Hecke parameters [α_vp^{2−(k+l)/2}, β_vp^{−(k−l)/2}, β_v^{−1}p^{1+(k−l)/2}, α_v^{−1}p^{(k+l)/2−1}], and it is p-distinguished if these are pairwise distinct, that is, if l > 2 or α_v ≠ β_v. If l > 2, the unit eigenvector is unique up to scalar and the ordered pair (α_v, β_v) is determined by π. If l = 2 and π is p-distinguished, only the set {α_v, β_v} is determined: there may also be an eigenvector with unit eigenvalues 1, β_v, α_vβ_v, and by Proposition 2.4.24 there always is. e_reg, e_irreg are the ordinary projectors of U_{Iw(v),1}U_{Iw(v),2} and U_{Kli(v),2}; K_p(I) = ∏_{v∈I}Kli(v)∏_{v∉I}Iw(v), e(I) = ∏_{v∈I}e_irreg∏_{v∉I}e_reg. Proposition 2.4.24: let π be ordinary p-distinguished of weights k ≥ l ≥ 2 with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v, β_v) (or {α_v, β_v} if l = 2), and assume k > l > 3 or l = 2. (1) If k > l > 3, or l = 2 and k > 2, π is an irreducible principal series. (2) If k = l = 2, π is of Roberts–Schmidt type Va if {α_v, β_v} = {1, −1}, IIIa if α_vβ_v = 1, IIa if #({α_v, β_v} ∩ {1, −1}) = 1, and otherwise an irreducible unramified principal series. In all cases π is generic and L(π) contains no other ordinary representation; if k > l > 3, dim e_reg π^{Iw(v)} = 1 with U_{Iw(v),i}-eigenvalues 1, α_v, α_vβ_v; if l = 2, dim e_reg π^{Iw(v)} = 2 with eigenvalues 1, α_v, α_vβ_v and 1, β_v, α_vβ_v, and dim e_irreg π^{Kli(v)} = 1 with U_{Kli(v),i}-eigenvalues 1, α_v + β_v, α_vβ_v. Definition 2.4.25: a cuspidal π with central character |·|^2 and weight (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞} is ordinary if every π_v, v | p, is ordinary of weights k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2. Proposition 2.4.26: for such π, fix p-adic units (α_v, β_v)_{v|p} with k_v > l_v > 3 or (l_v = 2 and α_v ≠ β_v) at each v | p, and let I ⊂ I′ = {v | p : l_v = 2}; then π is ordinary with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v, β_v)_{v|p} iff (⊗_{v|p}π_v)^{K_p(I)} contains a vector with U_{Iw(v),i}-eigenvalues 1, α_v, α_vβ_v for v ∉ I and U_{Kli(v),i}-eigenvalues 1, α_v + β_v, α_vβ_v for v ∈ I, and then dim e(I)(⊗_{v|p}π_v)^{K_p(I)} = 2^{#(I′−I)}. The note after it: if π is ordinary with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v, β_v)_{v|p} and v ∉ I′, the U_{Kli(v),1}-eigenvalue is not α_v + β_v but, up to the ordering of α_v and β_v, α_v + p^{l_v−2}β_v.

Layer 5: Taylor–Wiles places (§§2.4.27–2.4.31). Proposition 2.4.28: for characters χ_{v,1}, χ_{v,2} of k(v)^× and χ_v(a, b, cb^{−1}, ca^{−1}) = χ_{v,1}(ab^{−1})χ_{v,2}(abc^{−1}), if π is irreducible smooth with (π^{Iw_1(v)})^{χ_v} ≠ 0, then det(X − rec_{GT,p}(π)(σ)) = ∏_{i=1,2}(X − χ_{v,i}(Art^{−1}σ))(X − χ_{v,i}(Art^{−1}σ)^{−1}) for σ ∈ I_{F_v}, and dim(π^{Iw_1(v)})^{χ_v} = 1 if χ_{v,1}^{±1}, χ_{v,2}^{±1} are pairwise distinct. Proposition 2.4.30: let q_v ≡ 1 mod p, and let m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2} be the kernel of the map O[T(F_v)/T(O_{F_v})_1] → F̄_p induced by the character sending T(O_{F_v}) and β_{v,0} to 1, β_{v,1} to ᾱ_1 and β_{v,2} to ᾱ_1ᾱ_2. If π is irreducible smooth with central character |·|^2, (π^{Iw_1(v)})_{m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2}} ≠ 0 and ᾱ_1^{±1}, ᾱ_2^{±1} are pairwise distinct, then rec_{GT,p}(π) = γ_1 ⊕ γ_2 ⊕ ε^2γ_2^{−1} ⊕ ε^2γ_1^{−1} with γ̄_i = λ_{ᾱ_i}, and T(k(v)) acts on the localization through (γ_i∘Art_{F_v})|_{O^×_{F_v}}. Equivalently, rec_{GT,p}(π ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}) = γ′_1 ⊕ γ′_2 ⊕ ε^{−1}γ′_2^{−1} ⊕ ε^{−1}γ′_1^{−1} with γ′_i = γ_i·(|·|^{−3/2}∘Art_{F_v}^{−1}). Each γ′_i agrees with γ_i on inertia and has γ̄′_i = λ_{cᾱ_i}, where c ∈ {±1} is the image modulo λ of the fixed q_v^{3/2}; the T(k(v))-action is unchanged. This twisted form, with its sign, is the one exported to consumers; the proof of Theorem 7.9.4 uses it. Remark 2.4.31 gives the same for Δ_v. The 2025 paper's torus-character ideal at q ≡ 1 mod p (§7.4.5, with β_0 ↦ 1, β_1 ↦ α_1, β_2 ↦ α_1α_2) joins this layer, with a proved comparison to m_{ᾱ_1,ᾱ_2}.

Layer 6: monodromy and parahoric vectors. For irreducible π_v, n(π_v) is the rank of the monodromy operator of rec_GT(π_v) (§2.3). From Roberts–Schmidt, Table A.15, as used in the proof of Corollary 8.2.2: for irreducible π_v with π_v^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0, n(π_v) ≥ 1 iff π_v^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} = 0; n(π_v) ≥ 2 iff π_v^{GSp_4(O_{F_v})} = π_v^{Par(v)} = 0; n(π_v) = 3 iff π_v^{Kli(v)} = π_v^{Si(v)} = 0. The 'only if' directions hold for every irreducible π_v. The paramodular group Par(l^n) of level n (the 2025 paper's §7.5, with unit multiplier), and the paramodular level N_{π_l}, the least n with (π_l)^{Par(l^n)} ≠ 0. The 2025 paper's Proposition 7.5.1(1)–(3) join this layer. Let π be cuspidal of general type on GSp_4 over Q with central character |·|^2. Then the L-packet of π_l contains exactly one paramodular representation, its generic member (Schmidt 2018, Theorem 1.1). If π_l is generic, (π_l)^{Par(l^{N_{π_l}})} is one-dimensional (Roberts–Schmidt, Theorem 7.5.1). And N_{π_l} is the conductor of rec_GT(π_l) (Johnson-Leung–Roberts–Schmidt, Theorem 2.3.5).

Layer 7: archimedean parameters and weights (§2.6). φ_{w,n}: W_R → GL_2(C) and φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)}: W_R → GSp_4(C) (m_1 > m_2 ≥ 0) are as on arXiv p. 32. det φ_{w,n} is |z|^{2w} if n is odd and sgn·|z|^{2w} if n is even, and the GL_2(R) and GL_2(C) representations with parameter φ_{w,n} are cohomological iff n > 0 and w ∈ Z with w + n odd. For the antidiagonal J, the similitude of φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)}(j) is (−1)^{m_1+m_2+1}. Composed into GL_4(C) through the embedding of §2.2, φ_{(w;m_1,m_2)} becomes φ_{w,m_1+m_2} ⊕ φ_{w,m_1−m_2}. Its L-packet is {π^H, π^W}, holomorphic and generic; up to twist these are discrete series if m_2 > 0 and non-degenerate limits of discrete series if m_2 = 0. They have central character a ↦ a^w and are tempered when w = 0, and π^H has minimal K-type det^{m_2+2} ⊗ Sym^{m_1−m_2−1}C^2 of U(2) (after Schmidt, Rocky Mountain J. Math. 47 (2017)). In general the GSp_4(C)-parameter is not recovered from the GL_4(C)-parameter: the GL_4(C)-representation of φ_{(0;1,0)} preserves two symplectic forms whose similitudes differ by sgn. So the similitude stays part of the data. π has weight (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞} if k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2, k_v ≡ l_v mod 2 and π_v lies in the packet of φ_{(2;k_v−1,l_v−2)}; parallel weight 2 is (2,2) everywhere; GL_2 weight 0 means φ_{0,1} at every v | ∞. Lemma 2.6.1: (1) Ind_{W_C}^{W_R}φ_{w,n} and (2) φ_{(w;n,0)} composed into GL_4(C) are conjugate to φ_{w,n} ⊕ φ_{w,n}; (3) if ϕ: W_C → GL_2(C) has Ind_{W_C}^{W_R}ϕ conjugate to φ_{w,n} ⊕ φ_{w,n} and n ≠ 0, then ϕ ≅ φ_{w,n} or ϕ is the scalar parameter z ↦ |z|^wz^n|z|^{−n} or z ↦ |z|^wz^{−n}|z|^n; (4) if ϕ, ϕ′: W_R → GL_2(C) have ϕ ⊕ ϕ′ conjugate to φ_{w,n} ⊕ φ_{w,n} and n ≠ 0, then ϕ ≅ ϕ′ ≅ φ_{w,n}. Also planned here, for the re-pointed items: the archimedean L-packets of GSp_4(R) as Pilloni and Calegari–Geraghty use them. Also the infinitesimal character of the transfer of π_∞ to GL_4(R) through the spin representation (Calegari–Geraghty, after Sorensen): (λ_1, λ_2; λ_0) goes to ((λ_1+λ_2+λ_0)/2, (λ_1−λ_2+λ_0)/2, (−λ_1+λ_2+λ_0)/2, (−λ_1−λ_2+λ_0)/2). And the 2025 paper's weight and ordinarity normalization (§1.8.12): π_v has infinitesimal character −λ_v − ρ, and ordinarity is defined by a Jacquet-module character of valuation −λ_w, normalized to be unit-valued as in its Remark 1.8.15. Prove a dictionary from it to (k_v, l_v) and to §2.4.23; the 2025 paper writes regular weights as (k_v, l_v; 2) and its weight 2 as (1, 1; 2).

Layer 8: Galois representations (§2.7). Theorem 2.7.1: let F be totally real and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GSp_4(A_F) of weight (k_v, l_v)_{v|∞}, where k_v ≥ l_v > 2 and k_v ≡ l_v mod 2 for all v | ∞, with central character |·|^2, and fix a prime p. Then there is a continuous semisimple ρ_{π,p}: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) with (1) ν∘ρ_{π,p} = ε^{−1}; (2) for each finite v, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2})^{ss}, and if ρ_{π,p} is irreducible, WD(ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec_{GT,p}(π_v ⊗ |ν|^{−3/2}); (3) if v | p, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights ((k_v+l_v)/2 − 1, (k_v−l_v)/2 + 1, −(k_v−l_v)/2, 2 − (k_v+l_v)/2); (4) if ρ_{π,p} is irreducible, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is pure for each finite v. Theorem 2.7.2: under the same hypotheses, with p > 2 split completely in F (the standing hypotheses of §2.4, under which ordinarity is defined), assume moreover that π_v is unramified at all v | p and π is ordinary with ordinary Hecke parameters (α_v, β_v)_{v|p}. Then there is a continuous semisimple ρ_{π,p}: G_F → GSp_4(Q̄_p) with (1), (4), (2) at every v ∤ p, and (3): for v | p, ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is isomorphic to an upper-triangular representation with diagonal λ_{α_v}ε^{(k_v+l_v)/2−2}, λ_{β_v}ε^{(k_v−l_v)/2}, λ_{β_v}^{−1}ε^{−1−(k_v−l_v)/2}, λ_{α_v}^{−1}ε^{1−(k_v+l_v)/2}. Proofs: Mok's Theorem 3.5 (GL_4-valued), Bellaïche–Chenevier's Corollary 1.3 (pairing), Caraiani (purity), Geraghty's Lemma 2.32 with Proposition 2.4.6 (ordinary shape). Both theorems carry the conditional status of Arthur's multiplicity formula recorded at ML.0 and ML.4. The 2025 paper's Theorem 1.8.13 statements (p split completely in F; conventions as here, with (1.8.14) corrected) join this layer beside Theorems 2.7.1–2.7.2. So does its Proposition 7.5.1(4): if π is regular algebraic of general type over Q with central character |·|^2 and ρ_{π,p} is irreducible, then for every prime l the paramodular level N_{π_l} is the conductor of ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{Q_l}} (from (2) and Layer 6). The re-pointed statements need more than Theorems 2.7.1–2.7.2, so this layer also plans it. They are Pilloni's Theorem 5.1.7.1(2)–(5) with Remark 5.1.7.1, Calegari–Geraghty's Proposition 6.8 with the conjugation of R_p into GSp_4 for simple generic π, and Sorensen's Corollaries 1 and 3 and §4.5 (Doc. Math. 15 (2010)). What they need: (a) the construction over Q for π of discrete-series weight whose central character is an algebraic power of |·| times a finite-order character, the multiplier then carrying that character; (b) crystallinity at v | p when π_v is unramified, with the characteristic polynomial of crystalline Frobenius given by the Hecke polynomial as those sources state it (from Mok's Theorem 3.5 and the GL_4 crystalline comparison of AG2.6); (c) Sorensen's parahoric-level compatibility as those items use it, from (2) and Layers 5–6; (d) the conversions between (k_v, l_v) and the weights of Pilloni (λ_1, λ_2; c), Calegari–Geraghty (a, b) and the 2025 paper.

Layer 9: GSp_4 transfers. Mok's Proposition 4.13 (Compos. Math. 150 (2014)) is stated exactly from Mok. As used in Corollary 7.9.6 (arXiv p. 221) and Theorem 8.4.1 (p. 248), it gives the following. Let π be cuspidal of general type on GSp_4(A_F), of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2. Then there are a solvable extension of totally real fields F′/F and an automorphic representation Π of GSp_4(A_{F′}). F′/F is linearly disjoint from a given finite extension, p splits completely in F′, and F′ satisfies the local conditions at finitely many places imposed in those proofs. Π has parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 and is holomorphic at every infinite place. For every finite w | v, rec_{GT,p}(Π_w) = rec_{GT,p}(π_v)|_{W_{F′_w}}, and Π_w^{Iw(w)} ≠ 0 for every finite w. The choice of those local conditions belongs to AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity. At p. 248 they are: ρ̄ trivial on G_{F′_w}, unipotent ramification and q_w ≡ 1 mod p^2 at the relevant w ∤ p. Corollary 7.9.6 also needs the condition of Hypothesis 7.8.1(4)(a), a recorded gap. Roberts' Theorem 8.6 (Doc. Math. 6 (2001)) is stated with its own hypotheses. As used for Theorem 9.2.8: let K/F be a quadratic extension of totally real fields and 𝛑 cuspidal on GL_2(A_K) of weight 0 with trivial central character, not isomorphic to its Gal(K/F)-conjugate (in Theorem 9.2.8 this holds because ρ̄_q restricted to G_{F″} is irreducible). Then there is π on GSp_4(A_F) of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 whose transfer to GL_4 in the sense of §2.9 is the automorphic induction of 𝛑 ⊗ |·|. Hence a semisimple Galois representation matching π at almost all places, such as ρ_{π,q}, is Ind_{G_K}^{G_F}ρ_{𝛑,q}, and π is ordinary above q when 𝛑 is q-ordinary and unramified there (the paper's 'by construction'). The 2025 paper's solvable descent, Proposition 7.5.3(2)–(3), joins this layer. Let ρ: G_Q → GSp_4(Q̄_p) have multiplier ε^{−1}. Suppose either (2) F/Q is solvable Galois and CM, ρ|_{G_F} is irreducible and ρ|_{G_F} ≅ r_{π_F,p} ⊗ ε for a RACSDC π_F on GL_4/F; or (3) F^+/Q is solvable Galois and totally real, ρ|_{G_{F^+}} is irreducible and ρ|_{G_{F^+}} ≅ ρ_{π_{F^+},p} for a regular algebraic cuspidal π_{F^+} on GSp_4/F^+ with central character |·|^2. Then ρ ≅ ρ_{π,p} for a regular algebraic cuspidal π on GSp_4/Q with central character |·|^2. The proof uses ML.4's descent from GL_4 and imported solvable descent for GL_4. Its part (1), a statement about GL_4 alone, stays with its current owner.
