- ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.0, ML.4, ML.5.
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M0 and Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D5, for GSp_4 with ν, its root datum and Weyl group; this Part II adds only the conversion to the normalizations of §§2.4 and 2.6.
- Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.3 (the parahorics and Iw_1(v)), RG2.4 (double cosets), RG2.5 (the dual group GSpin_5 ≅ GSp_4).
- Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) Layer 9: pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes over ℤ.
- Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.0–SR.4, with Propositions 2.4.2–2.4.4, Satake, and the q ≡ 1 Iwahori–Hecke fact that Lemma 2.4.33 specializes.
- Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: parahoric centers (SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, proposed, not yet in the atlas), for the Bernstein presentation and centre. If that proposal is not accepted, the general Bernstein presentation and centre go to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1/SR.4 as a source, and this Part II still plans only the GSp_4 instance.
- GL₂ Automorphic Representations And Transfer (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer) R16.2–R16.3, with Lemma 2.4.15.
- Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.6.
- Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms) MP.3, MP.5, for Roberts' lift.
- Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.2–AL.4.
- Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations) R01.2; R01.3 for conductors (Layers 6 and 8); and G7 for §2.2 (the embedding {(A,B) : det A = det B} ⊂ GSp_4, inductions) and Lemmas 2.1.3 and 8.3.1.
- Automorphic Galois Representations PartII (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII) AG2.0–AG2.6, with purity of Weil–Deligne representations at AG2.5 and the crystalline comparison at AG2.6.
- P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory) R06.3–R06.4.
- Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.3.
- Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.0–AF.4.
- Adelic algebraic groups and arithmetic quotients (AdelicAlgebraicGroups) AA.0–AA.2.
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies) L0a, for ordinary projectors.

Not here. Theorem 2.7.3 and Corollary 7.9.6 need parallel weight 2, reached only through Hilbert–Siegel p-adic families, so they belong to Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular (AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity).

Consumers (never imported here):
- AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity.
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory), for Layer 4 and Remark 2.4.18.
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes), for T_{v,i}, Q_v and Layer 7 (π^H and the weights).
- Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting).
- Modularity of abelian surfaces (AbelianSurfacesModularity).
Re-point here the GSp_4-specific items that the Calegari–Geraghty (2020), Pilloni (2020) and 2025 extractions sent to GL_n-only or general layers:
- From AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII: Mok's Theorem 3.5; Calegari–Geraghty's Proposition 6.8 and its conjugation of R_p into GSp_4 for simple generic π; Sorensen's Corollaries 1 and 3 and §4.5; Pilloni's Theorem 5.1.7.1(2)–(5) with Remark 5.1.7.1.
- From SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups: GSp_4 Hecke parameters and parahoric vectors; Genestier–Tilouine's Proposition 3.2.3; the paramodular level; and the 2025 paper's Iwahori–Hecke statements at q ≡ 1 mod p (the §7.4.5 torus-character ideal, the §7.4 presentation and regular-orbit separation, the §7.4.12 spherical-to-Iwahori projection).
- From IHG.3: the spinor polynomial, and the 2025 paper's Q_ℓ, dual-spin P_ℓ and §1.8.28.
- From ML.0/ML.4: the archimedean L-packet of GSp_4(R) and the infinitesimal character of the transfer of π_∞ to GL_4(R).
- From AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups: the 2025 paper's weight and ordinarity normalization (§1.8.12).
- From EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison: the 2025 paper's Proposition 7.5.3(2)–(3).

routes.title: Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes
routes.brief:
This entry joins Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes). That is the Part II that PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 proposes and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20, PAPER-PILLONI-20 and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 join, under the same id, parent (Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, AutomorphicBundles) and title. The design job merges the five briefs. The layers stay those of the Calegari–Geraghty briefs: 1–4 from 2018 and 5–8 from 2020.

Source: Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni, "Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular", Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021):
- §§3.9–3.10 (arXiv:1812.09269v3 pp. 62–67 and 70–73; published pp. 226–232 and 236–240);
- the uses of Lan's Theorem 8.6 in §4.2.30 (arXiv p. 94; published p. 265) and §6.2.1 (arXiv p. 143; published pp. 325–326).

The paper adds the totally real case: F totally real, p totally split, G_1 = Res_{F/Q}GSp_4, K reasonable. The following come from Hilbert Modular Varieties And Shimura Curves, Part II: Hilbert–Siegel modular varieties for GSp_4 over a totally real field (HilbertSiegelModularVarieties): X_K and X_K^{G_1} with boundary D, ω^κ, the maps [g] and the Ekedahl–Oort filtration.

Results as printed, with corrections.
- Definitions 3.9.1–3.9.2. S is Noetherian and X, Y are S-schemes.
  - A correspondence is X ←p_2− C −p_1→ Y, with X, Y, C of the same pure relative dimension over S and p_1, p_2 projectively embeddable.
  - A cohomological correspondence from a coherent F on X to a coherent G on Y adds a map T: R(p_1)_*p_2^*F → G, equivalently p_2^*F → p_1^!G. It induces RΓ(X,F) → RΓ(C,p_2^*F) = RΓ(Y,R(p_1)_*p_2^*F) → RΓ(Y,G).
- §3.9.3. H^p = C_c^∞(G_1(A^{p,∞})//K^p, Z_p) and g ∈ G_1(A^{∞,p}).
  - [KgK] comes from X_K ←p_2− X_{K∩gKg^{−1}} −p_1→ X_K. Here p_2 is [g] followed by the map from K∩g^{−1}Kg ⊂ K (printed K∩gKg^{−1} ⊂ K).
  - It is built from three pieces: p_2^*ω^κ ≅ p_1^*ω^κ; a fundamental class p_1^*O → p_1^!O extending the trace of p_1 on the interior; and the adjunction trace R(p_1)_*p_1^! → Id.
  - The fundamental class exists because, for a cofinal set of cone decompositions, X_K and X_{K∩gKg^{−1}} are lci and smooth outside codimension 2.
  - It is defined likewise for ω^κ(−D), and on X_K^{G_1}.
  - Remark 3.9.4: over Q_p, products in H^p are respected, by Harris (J. Differential Geom. 32 (1990), Prop. 2.6). So H^p acts on the torsion-free part.
- Proposition 3.9.15, assuming K_p = ∏_{v|p}GSp_4(Z_p): "The Hecke algebra H^p acts on RΓ(X^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D)) and also on RΓ(X^{G_1}, ω^κ)". Remark 3.9.16 extends this to composites across tame levels.
- §3.10. S ⊃ S_p is finite, with K_v = GSp_4(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S, and T̃ = ⊗_{v∉S}O[GSp_4(F_v)//GSp_4(O_{F_v})]. A maximal ideal m is non-Eisenstein if two conditions hold:
  - T̃/m is finite over F_p;
  - for (any) T̃/m ↪ F̄_p, some irreducible ρ̄: G_F → GSp_4(F̄_p) has det(X − ρ̄(Frob_v)) ≡ X^4 − T_{v,1}X^3 + (q_vT_{v,2} + (q_v^3+q_v)T_{v,0})X^2 − q_v^3T_{v,0}T_{v,1}X + q_v^6T_{v,0}^2 (mod m) for all v ∉ S.
- Theorem 3.10.1. Let κ = (k_v,l_v)_{v|∞} with k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2 and k_v ≡ l_v (mod 2), and let m be non-Eisenstein.
  - (1) For i = 0, 1 there is an Ē[GSp_4(A_F^∞)//K]-equivariant inclusion ⊕_π(π^∞)^K_m ⊗ Ē ⊆ H^i(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2}_m ⊗ Ē (3.10.2).
    - Here |·|^2 means the diamond operators at v ∉ S act by |·|^2.
    - π runs over the cuspidal automorphic representations of GSp_4(A_F) of weight κ and central character |·|^2 that are holomorphic at every v|∞ with l_v > 2 and non-holomorphic at exactly i infinite places.
  - (2) There is an absolute constant R such that (3.10.2) is an equality if, for each v|∞, k_v − l_v > R and either l_v = 2 or l_v > R.
  - (3) For i = 0, (3.10.2) is an equality. Without localizing, there is an Ē[GSp_4(A_F^∞)//K]-equivariant isomorphism H^0(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2} ⊗ Ē = ⊕_π(π^∞)^K (3.10.3). Here π runs over the cuspidal π of weight κ and central character |·|^2 that are holomorphic at all infinite places.
- Corollary 3.10.5. Assume the hypothesis of (2), and let l_0 = #{v|∞ : l_v = 2}. Then dim_Ē H^1(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2}_m ⊗ Ē = l_0·dim_Ē H^0(X_K^{G_1}, ω^κ(−D))^{|·|^2}_m ⊗ Ē.
- Lemma 3.10.7. For κ and m as above, H^0(D, ω^κ)_m ⊗ Ē = 0.
  - The proof contains a recorded misprint that affects nothing (arXiv p. 72; published p. 238, identical).
  - Read [1,1,ϖ_v,ϖ_v] ↦ [1,1,ϖ_v,ϖ_v] + [1,ϖ_v,1,ϖ_v] + [ϖ_v,1,ϖ_v,1] + [ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1,1] = ([1,1,ϖ_v,ϖ_v] + [1,ϖ_v,1,ϖ_v]) + [ϖ_v,1,1,ϖ_v^{−1}]([1,1,ϖ_v,ϖ_v] + [1,ϖ_v,1,ϖ_v]).
  - The printed sum lists [1,ϖ_v,1,ϖ_v] twice and omits [1,1,ϖ_v,ϖ_v]. Each bracket of its second line repeats one term.
  - Like the paper, this omits the powers of q_v in the Satake normalization.
- Conditionality. The printed proofs use Arthur's multiplicity formula (m_cusp(π) = m_(2)(π) = 1), Lemma 2.9.1 and Theorem 2.9.3. All three are conditional, as recorded at Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.0 and ML.4.
  - (1) as printed needs only m_cusp(π) ≥ 1.
  - With each (π^∞)^K counted m_cusp(π) times, (2) and (3) hold unconditionally.
    - Under the hypothesis of (2), every contributing π_∞ is essentially tempered (Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan, proof of Thm. 4.2.3).
    - In degree 0, every contributing π_∞ is a holomorphic (limit of) discrete series, so it is tempered. Harris's Prop. 2.7.2 also gives cuspidality directly.
    - So Wallach's theorem gives m_(2)(π) = m_cusp(π), and Harris's two inclusions coincide.
  - Only the multiplicity-free forms as printed, and Corollary 3.10.5, use Arthur's results. State both forms, as Pilloni's brief does for its degree-0 display.

Additions, by layer.

Layer 3.
- Prove Definitions 3.9.1–3.9.2 to be a case of the layer's notion: the coherent case, with equidimensional and projectively embeddable legs. The layer's notion is Pilloni's Definition 4.3.1(2) and Remark 4.3.2, the discrete case of Boxer–Pilloni's solid notion.
- §3.9.3 and Remark 3.9.4 are instances of the layer's integral Hecke operators and of its characteristic-zero action of G_1(A_f^p).
- Plan Lemma 3.9.13 in general, beside Boxer–Pilloni's Proposition 2.9.9.
  - Take a filtration of X in which each Z_i∖Z_{i+1} → X is affine and is set-theoretically cut out in X∖Z_{i+1} by i Cartier divisors, with a cofinal system of lci thickenings.
  - Take a correspondence with p_1^{−1}(Z_i∖Z_{i+1}) = p_2^{−1}(Z_i∖Z_{i+1}). Along its p_1, local regular sequences must pull back to regular sequences, so that p_1^* = Lp_1^* on the thickenings. The paper asserts this without comment.
  - Use p_1^!RHom(O_Z, F) = RHom(Lp_1^*O_Z, p_1^!F) (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, Prop. III.8.8). It comes from Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) A0-extension, where the paper's Lemma 3.8.10 is its one-divisor case.
  - Conclude that the correspondence induces a correspondence of Cousin complexes, compatible with the augmentation. Read g ∈ G_1(A_f^p) (printed G(A_f^p)).
  - State the resulting principle for correspondences that are finite flat over the interior, not only finite étale. The principle has three steps: the Cousin correspondence, an injection into the interior complex, and relations checked on the interior.
  - Then Lemma 4.2.36 of Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory) is an instance. There the operators T_w and T_{w,1} at p act on the Cousin complex of the p-rank strata.
- The Hecke relations on RΓ remain one statement, as Pilloni's brief asks.
  - They hold on the interior, where the prime-to-p correspondences are finite étale.
  - The passage to the compactification needs Lan's theorem. So Proposition 3.9.11, Lemma 3.9.12 and the relations derived from them (Proposition 3.9.15, Remark 3.9.16) are stated in layer 5, after Lan's theorem.
  - Definitions 3.9.1–3.9.2, §3.9.3 and the general Lemma 3.9.13 stay here. There is no cycle, because Lan's theorem uses nothing from layer 3.

Layer 4.
- Integrally, the relations are proved only at hyperspecial level (layer 5). So define H^i_m ⊗ Ē at every reasonable level, as Pilloni's brief asks: take the generalized eigenspaces of the characteristic-zero action whose eigenvalues are p-integral.
- State T̃ and the non-Eisenstein ideals once, over any totally real F.
- Pilloni's extraction sends two statements to Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.3, which plans only GL_n. Re-point both:
  - The GSp_4 Hecke polynomial goes to Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: GSp_4, its local Langlands correspondence and Galois representations (GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations). That brief already takes the spinor polynomial.
  - The maximal ideal m_ρ̄ comes to this layer.
  - Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting) records the equivalence 'Definition 6.11 ⇔ m = m_ρ̄'. It then cites this layer instead of IHG.3.
- Pilloni's m_ρ̄ is the case F = Q, after the following dictionary.
  - Here T_{v,1} = [diag(ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1,1)] and T_{v,2} = [diag(ϖ_v^2,ϖ_v,ϖ_v,1)]. They are Pilloni's T_{ℓ,2} and T_{ℓ,1}, and T_{v,0} is his T_{ℓ,0}.
  - Q_v(X) = X^4·Q_ℓ(1/X). This paper uses det(X − ρ̄(Frob_v)) and Pilloni uses det(1 − Xρ̄(Frob_ℓ)), both with geometric Frobenius. So as ideals of the abstract Hecke algebra, the two conditions agree.
  - On cohomology the two conventions differ. Pilloni's operators are ℓ^{−3} and ℓ^{−6} times the geometric ones, with the twist of his Remark 5.3.1. The [K^pgK^p] of §3.9.3 carry no normalization on the |·|^2 part.
  - So one eigensystem matches ρ̄ in one convention and ρ̄ twisted by a power of ε̄ in the other. Prove the conversion.

Layer 5.
- Lan's Theorem 8.6 (IMRN 2017).
  - Proposition 3.9.11 needs it for ω^κ(−D) on X_K at K_p = G_1(Z_p), modulo p^n.
  - Two further uses stay in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory:
    - §4.2.30 (Proposition 4.2.33), on X_K^{G_1} modulo p and over opens of the minimal compactification;
    - §6.2.1, for the cuspidal sheaves on the formal models of §6.
  - §4.2.30 applies Lan's theorem to X^{G_1} without comment, but Lan states it for PEL toroidal compactifications.
    - X_K^{G_1} is the quotient of X_K by Δ. Δ acts freely on X_K (Proposition 3.5.4) but may fix boundary points of the minimal compactification.
    - On the generic fibre, the X_K^{G_1} case follows by taking Δ-invariants.
    - Modulo p^n it needs its own proof: either Lan's local computation on X_K^{G_1}, or the case where the orders of these stabilizers are prime to p.
  - Lemma 3.10.7 needs π_*O = O, π_*I_D = I_{∂X^*} and R^1π_*I_D = 0 for π: X_K^{G_1} → X_K^{*,G_1}, on the generic fibre only. It needs them at every level K at which Theorem 3.10.1 is applied, Klingen and Iwahori level at p included.
- Then prove the relations on RΓ at K_p hyperspecial, in this order.
  - Proposition 3.9.11. Ekedahl–Oort Cousin complexes compute RΓ(X_n, ω^κ(−D)), by Kempf's theorem from Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.2. The paper uses two facts about the pulled-back filtration without stating either. Import both from HilbertSiegelModularVarieties, with the filtration:
    - codim_{X_n}(Z_i) ≥ i, which that roadmap already plans;
    - no component of any Z_i∖Z_{i+1} lies inside D, which that roadmap must add.
  - Lemma 3.9.12. The sections of these complexes inject into sections over the interior. Write out its one-line proof. Each term is a colimit of Koszul quotients of ω^κ(−D) along a stratum. The boundary equation is a non-zero-divisor on each term, because no component of the stratum lies in D.
  - Proposition 3.9.15 and Remark 3.9.16, by layer 3's Lemma 3.9.13. The ω^κ case follows by Serre duality, through the layer's transpose.
- Two cautions.
  - The "G_1 direct factor" step uses Proposition 3.8.3 of HilbertSiegelModularVarieties, which needs p ∤ #Δ(K^p) (a recorded error). Carry that hypothesis, or argue on X^{G_1} directly.
  - Integrally, Proposition 3.9.15 gives the relations only at K_p hyperspecial.
    - Yet Theorem 3.10.1 is applied at Klingen and Iwahori level (§§6.6, 7.8, 7.9, 7.13 and 8.2).
    - §§7.8–7.9 also use the T̃-action on the Hida complexes of Theorem 4.6.1.
    - Prove the RΓ relations at every reasonable level, in the form Pilloni's brief requests for HigherHidaAndColemanTheory's formal complexes. Otherwise, record the integral T̃-action at Klingen and Iwahori level as a gap for that roadmap.

Layer 6.
- Harris's comparison.
  - Harris's Theorem 2.7 (Perspect. Math. 11 (1990)) is Calegari–Geraghty's Theorem 5.2.
  - State it once, in Harris's generality, which covers X_K^{G_1}. Put it beside Boxer–Pilloni's Su theorem, and use interior cohomology H̄^i as the layer already defines it.
  - Harris's Prop. 2.7.2 (the π contributing to H^0 are cuspidal) goes with it.
  - This paper's P^− is Harris's 𝒫_h, Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan's Q^− and the Q of Calegari–Geraghty (2018). The joined briefs write Lie Q^−, and only the Lie algebra matters.
- The Künneth formula, needed for F ≠ Q: H^i(Lie P^−_∞, K^h_∞; ⊗_v(π_v ⊗ V_{κ_v})) = ⊕_{Σj_v = i} ⊗_v H^{j_v}(Lie P^−_v, K^h_v; π_v ⊗ V_{κ_v}).
  - Prove it on the relative Lie algebra cochains of Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1.
  - Theorem 3.10.1 takes from it the count of non-holomorphic places and the one-dimensionality. The F = Q briefs do not need it.
- Theorem 3.10.1(3), the isomorphism (3.10.3), uses neither boundary vanishing nor localization.
  - It is the totally real form, on the |·|^2 part, of the layer's degree-0 statement H^0(Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = ⊕π_f^K (r ≥ 2). That statement is Calegari–Geraghty's Theorem 5.2(1) in degree 0.
  - State it once, over F, with the same multiplicity treatment. Its localization is the case i = 0 of (3.10.2).

Layer 7. Over F, the π contributing at a non-Eisenstein m are of general type (Lemma 2.9.1), with l_0 choices of generic place. This packet count, which lies behind Corollary 3.10.5, generalizes Pilloni's Proposition 15.2.4.1.

Layer 8, in this order.
- First, Lemma 3.10.7.
  - It is the degree-0, totally real case of this layer's boundary vanishing: Calegari–Geraghty's (2020) vanishing of localized boundary cohomology, from the proof of their Lemma 7.10. It generalizes Pilloni's degree-0 boundary steps.
  - By Remark 3.10.6, the all-degree form rests on Harris–Zucker, whose hypotheses these varieties do not satisfy. So over F ≠ Q, state degree 0 only; Remark 3.10.4 calls the other degrees expected.
  - Its inputs:
    - The stratification ∂X^{*,G_1} = ∂_0X^* ⊔ ∂_1X^* into points and Hilbert modular varieties for Res_{F/Q}GL_2, with the adelic description of ∂_1X^* through P_W and M_W (dim_F W = 1). These are needed at every neat level, on the generic fibre. Import them from HilbertSiegelModularVarieties, as the Hilbert–Siegel instance of the rational boundary components and minimal compactification of Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C1–C2. That roadmap's design must add them.
    - Three statements planned here, as the Hilbert–Siegel form of Pilloni's step (i) on AutomorphicBundles B3's pushforward to the minimal compactification. In non-parallel weight, sections of ω^κ vanish on π^{−1}(∂_0X^*). π_*(ω^κ|_{π^{−1}(∂_1X^*)}) is zero unless the l_v are all equal, and is then ω^{(k_v)} (Lan (2013); Brasca–Rosso, Prop. 1.5.8). And H^0(∂_1X^*, π_*ω^{(k_v)}) = (Ind_{P_W(A^∞)}^{G_1(A^∞)}M)^K.
    - Koecher's principle for Hilbert modular forms.
    - The Satake transform H_{G_1} → H_{M_W}, as corrected above.
    - The Galois representations ρ_π ⊕ (ρ_π ⊗ χ) for every Hilbert modular form in H^0(∂_1X^*, ω^{(k_v)}), Eisenstein series included. The cuspidal ρ_π come from R19.2. The GL_1 factor χ comes from Hecke characters of F by class field theory, and so do the Eisenstein series, whose representations are sums of such characters.
    - The conclusion against the irreducible ρ̄, by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt.
  - For F = Q the paper cites Freitag IV, Satz 4.4, whose coverage Pilloni's brief asks to check.
- Next, replace H^i(ω^κ(−D))_m by interior cohomology for i ≤ 1. This is the case i ≤ 1 of Calegari–Geraghty's (2020) Lemma 7.10 (localized cohomology equals interior cohomology), which Pilloni's brief places in this layer. State it once.
- Then Theorem 3.10.1(1)–(2) and Corollary 3.10.5.
  - For F = Q they overlap Pilloni's Corollary 15.2.3.1 and Calegari–Geraghty's h^1 = h^0. The overlap of (3.10.3) is in layer 6.
  - Calegari–Geraghty prove h^1 = h^0 for all a ≥ 2, without R; keep that range.

Acceptance.
- For F = Q, the [K^pgK^p] of §3.9.3 agree with Calegari–Geraghty's (2018) T_γ and with Pilloni's T'_{ℓ,i}. The two non-Eisenstein conditions correspond under the twist of layer 4.

New imports:
- HilbertSiegelModularVarieties: as above, with Theorem 3.5.1, Propositions 3.5.4 and 3.8.3, and codim_{X_n}(Z_i) ≥ i. Its design must add two things: the position of the Ekedahl–Oort strata relative to D, and the boundary strata of X_K^{*,G_1}.
- GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations: T_{v,i} and Q_v(X), which also take Pilloni's GSp_4 Hecke polynomial.
- Galois representations attached to modular and Hilbert modular forms (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations) R19.2, for cuspidal Hilbert forms.
- Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory), layer 11 (global Artin reciprocity), for the Galois characters of Hecke characters of F.
- ShimuraCompactifications C6, for the Hilbert boundary strata and Koecher.
- Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions (AutomorphicSpectralTheory) AS.5, for Wallach.
- ML.0.

Already imported:
- SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2, for Kempf;
- AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension;
- Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1–SR.4;
- AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1, AF.3, AF.4;
- AutomorphicBundles B3;
- ShimuraCompactifications C1–C5;
- AS.4 and ML.4;
- Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations) R01.1 and R01.5, and The Chebotarev density theorem (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev), which Pilloni's brief brings.

D5 is to 'Define neatness with representation independence and the arithmetic subgroup attached to a compact open level' and to construct 'all Siegel data' with explicit examples. It already plans Definition 3.2.1 (item 36), whose prime-to-p variant for K^p ⊂ G_1(A^{∞,p}) should be instantiated there. It gets Lemma 7.8.3 (arXiv p. 212; published p. 409): an open compact K = ∏_vK_v ⊂ GSp_4(A_F^∞) with K_v = Iw_1(v) at some absolutely unramified place v of residue characteristic greater than 5 is neat. The proof: a root of unity ζ that is an eigenvalue of an element of Iw_1(v) has v(1 − ζ) ≥ 1/4, since the characteristic polynomial reduces to (X − 1)^4, while for ζ ≠ 1 either v(1 − ζ) = 0 or v(1 − ζ) ≤ 1/(l − 1) < 1/4. This is an explicit neatness criterion of the kind D5 records beside its examples; ShimuraVarieties V0 proves only that neat levels exist. The GSp_4 root datum in the paper's coordinates belongs to ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.5, which states the conversions to the coordinates that the Pilloni (2020) and Calegari–Geraghty (2020) extractions send here; D5 imports it and adds only what depends on the Siegel datum. Consumers: AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (the levels K_0^p(Q) and K_1^p(Q) of §§7.7–7.8 and Definition 7.13.4) and HilbertSiegelModularVarieties.

The paper states §2.4.1 for an arbitrary split reductive group ('It costs us nothing to recall these in a more general setting'). SR.1 must 'Construct compactly supported locally constant functions and convolution' and 'integral double-coset operators by finite correspondences'; SR.2 must build 'normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character'. They receive: the pro-v Iwahori Hecke algebra H_1 over O and Proposition 2.4.2 (multiplicativity of the double cosets on T(F_v)^+, their invertibility in H_1[1/p], and in H_1 if v ∤ p, and the resulting homomorphism T(F_v) → (H_1[1/p])^× twisted by δ_B^{1/2}, with kernel T(O_{F_v})_1, together with its Iwahori analogue E[X_*(T)] ↪ H[1/p]); Proposition 2.4.3 (Borel–Casselman: π^{Iw_1(v)} ≅ (π_U)^{T(O_{F_v})_1}); Proposition 2.4.4 (the semisimplified Jacquet module of a principal series); and the resulting criteria for constituents of tame and unramified principal series. Calegari–Geraghty (2020) already route Borel–Casselman here. The GSp_4 instances (Hecke parameters, the Bernstein presentation, Lemmas 2.4.33–2.4.37) stay with GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations, which imports these general statements (the GSp_4 Iwahori–Hecke calculations that the Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2025) extraction sends here belong there as well), as does AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity for Proposition 7.13.11. Recorded misprint: §2.4.1 (arXiv p. 20; published p. 174) defines Iw(v) and Iw_1(v) as kernels of G(O_{F_v}) → B(k(v)) and → U(k(v)); they are the preimages of B(k(v)) and U(k(v)). Sources to add: Casselman, Introduction to admissible representations of p-adic groups (Lemmas 4.1.1 and 4.1.5, Proposition 4.1.4, Theorem 6.3.5); Vignéras, Pro-p-Iwahori Hecke ring and supersingular representations (Math. Ann. 331, 2005), Corollary 1.

A4 is to 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration'. The Pilloni (2020) and Boxer–Pilloni (2026) extractions route Katz's canonical coordinates, its standard consequence, here, and this paper uses them in the proofs of Lemmas 4.5.4, 4.5.10 and 4.5.13. A4 gets: for A_0 ordinary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and every artinian deformation A/R, the bilinear form q(A/R; −, −) on T_pA_0 × T_pA_0^t with values in Ĝ_m(R), identifying the deformation space with the formal torus Hom(T_pA_0 ⊗ T_pA_0^t, Ĝ_m) of dimension g^2; the criterion for a homomorphism f_0 to lift; and the subtorus Hom(Sym^2 T_pA_0, Ĝ_m) of dimension g(g+1)/2 for a principal polarization. As the Pilloni (2020) extraction asks, it must state these for polarized ordinary abelian schemes in general, since the paper also works at paramodular level, where the chart is (X, pZ; Z, Y). The application at points of the formal schemes of §4.5, with its open questions at paramodular level and at points of p-rank one, belongs to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. Imports: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1–R07.2. Source already added by the Pilloni (2020) extraction: Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli (LNM 868, 1981).

R02.2 is to 'Prove restriction/corestriction identities and the precise descent consequences for finite extensions of number fields', and R02.4 to 'Prove the finite-module duality and exact sequence from the global class-field-theory and local-duality inputs'. The Allen et al. (2023) and Boxer–Calegari–Gee et al. (2025) extractions route square roots of characters and the Grunwald–Wang globalization of local characters here, and Tau Ceti's class field theory roadmap leaves Grunwald–Wang out. This paper uses both, in Theorem 8.5.2 and Lemma 9.2.7: (i) the obstruction to a square root of a finite-order character χ of G_F is a class in the 2-torsion of Br(F), trivial where χ is unramified and, for χ totally even, at the infinite places; so after a quadratic totally real extension, split at p, linearly disjoint from a given field and of local degree 2 where the class is nonzero, χ has a finite-order square root; (ii) such a square root can be twisted by a quadratic character to become trivial at a prescribed finite set of places (Artin–Tate, Chapter X, Theorem 5). The layer states both with the local conditions explicit. Consumer: AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity. Source to add: Artin–Tate, Class field theory (AMS Chelsea, 2009), Chapter X.

AF.1 defines '(g,K)-modules' and 'relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k),V)', AF.3 cusp forms and their square integrability, and AF.4 'algebraic highest weights, infinitesimal characters and cohomological representations'. The Calegari–Geraghty (2020) extraction routes the F = Q forms of this paper's archimedean inputs here, with the (q,K)-complex of the θ-stable parabolic, the positive system of GSp_4(R) and Harish-Chandra's parametrization. The proof of Theorem 3.10.1 (arXiv p. 73) needs, at each real place of F: (a) Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan (proof of Theorem 4.2.3, with Proposition 2.4.5): if the infinitesimal character is far enough from the root hyperplanes it does not lie on, π_∞ is essentially tempered, which through the Casselman–Osborne relation is the condition on κ in Theorem 3.10.1(2); (b) Mirković's theorem (Harris, Theorem 3.5) and Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan's Theorem 3.2.1: the (Lie P^−_v, K^h_v)-cohomology of π_v ⊗ V_{κ_v} with π_v essentially tempered vanishes except for the holomorphic discrete series (l_v > 2, degree 0) and the holomorphic and generic limits of discrete series (l_v = 2, degrees 0 and 1), where it is one-dimensional; (c) lowest-weight theory (Pitale–Schmidt): nonzero H^0 forces the holomorphic discrete series or its limit; then the Künneth formula over the real places. Consumer: IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (Theorem 3.10.1). Sources to add: Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan (Duke Math. J. 73, 1994); Harris (Perspect. Math. 11, 1990); Pitale–Schmidt, Bessel models for lowest weight representations of GSp(4,R) (IMRN 2009).

AS.4 is to 'Construct discrete cuspidal and residual subspaces' with 'the separation of residual and continuous terms', and AS.5 to compare 'relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms' with that of all smooth functions. Wallach's theorem belongs there: an automorphic representation occurring in the space of square-integrable automorphic forms whose archimedean component is essentially tempered is cuspidal. The Calegari–Geraghty (2020) extraction routes the same theorem to these stages. This paper applies it to GSp_4(A_F) over a totally real field with central character |·|^2: in Theorem 3.10.1(2) it turns the two inclusions of Harris's comparison into equalities, and with Clozel's lemma that an algebraic cuspidal Π has essentially tempered Π_∞ it gives cuspidality in Theorem 2.9.3. The layer should state it for a general reductive group with its central-character normalization, the Hilbert–Siegel case being an instance. Consumers: IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (Theorem 3.10.1) and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 (Theorem 2.9.3). Source to add: Wallach, On the constant term of a square integrable automorphic form (Monogr. Stud. Math. 18, 1984), Theorem 4.3.

R28.4 is to 'Derive semisimplicity of V_ℓ(A) and the comparison Hom_F(A,B)⊗Q_ℓ ≅ Hom_{G_F}(V_ℓ(A),V_ℓ(B))'. Serre's theorem, that for an abelian surface A over a number field F with End_C(A) = Z the image of ρ̄_{A,l} is GSp_4(F_l) for all sufficiently large l, starts from these results, but its proof goes beyond R28.4, and R28.6 explicitly avoids it. The paper uses it, with Lemma 7.5.15, in Lemma 9.2.2 to make ρ̄_{A,l} vast and tidy for a density-one set of l. The Calegari–Geraghty (2020) extraction proposes OpenImageTheoremsForAbelianVarieties, 'Faltings finiteness, semisimplicity and isogeny theorems, Part II: ℓ-adic and residual images of abelian varieties (Serre's open-image theorems)', for the same statement over Q. That proposal is the natural owner and should state the theorem over an arbitrary number field, as this paper needs; if it is accepted, the theorem belongs there, and R28.4 only supplies its inputs. Consumer: AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity. Source to add: Serre, Lettre à Marie-France Vignéras du 10/02/1987 (Collected Papers IV, 2000, 38–55).

R07.1 is to 'Develop Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences over the allowed bases, generic and special fibres, finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions, and fpqc descent'. The Pilloni (2020) extraction routes the rigidity of multiplicative groups and the unique lifting of homomorphisms to étale groups along nilpotent thickenings here. This paper uses the same input, without reference, for every Hecke operator at p of §4.5: for H finite locally free of multiplicative type over a scheme or p-adic formal scheme S and N finite locally free, Hom_S(H, N) = Hom_S(N^D, H^D) with H^D étale, so homomorphisms H → N lift uniquely along nilpotent thickenings and over completed local rings, and the vanishing locus of a homomorphism is open and closed. This makes open and closed the loci of the correspondences 𝔠_{w,1}(p^m), 𝔠_{Kli(w),1}(p^m) and 𝔠_{w,2,1}(p^m) where the kernel of the universal isogeny meets the multiplicative part trivially (§§4.5.1 and 4.5.6, Lemma 4.5.9). R07.1 must state rigidity over general bases; Tau Ceti has groups of multiplicative type only over a field. Consumer: HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. Source to add: SGA 3, Exposés IX–X.

L4 is to 'Prove continuity and compactness ..., nuclear/Fredholm determinants in the precise compact-operator setting, slope decompositions, and compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids'. As the Pilloni (2020) extraction asks, it must add the complex setting (§6.1.1, arXiv p. 139, and the proof of Theorem 6.3.16): over an affinoid algebra A of weight space, compact endomorphisms of perfect complexes of A-modules, meaning endomorphisms with a representative on a bounded complex of projective Banach A-modules that is compact in each degree; their characteristic series ∏_i det(1 − XŨ | M^i); and Coleman's local constancy of slope-zero dimensions (Coleman, §A5), used as in Pilloni §13.4. The paper is also a source for the slope decompositions of §6.1.1 (item 147), which L4 already plans. Recorded misprint: in the third condition of the paper's definition of an h-slope decomposition, 'whose roots all have valuation less than h' should read 'at most h', matching the second condition and Urban's definition of slope at most h (Ann. of Math. 174, §2.3.1), which gives uniqueness. PadicFamilies L2a builds the spectral variety of a complex on this. Consumer: HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (Theorem 6.3.16). Sources already added by the Pilloni (2020) extraction: Coleman, P-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms (Invent. Math. 127, 1997); Urban, Eigenvarieties for reductive groups (Ann. of Math. 174, 2011), §2.

R11.5 is to 'Prove Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich and the good/semistable Galois comparisons required here' and to 'Relate monodromy and component data to the characteristic-zero local Euler polynomial'. Proposition 2.8.1 (arXiv p. 36; published p. 194) extends exactly this to every finite place at once: for an abelian variety A over a number field and 0 ≤ i ≤ 2 dim A, the H^i(A_F̄, Q̄_l) form a strictly compatible system, pure of weight i and defined over Q, where strict compatibility includes the Weil–Deligne comparison at the places above l. The layer must prove it as the paper does: reduction to i = 1 by H^i = ∧^iH^1; Noot (2013, Cor. 2.7) away from l; Noot (2017, Cor. 2.2) at l for semistable A; the general case by Saito's base-change trick as in Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor (2014, Thm. 2.1); purity through Raynaud's 1-motives (1994, Thm. 4.2.2, Props. 4.6.1 and 4.7.4). Imports: PadicHodgeTheory R06.3 and R06.6, and R11.3. Definition 2.8.2 and Remark 2.8.3, the GSp_4 conventions for abelian surfaces, belong to AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity. Consumers: PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.1 (Λ_i(A,s) is well defined) and AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity. Recorded misprint: the statement prints '0 ≤ i ≤ 2 dim X' for 2 dim A, in both versions. Sources to add: Noot (Algebra Number Theory 7, 2013; J. Number Theory 172, 2017); Raynaud, 1-motifs et monodromie géométrique (Astérisque 223, 1994); Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, Local-global compatibility for l = p, II (Ann. Sci. ÉNS 47, 2014).

R21.2 imports Hida control and must 'Prove the additional nearly ordinary totally real ... control statements', 'specifying p-distinguishedness, tame characters'; the Newton–Thorne (2026) extraction routes Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty's ordinary lifts of Hilbert modular forms (in a form with a Steinberg place) here, with Hida families for Hilbert modular forms. This paper uses it in Proposition 10.1.3, Theorem 10.1.4 and Theorem 10.2.6: for E totally real, p ∈ {3, 5} unramified in E, and ϱ̄: G_E → GL_2(F̄_p) modular with determinant ε^{−1}, with ϱ̄|G_{E(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible and ϱ̄ restricted to inertia at each w | p an extension of ε^{−1} by 1, ϱ̄ arises from an ordinary Hilbert modular form of parallel weight 2 and trivial nebentypus (their Theorem A). The layer must state it with these exact hypotheses; for p = 5 the determinant condition and the unramifiedness of E at 5 are what exclude projective image A_5. Consumer: AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity. Source to add: Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty, Congruences between Hilbert modular forms: constructing ordinary lifts, II (Math. Res. Lett. 20, 2013).

S1 is to 'Extend the construction to the minimal compactification using the boundary/normalization construction of the source', and S3 to extend the Hodge–Tate period map 'to the compactification in the precise Hodge-type form provided by the source, distinguishing auxiliary normalized compactifications from the canonical minimal one'. The Pilloni (2020) extraction routes Scholze's finite-level Siegel models here; this paper needs their Hilbert–Siegel form (§6.2.1, arXiv pp. 144–145): an integer N such that for n ≥ N there are a normal admissible formal scheme 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)} and a projective map 𝔛^{*−mod}_{K(p^n)} → 𝔛^{*−HT}_{K(p^n)}, an isomorphism on generic fibres, to which det ω^mod descends as an ample invertible sheaf; and, for each ε > 0 and n ≥ n(ε), sections congruent modulo p^ε to ⊗_{v|p} HT(e_{v,i_v}) ∧ HT(e_{v,j_v}). The layer records 𝔛^{*−HT} as an auxiliary normalized model, importing 𝔛^{*−mod} and det ω^mod from HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T5. The affine opens cut out by these sections and Theorem 6.2.6 belong to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. Sources: Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties (Ann. of Math. 182, 2015), proof of Theorem 4.3.1, already a source; Pilloni–Stroh (Ann. Math. Qué. 40, 2016), Theorem 1.16, to add.

PA.5 ('Compatible systems and reusable transport') provides 'comparison lemmas for restriction to field extensions, tensor products, duals, characters and symmetric powers using the compatible-system owner', stating properties 'only where proved'. The Allen et al. (2023) and Boxer–Calegari–Gee et al. (2025) extractions route Lemmas 7.1.1–7.1.3 of Allen et al. here, and Lemma 9.1.10 is those lemmas for rank-two weakly compatible systems in this paper's §2.8 sense. The layer gets §9.1's definitions (irreducible on a density-one set of primes, strongly irreducible, weight 0, odd) and Lemma 9.1.10: (1) irreducibility of the system, of every r_λ and of some r_λ agree; (2) for an irreducible regular system, strong irreducibility and irreducibility of Sym^2 (of the system, of every or of some Sym^2 r_λ) agree, and otherwise the system is induced from a compatible system of characters of a quadratic extension; (3) large residual image. Recorded mistake in the paper (an error in a stated result): part (3) as printed, that the image of r̄_λ contains SL_2(O_M/λ), is false (a twist of a non-CM elliptic curve by a quartic character, with M = Q(i) and l ≡ 3 mod 4). Allen et al. Lemma 7.1.3 gives a conjugate of SL_2(F_l) in r̄_λ(G_{F̃}) for strongly irreducible systems, without regularity; state that. Its one use, the type B[C_2] case of Lemma 9.2.2, then needs a separate large-image argument in the real-multiplication subcase, which AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity must supply. Source already present: Allen et al., Potential automorphy over CM fields (Ann. of Math. 197, 2023), §7.1.

C3 is to 'Prove the structure-sheaf pushforward and the normality statements used to compare sections under refinements', and C5 builds the integral toroidal and minimal compactifications with 'the Hodge-line positivity'. The Pilloni (2020) and Calegari–Geraghty (2020) extractions route Koecher's principle for Siegel threefolds here, and C6 has it only for Hilbert modular varieties. This paper needs the Hilbert–Siegel case: the boundary of the minimal compactification of the Hilbert–Siegel variety has codimension at least 2 (by an analysis of the blow-up in the boundary charts), so sections of line bundles pulled back from the minimal compactification, such as ω^2, extend from the complement of the boundary; §8.2 (arXiv p. 240) uses this to compute its cohomology on good-reduction loci, and the paper also uses Koecher's principle on p. 72 and, as Lan's Theorem 8.7, on p. 141. The general Hartogs extension for normal schemes is imported from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0, where the Česnavičius, Gille–Parimala and Kisin–Pappas extractions route it, and its formal-scheme form from AdicSpacesPartII R2; this layer adds the codimension statement and its consequence for automorphic line bundles. Consumers: HilbertSiegelModularVarieties, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups (the extension of the Hodge–Tate map over the boundary) and AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (§8.2). Source to add: Lan, Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions (IMRN 2017), Theorem 8.7.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.4.20, the sentence that appeals to Proposition 2.4.17 (arXiv v3 p. 24; published p. 180, with the statement and the start of the proof on p. 179)
sourceIssues.printed: Comparing to Proposition 2.4.17, without loss of generality, we may rearrange the Hecke parameters of π so that we deduce the two equations α′_v + β′_v = α_v + β_v,  α′_v β′_v = α_v β_v,
sourceIssues.correction: Replace "Comparing to Proposition 2.4.17," with the following. The computation cited for Proposition 2.4.17, [GT05, Prop. 3.2.1, Cor. 3.2.2], needs no genericity. For every unramified character χ′, the operators U^naive_{Kli(v),i} act on the 4-dimensional space π(χ′)^{Kli(v)} by upper-triangular matrices in the basis (e_w), w ∈ W_{M_1}\W. Their diagonal entries are the four systems (q_v^{-2}, a+b, q_v^{-1}ab), one for each edge {a,b} of the square [α′_v, β′_v, q_v(β′_v)^{-1}, q_v(α′_v)^{-1}]. Taking Kli(v)-invariants is exact in characteristic 0, so π^{Kli(v)} is a Hecke-stable subquotient of π(χ′)^{Kli(v)}. Hence the given eigenvector has one of these four systems. Then continue with "hence, without loss of generality, we may rearrange ... α′_v + β′_v = α_v + β_v, α′_v β′_v = α_v β_v" as printed.
sourceIssues.reason:
Proposition 2.4.17 is stated only for a general unramified principal series. By Definition 2.4.11, "general" means that the four Hecke parameters are pairwise distinct and that no ratio of two of them is q_v. In the proof of Proposition 2.4.20, π is known only to be a constituent of some unramified principal series π(χ′) with parameters [α′_v, β′_v, q_v(β′_v)^{-1}, q_v(α′_v)^{-1}], and nothing forces π(χ′) to be general. It may be reducible. Then Proposition 2.4.17 says nothing about the constituent π, and the proof never addresses the passage from π(χ′) to π. It may also be irreducible, satisfy every hypothesis of 2.4.20, and still have repeated parameters. For example, q_v = 5 and α_v = β_v = 2 give the square {2, 2, 5/2, 5/2}. No ratio in it is 5, so the principal series is irreducible and satisfies 2.4.20, but it is not general, and there two different edges {2, 5/2} give the same eigensystem. So the step invokes Proposition 2.4.17 outside its hypotheses: it is asserted without adequate proof.

The step is true and fills in directly. The computation that the paper itself cites for 2.4.17, [GT05, Prop. 3.2.1, Cor. 3.2.2], is carried out for an arbitrary unramified character. In the basis (e_w) of π(χ′)^{Kli(v)} the Klingen operators are upper-triangular, with the four edge systems (q_v^{-2}, a+b, q_v^{-1}ab) on the diagonal. Kli(v)-invariants are exact on smooth representations in characteristic 0, so π^{Kli(v)} is a Hecke-stable subquotient of π(χ′)^{Kli(v)}. The invariant flag induces a flag on it whose graded pieces are subquotients of the one-dimensional diagonal pieces. So any simultaneous eigenvector in π^{Kli(v)} has one of the four edge systems. Matching u_{v,1} and u_{v,2} gives a+b = α_v+β_v and ab = α_vβ_v, so {a,b} = {α_v, β_v}. Since D_8 acts transitively on the edges of the square, the parameters can be rearranged so that {a,b} = {α′_v, β′_v}, which gives exactly the two equations the proof uses. The rest goes through unchanged: α′_v = α_v and β′_v = β_v up to reordering, so no ratio of the parameters of π(χ′) is q_v, and π(χ′) is irreducible by Proposition 2.4.6 and equals π. Proposition 2.4.20 is therefore true as stated, and only the justification of this one step is missing.

sourceIssues.reason:
The paragraph before (4.2.17) defines T'_w and T''_w on the ≤_w1 locus for l_w ≥ p+1. The T̃_w clause adds no bound on l_w, so it also claims both identities at l_w = p+1.

Lemma 4.2.19 gives T'_{w,m} = T'_{w,00} = 0 and T''_{w,m} = 0. Expanding the composite therefore gives T̃_w = T''_{w,et}∘T'_{w,et} + T''_{w,00}∘T'_{w,et}. However, Lemma 4.2.19 gives T''_{w,00} = 0 only for l_w ≥ p+2. [Pil20, Rem. 7.4.2.1(1)] records that at l_w = p+1 this piece (Pilloni's T_2^{oo}) does not vanish.

The printed argument for T_w does not carry over:
- For T_w = T'_w∘T''_w, the composite passes through X_{K'',1}^{=_w1}. That space splits into its 00 and m-et parts compatibly with p_2 by (4.2.17)–(4.2.18), so the cross terms vanish, and T'_{w,00} = 0 removes the rest.
- For T̃_w = T''_w∘T'_w, the composite passes through X_{K,1}^{=_w1}, which has no such splitting. At a point of p-rank 1, G_w[p] ≅ μ_p ⊕ E[p] ⊕ Z/p (E supersingular) has exactly one étale, one multiplicative and one α_p subgroup of order p. So all three components of X_{K',1}^{=_w1} lie over every point, and the term T''_{w,00}∘T'_{w,et} has nonempty support.

At l_w = p+1, then, the first identity holds exactly when T''_{w,00}∘T'_{w,et} = 0. The second identity needs the same vanishing. At the shifted weight l_w + p² − 1 ≥ p+2 we have T''_{w,00} = 0, and T'_{w,et}, T''_{w,et} commute with Ha' by Lemma 4.2.19. Since Ha'(G_w) is invertible on the =_w1 locus, T̃_w Ha' − Ha' T̃_w = −Ha'∘T''_{w,00}∘T'_{w,et}. The paper gives no argument for this vanishing, and its truth is not settled, so this is a gap and not an error.

The reach is a stated result: Lemma 4.2.20 is unproved as printed at l_w = p+1, and the printed "essentially identical" proof of the T̃_w part of Corollary 4.2.21 rests on it. Nothing further is lost:
- The T̃_w part of Corollary 4.2.21 still holds for l_w ≥ p+1 by the identity (S T̃_w)^n = T''_w (T^{I_b,J})^{n−1} T'_w S.
- The second diagram of Lemma 4.2.22, and Lemma 4.2.24, assume l_w ≥ p+2.
- Lemma 4.2.25 (l_w = p+1) cites Lemma 4.2.20 only for T_w. It uses T̃_w only at weight l_w + p² − 1 on the ≤_w1 locus.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 5.5.1, hypothesis on φ (arXiv v3 p. 123; publ. p. 302), as applied in the proofs of Proposition 5.6.1 (arXiv v3 p. 125; publ. p. 304) and Proposition 5.7.5 (arXiv v3 p. 130; publ. p. 310)
sourceIssues.printed: Suppose that (A, ι, λ) and (A′, ι′, λ′) are tuples as above and that we have a prime to p quasi-isogeny φ : A → A′ satisfying φι = ι′φ and φ^tλ′φ = xλ for some x ∈ O_F ⊗ Z_(p).
sourceIssues.correction: Replace "a prime to p quasi-isogeny φ : A → A′" by "a quasi-isogeny φ : A → A′ lying in Hom(A, A′) ⊗ Z_(p)". It need not be prime to p, and any isogeny qualifies, for example one of p-power degree. The rest of the statement and the printed proof are unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason:
Proposition 5.5.1 is used exactly twice: in the proofs of Propositions 5.6.1 and 5.7.5. Each proof reads only "This follows from Propositions 5.5.1 and 5.5.2". Neither use satisfies the hypothesis that φ be prime to p. The paper fixes this notion in §3.3 as Lan's Z_(p)^×-isogeny [Lan13, Defn. 1.3.1.17].

In 5.6.1, φ is the étale isogeny π : A → A/L_w. Its kernel L_w is a maximal isotropic subgroup of A[w], so it has order p^2. Here π^tλ′π = x_wλ, where x_w is a uniformiser at w (p splits completely in F).

In 5.7.5, φ is the universal isogeny p_1^*G → p_2^*G. Its kernel is a subgroup of G_w[p^2] of order p^4. Here φ^tλ′φ = x_w^2 λ, which is where the factor N(x_w)^6 comes from.

Under the printed hypothesis these cases cannot occur. If φ, λ and λ′ are all invertible in Hom ⊗ Z_(p), then so is xλ. So x is a unit of O_F ⊗ Z_(p), and N_{F/Q}(x)^3 is prime to p. But 5.6.1 and 5.7.5 print factors N(x_w)^3/p^3 and N(x_w)^6/p^6 in Z_(p)^×, which need v_p(N(x)^3) = 3 and 6. The remark after 5.6.1 says the same: some maps in the square reduce to 0 modulo p.

The case actually used holds, and the printed proof proves it:
- Take φ in Hom(A, A′) ⊗ Z_(p) and put φ^† = λ^{-1}φ^tλ′, which lies in Hom(A′, A) ⊗ Z_(p) because λ is prime to p.
- Then φ^†φ = x, so (φφ^† − x)φ = 0.
- Some prime-to-p multiple of φ is an isogeny, so φ can be cancelled on the right, giving φφ^† = x.
- Pulling back to ω gives (φ^t)^*(λ^*)^{-1}φ^* = (λ′^*)^{-1}x^* on ω_{A′}.
- Functoriality of Kodaira–Spencer gives KS_A∘φ^* = Lie(φ^t)∘KS_{A′}. Combining the two, KS_{(A,λ)}(φ^*a ⊗ φ^*b) = KS_{(A′,λ′)}(a ⊗ xb).
- On top exterior powers this gives the factor N_{F/Q}(x)^3.

The integrality of φ is what makes φ^* a map of sheaves over a Z_(p)-base. So an arbitrary quasi-isogeny, with p in a denominator, is not allowed.

Nothing printed is false: 5.5.1 is true as stated, and 5.6.1 and 5.7.5 are true. But the proofs of 5.6.1 and 5.7.5 rest on a case of 5.5.1 that the paper never states. That is a step without adequate justification, so this is a gap.

It is not a misprint. The printed hypothesis is a defined notion and reads coherently where it stands. That it must be dropped, and that the proposition survives without it, becomes clear only from the applications. It also needs the cancellation argument above: for such φ, the identity φφ^† = x can no longer be obtained by conjugating with φ^{-1}.

The reach is the proofs of 5.6.1 and 5.7.5. Every numbered statement stands once 5.5.1 is read with the corrected hypothesis.

sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 6.4.3, last sentence of the statement (isomorphism for i = 1 when k_v − l_v ≥ 3), together with the last sentence of its proof; arXiv v3 p. 153 (statement) and p. 154 (end of proof); published pp. 338 (statement) and 339 (end of proof)
sourceIssues.printed: "It is an isomorphism for i = 1 if we further assume that k_v − l_v ≥ 3 for all v|p." ... "The corollary therefore follows from the slope bounds of Propositions 6.4.1."
sourceIssues.correction: Replace "k_v − l_v ≥ 3 for all v|p" by "k_v − l_v ≥ 3N for all v|p, where N = #I + 2#I^c is the number of factors U_{v,1}, U_{v,2} in U^I". The same change is needed where the proof of Proposition 6.6.2 repeats "≥ 3". Keeping threshold 3 would need a slope bound ≥ −3 on H^1 for U^I itself, and the paper does not prove one.
sourceIssues.reason:
To get the i = 1 isomorphism, e(U^I) must kill E_1^{1,1} = ⊕_{v|p} H^1(X_{K(I,p^n)}(ε), F^{w_v•κ,w^-} ⊗ (det ω_G)^2(−D)). On the v-summand of that sum, U_{v,2} acts twisted by p^{k_v−l_v+1}. E_1^{2,0} is already killed by the H^0 bounds.

Proposition 6.4.1 bounds each operator on its own: on H^1, every U_{v,1} (v ∈ I^c) and every U_{v,2} (v|p) has slopes ≥ −3. But U^I = ∏_{v∈I} U_{v,2} ∏_{v∈I^c} U_{v,1}U_{v,2} is a product of N = #I + 2#I^c commuting factors. On a joint eigencharacter of the v-summand, these bounds give only slope(twisted U^I) ≥ (k_v − l_v + 1 − 3) − 3(N − 1) = k_v − l_v + 1 − 3N. This is > 0 exactly when k_v − l_v ≥ 3N.

When 3 ≤ k_v − l_v < 3N, Proposition 6.4.1 allows a character in which the twisted U_{v,2} has slope ≥ 1, the other factors have slopes ≥ −3, and the total slope is 0. So the differential E_1^{0,1} → E_1^{1,1} is not shown to vanish on the ordinary part. Going back to the integrality argument does not help either: each U_{v,1} and U_{v,2} carries its own p^{−3}Tr normalisation (p^{−6}Tr for U_{v,1}U_{v,2}), so that argument gives only −3N for U^I.

Threshold 3 is right only when N = 1, i.e. F = Q and I = {p}, where there is a single operator. When I = ∅, H^1 vanishes by Proposition 6.3.7, so the claim holds trivially. Since p splits completely, #I ≥ 1 and [F:Q] ≥ 2 give N = 2[F:Q] − #I ≥ 2 (for #I = 1, N ≥ 3). In that case the claim is not proved.

The claim may still be true, since a bound ≥ −3 for U^I itself would give it, so this is a gap and not an error. As printed, however, the last assertion of the numbered Corollary 6.4.3 is unproved. Only the per-factor argument's threshold 3N is established.

The i = 0 isomorphism and the i = 1 injectivity use only the H^0 bounds and still hold. The i = 1 isomorphism is used only in the proof of Proposition 6.6.2. There, local constancy of Euler characteristics lets one take k_v − l_v ≥ C with C as large as needed, so C ≥ 3N works. Proposition 6.6.2, Theorems 6.6.4 and 6.6.5, and the main results therefore stand.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 7.4.10(2), proof of the case i = 2, last paragraph ("Étale locally, one may trivialize ψ′ …") (arXiv v3 p. 191; published p. 384)
sourceIssues.printed: Let A′ be the étale A-algebra A[√ψ′(f₁, f₁), √ψ′(f₂, f₂)], so that over U′ = Spec A′, (𝒪⁴_{𝒩₂}/ker N)_{U′} has a basis f₁′ = f₁/√ψ′(f₁, f₁), f₂′ = f₂/√ψ′(f₂, f₂) with ψ′(f₁′, f₁′) = ψ′(f₂′, f₂′) = 1 and ψ′(f₁′, f₂′) = 0. Now lift f₁′ and f₂′ to sections e₁ and e₂ of 𝒪⁴_{U′}. We may further arrange that ψ(e₁, e₂) = 0 by replacing e₂ by e₂ − ψ(e₁, e₂)Ne₁. Then Ne₂, Ne₁, e₁, e₂ forms a symplectic basis for 𝒪⁴_{U′}, and if we let g ∈ GSp₄ have these elements as columns, then N_{U′} = gN₂g⁻¹.
sourceIssues.correction: Let A′ = A[√ψ′(f₁, f₁), √(−ψ′(f₂, f₂))] (étale since p > 2) and f₂′ = f₂/√(−ψ′(f₂, f₂)), so that ψ′(f₁′, f₁′) = 1 = −ψ′(f₂′, f₂′) and ψ′(f₁′, f₂′) = 0. Lift h₁ = (f₁′ + f₂′)/2 and h₂ = f₁′ − f₂′ (ψ′-isotropic, with ψ′(h₁, h₂) = 1) to sections e₁, e₂ of 𝒪⁴_{U′}, and arrange ψ(e₁, e₂) = 0 by replacing e₂ by e₂ + ψ(e₁, e₂)Ne₂. Then Ne₁, Ne₂, e₁, e₂ is a symplectic basis for 𝒪⁴_{U′}, and the g ∈ GSp₄ with these columns satisfies N_{U′} = gN₂g⁻¹.
sourceIssues.reason: By §2.1.1, ψ(v, w) = vᵗJw with J = (0 s; −s 0), s = (0 1; 1 0). So a basis b₁, …, b₄ is symplectic when ψ(b₁, b₄) = ψ(b₂, b₃) = 1 and every other pairing with i < j is 0. On the same page N₂ = E₁₃ + E₂₄. On 𝒩₂ we have N² = 0 and ψ(Nv, w) = −ψ(v, Nw). The printed step goes wrong twice. (i) ψ(e₁, Ne₁) = −ψ′(f₁′, f₁′) = −1, so for c = ψ(e₁, e₂) we get ψ(e₁, e₂ − cNe₁) = 2c, which is not 0. The sign has to be +. (ii) Even after that fix, the columns b = (Ne₂, Ne₁, e₁, e₂) satisfy Nb₃ = b₂ and Nb₄ = b₁. So g⁻¹Ng = E₁₄ + E₂₃, not N₂. Reordering the columns does not help. If g⁻¹Ng = N₂ for some g ∈ GSp₄, then Nb₃ = b₁ and Nb₄ = b₂, so ψ′(b₃, b₃) = ψ(b₁, b₃) = 0 and ψ′(b₄, b₄) = ψ(b₂, b₄) = 0. That makes ψ′ hyperbolic. On A′ as constructed, however, ψ′ has an orthonormal basis, so ψ′ ≅ x² + y², and this form is anisotropic at every point whose residue field has −1 as a non-square. For a concrete case, take the residue field of 𝒪 to be F₃ and let N = E₁₄ + E₂₃ ∈ 𝒩₂(𝒪). Its form ψ′ on ⟨e₃, e₄⟩ has Gram matrix I. The printed recipe gives g = 1 at this point, and no element of GSp₄(F₃) conjugates N₂ to E₁₄ + E₂₃, because conjugation by g multiplies ψ′ by ν(g), and x² + y² is anisotropic over F₃. So the step fails as written and cannot be repaired by fixing a sign or reordering: ψ′ has to be normalised to a hyperbolic form. Statement (2) is still true, because it is only étale-local. Adjoining √(−ψ′(f₂, f₂)) in place of √ψ′(f₂, f₂) is étale since p > 2, and it gives ψ′ the Gram matrix diag(1, −1). The hyperbolic basis h₁, h₂ and the columns Ne₁, Ne₂, e₁, e₂ then give gᵗJg = J and gN₂g⁻¹ = N_{U′} (ψ(e₁, Ne₂) = −1 makes the adjustment kill ψ(e₁, e₂)). Proposition 7.4.10(3), Proposition 7.4.14 and Corollary 7.4.15 use only the statement of (2). So only the proof is affected.

sourceIssues.printed: Since the automorphism group of PSL₂(k) is PGL₂(k), it follows that the projective representations associated to r̄ and r̄^σ have the same image if and only if they are the same.
sourceIssues.correction:
Since the automorphism group of PSL₂(k) is PΓL₂(k) = PGL₂(k) ⋊ Gal(k/F_p), images that are not disjoint force Proj r̄^σ ≅ τ∘Proj r̄ for some τ ∈ Gal(k/F_p).

Cases already settled:
- τ = 1 is excluded by hypothesis.
- For p = 3, every τ is excluded by the disjointness hypothesis, since Proj r̄ and τ∘Proj r̄ have the same kernel.
This settles k = F_p and p = 3.

For p ≥ 5 and k ≠ F_p, the case τ ≠ 1 needs its own argument:
- Then τ² = 1, so τ is the involution of k over a subfield k₀ with #k₀ = q₀ ≥ 5.
- In a suitable basis, the image G of ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is an index-2 extension of N = {(A, ±τ(A)) : A ∈ SL₂(k)}, not SL₂(k) ≀ Z/2Z.
- G is still enormous:
  - (E2) holds because V ≇ V^τ.
  - (E1) holds because H¹(SL₂(k), Sym²V) = 0 (as #k ≥ 25) and H¹(SL₂(k), V ⊗ V^τ) = 0 (as p ≥ 5).
  - (E3) follows from Lemma 7.5.17. Here As(V)|N = V ⊗ V^τ is irreducible, and Ind ad⁰V restricted to N is Sym²V ⊕ Sym²V^τ, whose two summands are non-isomorphic and swapped by G. Apply the lemma to g = (C, ±C)·w ∈ G∖N, where w is the swap and C ∈ SL₂(k₀) has order q₀+1. Then g² = ±(C², C²) ≠ ±1 has order prime to p.
- G has no quotient of p-power order, so ρ̄ is vast.
- Lemma 7.5.13 does not give tidiness here, because Δ is not contained in the image. Instead take ρ̄(g) for g ∈ G_K with r̄(g) = diag(a, −a⁻¹), where a generates k^×. Then ν = −1, and no two of the eigenvalues a, −a⁻¹, ±τ(a), ∓τ(a)⁻¹ have ratio −1.
sourceIssues.reason:
In §7, k is the residue field of an arbitrary finite extension of Q_p, and Lemma 9.2.2 applies Lemma 7.5.22 with k = O_M/λ. So k need not be a prime field.

For #k > 3, Aut(PSL₂(k)) = PΓL₂(k), which is strictly larger than PGL₂(k) when k ≠ F_p, so the printed fact is false. Goursat's lemma then only shows that images which are not disjoint force Proj r̄^σ ≅ τ∘Proj r̄ for a field automorphism τ. For p = 3 the disjointness hypothesis rules this out, but for p ≥ 5 the hypothesis Proj r̄^σ ≇ Proj r̄ does not.

The case actually occurs:
- Let A/F have type B[C₂]. Its real multiplication by a real quadratic field is defined over K, and σ acts on that field nontrivially.
- Take l inert in that field. Then r̄ = s̄_λ : G_K → GL₂(F_{l²}) satisfies every hypothesis of the lemma: the image contains SL₂(F_{l²}) for density-one l, det = ε̄⁻¹, and Proj s̄^σ ≅ Frob∘Proj s̄ ≇ Proj s̄.
- But ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄_{A,l} ⊗ F_{l²} has image in a conjugate of GSp₄(F_l). Since 2|SL₂(F_{l²})|² = 2l⁴(l⁴−1)² > l⁴(l²−1)(l⁴−1) = |Sp₄(F_l)|, the image over F(ζ_l) cannot be SL₂(F_{l²}) ≀ Z/2Z, as the proof asserts.
- Δ is not contained in this image either, so the appeal to Lemma 7.5.13 for tidiness also fails.
- Inert primes make up half of all primes, so the density-one claim of Lemma 9.2.2 depends on this case.

The step is therefore false, not a slip, and the kind is error.

Both statements survive. In the twisted case, τ is an involution and the image over F(ζ_p) is an index-2 extension of {(A, ±τ(A))}. This group is enormous: V ≇ V^τ; H¹(SL₂(k), Sym²) = 0 since #k ≥ 25; H¹(SL₂(k), V ⊗ V^τ) = 0 since p ≥ 5; and Lemma 7.5.17 applies to an element (C, ±C)·swap with C of order q₀+1 in SL₂(k₀). The group has no p-power quotient, so ρ̄ is vast. An element with first block diag(a, −a⁻¹) gives tidiness. So Lemmas 7.5.22 and 9.2.2 hold as stated, and only their proofs need the extra case: the reach is the proof.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 9.2.7: property (4), the first bullet of (5), and the choice of φ̄_{w_1}, φ̄_{w_2} in its proof. This carries over to the v|q step of the proof of Theorem 9.2.8. arXiv v3 pp. 256–257; published pp. 462–464 (lemma pp. 462–463, proof of the theorem p. 464).
sourceIssues.printed: "(5) Set ρ̄_q := Ind^{G_{F′}}_{G_{F′F_1}} r̄_q : G_{F′} → GSp_4(F_q) with similitude factor ε̄^{−1}. Then • for any place w|q of F and any place w′|w of F′, ρ̄_q|_{G_{F′_{w′}}} ≅ (ρ̄_{A,q}|_{G_{F_w}})^{ss}," … [proof] "If w|p, then the eigenvalues of (A[q]^∨|_{G_{F_w}})(Frob_w) can be written as α_w, β_w, pβ_w^{−1}, pα_w^{−1}, while if w|q we use the notation above. In either case, we choose φ̄_{w_1} to correspond to the representation (λ_{α_w} 0 ; 0 ε^{−1}λ_{α_w}^{−1}), and φ̄_{w_2} to correspond to (λ_{β_w} 0 ; 0 ε^{−1}λ_{β_w}^{−1})." … [Thm 9.2.8] "Finally, if v|q, the canonical lift of A modulo v gives a point of Y(F′_v)."
sourceIssues.correction:
The data at q must change.

(a) In Lemma 9.2.6, first fix p. Then also require q > p^2 and that Frob_q be conjugate to complex conjugation in the Galois closure over Q of F(A[p], ζ_p, √Δ_v : v|p), where Δ_v = a_1(v)^2 − 4a_2(v) + 8p. This is a positive-density Chebotarev condition on primes that split completely in F, so good q of this kind exist. It gives q ≡ −1 mod p and q split in each real field Q(√Δ_v).

(b) In the proof of Lemma 9.2.7:
- For w|p, take φ̄_{w_1}, φ̄_{w_2} unramified and F_q-rational, with Frob_w-characteristic polynomials (x−α_w)(x−pα_w^{−1}) and (x−β_w)(x−pβ_w^{−1}). These lie in F_q[x] by (a).
- For w|q, take φ̄_{w_1} = diag(λ_a, ε̄^{−1}λ_a^{−1}) and φ̄_{w_2} = diag(λ_b, ε̄^{−1}λ_b^{−1}), with a = p and b = −p in F_q.
- Replace the first bullet of (5) by ρ̄_q|_{G_{F′_{w′}}} ≅ λ_a ⊕ λ_b ⊕ ε̄^{−1}λ_b^{−1} ⊕ ε̄^{−1}λ_a^{−1}.

(c) In the proof of Theorem 9.2.8, for v|q, replace "the canonical lift of A modulo v" by the canonical lift of E × E′. Here E, E′/F_q are elliptic curves with traces p and −p, which exist by Deuring since p < 2√q.
- It is ordinary.
- Its q-torsion is ρ̄_q^∨ locally.
- Its p-torsion is symplectically isomorphic to A[p]|_{G_{F_w}}: on both, Frob_w acts as an involution of multiplier −1 with 2-dimensional ±1-eigenspaces.

Everything else stands, including Theorem 9.2.8.
sourceIssues.reason:
Property (4) makes r̄_q take values in GL_2(F_q). Let w|q. Since q splits completely in F′F_1, the restriction of ρ̄_q = Ind r̄_q to the decomposition group at w′|w is r̄_q|_{w′_1} ⊕ r̄_q|_{w′_2}. Each summand is F_q-rational with determinant ε̄^{−1}, and ε̄^{−1} is ramified at q because q ≥ 3.

So each summand has exactly one unramified and one ramified constituent among λ_ᾱ, λ_β̄, ε̄^{−1}λ_β̄^{−1}, ε̄^{−1}λ_ᾱ^{−1}. The determinant, together with ᾱ_w ≠ β̄_w, forces the constituents to be λ_x and ε̄^{−1}λ_x^{−1} with x ∈ {ᾱ_w, β̄_w}. Frobenius acting on the coefficients sends λ_x to λ_{x^q}, which is still unramified. F_q-rationality therefore forces x^q = x. Hence the first bullet of (5) can hold only if ᾱ_w, β̄_w ∈ F_q.

These are the roots of x^2 − a_1(w)x + a_2(w) mod q, and being a good prime does not put them in F_q:
- Definition 7.3.1 takes λ_x with x in the residue field k of a coefficient field that may be enlarged.
- The proof of Lemma 9.2.5 uses only the condition q ∤ a_1^2 − 4a_2.

The roots lie outside F_q whenever a_1^2 − 4a_2 is a non-square mod q. For example, for the Jacobian of y^2 + (x^3+1)y = x^2 + x over Q, point counting at q = 97 gives a_1 = 10 and a_2 = 82. The reduction is ordinary, and a_1^2 − 4a_2 ≡ 63 is a non-square mod 97.

For such q, no r̄_q satisfies both (4) and (5), so Lemma 9.2.7 is false as printed. The step of the proof that fails is the choice φ̄_{w_1} = diag(λ_{α_w}, ε^{−1}λ_{α_w}^{−1}). It is not GL_2(F_q)-valued, which Propositions 9.1.12 and 9.1.11 require.

The same printed choice at w|p also needs α_w ∈ F_q. There, (5) needs only that the pairs {α_w, pα_w^{−1}} and {β_w, pβ_w^{−1}} (the pairing is forced, because their products must equal p) be Frobenius-stable over F_q. This means Δ_w is a square mod q. It fails for a positive density of q, but a Chebotarev condition can impose it.

At q, no Chebotarev condition helps, because ᾱ_w is the reduction mod q of the Frobenius at q itself. So the data at q must change. With it changes the point of Ω_v at v|q in Theorem 9.2.8, which relied on the canonical lift of A having q-torsion (ρ̄_{A,q}|_{G_{F_w}})^{ss}.

With the choices in the correction:
- Propositions 9.1.12 and 9.1.11 receive F_q-rational diagonal data.
- (6) still follows from (4) via Lemma 7.5.22.
- ρ̄_{B,q} stays q-distinguished, since p ≢ −p mod q.
- The canonical lift of E × E′ lies in Ω_v.

So Theorem 9.2.8, and the results drawn from it, survive. But the numbered Lemma 9.2.7 is false as printed, and its proof step fails. Hence this is an error affecting a stated result.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 9.2.7, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs, from "The obstruction to the existence of a square root" to "has a square root" (arXiv v3 p. 257; published p. 463)
sourceIssues.printed: The obstruction to the existence of a square root of ε̄ det r̄_q is therefore a class in the 2-torsion of Br_{F_1F′} which is trivial at all places dividing pq𝔯∞. We can therefore replace F′ by a quadratic totally real extension in which p, q, 𝔯 split completely, and assume that ε̄ det r̄_q has a square root.
sourceIssues.correction: Build r̄_q with det r̄_q = ε̄^{-1} from the start. Run the Moret-Bailly argument of Proposition 9.1.12 on the variety of GL_2(F_q)-torsors whose determinant torsor is the F_q^×-torsor given by ε̄^{-1}, instead of on X_G for G = GL_2(F_q). Equivalently, use torsors under the twist of SL_2(F_q) by ε̄^{-1}. Keep the same local data: every φ̄_w has determinant ε̄^{-1}, and det c_v = −1 = ε̄^{-1}(c_v). Condition (2) of that proposition becomes L′ ∩ K′F^{(avoid)} = K′(ζ_q). Then (3) holds by construction, (4)–(6) follow as printed, and the square-root paragraph is deleted.
sourceIssues.reason:
Write K′ = F_1F′ and ψ = ε̄ det r̄_q : G_{K′} → F_q^×. Twisting r̄_q must keep it valued in GL_2(F_q). Condition (4) needs this, and so does Theorem 9.2.8, which identifies B[q] with ρ̄_q^∨. So the proof needs a character θ : G_{K′} → F_q^× with θ^2 = ψ.

Squaring on F_q^× has image of index 2. So such a θ exists only if ψ takes square values, i.e. ψ^{(q−1)/2} = 1. Only after that does the obstruction lie in H^2(G_{K′}, ±1) = Br_{K′}[2]. The Brauer-class description is correct only for F̄_q-valued square roots. The printed claim that the obstruction "is a class in the 2-torsion of Br" is therefore false for the root that is needed.

The missing first obstruction does not vanish here. By Proposition 9.1.12(2), L′ is linearly disjoint over K′ from K′F^{(avoid)}. That field contains K′(ζ_q), since ζ_q ∈ F(A[q]) by the Weil pairing. Also [K′(ζ_q):K′] = q−1, because q splits completely in K′. So (r̄_q, ε̄) maps G_{K′} onto GL_2(F_q) × F_q^×, and ψ is onto F_q^×. Hence no F_q^×-valued square root exists over F_1F′.

Replacing F′ by a quadratic extension F″ chosen to kill a Brauer class does not change this. For ψ to become square-valued, F_1F″ would have to contain the quadratic extension of K′ cut out by ψ^{(q−1)/2}, and the argument does nothing to arrange that.

An F̄_q-valued root does not help either. Pick g with r̄_q(g) = 1 and ε̄(g) a non-square. The twist sends g to a scalar θ(g)^{-1} ∉ F_q, so the twisted representation is not valued in GL_2(F_q). The step therefore fails; it is not merely left unjustified.

The reach is only the proof. The local data already have determinant ε̄^{-1} everywhere, so the fixed-determinant form of the Moret-Bailly construction gives r̄_q with (1)–(3) directly. Its restriction to G_{K′(ζ_q)} has image SL_2(F_q), and (4)–(6) then follow exactly as printed, via the places above 𝔯 and Lemma 7.5.22. Lemma 9.2.7, and Theorem 9.2.8 which uses it, remain true.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 10.1.3, conclusion (the definition of "ordinarily modular"): arXiv v3 p. 266, with the statement starting on p. 265; published p. 474, with the statement starting on p. 473. The same words occur in the hypothesis of Proposition 10.1.1 (arXiv v3 p. 265; published p. 472) and in the proof of Theorem 10.1.4 (arXiv v3 p. 267; published p. 476).
sourceIssues.printed: Then ρ̄_p is ordinarily modular, that is, there exists π of parallel weight 2 and central character | · |² which is unramified and ordinary at all v|p, such that ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄, and ρ_{π,p}|_{G_{F_v}} is pure for all finite places v of F.
sourceIssues.correction: Delete "unramified and" in all three places. In Proposition 10.1.3 read "there exists π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|² which is ordinary at all v|p, such that ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄, …". In Proposition 10.1.1 read "…central character |·|² which is ordinary at all v|p, such that ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄_{A,p}, …". In the proof of Theorem 10.1.4 read "…we construct a π of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|² which is ordinary at all v|p such that ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄". This agrees with Theorem 1.1.7 and with Theorem 8.4.1(4).
sourceIssues.reason:
By §2.4.7, "unramified" means π_v^{GSp4(O_{F_v})} ≠ 0, which is a stronger condition than ordinary. By Proposition 2.4.24, an ordinary π_v of weight (2,2) that is also spherical must be an irreducible unramified principal series, because types IIa, IIIa and Va have no spherical vector. Hence α_v², β_v² and α_vβ_v are all different from 1.

The hypotheses of Proposition 10.1.3 allow ϱ̄|G_{E_w} to be très ramifiée at a place w|p. Definition 7.3.1 leaves the upper-right block arbitrary. For example, take p = 5 and E totally real with 5 unramified. Apply Lemmas 7.5.26–7.5.27 to r̄ = the dual mod-5 representation of an elliptic curve over F with surjective mod-5 image and multiplicative reduction at some v|5 with 5 ∤ v(q). The result is a ρ̄ = Ind(r̄|G_E ⊗ δ) that satisfies (2), and its ϱ̄ is not finite flat at w|v. Theorem 10.1.4 likewise allows semistable ordinary reduction at 5.

In this case the proof fails. The weight-2 ordinary Hilbert modular form lifting ϱ̄ cannot be unramified at w. If it were, its Galois representation at w would be crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1, and ϱ̄|G_{E_w} would then be finite flat. So the form is of Steinberg type at w, and its automorphic induction is not spherical at v. The proof only shows that π is ordinary.

The conclusion itself is also false in this case. Suppose π were spherical and ordinary at v with ρ̄_{π,p} ≅ ρ̄. By local–global compatibility at p (Corollary 7.9.6(4)), ρ_{π,p}|G_{F_v} is an extension of ε^{-1}λ_{β_v^{-1}} ⊕ ε^{-1}λ_{α_v^{-1}} by λ_{α_v} ⊕ λ_{β_v}. The extension classes lie in the groups H^1(Q_p, ελ_z) with z ∈ {α_v², α_vβ_v, β_v²}. Since z ≠ 1, every class in these groups is crystalline. So ρ_{π,p}|G_{F_v} is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights in an interval of length 1. By Fontaine–Laffaille (p ≥ 3, F_v = Q_p), ρ̄|G_{F_v} would be finite flat, and so would its summand ϱ̄|G_{E_w}. That is a contradiction.

So Proposition 10.1.3 is false as printed. Deleting "unramified and" gives exactly what the proof establishes. Theorem 8.4.1(4) and Hypothesis 7.13.1(6) require only "ordinary". So Proposition 10.1.1 with the weaker hypothesis, which is Theorem 1.1.7 of the introduction, and Theorem 10.1.4 still follow. The deletion in 10.1.1 is needed so that the corrected 10.1.3 still supplies its hypothesis (as after 10.1.3 and in the proof of Theorem 10.2.6). The deletion in the proof of 10.1.4 is needed because the π built there is not spherical at v for curves with multiplicative reduction.
